releases.title: Sign-in polish: Touch ID in the app, no more spinning tabs, connector landing pages

items.label: Touch ID works in the installed app: the unlock prompt (⌘↩ on the profile screen) no longer fails with an 'invalid domain' error
Signing in with Google or Apple now ends on a clean 'You're signed in — close this tab' page instead of leaving the browser spinning, and Job Tracker comes to the front by itself
Connecting Gmail or Outlook ends on a tidy confirmation page (no more full app rendered inside a browser tab), and the Mail settings update the moment you return — no refresh needed
The signed-in line shows how you signed in (Google/Apple/email) and your Google profile photo
The sign-in dialog no longer shows a stale spinner when reopened after a successful sign-in
Clearer message when an account feature needs you to sign in first
Note: this update moves the app to a new internal address, so you'll be asked for your profile password once after upgrading — nothing is lost and it won't happen again

releases.title: Auto job descriptions, document seeding, smarter attachments, tidier detail pages

items.label: New opportunities get their job description automatically: when the listing URL (or fetched text) is known, the app scrapes, AI-formats, and saves job-description.md — no more manual fetch-then-format
“Fetch from URL” now AI-formats the scraped posting before it lands in the editor

Tailored Resume starts itself: jobs with an attached résumé PDF get a mirrored structured version (one logged AI call); otherwise your template’s cached version seeds instantly — cover letters seed from their attached PDF too

Attachments: one configurable document folder (Settings → Data) now powers the résumé/cover/JD pickers and fuzzy suggestions — previously two different hardcoded folders; “Import from folder” works on every tab, not just offer letters
If a job has a Canva design link but no PDF, the Attachments card shows the Canva link instead of “No PDF attached”
Job pages stay focused: Interview & Offer sections collapse to a one-line summary until your statuses make them relevant, then expand automatically (your manual choice is remembered)

releases.title: Gmail reconnect detection, roadmap drift line, calendar cancellations

items.label: Gmail now detects a dead connection: if Google rejects the saved sign-in, the Mail settings show 'Needs reconnect' with what happened and how to fix it for good (instead of a green badge over a broken link)
The email-import dialog live-checks the Gmail connection when it opens, so a dead token surfaces before you search — not as an error after
The AI connection troubleshooter gives correct Gmail advice (Desktop-app client, no redirect URIs to register) and names the real cause of weekly disconnects — a consent screen left in Testing mode
Roadmap: the Completed section shows the latest stamped release next to the app version, so unstamped releases are visible at a glance; finished items without a recorded release now say so
Cancelled interview rounds are retracted from subscribed calendars (STATUS:CANCELLED) instead of lingering as upcoming events

releases.title: Current Job Status: the AI knows you're employed

items.label: New Current Job Status context section — employer, title, start date and current comp, with tenure derived from the date so it never goes stale
Recruiter replies, cover letters, interview prep and every comp prompt now read your real employment status instead of assuming you're between roles
Notice period is a duration again — it no longer doubles as an employment claim that leaked "available immediately" into drafts
Confidential-search mode: drafts never name your current employer or suggest anyone there be contacted
Comp anchor is now your CURRENT package rather than an older floor, with an only-go-up rule for weighing a move
Needs-Action nudge when you accept an offer but your profile still says otherwise, with one-click apply from the offer record
Onboarding audit flags a notice period that smuggles an employment claim, and the Collection Guide no longer leaks your employer or salary into a family member's guide

releases.title: Opt-in auto-inactivate: quiet leads move along the ladder on visit

items.label: Completes the inactivity feature: a new Settings → Thresholds toggle "Auto-apply on visit" (OFF by default). When on, leads / recruiter-outreach engagements past your silence thresholds move themselves along the ladder (active→dormant→abandoned) on your next visit, with an Undo — but never ones you've dismissed, snoozed, converted, or already abandoned. Off = byte-identical: you keep getting suggestions to apply by hand.

releases.title: Inactive-lead nudges: per-record chip, stale filter, bulk review sweep

items.label: Follow-on surfaces for the inactivity detector: each lead / recruiter-outreach engagement detail page now shows an in-context "Gone quiet" nudge (Apply the suggested Dormant/Abandoned move or Dismiss — kept in sync with the Priorities queue); the Recruiter Outreach list gains a "Stale only" filter to match Leads; and both lists get a "Gone quiet (N)" bulk review sweep to clear the backlog — apply each suggestion or all at once.

releases.title: Detect inactive leads & recruiter outreach, suggest a status update

items.label: Leads and recruiter-outreach engagements that have gone quiet on comms now surface a suggestion in Priorities / Needs-Action to mark them Dormant (after 21 days of silence), then Abandoned (after 60) — one click applies it. Distinguishes "awaiting their reply, gone cold" from "no activity at all"; never touches converted or abandoned leads. Tune the day thresholds in Settings → Thresholds.

releases.title: Logs: end-to-end error trails, diagnostics sharing & AI reliability

items.label: Logs: end-to-end error trails, diagnostics sharing & AI reliability

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach pitched-role & meeting pages no longer flash to Leads

items.label: Pitched-role and meeting detail pages for recruiter engagements now live under /recruiter-outreach/[id]/… instead of /leads/[id]/…, so the sidebar stays on Recruiter Outreach with no flash and the browser back button no longer 404s. Old /leads/… links for engagements redirect to the canonical path automatically; regular leads are unaffected.

releases.title: Logs: copy buttons + "what I was doing" error breadcrumbs

items.label: The Logs → System tab has copy buttons now: “Copy details” on any operation or error gives a clean, paste-ready block (function, entity, error, full context), and “Copy N” grabs all the filtered rows at once. Errors also record what you were doing just before they happened — your recent page navigations and clicks — under a “What I was doing” section, so a crash or a broken-link 404 is far easier to diagnose.

The “Refer a friend” panel now shows your referral code alongside a running count of how many people have used it, with honest framing that bonus days aren’t active yet and will apply once referrals go live.

Behind the scenes: inert reliability groundwork from a parallel hardening pass — your access token now refreshes when you switch profiles, plus dormant plumbing for per-profile AI-usage attribution and a double-pay safeguard on referral-bonus settlement. Everything stays gated off behind the current enforcement switches, so there’s no visible change today.

releases.title: Fixed a 404 when returning from a pitched role to its recruiter engagement

items.label: Opening a pitched role (or a meeting) inside a Recruiter Outreach engagement and then going back no longer hits a “404 — page not found.” The back link now correctly returns to the engagement on the Recruiter Outreach page, instead of trying the Leads page (where recruiter engagements don’t live).

releases.title: “Add Pitched Role” is now a first-class AI feature

items.label: The new “Add with AI” for pitched roles is now properly registered as its own AI feature: it shows a clear label in AI Logs, counts as free-eligible (matching the parse engine it runs on, instead of silently defaulting to a paid tier), and is linked to the shared parse prompt under Settings → AI Prompts. Purely a wiring fix — the feature already worked.

releases.title: Add a pitched role with AI on recruiter engagements

items.label: New “✨ Add with AI” on a recruiter engagement’s Pitched roles: when a recruiter floats another role mid-conversation, paste their message (or scan the conversation already captured here) and the AI extracts the role(s) they pitched — with the end-client company and any staffing vendor, not the agency. Review and tweak each one, then add. In paste mode the message is also saved to the conversation and linked to the new role, and roles you already track are skipped so you don’t get duplicates.
The per-role “Update with AI” (re-score fit/interest and fill in comp, JD, and requirements from a follow-up) is now a clearly labeled button instead of just a ✨ icon, so it’s easy to find.

releases.title: Behind the scenes: AI backend for adding pitched roles to an engagement

items.label: Groundwork for a new “Add pitched role with AI” capability on recruiter engagements — the app can now read a recruiter’s new message (or the existing conversation) and extract the role(s) they pitched, skipping ones you already track. Not wired into the screen yet — that lands next; nothing changes for you today.

releases.title: Recruiter engagements with a deadline date now save — plus clearer save errors

items.label: Fixed a bug where adding a recruiter engagement (or a job) could fail to save with an “Invalid” error when the recruiter message or job description carried a closing / deadline date. The deadline’s timeline marker was being stored without a timezone, which the save quietly rejected — deadlines now save correctly.

When a save is ever rejected, the app now names the exact field that failed (in the error toast and under Logs → System) instead of a generic “Invalid” message, so problems are diagnosable instead of a dead end.
Fixed the sidebar switching to “Leads” when you open a pitched role or a meeting inside a Recruiter Outreach engagement — it now correctly keeps “Recruiter Outreach” highlighted.

releases.title: One-click invite links + household join over sign-in

items.label: Invite links open the app straight to a prefilled join screen, so joining takes no typing
Join a household with your own Google or Apple account — a shared plan with private data

releases.title: QA follow-ups: merge summary shows the offer; blocked URLs return 400

items.label: The merge review now lists the offer among the items moving into the survivor, so it can no longer fold in silently
Pasting an internal/blocked URL into the parser now returns a clean bad-request error instead of a server-error (500)

releases.title: First-run 'Create or join' onboarding fork

items.label: New first-launch screen to create your own workspace or join someone with a code, shown before setup
Guided join: paste a code, confirm the plan, and sign in with Google or Apple to attach your workspace to it

releases.title: Attachment filenames with commas import correctly

items.label: A single imported attachment whose filename contains a comma is no longer split into several broken attachment entries

releases.title: Interview-result labels no longer overwrite AI-applied ones

items.label: When AI applies interview-result labels to a job, toggling a result chip afterward now keeps the AI’s labels instead of overwriting them with a stale selection

releases.title: Switching profiles during a save can no longer corrupt data

items.label: If you switch profiles at the exact moment a job change is being saved, the save is now pinned to the profile it started on, so it can no longer write into (and overwrite) the other profile’s data

releases.title: Enforce the write-permission guard across every record edit

items.label: When role-based permissions are turned on, every job/lead/contact/message edit now checks write permission — previously only the top-level create/edit/delete routes did, leaving most edits ungated

releases.title: Hardening: cleaner AI limits, self-healing proxy, safer profile creation

items.label: When AI access limits eventually turn on, hitting a limit shows a clean message instead of an error, and a rate-limited app-provided AI now recovers on its own instead of staying stuck
A spaced {{ careerContext }} token is now filled in correctly, and creating a profile can no longer overwrite data on a not-yet-migrated install

releases.title: Sturdier lead edits, promotions, and settings dialogs

items.label: Promoting two similar leads on the same day no longer fails with an error — the second gets a distinct job id
Lead edits are now validated, and a contact edit can no longer accidentally re-link the contact to the wrong person
The split-conversation dialog no longer remembers a stale selection, and a half-typed company alias no longer jumps to the wrong group after you delete one

releases.title: Imports dedupe correctly and a bad web page can’t break scraping

items.label: Appending a CSV/iMessage/email/paste import to an existing conversation now correctly finds its prior messages, so it dedupes instead of double-inserting and inherits the right contact
Re-importing no longer drops a genuinely new message that happens to be within two minutes of an earlier one
Deleting a job that a watch-role was promoted into now frees that role to be tracked/re-promoted instead of being stuck Promoted
A malformed job-posting page can no longer crash the URL scraper, and lead imports now give the AI the lead’s real details

releases.title: Dates land on the right day everywhere

items.label: Offer received-on dates, the create form’s default date, calendar deep-links, and scheduled-round times no longer shift by a day/hour depending on the time of day or timezone
Upcoming rounds sort chronologically even when times are stored in different ISO formats, and the AI cost-by-day chart no longer drops a day around the spring clock change

releases.title: Desktop reliability: no leaked windows, dialogs, DB handles, or wiped keys

items.label: A transient Keychain read hiccup can no longer wipe your saved API keys — the app leaves the secure store untouched instead of overwriting it
The résumé PDF export no longer leaks a hidden window when you cancel or it fails; the manual update check no longer pops a stray dialog later
Deleting a profile now releases its database handle, and permanently deleting a lead cleans up its attachment files

releases.title: Adding a message no longer drops a simultaneous one

items.label: Logging, editing, or deleting a message while another change to the same conversation is being processed no longer silently discards one of them

releases.title: Concurrent settings and feedback edits no longer overwrite each other

items.label: Editing a résumé template (or provider API keys, or AI feedback) while another change is in flight no longer silently discards one of the two edits
Clearing a provider API key now writes atomically, so an interrupted save can’t truncate the env file

releases.title: Interview status stays accurate across rounds and cancellations

items.label: An earlier round is no longer auto-marked Advanced just because a later-numbered round exists — progression now follows real dates, not round numbers
A conversation that got one reply long ago and went quiet now correctly shows as Delayed / Gone Cold instead of staying warm forever
Cancelled or withdrawn interview rounds no longer show up as upcoming interviews to prepare for
Setting a round back to a pre-interview status (Scheduled/Discussing) no longer marks it as already completed

releases.title: AI prompt improvements actually take effect

items.label: Applying an AI-improved prompt now changes what the model actually receives (previously it activated a variant the runtime never read)
The prompt improver now works from your editable template with its {{placeholders}} intact, instead of a resolved copy with one profile’s facts baked in
Lead enrichment is now tracked under its own feature, so its model pin, context, and feedback apply correctly

releases.title: Close SSRF and cross-record file-deletion gaps

items.label: The image proxy and URL scraper now refuse internal/private addresses and re-check every redirect hop, closing two server-side request-forgery gaps
Deleting a message attachment now verifies it belongs to that message, so a crafted request can no longer remove another record’s files
A profile avatar can only be fetched for a real profile, closing a path-traversal read

releases.title: Imported or partial jobs no longer crash the dashboard

items.label: A job imported or saved without complete document/compensation data no longer 500s the dashboard, jobs list, export, or merge
Deleting the last résumé or cover-letter version now sticks instead of a phantom Existing… version reappearing on the next load

releases.title: Merging a duplicate role no longer deletes its files

items.label: Merging a duplicate role now keeps its résumé, cover letter, JD, offer letters (and their extracted text), and interview attachments/transcripts instead of deleting them; offer-cycle links, blank contact fields, and tag states are preserved too

releases.title: A permanent download link for sharing the app

items.label: The macOS installer now lives at a permanent, version-independent download link, so an invite or a shared link always points at the latest version — the groundwork for inviting family and teammates to their own workspace.

releases.title: Shared account plans, a clearer profile picker, and setup polish

items.label: Settings → Profiles now has “Your account’s workspaces” — add a profile to your online account so its AI usage counts toward one shared plan, and the profile picker shows which profiles are on your plan.
A fresh install now starts with a neutral profile name instead of a pre-filled one.
When your account’s shared AI is running low, a heads-up appears with the option to start your own plan.
New “pro tips” tour for setting up your Connections.
Polished the invite-by-email preview so it no longer clips.
Under the hood: fixed a packaging issue where the app could gradually break its own security seal after optimizing images — protecting auto-updates, Gatekeeper, and secure storage.

releases.title: Onboarding polish — sample-data logos, richer examples, a Hide toggle, and a Connections setup tour

items.label: The built-in sample data now uses recognizable companies (with their logos) and richer multi-message conversations, so exploring the app feels real — and the roles are generic software-engineering positions rather than one narrow field.

New profiles now start with the sample data loaded automatically, so the app is never an empty shell — and the Getting Started checklist steps aside once your profile has real info (career context or real records).
New “Hide sample data” toggle (Settings → Onboarding, and the dashboard banner): filter the sample out of every view without deleting it — reversible, alongside the existing one-click Remove.

New guided “pro tips” tour on Settings → Connections: walks you through connecting Gmail/Outlook, desktop notifications, Mac access, and iCloud photos — including the one-time gotchas (Google's test user, Microsoft's account type, the Mac permission context, app-specific passwords). Replay it from the help lightbulb's “Pro tips”.

releases.title: Fixed a desktop-app crash when switching profiles

items.label: Selecting or switching a profile in the macOS desktop app could pop a “A JavaScript error occurred in the main process” dialog. The app’s window could be torn down at the exact moment a page finished loading, which crashed the main process; the window lifecycle is now handled safely so switching profiles is smooth. (Shipped alongside the 5.55.0 changes.)

releases.title: AI Logs: paste rows with no saved record now show what they were — and why

items.label: When a paste-parse didn’t produce a linked record — you didn’t save the parsed job/lead, or the parse errored — the AI Logs “Target” no longer shows a bare “(pasted text)”. It now shows what the paste was about (e.g. “Shopify · Senior ML Engineer”) with a muted note explaining why there’s no link — “no opportunity linked” for a job/lead paste, “no contact linked” for a person, or “parse failed” when the parse itself errored.
“Add contact with AI” now records its Target too: save the parsed person and the log resolves from “(paste)” to their name (e.g. “Dana Lee · Initech”) instead of a generic label.

releases.title: AI Logs: backfilled older “(pasted text)” rows to the job/lead they created

items.label: Older “Parse Job Listing” rows in the AI Logs — the ones from before v5.53 — still showed their Target as a generic “(pasted text)”. A one-time, backend-aware backfill now matches each historical parse to the job, lead, or recruiter engagement it produced (comparing the parsed company/title against your saved records) and links them, so those rows deep-link too. Conservative by design: it links only on a confident match, leaves ambiguous ones untouched, never overwrites an existing link, and is fully reversible.

releases.title: AI Logs: paste-parse rows now show what they created, not just "(pasted text)"

items.label: In the AI Logs, a "Parse Job Listing" row (or any paste-driven parse) used to show its Target as a generic "(pasted text)". It now resolves to the record the parse actually created — the job, lead, or recruiter engagement — as a clickable deep link (e.g. "Genesys · AI Architect" → the job). Recorded when you save the parsed opportunity; a small sidecar joins it onto the log at read time, so the append-only call log is never mutated.

releases.title: Richer AI feedback — tell it what you actually did, with emoji

items.label: AI feedback now captures two separate things: what you DID with a result — ✅ used it · ✏️ used it with edits · 🚫 didn't use it — and how you RATE it — 👍 / 👎 — independently. So you can say 'I had to use it but 👎' or '👍 even though I tweaked it', which is a much better signal for improving the prompts than a single thumbs-up.
There's now an explicit 🚫 'Didn't use' button on every AI result and in the Logs drawer — so skipping a generation is captured, not just silent.
When you apply a text result and edit it first, the app still detects that and keeps the exact before→after diff, so you (and the prompt-tuning) can see what you changed.
The Logs → Feedback tab and AI-call rows now show your feedback as emoji (no more 'Helpful' label), filterable by outcome and by 👍/👎, with a quick 👍/👎 you can set right in the list.

Insights → AI now breaks feedback down by what you did with each result — ✅ used / ✏️ edited / 🚫 didn't use — and by 👍/👎, per prompt, so a high edit rate (needs tuning) is distinct from a high abort rate (may be broken).
The Developer 'Suggest a prompt improvement' tool now learns from the full signal — including the results you generated but didn't use, not just the ones you edited or disliked.

You can now give feedback right where the AI runs — an easy, optional 👍/👎 (and, where it applies, ✅ used / ✏️ edited / 🚫 didn't use) now sits on cover letters, the interview question bank, JD formatting, mock interviews, comp benchmarks, negotiation coaching, and tone checks — not only buried in the Logs. Re-running or rebuilding a result also auto-counts the previous one as 'didn't use'.

Settings → Developer 'Analyze prompt performance' is now a full, transparent loop: once a prompt has enough rated results with a shortcoming (configurable, default 20), the AI first diagnoses WHY it's not landing (from your edits, skips, and 👎-comments), then proposes an improved prompt with a plain-English rationale — and, if the problem is the model rather than the wording, a suggested model change. You see the current prompt + model, the diagnosis, an editable suggestion, and even the exact prompts doing the analysis; edit it if you like, then Apply to make it live (optionally switching the model too) and start tracking the new version.

Structured AI results learn from your edits too now: editing an AI-tailored résumé before saving records exactly which sections you changed, and applying only some of the offer-analysis suggestions records which you kept — so those prompts improve the same way emails and notes already do.

releases.title: Menus open instantly — no more full-page reloads

items.label: Opening Settings, Connections, or Help from the app menu now transitions instantly in place instead of reloading the whole app — the same smooth navigation you get clicking around the sidebar.
Under the hood: desktop releases are now built, signed, and notarized automatically in the cloud, and the app's background server runs with a tightened, least-privilege environment.

releases.title: A Feedback tab in Logs — review every AI result you've rated

items.label: Logs has a new Feedback tab: every AI result you've rated, in one place — the ones you applied as-is, the ones you edited before applying, and the ones you 👎'd — each with your dislike reason and the exact raw→final diff of what you changed, filterable by verdict. It's the review companion to the per-prompt 👍/👎 rates on Insights → AI.

releases.title: ‘Parse with AI’ works again — fixed a schema error that could block parsing

items.label: Fixed a red “Invalid schema” error that could make ‘Parse with AI’ / ‘Add with AI’ fail outright when parsing a recruiter InMail or a job posting. The AI parser’s pay/compensation schema tripped OpenAI’s strict structured-output validation; it now uses a strict-clean schema, so parsing works again across every mode — job, recruiter engagement, and lead.

releases.title: Guided tours remember they've run — even after restarting the app

items.label: The guided page tours now remember they've already shown for your profile and won't replay every time you reopen the desktop app — the 'already toured' memory is saved with your profile instead of the browser session, so it survives restarts, cache clears, and reinstalls.

releases.title: Rate more of the AI — interview prep and notes now learn from your feedback

items.label: The 👍/👎 feedback controls now cover the last of the interview AI tools — drafted round and meeting prep, and the synthesized 'overall notes' for a job. Rate a result (or tweak it before applying) and that signal quietly tunes the prompt behind it, exactly like the résumé, email, and offer tools already do.

Behind the scenes: groundwork for app-provided AI, so a future plan won't require your own API key. The app can now read the remaining quota and tier from the hosted service and fall back to copy-a-prompt if it's ever unavailable. Inert until turned on — nothing changes for you today.

releases.title: Households and role-based access controls

items.label: Households: group profiles into a household with a shared admin. Create, rename, or delete them and assign profiles from Settings → Profiles; the profile switcher and the /select picker now group profiles by household. Local to this device and off by default.

Role-based access control is now fully wired end-to-end (and stays inert until you turn on role enforcement): admin-only Settings tabs, prompt editing that's read-only for lower roles with one-click reset-to-default, a Viewer role that's read-only for records, Owner-only system diagnostics, and lockout-safe profile switching that routes through the normal unlock flow.
With enforcement off (the default) nothing changes — Owners keep full access to everything, exactly as before.

releases.title: Smarter contacts: photo sources, pull-from-Mac-Contacts on lists, named group chats, and AI fixes for iMessage/iCloud

items.label: Every contact avatar now shows where its photo came from — hover to see 'Photo from LinkedIn', 'Mac Contacts', or 'Uploaded'.
Pull a contact's photo from your Mac Contacts right on the People and Contacts lists — no need to open the editor first.
Imported iMessage group chats now label each person by name (from your Mac Contacts) instead of a raw phone number.
When a connection fails, you now get AI-guided fix steps for local Messages (Full Disk Access) and iCloud (app-specific password) too — not just Gmail/Outlook.
Behind the scenes: the AI paste-importer's entitlement check now runs through the single shared gate (no duplicate gating).

releases.title: Version number now shows correctly

items.label: The version shown in the sidebar now always matches the installed release (it is read from the build instead of a separate constant that could fall out of sync).

releases.title: Notarized build + hardened release pipeline

items.label: The desktop app is now notarized by Apple, so it installs and auto-updates with no Gatekeeper warning.

releases.title: Feedback capture reaches the interview AI tools

items.label: Drafting an interview debrief from a transcript, and extracting real-time notes from a transcript, now record an 'applied' signal — so those AI prompts also improve from your feedback (and show up in the prompt-performance analyzer).

releases.title: Account sign-in moved to the profile picker

items.label: Sign in or create your account right from the profile picker (the 'Who's using Job Tracker?' screen), alongside choosing a profile — your account is your identity + AI plan, separate from which profile's data you're working in.
Settings → Account is now just for managing a signed-in account (change your password, for email/password accounts); signing in itself lives on the profile picker.

releases.title: AI feedback polish: confirmation, hints & sharper dislikes

items.label: Rating an AI result now confirms it ('✓ noted — this tunes the AI'), and a one-time hint makes clear that your 👍/👎 improves future prompts over time.
The 👎 box now offers quick reasons (wrong tone / inaccurate / too long / too generic / missing context) so a dislike carries sharper signal, on top of the freeform note.
Insights → AI 'Feedback & quality' now explains the capture→improve loop and, for the owner, links straight to the prompt-improvement analyzer on the Developer page.

releases.title: AI suggests prompt improvements from your feedback

items.label: Owner-only: Settings → Developer → Prompt performance now has a 'Suggest an improvement' button on each AI prompt that has feedback. It reads your edits and dislikes for that prompt and proposes a concrete improved prompt — which you can stage as an inactive variant to A/B in Settings → AI Prompts (never auto-applied).

releases.title: Your account now lives in the profile menu (and works in the desktop app)

items.label: Your account moved to the profile menu (top-left), under its own 'Account' section — clearly separate from switching profiles. Sign in or manage it from there; the tracker stays free without an account. (Settings → Account is still there for the full view.)
Fixed: the account area now appears in the desktop app too — it was only showing up in the browser before.

releases.title: Sign in to an account (Settings → Account)

items.label: New Settings → Account tab — sign in or create an account to manage your AI plan, with your current plan and free-trial status shown. The tracker itself stays completely free; an account only covers the AI features. Email/password works now; Apple & Google sign-in are coming soon.

releases.title: Foundation for online accounts and app-provided AI (behind the scenes)

items.label: Behind the scenes: the backend for optional online sign-in and app-provided AI is now in place — accounts, a securely signed plan token, and a metered AI proxy. Nothing changes in the app today; it stays exactly as it is now until these are switched on.
Groundwork so Settings → Plan & AI access can show real trial and plan details once accounts go live (no change today).

releases.title: Paste from LinkedIn — with a clear Message vs InMail toggle

items.label: New 'From LinkedIn' button on a role's outreach card — opens the AI paste importer pre-set to LinkedIn, so you can drop in a copied LinkedIn conversation in one step.

When importing a LinkedIn thread, a clear 'Message / InMail' toggle lets you tag it correctly — InMail (cold recruiter outreach, with a subject line) vs a regular 1:1 message — so it's stored and shown with the right type.

releases.title: Settings tabs adapt to your role

items.label: When an account turns on role enforcement, the Settings tabs now match what each role can actually do: AI Provider, AI Models, Data, and Profiles show only for Admins (and the Owner), and Developer stays Owner-only — so lower roles no longer click into a tab just to be told they can’t use it. With enforcement off, everyone still sees every tab exactly as before.

releases.title: AI tiering groundwork: model-tier clamp + proxy quota logic

items.label: Groundwork for app-provided AI tiers (no change yet — only active once the paywall is switched on): free and trial accounts will run eligible AI features on the cheapest model, finalized against the per-feature free/paid map.
Client-side handling for the hosted AI proxy's quota responses (remaining-allowance display plus upgrade / retry / copy-prompt fallbacks), ready for the metered proxy when it goes live.

releases.title: Suggest a feature — send ideas straight to the developer

items.label: New 'Suggest a feature' page (in the sidebar under System): a quick form to send an idea, improvement, or bug report straight to the developer. Send-and-thank — you get a confirmation, no account needed.

The Roadmap is now Owner-only at the route level (not just hidden in the nav) — anyone else who lands on it is sent to 'Suggest a feature' instead. Inert today (everyone's an owner until role enforcement is turned on).
Owners see the submitted suggestions right on the Roadmap page, so ideas feed the roadmap.

releases.title: Prompt editing can be made read-only by role, with one-click reset to default

items.label: When an account turns on role enforcement, the AI Prompts editor (and the onboarding Prompts tab) renders read-only for roles that can’t edit prompts — Owner always can; an Admin can when the Owner grants it; Members & Viewers read but can’t change them. Your personal AI context stays fully editable for everyone.

Each prompt now shows a “Customized” badge when you’ve overridden the shipped default, plus a one-click “Reset to default” that clears just that override and restores the packaged prompt — your saved prompt variants are kept.
Read-only is cosmetic on top of the existing server gate — prompt changes were already blocked server-side for roles without permission; now the UI matches, so there’s no edit-then-fail.

releases.title: A guided “pro tips” tour for Communication, and a nicer Onboarding section

items.label: Communication has a guided “pro tips” tour: open any conversation and we'll offer a quick walkthrough of everything you can do with a thread — set the contact, draft an AI follow-up, summarise, re-classify, import past emails, merge or split, and jump to the role. Replay it any time from the help lightbulb's “Pro tips”
The Onboarding settings section got a friendlier header and clearer layout

releases.title: Offer-AI feedback + a prompt-performance view for Owners

items.label: Feedback capture now covers the offer AI tools too: filling offer blanks and OCR-ing an offer letter into fields record an 'applied' signal, and the version-comparison gets a thumbs up/down.

New Owner-only 'Prompt performance' panel on Settings → Developer: per-prompt helpful / edited / disliked rates, sorted by what needs attention, with a drill-down into the actual edits and dislike comments — the groundwork for AI-suggested prompt improvements.

releases.title: Onboarding is now its own top-level Settings section

items.label: Onboarding moved out from under “AI Prompts” into its own top-level Settings → Onboarding tab — one obvious place to get set up, check profile readiness, and restart the guided tours or sample data

releases.title: Connect iCloud to pull contact photos that aren't on your Mac

items.label: New Settings → Connections → 'iCloud contact photos': sign in once with an Apple ID + app-specific password (created at account.apple.com — your real password is never entered or stored) and click 'Sync photos now' to cache photos for contacts that live only in iCloud and aren't on this Mac.

Once synced, 'Pull photo from Mac Contacts' uses the iCloud cache as a fallback — so it can fetch a photo even when Full Disk Access isn't granted, and even for contacts not in your local Mac Contacts.
Most people won't need this: your local Mac Contacts already include iCloud-synced photos. The connector only fills the gap for iCloud-only contacts.

releases.title: Clearer on/off switches; Owner can let Admins edit prompts

items.label: Settings toggles are now sliding ON/OFF switches (with a lock-icon variant) instead of same-shape buttons — the state reads at a glance

Developer page (Owner-only): a new 'Allow Admins to edit prompts' switch. Off by default (only the Owner edits prompt instructions); Members & Viewers stay read-only; everyone's personal AI context is always editable

releases.title: AI feedback capture reaches more places

items.label: The thumbs up/down + 'applied' signal from 5.24.0 now also covers: enriching a pitched role or a lead from a message, AI status updates, and interview section summaries — so those AI results learn from you too.

Closed two gaps from the first release: sending an AI-drafted message via 'Open in app' (not just Save) now counts as applied, and creating a Job from an AI parse now records feedback like the Lead path already did.

releases.title: Clearer Mac Contacts photo pull: source badges + a heads-up when a contact is in your Contacts

items.label: Editing a contact now shows whether they're in your Mac Contacts the moment you open the editor — 'In your Mac Contacts ✓ (has a photo)', 'Not found', or a prompt to grant Full Disk Access — so you know before you click.
Each contact photo now carries a source badge — 'Photo from LinkedIn', 'Photo from Mac Contacts', or 'Uploaded' — so you can tell where it came from at a glance.
If a contact already has a photo, the button reads 'Replace photo from Mac Contacts' and shows their current photo, so a pull never silently overwrites without you seeing it.

releases.title: Guided tours: an animated cursor, a real “try your AI” button, and more page tours

items.label: Onboarding tours now show an animated pointer that glides to whatever a step is highlighting, so each step is demonstrated rather than just described — and it fully respects your “reduce motion” setting

AI tour steps gained a “Run it for real” button: make a genuine AI call on a sample listing to confirm your AI works end to end, with a friendly “connect a key” fallback so nothing breaks when you haven't set one up
New first-visit tours on the Parse-with-AI and Add-a-role-by-hand pages

releases.title: AI paywall reads the ratified free/paid map; Owner enforcement toggles on the Developer page

items.label: The AI entitlement gate now reads the per-feature free/paid map (decoupled from model tier), so the paywall line matches the published tier story exactly. Still off by default

Developer page (Owner-only): role enforcement and AI-paywall enforcement are now in-app toggles — with a clear warning that turning the paywall on enforces the free tier (paid AI blocked) until an AI plan exists

releases.title: Tell the AI what worked — feedback capture on AI results

items.label: AI results now learn from you: applying a suggestion as-is counts as a quiet thumbs-up, editing it before you apply records what you changed (the AI's version vs. your final, with a diff), and a 👎 with an optional note flags a miss — applying is never blocked on feedback.

Thumbs up/down controls appear right where you apply AI output (email drafts, résumé tailoring, offer analysis, Add-with-AI parsing, company briefs, card polish) and retroactively on any past call in the AI Logs drawer.
The AI Logs page now shows each call's outcome (Helpful / Edited / Disliked) as a badge, with a new filter to find them — and the drawer shows your note plus the raw-vs-final diff for edited results.
Insights → AI gains a 'Feedback & quality' section: how often results are applied, edited, or disliked, broken down by prompt type, so you can see which prompts need tuning.
Feedback is stored locally alongside your AI logs and is preserved even if you clear the active log.

releases.title: Pull contact photos & names from your Mac Contacts

items.label: Edit a contact → Mac Contacts → 'Pull photo from Mac Contacts': matches their phone/email to your macOS Contacts and pulls their photo — including iCloud-synced photos, which macOS keeps on your Mac, so it works offline with no Apple sign-in. The photo is saved locally so it stays even if Contacts changes.
If the contact is saved in your Mac Contacts under a different name, that name is suggested (your saved name is never overwritten).
The 'Pull from Messages' button now only appears on the desktop edition that can read local Messages (hidden where Full Disk Access isn't possible).
Reading your Mac Contacts needs Full Disk Access granted to whatever launches the app (Terminal or Job Tracker) — same one-time grant as the Messages import.

releases.title: Internal: the per-feature free/paid map for the AI plan, plus a clearer “How AI access works” guide

items.label: Groundwork for the coming AI plan: a single per-feature map decides which AI features are free vs paid, so the app and the in-app guide can never disagree about what's included. Off by default — nothing changes today

The “How AI access works” guide now spells out what's free (parsing, classification, short drafts, tone check, paste-import, company research, the daily focus digest) versus paid (résumé tailoring, interview prep & debrief, transcription, deep offer analysis, cross-portfolio insights)

releases.title: Owner-only Developer page (access state, capabilities, AI tooling)

items.label: New Owner-only Developer tab in Settings: enforcement/flag state, a live capabilities snapshot, observability links, and a home for upcoming AI prompt-performance tooling. Hidden from every other role

releases.title: Internal: AI entitlement gate wired at the single AI seam (inert groundwork)

items.label: Groundwork: every AI feature now flows through one entitlement checkpoint, with first-run/setup and connection-help always free. Off by default — nothing changes today; it's the foundation for the paid AI plan

releases.title: AI connection now shows as connected, plus a new Plan & AI access tab

items.label: Settings → AI Provider: the AI connection card now clearly shows CONNECTED when you've set your own API key — with the right provider name (it follows your active provider), a plain-language status, and the key-setup steps tucked under 'Manage or switch your key' once connected

New Settings → Plan & AI access tab: see the tier your account is on and how AI is powered (your own key, or the built-in plan), plus a clear breakdown of how AI access works — your own key (available now) and the free-trial / free / paid tiers coming with the built-in AI service

Honest status today: with the built-in AI service not live yet, the connection reflects your real setup — your own key if set, otherwise a copy-paste fallback — and never implies a plan you don't have

releases.title: Shared AI access for group accounts: request → admin approves

items.label: Group/household AI access control on Settings → AI Provider: a member can request access to the account's shared AI, and an Owner/Admin approves or denies the pending request
Off by default — everyone can use the shared AI until you turn on 'Enforce roles'; Owners and Admins are always authorized

releases.title: Onboarding: a Getting-started checklist, restart-tours, an AI-access guide, and a try-it preview

items.label: New 'Getting started' checklist on a fresh dashboard — load sample data, take the tour, fill your career context, connect email, add your first role — with progress and one-click actions (replaces the old stacked setup banners)
Restart the page tours any time — from the help lightbulb (now showing 'toured X of N pages') or Settings → Data → Onboarding & tours, which also loads / resets / removes the sample data
The setup wizard now honestly signposts the coming built-in AI plan (free metered tier + paid), matching the Settings AI-connection card — your own key stays the path today
The new in-app guide explains how AI access works — trial, a free floor, paid, and bring-your-own-key — and which features are free vs. paid
The Jobs tour's AI step now reveals a sample parsed result end-to-end — a hands-on 'try it' with no API call

releases.title: Behind the scenes: app-provided-AI token wiring + proxy contract accuracy

items.label: Groundwork for app-provided AI (no change to how the app works today): the AI client now sources its proxy auth token from the shared entitlement seam, so when the hosted AI service goes live it activates with no further client change

releases.title: Onboarding fixes + richer profile setup, get-a-key help, and keyboard roving on Jobs

items.label: Fixed: the Settings page now gets its first-visit tour (it was silently skipped), and the help lightbulb now shows page-specific guidance on every page (was missing on half of them)
Fixed: a new profile with no name set no longer borrows another profile's name in its AI prompts — it seeds the name on creation and falls back to a neutral 'Candidate'
Fixed: page tours mark themselves seen the moment they're shown, so glancing at a page and clicking away (or reloading) behaves consistently and a seen page won't re-pop
New-profile setup now asks for a LinkedIn URL and won't continue empty — it requires a name plus at least one of about-text / résumé / LinkedIn, with copy that nudges the specifics the AI uses
The API-key setup step now links straight to your Anthropic or OpenAI key page with step-by-step instructions (and points to Settings → Connections for Outlook/Gmail)
Keyboard list-roving (j/k then Enter) now works on the Jobs table — highlight a row and open it without the mouse; the tour 'skip page' hint is clearer
A fresh dashboard no longer stacks the 'finish setup' and 'fill your goals' nudges at once

releases.title: Per-profile company aliases, cleaner data paths, role-aware profile list, notification setup help

items.label: Company aliases are now PER-PROFILE — each profile curates its own company-name groupings (they used to be shared across every profile). Your existing aliases were copied into each profile, so nothing changes until you edit them. Edit them under Settings → Company Aliases.
Settings → Data shows a home-relative path (~/…) for the data + backups locations instead of your full home folder — and now reflects the real current location, not a stale stored one.
Settings → Profiles: when role enforcement is on, Members and Viewers only see their own profile instead of the whole roster (no change when enforcement is off).

Settings → Thresholds: the desktop-notifications card now shows live browser-permission status with a Re-check button and a one-click link to macOS System Settings → Notifications — the same assist as the Connections page.

releases.title: AI connection guide + your-own-key setup (Settings → AI Provider)

items.label: New 'AI connection' card on Settings → AI Provider: clear status, step-by-step instructions, and a direct link to get an Anthropic or OpenAI API key
Power-user nudge: heavy AI users are offered to add their own key for unlimited use (never a hard limit)
Capability model now tracks app-provided vs your-own-key AI (aligned with the app-provided-AI proxy contract); provider keys & model config stay Admin-only

releases.title: Groundwork for app-provided AI (no user-visible change yet)

items.label: Internal foundation: the app can now route AI through a hosted, metered proxy (the app's key behind a firewall — no key of your own) once that service goes live. Nothing changes today — AI still uses your own key or copy-paste mode — but the client side is ready so free/trial accounts will get app-provided AI without a setup step, while bring-your-own-key keeps bypassing it. Shared cross-track contract: docs/app-provided-ai-proxy-contract.md.

releases.title: Manage profiles straight from the landing — view, edit, and delete without entering one

items.label: New 'Manage profiles' page opens right from the profile-picker landing — rename, change photo & accent, archive, delete, and manage locks without entering a profile first
The landing's 'Manage profiles →' link now opens that page instead of sending you into the active profile's Settings
Deleting a profile is now reachable from the landing (gated behind admin view when an admin passphrase is set, matching Global settings)

releases.title: Roles go live: assign access roles, enforce them, and gate admin settings

items.label: Assign an access role (Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer) to each profile in Settings → Profiles
Owner-only 'Enforce roles' toggle — off by default (everyone has full access); turn it on to make roles bite
When enforced, the sidebar hides Owner-only areas (like Roadmap) for lower roles
Server-side guard on settings: provider keys & model config require Admin; prompts are read-only below Owner; personal AI context stays editable for everyone
Role changes can't escalate above your own role, and only an Owner can grant or change the Owner role

releases.title: Connections fixes: Outlook in the email-import buttons + clearer Full Disk Access steps

items.label: The "search & import email" buttons on the Communication page and job/lead cards now read "Mail.app / Gmail / Outlook" — Outlook was already selectable in the import dialog, the button tooltips just hadn't caught up.

Clearer Full Disk Access guidance for the Messages connector: macOS attaches the permission to whatever LAUNCHED the running server, so the steps now say to grant it to the app you start Job Tracker with (the Job Tracker app, or Terminal) and RELAUNCH from there — a server already running from a deploy or another terminal keeps that context's access, not the one you just granted.

releases.title: Onboarding polish: Help & Shortcuts moved into the sidebar

items.label: The Help (💡) and Shortcuts (⌨) buttons now live in the sidebar footer next to What's New, instead of floating in the corner — and the page tours point at them there

releases.title: Connections polish: live permission status, clearer setup, editable diagnosis prompt

items.label: The Connections tab now shows LIVE status for the Mac permissions — Full Disk Access and Notifications flip to "Ready" once granted (instead of always reading "Needs permission"), with a Re-check button.

Clearer macOS setup instructions: because Job Tracker currently runs as a local server, Full Disk Access is granted to the app that launches it (the Job Tracker app, or Terminal) — the steps now say exactly that, with a reminder to fully quit and reopen after granting.

The connection-setup error diagnosis is now an editable prompt under Settings → AI Prompts ("Connection Setup Diagnosis") — you can tune the diagnostician's role and rules, while the per-provider known-correct facts and the deterministic playbook stay code-injected so they can't be broken.

releases.title: Résumé builder polish: divider styles, editable headings, bottom-pinned footer, richer colours, smarter tailoring

items.label: Dividers: choose where the line sits — under each section heading (as before) or as a rule BETWEEN sections — plus an optional vertical line between the two columns. (Lines use the divider style you pick; set it to “Full line”, “Dotted”, etc. — “Blank” shows none.)
Rename any section heading (Profile, Work Experience, Skills, …) right in the Layout panel — leave a field blank to keep the default.

“References available upon request” now pins to the bottom of the page even when there's empty space above; the app also auto-adds a little spacing to fill a short sidebar, and a new “Section spacing” slider lets you fine-tune.
Fuller colour control: dedicated Muted (secondary text) and Headings (script-header) colour pickers, and you can now save the current colours as a reusable named palette.
Serif Sidebar: the script “Profile” heading now sits centered beside its paragraph.
Regenerate a résumé section with a note — tell the AI how to improve it (e.g. “lead with the RAG work”, “make it punchier”) and it regenerates that section accordingly.
Tailoring no longer forces every past role onto the résumé — the AI may drop roles that genuinely don't fit the target (still grounded; it never invents).

releases.title: Onboarding & help: sample data, keyboard shortcuts, per-page tours, and an in-app guide

items.label: Example sample data — a fully lived-in fictional dataset (jobs across every stage, recruiter outreach with a promoted watch role, leads, and people with message history) that loads on first run; reset or remove it in one click from the dashboard banner
Global keyboard shortcuts — jump between pages with g + a letter or ⌃⇧ + a letter, focus search with /, move through lists with j/k and open with ↵, and press ? anywhere for a sheet of every shortcut
Interactive per-page tours that run the first time you visit each page, with spotlighted call-outs, a no-spend preview of what an AI action would send, and ↵ for next / ⌘↵ to skip
An always-on help lightbulb on every page (what it's for, what you can do, and the AI features there with their model tier) plus a searchable, deep-linkable capabilities guide at /guide

releases.title: Résumé builder: configurable templates, page-filling PDF, and layout-aware tailoring

items.label: New "Layout & PDF" tab on a structured résumé — design the look live: two starter templates (Modern Two-Column and a Serif Sidebar with script "Profile"/"Contact" headers), colour palettes + custom colours, bundled offline fonts, paper size, 1 / 2 / auto pages, per-section show + placement, experience reorder and per-page assignment, skills layout modes, dividers, and an icon contact card. Your existing Content & AI editing view is unchanged under its own tab.

Page-filling PDF: a print-perfect, chrome-free view sizes the résumé to FILL the page(s) — Letter or A4, 1 or 2 pages, with real (crisp) font sizes — and the on-screen preview matches it 1:1. "Download PDF" opens it for Save-as-PDF (one-click in the desktop app).
Save your look as a reusable template (stored per profile) and re-apply it across jobs; each résumé version now remembers the layout it was designed in.

Layout-aware tailoring: the AI selects + groups the most role-relevant skills from your full career context, and tailors how much content each role gets so it fills the chosen layout cleanly (recent roles fuller, older ones condensed). A new "Re-tailor to this layout" action rewrites the content to fit the exact layout you designed.

releases.title: Connections: Outlook mail + a Connections & Notifications hub

items.label: Connect Outlook / Microsoft 365 email (OAuth) — the same read-only "pull a contact's mail into a chain" flow as Gmail, now for personal (outlook.com / hotmail) and work / school accounts. Set it up under Settings → Mail or the new Connections tab; the email import dialog gains an Outlook source.

New Settings → Connections tab: one place to connect Gmail + Outlook, turn on desktop notifications, and (on the direct-download edition) jump straight to the exact macOS System Settings pane to grant Full Disk Access / Automation / Accessibility for the Messages connector. Live status per row; edition-aware.

The AI paste-importer's parse runs on the always-free cheap-model floor (it's a parse/classify call), gated through the new capability resolver — so it stays usable on the free tier, with the no-AI Manual mode as the offline/free fallback.

Pull from Messages (Direct edition): read a contact's iMessage / SMS history straight from the Messages app and import the picked messages into a chain — the live replacement for the CSV-export round-trip. Needs Full Disk Access (the dialog deep-links you to grant it); the App Store edition keeps using the AI paste-importer.
Imported messages now record their true source — "outlook" (Microsoft), "paste" (AI paste-importer), and "imessage" (Messages connector) — alongside gmail / mail-app / csv / manual.

When a Gmail or Outlook connect fails, an AI evaluator now turns the raw OAuth error into specific, ordered fix steps — what to click, the exact value to paste (with copy chips), whether a rebuild is needed, and whether you can retry right away — grounded in a deterministic AADSTS / Google playbook (so it still helps with no AI key) and a secret-free snapshot of your setup (never your secret).

releases.title: Roles & entitlement foundation (Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer + capability resolver)

items.label: 4-role model (Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer) on profiles; existing profiles default to Owner, so nothing changes until roles are assigned
Server-side role gate in the proxy for admin/developer routes — enforced on the server, not just hidden in the UI (inert until enabled)
Single capability resolver over edition, AI entitlement, and online state — one gate the whole app reads
Offline-first licensing scaffolding: signed entitlement token with an offline grace window (online account + billing backend to follow)
Prompt access control: prompt instructions can be made read-only by role, while personal AI context stays editable by everyone

releases.title: SQLite storage + configurable data directory (foundation)

items.label: Data directory is now relocatable behind a pointer (JOB_TRACKER_DATA_DIR env var, a pointer file, or the repo-local fallback); packaged default is ~/Library/Application Support/JobTracker

Storage migrated to SQLite (better-sqlite3) behind the repo interface — jobs, leads and logs; transactions replace the file lock; FTS5 full-text index; denormalized indexed columns for fast filter and sort
One-shot JSON to SQLite migration runner (verified, idempotent, auto-backed-up) with an opt-in cutover; the app keeps running on JSON until you flip it
JSON export/import bridge so editing the data in a Claude chat still works after the SQLite move
SQLite online-backup preserves the rolling data/backups safety copies

releases.title: Add conversation with AI — paste-to-chain importer

items.label: New "Add conversation with AI": paste a whole conversation — text/iMessage, SMS, WhatsApp, a LinkedIn message or InMail, an email back-and-forth, or phone-call notes — pick the channel, and AI parses it message-by-message into an editable chain (who sent it, time, interaction kind, subject, cleaned body). Fix anything in the message-by-message preview, then import it in one click as a chain that looks identical to one pulled from Gmail/Outlook. Available on the Communication page and on each job/lead.

Free-tier friendly: the paste parse runs on the cheapest (light) AI model — the always-free AI floor — and there's a no-AI Manual mode to build a chain by hand. Duplicate messages are skipped on import. The CSV text-message import is unchanged (kept as the App-Store-safe path).

releases.title: Prompt editor: preview the USER prompt with a sample record

items.label: You can now preview the USER prompt (the per-record half that's normally only built at run time — previously not shown at all) using inline sample data, so you see the WHOLE prompt, not just the system half. Added a "Preview USER prompt (sample record) →" toggle to Cover Letter, Company Brief, and Tone Check; per-record variables show in red, and {{context/identity}} tokens resolve as they would at send time.
Built on a generic, extensible mechanism (a sample-user preview kind keyed by feature) — more prompts can be added to the sample preview the same way.

releases.title: Prompt editor: two-color variables (blue context, red per-record) + green context section

items.label: Injection variables are now color-coded everywhere (editor, raw template, and resolved preview): BLUE = {{tokens}} from your Context/Identity (resolve in the preview); RED = per-record / per-card runtime variables ({name}, {interactionKinds}, card fields, etc.) that get filled from the actual job / lead / message / card at send time and so don't preview. JSON-shape braces in prompts are left untouched. A small legend explains the colors.

In the resolved preview, the appended Context section is now tinted green to match the green context-block chips, so it's clear which part of the prompt is your injected Context vs the prompt's own instructions.

releases.title: Prompt editor: context blocks shown, variables panel on top, colored variables

items.label: The "Variables in this prompt" panel now also lists the CONTEXT BLOCKS each prompt injects (Career, Goals & Interests, AI Authoring Rules, Voice & Framing, Offer Preferences, etc.) — these are appended as a context section, not as {{tokens}}, so they weren't visible before. Each block is a chip: green = filled, amber = empty, and it links straight to that Context editor. Now you can see every context area a prompt actually uses.

Moved the variables panel ABOVE the prompt text (so you see what's injected before reading the prompt), and injection variables are now color-highlighted in blue — both while you edit (a highlight overlay on the textarea) and in the raw preview — so it's obvious which bits come from your Context/Identity vs the prompt's own words.

releases.title: Prompt editor: "Variables in this prompt" with inline career-version + token swaps

items.label: Each prompt in Settings → AI Prompts now shows a "Variables in this prompt" panel: the {{tokens}} that prompt actually uses, each with what it resolves to for your profile. For {{careerContext}} there's an inline version selector (Default / Condensed / Balanced / Full) that sets the per-prompt career fullness right there — no more hopping to the Prompt Access matrix.

Where a variable has equivalents, a one-click "swap →" rewrites it in the prompt: {{careerContextCondensed/Balanced/Full}} (pin an explicit version), {{compFloor}} ↔ {{compFloorByLevel}}, the name forms ({{name}}/{{firstName}}/{{lastName}}/{{firstNameUpper}}), and {{location}} ↔ {{addressLine}}. The resolve-prompt preview also reports the career version whenever the prompt uses the token.

releases.title: Pronoun selector in Identity + gate now guards against baked pronouns

items.label: Your pronouns are now a proper choice in Settings → Onboarding → Identity (he/him, she/her, or they/them) instead of an unset field. The selection drives the {{they}}/{{them}}/{{their}}/{{themselves}} tokens the AI uses to refer to you across every prompt — drafted messages, fit memos, interview prep — and other people's pronouns are never touched.

Hardened the placeholder gate: alongside the existing baked-name (fail) and profile-fact (warn) scans, it now FAILS if a bare owner pronoun (he/his/him/himself) is hand-written into a prompt body — it must be a token, or, if it refers to a third party, explicitly allow-listed. Regression protection so identity can't leak back into prompts.

releases.title: 5 more AI prompts now editable (enrich-lead, decline, extract-notes, draft/update context, mock interview)

items.label: Five live prompts that had no editor slot are now editable in Settings → AI Prompts and respect your override: Enrich Lead (the lead-level half of "Update with AI"), Decline Role, Extract Notes, the ✨ Add-with-AI Context drafter, and the Mock Interview interviewer. They also appear in the Per-prompt models picker.

For the two parameterized prompts, only the static instructions are the editable default — the per-block SECTION/PURPOSE (context drafter) and the per-interview role header + expected questions (mock interview) are still injected in code, so an override tunes behavior without losing the dynamic context. With no override set, all five are byte-identical to before.

releases.title: Owner pronouns → explicit tokens; retired the global pronoun remap

items.label: Pronouns that refer to YOU in AI prompts are now explicit placeholders — {{they}}/{{them}}/{{their}}/{{themselves}} (and capitalized {{They}}/{{Their}}) — resolving to your set (he/him, she/her, they/them) on every send path, including user + copy-prompt where the old approach didn't reach. ~30 owner-pronoun sites across 12 prompt files were converted; they appear in the placeholder palette like every other token.

Retired the global he→she/they regex remap. It only ran on system prompts AND blindly rewrote OTHER people's pronouns too — e.g. "send the recruiter your resume so he can forward it" would wrongly flip "he" for a she/her profile. Now a third party's pronouns stay exactly as written, and the gate verifies both profiles resolve cleanly (Alex→he/his, Chelsea→she/her).

releases.title: Generic offer-prefs starter + preview suffix fix

items.label: The Offer Preferences starter template no longer ships with one person's specific personal-project list or province-specific legal text — the IP/side-work section is now generic guidance with a placeholder, and the termination-clause note frames Ontario/Waksdale as an example to check against your own jurisdiction. New profiles get neutral scaffolding to fill in.

Prompt preview: the injected Context suffix now resolves its {{placeholders}} (e.g. the "CONTEXT ABOUT …" header) in the dual-view, so the preview matches exactly what's sent (the actual send already resolved correctly).

releases.title: Context cards: Add / Update with AI + presets (Phase 4E)

items.label: Every Context card now has a context-aware AI button. EMPTY card → ✨ Add with AI (describe it → AI drafts it). FILLED card → ✨ Update with AI: pick any combination of quick actions — Expand on, Reword, Tighten, Improve formatting, Polish, and tone shifts (More professional / Warmer / More confident) — AND/OR type exactly what to add, remove, reword, or adjust. All selections + your instruction are sent together with the current content; the AI applies them, slotting new info into the logical place and preserving everything else.

Both modes PREVIEW the result first (rendered) with Apply / Discard / Regenerate, so nothing changes until you accept it — and you still review + Save as usual. Never invents facts you didn't give. Works for any profile; with no API key it copies the prompt to run elsewhere.

releases.title: All AI prompts now editable — 11 newly surfaced (wiring)

items.label: 11 AI prompts that were previously code-only are now editable in Settings → AI Prompts and respect your override at run time: Comp Benchmark, Fit Re-score, Offer Decision, Negotiation Coach, Cross-Record Findings, Question Bank, Loss Pattern Analysis, Propose Round, Propose Meeting, Résumé OCR, and a dedicated Status Update · Watch Role (separate from the Job one). Two new editor tabs group them: "Offer & negotiation" and "Analysis & insights".

Each reads its own settings.prompts override key (e.g. compBenchmarkSystem); with no override set the prompt is byte-identical to before. All 11 already appear in the Per-prompt models picker (catalog-driven); added the missing Loss Pattern Analysis catalog entry.

releases.title: Prompt editor: grouped placeholder palette with live previews (Phase 4D)

items.label: The placeholder palette in the prompt editor is now grouped by category (Identity, Targeting, Compensation, Links, Career) and each token shows a live → preview of what it resolves to for the active profile (e.g. {{compFloor}} → your actual floor), with the full value + description on hover. Makes it obvious which token to insert and what it'll become.

releases.title: Just-in-time context nudges (Phase 4B)

items.label: AI actions now warn you before they run if they read a REQUIRED context block you haven't filled yet — a gentle, dismissable banner naming the gap with one-click links to fill it (e.g. Cover letter → "fill Cover Letter Voice"). It never blocks: every prompt still has a generic fallback, so the nudge just fires the right onboarding section first. Wired into Add/Parse, Cover Letter, Résumé tailoring, Company Brief, Outreach/Follow-up, Weekly Focus, and Mock Interview.

The Context → Prompt Access matrix now flags each feature whose enabled-but-empty required blocks would fall back to generic, with inline links to fill them. Optional blocks (Offer Preferences, Personal Projects, Target Companies) never trigger a nudge.

releases.title: Onboarding: ✨ Draft any Context block with AI (Phase 4C)

items.label: Every Context block (Goals, Voice, Offer Preferences, Company Research, Personal Projects, etc.) now has a ✨ Draft with AI button in its editor: describe in plain language what you want, and the AI writes the block in your voice from your career context. It won't invent facts you didn't give — thin descriptions yield a clearly-generic starting point to edit. Makes optional-but-useful blocks (especially Offer Preferences) painless to set up.
Works for any profile and routes through the normal model/provider + AI-logging path; with no API key it copies the prompt to run in your own AI chat.

releases.title: Onboarding: optional context (Phase 4A) — fill only what's relevant

items.label: Context that isn't needed by everyone is now marked OPTIONAL and no longer drags your onboarding readiness %: Offer Preferences, Personal Projects / IP, Target / Avoid Companies, and the optional identity anchors (LinkedIn / portfolio / GitHub URLs, contract rate, comp-by-level, address line). Required anchors still count.

The completeness checklist now lists each optional block with a plain-English note on what an empty one means (e.g. "empty → offer analysis uses generic checks"), so you can see exactly what you give up by skipping it vs. what's safe to leave blank.

releases.title: Prompt generalization: fixed remaining profile-fact leaks + source-scanning guard

items.label: Fixed the last cross-profile leaks the prompts could spring: the recruiter first-reply copy-prompt no longer bakes one profile's target roles / Toronto / $200K (now reads {{targetRoles}}/{{seniority}}/{{location}}/{{workArrangement}}/{{compFloor}}/{{contractRate}}), the offer-analysis termination check reads {{jurisdiction}} instead of hardcoding Ontario/Waksdale, and the gen-fit voice examples no longer reference one profile's specific project/comp. Each resolves to the active profile's own facts.

Made owner-referring wording gender-neutral where it isn't auto-substituted (copy-prompt + the Analyze-CSV-Import system prompt): 'his Job Tracker' / 'lock it in himself' → 'their' / 'themselves', so non-default profiles read correctly.

Hardened the placeholder gate (scripts/verify-placeholders.ts): it now scans the real prompt source for baked owner-NAMES (hard fail) and profile-FACT literals (review warning), not just a synthetic test string — so future name/fact bakes get caught.

releases.title: Prompt generalization: exhaustive name tokenization complete

items.label: Final pass tokenized the last owner-name literals in prompt strings — copy-prompt builders, card blurbs, the universal Generate/Format/Translate defaults, transcript author-labels, and the shared CONTEXT-ABOUT header. Every name the model sees now resolves from the active profile; only the substitution engine + a couple of match/example strings stay literal.

releases.title: Add-with-AI: a parsed LinkedIn recruiter message defaults to InMail; your reply is a regular message

items.label: When you “Add with AI” a recruiter’s LinkedIn message, its protocol now defaults to InMail (you’re not connected yet) instead of a regular message — and your own reply in the thread is set as a regular LinkedIn message (it’s no longer an InMail once the conversation’s going). Saves the edit you kept having to make. If you were already connected, you can still switch it to a regular message.

releases.title: Prompt preview: token cost + sign-off tokens + copy-prompt token resolution

items.label: The prompt preview now shows an approx token cost (~chars/4) of exactly what's sent, and — for prompts that read your career — which Career version {{careerContext}} resolves to, with a reminder you can swap the fullness in Context → Prompt Access (or use {{careerContextFull}}/{{careerContextBalanced}} directly).

Sign-offs are now tokenized: "Best, Alex" → {{signOff}} and "Thanks, Alex" → "Thanks, {{firstName}}" across the email / outreach / channel-style prompts (e.g. the Follow-Up Email no longer hardcodes the name). Resolves to each profile's own sign-off.
Copy-prompt mode now resolves {{placeholders}} too (token-only, so pasted record data is untouched) — so tokenized prompts paste correctly for any profile, not just the default.

releases.title: Profile generalization (Phase 3): exhaustive placeholder sweep + career token

items.label: Swept ~150 hardcoded owner-name literals across 21 prompt files into visible {{name}} / {{firstName}} / {{firstNameUpper}} placeholders — resolved-identical, so output is unchanged for both profiles (cold outreach, interview, offer, digest, etc. now show tokens in the raw template instead of a baked-in name).

Placeholders now also resolve in USER prompts (token-only, so interpolated record data is never rewritten) — fixing name references for non-active profiles (Chelsea's prompts no longer say the wrong name).

Parse Listing's career blob is now the {{careerContext}} placeholder: the raw template shows a token, and it resolves at send time to the version that feature is configured to read — swappable Condensed / Balanced / Full via Prompt Access, or use {{careerContextFull}} / {{careerContextBalanced}} explicitly.
Added scripts/verify-placeholders.ts — a both-profile gate that asserts every prompt resolves with no unresolved tokens and no cross-profile name leak.

releases.title: Profile generalization (Phase 3 start): parse-listing placeholders + IP block filled

items.label: The Parse Listing prompt now shows visible {{name}} / {{firstName}} / {{firstNameUpper}} placeholders in its header instead of a baked-in name — the resolved output is byte-identical per profile (the legacy substitution already produced the same text), so no change to results for Alex or Chelsea.

Filled the Personal Projects / IP context block for Alex from his 26 Pre-Engagement Inventions, and removed the now-duplicate inline tools list from his Offer Preferences (the list lives in one place; offer prompts get it once).

releases.title: Profile generalization (Phase 2 complete): recruiter fallback de-hardcoded

items.label: The recruiter-reply prompt no longer has an Alex-specific hardcoded fallback — a profile with no identity facts on file now gets a profile-neutral fit checklist that asks for what is missing. Profiles WITH facts (incl. both current ones) are unchanged.
Onboarding completeness, the Collection Guide, and the JSON skeleton auto-include the new identity fields + context blocks (registry-driven), so new profiles are prompted to fill them.

releases.title: Context editor: Personal Projects / IP + Target / Avoid Companies tabs

items.label: The two new context blocks now have their own Settings → Context tabs (Personal Projects / IP, Target / Avoid Companies) so they are first-class editable, not just in the onboarding Setup form.

releases.title: Profile generalization (Phase 2a): atomic identity fields + new context blocks

items.label: New atomic identity fields you can fill (Settings → AI Prompts → Onboarding → Setup): LinkedIn URL, website/portfolio, GitHub, address/city line, employment jurisdiction, and comp-floor-by-level — each its own injectable {{placeholder}} so prompts can reference one fact without pulling the whole career blob. {{email}}/{{phone}}/{{lastName}} resolve from data you already have.

Two new Context blocks: Personal Projects / IP (carve-outs for offer analysis + response emails) and Target / Avoid Companies (injected into the weekly digest, fit re-score, and loss analysis). Editable in Settings → Context; captured in onboarding + the AI seed for new profiles.
Backfilled LinkedIn URL, jurisdiction, and address line for both profiles from existing context. No prompt references the new tokens yet (that's the next phase), so current AI output is unchanged.

releases.title: Audit stats: Lifetime ⇄ This-session toggle, and an Audit section on Insights

items.label: The audit dashboard tiles now have a Lifetime / This session toggle — flip between cumulative resolution totals and just what you've resolved in the current visit.

The Insights page gained an “Audit & data quality” section: lifetime Resolved by AI, Resolved by you, Total resolved, and currently Needs-review (open flags across N jobs), with a link to the Audit page.

releases.title: Prompt preview: Raw ↔ Sent toggle + readable markdown view

items.label: The prompt preview is now a 3-way toggle: Raw template (the editable prompt, with {{placeholders}} left unresolved) · Sent · plain (exactly what the API receives — what the AI sees) · Sent · readable (the same resolved content with markdown rendered, since Context is markdown-heavy).

releases.title: Prompt placeholders + “resolved for my profile” preview (generalization, Phase 1)

items.label: New {{placeholder}} vocabulary for prompts — {{name}}, {{firstName}}, {{signOff}}, {{targetRoles}}, {{seniority}}, {{compFloor}}, {{location}}, {{jurisdiction}}, and more — that fill from your profile’s Context at send time, so a prompt template stays generic across profiles instead of baking in a name or facts. Each token has a safe fallback when a field is empty.

Settings → AI Prompts now has a clickable placeholder palette (insert a token into any prompt) and a “Preview resolved for my profile →” view on every prompt: see the raw template vs. exactly what’s sent to the API — your profile facts filled in and your Context (career / goals / rules) injected. Per-record data (a specific job or message) is shown as a run-time marker.

Foundation only — no existing prompt wording changed yet, so Alex’s and Chelsea’s output is byte-identical. Personalization now runs through one shared resolver (name/pronoun substitution + placeholders) applied centrally to every AI call.

releases.title: Audit dashboard tracks lifetime resolution totals (no longer resets to 0)

items.label: The “Resolved by AI” and “Resolved by you” tiles are now LIFETIME totals computed from persisted data (every job's aiResolutions + confirmedFields), so they keep their counts when you navigate away and back — and still show what's been resolved even when there's nothing left to audit.
“Still need you” and “Open suggestions” stay current (what's left to do), and each resolved tile shows a “+N this session” note when you've resolved items in the current visit.

releases.title: Auto-resolve with AI can now mark compensation “not disclosed”

items.label: The audit AI resolver now knows about the “not listed on posting” option: when a posting's comp text has no real figure (e.g. “Competitive salary”, “TBD”), it proposes marking compensation as not disclosed instead of inventing min/max — auto-applying at high confidence or suggesting it for one-click accept.

releases.title: Audit: mark compensation “not listed on the posting” instead of inventing numbers
