items.label: When a posting doesn't disclose a salary (e.g. “Competitive salary”), the compensation audit flag now offers a “Not listed on posting” action alongside “Set compensation” — so you can confirm there's genuinely no figure without inventing min/max.

Marking it sets compensation.notDisclosed, which resolves the audit item (it stops nagging) and shows a muted “not disclosed” tag next to the posting's own wording on the job detail + jobs table. It's not terminal — if you later learn the numbers, setting them clears the flag.

releases.title: Engagement & response insights; “Self-found” origin

items.label: **New “Engagement & response” breakdown on Insights → Pipeline.** Your pipeline split by engagement (applied or skipped vs not-yet-acted-on) across active and inactive roles, plus the REAL (human) response rate cut by active-applied vs inactive-applied — so you can see, e.g., that active roles respond far more often than ones that went cold. System-only (auto-ack / system rejection) replies are surfaced separately.

**“Initiated by” → “Self-found” (was “Self-applied”).** That field is about how an opportunity ORIGINATED — you found it yourself vs a recruiter / network / hiring-team reaching out — not whether you applied (which is tracked separately). All self-originated roles now read “Self-found”.
**Confirmed:** a role promoted from a recruiter outreach already auto-sets its origin to “Recruiter outreach”.

releases.title: Response rate counts real responses; pending interviews tightened

items.label: **Response rate now measures REAL (human) responses.** An automated acknowledgement or a system rejection email no longer counts as a response — only a reply from an actual person, reaching interviews, or genuine forward progress does. The card now shows engaged responses vs system-only (e.g. “11/55 real · 26 system-only”), so an autoresponder can't inflate the rate. This applies everywhere the response rate is shown (Dashboard, Insights, Job Opportunities).

**Pending Interviews now counts only your IMMEDIATE next real interview** — a Scheduled or Discussing next round — and breaks it out as scheduled vs discussing. Speculative future rounds you've sketched in (round 3/4 “Expected”) no longer count until the round before them happens.

releases.title: New “Offer Withdrawn” status + clearer offer outcomes

items.label: **New “Offer Withdrawn” offer status** for when an offer (even a verbal one) was extended and then rescinded by the company — distinct from “Went with Another Candidate” / “No Offer Made”, which mean no offer was ever made. It counts as an offer received in your stats.

**The Offer Status dropdown is now grouped** into “Offer extended / decided” (Waiting on Offer → Accepted / Declined / Withdrawn) vs “No offer made (lost / ended)” (No Offer Made / Went with Another Candidate / Withdrew from Process / Interview Process Ended), so the outcome you pick is unambiguous.
**Offers stat now breaks out accepted / declined / withdrawn / live**, so a withdrawn offer still shows as an offer you received.

releases.title: Accurate Job Opportunities stats + round counts

items.label: **The top stat cards are now accurate.** *Pending Interviews* counts only ACTIVE jobs that are actually mid-interview (was counting inactive roles + completed/ended interviews — 18 → 4). *Stale* now counts only ACTIVE opportunities (dormant/inactive roles are stale by definition), split into engaged vs not-yet-applied. *Offers* now counts offers you actually received — accepted/declined/live — instead of only live ones (0 → 2: “1 accepted · 1 declined”). *Avg Overall* now breaks out applied vs skipped.

**Round counts reflect reality.** The “R{N}” chip and the “Round x/y” footnote in the Interview Status column now count real rounds (held + booked) and show planned-but-unbooked rounds as “(+N planned)”, and the footnote shows the interview brain's mid-flight pulse between rounds — so a role with 1 interview and 3 sketched-in future rounds reads “Round 1 · … (+3 planned)” instead of a misleading “Round 2/4”.

**New “Entered Offer Stage” interview pulse.** When interviews complete and you've reached an offer, the mid-flight pulse now shows “Entered Offer Stage” (instead of going blank) — mirroring how application progress shows “Application Progressed”.

releases.title: Rounds auto-advance + close out with the process

items.label: **Earlier rounds now auto-advance.** When you schedule or hold a later round, any earlier round still marked “Held” is automatically moved to “Advanced” — you can't reach round 2 without clearing round 1, so you no longer have to update each prior round by hand. The same logic bumps a prior offer-discussion meeting when you book a new one.

**Rounds close out when the offer is decided.** Once an offer is Accepted / Declined / No Offer Made / Went with Another Candidate (and nothing newer is still booked), the latest round is automatically marked “Concluded” — signalling the process is closed with no more meetings.

releases.title: Interview brain: the pulse now cools over time

items.label: **The mid-flight pulse now decays as a process goes quiet.** The interview brain factors in how long it's been since the other side last engaged (plus your re-engage nudges): a positive process that's gone silent is suggested down through **Awaiting Next Steps → Delayed → a new “Gone Cold” pulse** that flags a stalled process heading toward inactivation. So e.g. a role you haven't heard from in a month is flagged Gone Cold, and one you just followed up on reads Awaiting Next Steps.

**A scheduled round whose time has passed (but you haven't logged the result yet) no longer reads as an upcoming interview** — the brain treats it as “happened, awaiting next steps” instead of an older round's stale due-date.

**The round counter now reflects reality.** Speculative future rounds you've sketched in (Discussing/Expected, not yet booked) no longer inflate the count — a job with 1 round held and 3 planned now reads **“Round 1 +3 planned”** instead of a misleading “Round 4”.

releases.title: Dialog titles now name the record they're about

items.label: **Dialogs now carry entity context in their title** — e.g. “Add Round 6 · Genesys”, “Edit Round 2 · …”, “Rename job · …”, “Rename lead · …”, “Log a communication · …”, “Schedule the interview · …”, “Reschedule meeting · …”, “Draft Follow-Up · …”. So you (and screen readers) always know which role/lead/person a dialog concerns at a glance, instead of a generic title.

releases.title: Interview brain respects the offer stage

items.label: **The interview suggestion now backs off once you're in the offer stage.** Previously a job where you'd already received or accepted an offer could still be nudged with “Coordinating Next Round” off its last round. Now, when any offer state exists, the brain treats the interviews as done — it only suggests marking the interview status “Completed” if it's stale, and never proposes an in-flight interview pulse on top of an offer.

releases.title: Dictation hotkey now tells you what's happening

items.label: **Fixed: the ⌃⇧D dictate hotkey no longer fails silently.** If you press it without a text field focused, you now get a hint to click into a field first; if the mic is blocked or the engine isn't available, the error is shown instead of nothing. The most common reason it “did nothing” was simply that no field was focused.

**Fixed a first-use cancel:** the browser's microphone-permission prompt could blur the window and cancel dictation before it started. Dictation now only auto-stops when you actually switch away from the tab, so granting mic access the first time works smoothly.

releases.title: Prompt variants: logged + a delete fix

items.label: **AI call logs now record which prompt variant produced each call.** If you've set up custom prompt variants (Settings → AI Prompts), the active variant's name now shows on the log entry (with a ✨ badge) — so you can finally tell from the logs which variant generated a given result. Calls on the packaged default are left unmarked.

**Fixed: deleting the active prompt variant no longer drops you back to the packaged default when other variants exist.** It now falls through to the next remaining variant, so you don't silently lose your selection.

releases.title: Dictate anywhere: ⌃⇧D push-to-talk into any field

items.label: **Hold ⌃⇧D (Ctrl+Shift+D) anywhere in the app to dictate into whatever text field is focused** — release to insert. It’s push-to-talk: hold while you speak, let go when you’re done, and the transcribed text drops in at the cursor. A small “Listening…” pill shows live state. It reuses your existing dictation engine (Web Speech or Whisper, per Settings → AI), so it works in any input or textarea without reaching for the per-field mic button.

releases.title: Interview brain: status suggestions from your rounds

items.label: **Your interview status can now be suggested straight from the rounds you log.** A new read-only “✨ Suggested from your rounds” chip on the Interview Status card reads your rounds and proposes the right interview status / pulse (e.g. a booked round → “Interview Scheduled”, an advanced round with none booked yet → “Coordinating Next Round”, an overdue follow-up → “Delayed”, a final round done → “Awaiting Decision”). One click applies it — nothing is ever changed automatically.

**It’s deliberately careful.** It reads rounds in real chronological order (not round numbers), never relabels a process you’ve closed, skips placeholder/skeleton rounds, respects any field you’ve confirmed, and won’t nag a lateral change to a status you set by hand. Dismissing a suggestion just confirms your current values so it stays quiet.
**New per-round “Final / offer-stage round” toggle** so the brain knows exactly when an interview loop is wrapping up and you’re awaiting a decision.

releases.title: Remove attachments from interview rounds & meetings

items.label: **You can now delete an attachment from an interview round or a lead meeting.** Each attachment gets a small × next to it — clicking it removes the file from the round/meeting and cleans the underlying file off disk. Previously attachments could only be added, so a wrong upload was stuck there.

releases.title: Awaiting reply — grouped conversations + smart re-engage

items.label: **The Awaiting-reply inbox now groups by conversation.** Multiple open threads with the same person about the same role are clustered under one header (e.g. “Quantiphi · Mitali — 3 threads, last reached out 1d ago · oldest 45d”) instead of scattered rows. Each thread shows a re-engagement stage pill (1st nudge / 2nd nudge); once a 2nd nudge has gone unanswered past the wait window, its action becomes “Close out” to mark the role inactive. Plus tighter rows, “By person / By company” grouping, a longest-waiting ↔ recent-activity sort toggle, and page quick actions (g to regroup, s to re-sort).

releases.title: Sturdier interview-prep saves + a smarter audit nudge

items.label: **Interview-round and meeting edits now validate the prep section on the server.** Saving a round or meeting checks the (sometimes AI-generated) prep against the schema before writing it, so a malformed prep payload is rejected instead of silently corrupting the record.

**The audit now spots a likely “Network outreach” mix-up.** When a job is marked self/recruiter-initiated but a contact is tagged an external referrer, the audit flags it (with the referrer's name) so you can correct the initiated-by — instead of the generic “was inferred” note.

releases.title: Cross-record: prior-rejection heads-up + dismissible nudges in your action list

items.label: **The “assistant noticed” card now flags companies that passed on you before.** When you have an active role at a company where an earlier application was rejected or went unanswered, you’ll see that history — so you can decide whether to tailor your approach or reconsider. You can also dismiss any observation for two weeks if it isn’t useful right now.

**Your most pressing cross-record nudges now show up in Needs-Action (and desktop notifications), not just on the dashboard** — for example, a dormant lead at a company you’re actively interviewing with. Lower-signal observations (duplicate roles, low-converting recruiters) stay on the dashboard card so they don’t crowd your action list.

releases.title: Lighter, smoother Job Opportunities list

items.label: **The Job Opportunities list loads lighter and scrolls smoother.** The page now ships only what the table shows instead of every job's full message history, contacts and interview prep — roughly halving the page payload — and skips rendering rows that are off-screen. Exporting a selection as JSON still includes the complete records.

releases.title: Cross-record: spot live leads at companies you're pursuing

items.label: **The “assistant noticed” card now also flags *live* leads at a company you have an active role with** — not just dormant ones. When a relationship and an application overlap at the same company, you’ll see a nudge to coordinate them (or use the lead to backchannel the live process) instead of crossing wires. Leads that already became the job are excluded.

releases.title: Faster job & communication pages (lazy-loaded dialogs)

items.label: **The job-detail and Communication pages load less code up front.** The three heaviest editors (add/edit message, draft follow-up, new-chain outreach — ~5,900 lines combined) now load on first use instead of with the page, so those screens open quicker. Once you open one it stays loaded, so re-opening is instant.

releases.title: The assistant noticed — cross-record insights

items.label: **The assistant now spots connections across your records.** A new “The assistant noticed” card on your dashboard surfaces things no single job or lead can show on its own — a dormant lead at a company you’re now actively interviewing with, a recruiter whose roles never reach an interview, or duplicate active roles at the same company. Each finding shows the company logos and links straight to the jobs and leads involved, and a one-click “Generate insights” explains why it matters and the single next move to make.

releases.title: Awaiting reply — one inbox for unanswered outreach

items.label: **New “Awaiting reply” inbox.** One list of every conversation — across jobs and leads — where you sent the last message and haven’t heard back, sorted by how long you’ve been waiting (amber after a week, red after three). Each row links to the thread, offers a one-click re-engage, and can be snoozed for a week. Find it under People & comms → Awaiting reply.

releases.title: Desktop notifications for what needs action

items.label: **Get a desktop notification when something needs action.** Turn it on in Settings → Thresholds → Desktop notifications: choose which urgencies to be alerted about (overdue / due-soon / info), how often to check, and an optional once-a-day summary. Notifications fire while Job Tracker is open in a tab; clicking one jumps straight to the item.

releases.title: This Week's Focus — company logos + role links

items.label: **This Week's Focus now shows company logos and links to the role.** Each priority that's about a company shows its logo next to the bullet number, and the title links straight to that job — and a bullet that names two companies (e.g. “Genesys and Calabrio”) shows both logos. Matched automatically from your active roles (handles name variants like “People In AI” vs the full company name).

releases.title: Batch/cache cost insights, log filters & fixes

items.label: **Insights → AI now has a Batch API section** — how many calls you've run through the Batch API, what they cost, and what that saved versus the full sync price (alongside the existing cache-efficiency stat).
**Filter the AI call log by Batch or Cached.** New filter chips show only the calls that got a batch and/or cached discount.
**Fixed the empty “Spend · last 14 days” chart** on the AI calls tab — the bars were collapsing to zero height (a CSS bug); the daily spend now renders.
**The would-have-cost strikethrough now sits below the actual price** instead of beside it, so the cost columns stay narrow.

releases.title: Smart “Decline a role” now works for all leads + watch roles (recruiter-outreach parity)

items.label: The smart “Decline…” action — previously recruiter-outreach only — now works for EVERY lead and its watch roles (referral, networking, head-hunter, reconnect, etc.). On the watch-role card AND on the contact's message: it dismisses the role and, when it's the last active one, lets you keep the lead Dormant (circle back / may surface other roles) or close it out. Regular leads keep their quick one-click Dismiss alongside the new smart Decline.

The wording and the AI adapt to the lead type — a referral/networking contact is framed as a “contact” weighing ongoing relationship value, not a recruiter pitching future roles. The AI is only consulted when there's a conversation to read.

Hardened: declining a leftover role on an already-closed lead (converted/abandoned) no longer re-opens or downgrades it — only the role is dismissed, and the dialog says so. Guarded in both the preview and the server.

releases.title: Communication import quick actions (scoped to the focused role)

items.label: **Communication quick actions for the role you're viewing.** Import a text-message CSV (I) or search/import email (E) straight into the currently-selected role as a new chain, add a message to the open chain (A), start a new conversation (M), or log a comm (C) — each with a hotkey, scoped to your current selection.

releases.title: Action quick-shortcuts: needs-action, threads, stale roles, audit

items.label: **Quick actions that DO things, not just navigate.** Dashboard & Priorities — Focus / Snooze / Complete the top Needs-Action item (F / S / D). Priorities — summarize the top contact thread, and re-engage or inactivate the top stale role. Audit — focus by severity (All / High / Medium / Low) and hide/show resolved flags. Each with a sidebar action + hotkey.

releases.title: Smart “decline a pitched role” for recruiter outreach

items.label: When a recruiter pitches a role that's a bad fit, a new “Decline…” action — on the pitched-role card AND on the recruiter's own message in the conversation — dismisses the role. When it's the LAST active pitched role, it then either keeps the recruiter as a Dormant engagement (if they'll watch for future-fit roles) or abandons the outreach. If other pitched roles are still live, the engagement stays active.

AI reads the conversation + your offer preferences to pre-fill the decline reason (too junior / comp below your floor / their ceiling under your minimum) and pre-select keep-as-dormant vs abandon — you confirm or edit, see a before→after preview, then apply it as one atomic update.

releases.title: More page quick actions: pipeline, roadmap, dashboard, priorities, fit

items.label: **More pages got their own quick actions.** Pipeline — switch the timeline range (30d / 90d / 6mo / 1yr / YTD / All). Roadmap — collapse/expand all sections, show/hide completed. Dashboard — refresh This Week's Focus. Priorities — flip Needs-Action grouping between urgency and type. Insights → Fit re-score — trigger a re-score. Each has a sidebar action and a hotkey.

releases.title: Quick actions adapt to page state; defaults pruned

items.label: **Quick actions now react to what's on the page, with labels that flip as you go.** On the Calendar the action reads "Swap to Week view", then once you're in Week it offers "Swap to Grid view" / "Swap to List view". Leads & Recruiter Outreach get a Card/Table swap plus Update with AI; Contacts can jump between Company / Job / Contact-first views; People can change its sort — all from the sidebar (and their hotkeys).

**Pages where the generic actions didn't fit no longer show them.** Dashboard, Priorities, Audit, Logs, Roadmap and Settings no longer show "Add job / Parse / Log comm" — those pages get their own relevant actions (or none) instead.

releases.title: People: filter/sort by photo status, color-coded markers, and set the 'no photo' reason right in the detail + Edit Contact

items.label: New 'photo' filter on People — All photos / No photo / and each no-photo reason — so you can pull up exactly who's missing a photo and why. Plus a 'Photo status (reason)' sort that groups people by reason.
The no-photo marker is now color-coded so it's easier to tell apart at a glance: amber = no photo on their LinkedIn, rose = no online profile found, sky = same-name profile (unconfirmed).
You can now set the reason right in the People detail panel (no need to open 'Change photo') — and it's also in the Edit Contact dialog as a 'Photo status' field.

releases.title: Logs show batch/cached savings; timezone date fixes

items.label: **AI call logs now show how a call saved money.** Batch-API calls get a **batch** badge and cached-input calls get a **cached** badge (a call can have both). When a discount applied, the cost columns strike through the un-discounted would-have-cost next to the actual — e.g. a batch call shows the full price crossed out beside the 50%-off price, and a cached call shows the savings from input being billed at ~10%.

**Fixed dates/times that could read in UTC instead of your timezone.** Swept the app for raw-ISO date displays (which could show the wrong day near midnight) and datetime pickers that pre-filled ~4 hours off (interview-round scheduling, debrief times) — all now use the timezone-correct helpers.

releases.title: Fixed the phone-number input corruption, added a 'no photo available' marker, and moved the record icons to a consistent spot

items.label: Fixed a phone-number entry bug: typing a number (e.g. 6479195187) used to corrupt into the wrong digits (the +1 got pulled into the area code → 164…), and deleting ran away into +1 (111) 111-1111. The formatter is now idempotent — it formats cleanly as you type and deletes cleanly.

You can now mark WHY a person has no photo so the blank avatar reads as intentional: 'No photo on their LinkedIn', 'No online profile found', or 'Same-name profile, unconfirmed'. A small person icon appears on the avatar (People + Contacts), with a tooltip. Set it from the photo control.
Moved the job / lead / recruiter-outreach record icons to just left of the rec(s) / msg(s) text, so they sit in the same place for every person.

releases.title: People: record-type icons + filter, Recruiter Outreach labeling, and pasted photo URLs are now downloaded permanently

items.label: Each person now shows small icons for which record types they appear in — blue briefcase (job), green sprout (lead), purple chat (recruiter outreach). A person can show all three.
New 'records' filter on People: All / Only jobs / Only leads / Only recruiter outreach / In multiple types — so you can see the breakup of where people come from.
A recruiter-outreach record now reads as 'Recruiter Outreach' (purple) in a person's records list, not 'Lead' — matching the rest of the app.
Pasted photo URLs (e.g. a LinkedIn licdn address) are now DOWNLOADED and stored permanently on the contact, so they don't break when the URL's signed expiry passes. The original URL is remembered.
Press 'Change photo' and you'll now see the current photo's source URL (clickable), so you can review or re-grab it.

releases.title: Contacts page now groups conversations like the rest of the app

items.label: **The Contacts page now threads conversations through the same shared logic as the Communication page and calendar.** Previously it grouped chains by a slightly different rule and ignored received-reply times when ordering — so a contact's chains could differ from what you saw elsewhere. They now match exactly (verified identical across all current contacts).

releases.title: Quick actions now adapt to each page

items.label: **Sidebar quick actions are now page-specific.** Instead of the same three actions everywhere, each page shows only what's useful there — and only those keys fire. On **Calendar**: Month view (1), Week view (2), Jump to today (T). On **Contacts/People**: Add contact with AI (A), Log comm (C). On **Communication**: New conversation (M), Log comm (C). On **Leads/Recruiter Outreach**: Add with AI (A), Log comm (C). **Jobs/Dashboard/Priorities** keep Add job (N), Parse with AI (P), Log comm (C). Read-only pages (Insights, Pipeline) show none.

releases.title: Fixed a 404 from People → recruiter-outreach records, started logging 404s, and contact photos now show on the Contacts page

items.label: Fixed: clicking a recruiter-outreach record from a person on the People page 404'd (it linked to /leads/… but recruiter-engagement leads live at /recruiter-outreach/…). The People records list — and the activity-log link builder — now route recruiter leads to the right page.

404s are now tracked: hitting a missing page shows a proper in-app 404 screen and records the attempted path + where you came from to the System tab of /logs, so broken/stale links are visible and traceable.
Contact photos now show on the Contacts page (the company-first / job-first contact cards), not just the People page — matching the contact-first view.

releases.title: Leads polish: Add with AI, multi-company logos, dashboard time fix

items.label: **Leads now has an "Add with AI" button** (matching Recruiter Outreach). Paste a message or a quick description and it drafts a new lead — and captures a watched role if one is named — before you save.

**Leads with multiple companies now show a logo in the list.** A lead spanning more than one company (e.g. a referral that touches both an anchor company and a role's end-client) was falling back to a generic icon; it now shows the anchor company's logo, matching the lead's own page. Pure networkers with no company still show the people icon.
**Fixed the dashboard "This Week's Focus" timestamps showing ~4 hours ahead.** The "Showing data from" and "Batch refresh pending since" times now display in your local timezone instead of UTC.

releases.title: People page polish — company logos on records, contact photos on Contacts, quick-edit + jump, easy LinkedIn open

items.label: Each linked record in a person's detail now shows the real company logo (not just initials).
The Contacts page now shows the contact's photo next to their name (list + detail) wherever one is set — falling back to the company logo / initials.

From a person on People you can now: 'Quick edit' their name / role / email / phone / LinkedIn inline (syncs across their linked records), and 'Open in Contacts ↗' to jump straight to them on the Contacts page.

The Add-photo control now has an 'Open their LinkedIn ↗' link right next to the paste field — open the profile, right-click the photo → Copy image address → paste. (Auto-fetch from a LinkedIn URL still isn't possible — LinkedIn blocks it.)

releases.title: Page-aware quick actions + keyboard shortcuts

items.label: **Sidebar quick actions now adapt to the page and have keyboard shortcuts.** Each action shows its single-key hotkey as a badge — Add job (N), Parse with AI (P), Log comm (C) everywhere, plus page-specific ones like New conversation (M) on the Communication page. Press the key from anywhere (when you're not typing in a field) to fire it — no modifier needed.

releases.title: Sidebar nav grouped by theme

items.label: **The left nav is now grouped into themes** — Overview (Dashboard · Priorities · Calendar) · Pipeline (Job Opportunities · Pipeline · Insights) · Sourcing (Leads · Recruiter Outreach) · People & comms (Communication · Contacts · People) · System (Audit · Logs · Roadmap · Settings) — with a dotted separator between each group, so related pages sit together.

releases.title: Dashboard: batch refresh now updates + clearer timestamps

items.label: **Fixed: a batch "This Week's Focus" refresh now actually takes effect.** Previously, refreshing with "Run as batch" submitted the job but the card never changed. Now the card immediately shows "Batch refresh pending since …", checks in the background, and auto-updates when the (cheaper) batch result lands — no manual reload.

The card now spells out **when the shown data is from** ("Showing data from …") and, when a batch refresh is in flight, **when it was kicked off** — so you can tell current data from a pending refresh at a glance.

releases.title: Communication Power: "Let AI pick" replies + AI-prompts reorg

items.label: **"Let AI pick" is back in the Draft dialog** — and now actually works. When you choose it, the AI reads the last message in the thread, classifies it, and picks the best focused-reply type for you (then drafts with that type's finetuned prompt). Joins Auto-detect and the manual reply-type chips.

**Settings → AI Prompts is reorganized** into clearer, intuitive groups — the focused/reply-drafting prompts now sit together (Reply drafting · Cold outreach), and the old catch-all Helpers / Classification & Audit tabs are split into Summaries & digest · Writing helpers · Classification & linking · Audit & merge. Same prompts, just easier to find.

releases.title: Needs-Action polish: split application deadlines from next-actions + editable snooze presets

items.label: The “Needs action” queue (dashboard + Priorities) now distinguishes Application deadlines from Next actions — separate labels + icons + “By type” groups — so an “apply by” date reads differently from a “follow up by” date.
New Settings → Thresholds → “Needs-Action snooze presets”: customize the snooze options (in days) and which one is the default offered in the queue. (“Pick a date” stays available inline.)

releases.title: Contact photos on People — paste a photo URL or upload one, synced across each person's records

items.label: People now show real contact photos instead of just initials — in the list and the detail panel. Add one from a person's detail with 'Add photo': paste a direct image URL (tip: right-click their LinkedIn photo → 'Copy image address') or upload an image file, just like company logos. Initials remain the fallback.
A photo is person-level: set it once and it syncs across all of that person's linked records (same as name / phone / LinkedIn). Remove it anytime.

Note on LinkedIn: pulling a photo automatically from just a LinkedIn profile URL isn't possible — LinkedIn blocks automated access (returns a bot wall). Pasting the image address (or uploading) is the reliable path.

releases.title: Smarter Re-engage gating + Leads view toggle

items.label: **"Re-engage" now only shows for a contact you can actually reach.** A stale role offers Re-engage only when there's a real (non-no-reply) email, a phone, an existing email/text thread, or a genuine LinkedIn conversation. A contact that's just a saved LinkedIn URL — with no messages exchanged — no longer counts, so a role like that now correctly shows "Inactivate · no contact" instead of "Re-engage."
The Leads list's Card/Table switch now uses the same compact icon toggle as Recruiter Outreach (instead of text buttons).

releases.title: Priorities is now one unified, triageable “Needs action” queue (group by urgency or type)

items.label: The Priorities page now runs on the same “Needs action” engine as the dashboard — one unified queue you can triage (snooze / mark handled, with a snoozed/handled section to restore) and group by urgency (Overdue / This week / Later) or by type (Offers / Interviews / Deadlines / …). Offers, interviews, deadlines, and lead/job next-actions all live in the queue, computed once. Your rich sections stay: stale-applications triage (inactivate / re-engage), open contact threads, high-priority list, and draft follow-ups.

releases.title: People: sort by # of messages + a wider, word-wrapping Link dialog · Leads: one-click close-out

items.label: People can now be sorted by # of messages (alongside Name, # of records, and Recently contacted).

Fixed the 'Link N records' dialog: long record labels used to overflow off the right edge (hiding the record type + pushing the buttons out of reach). They now word-wrap inside a wider dialog, so everything stays visible.

A lead can now be closed out in one click from its Status card — 'Mark dormant' (alive but quiet, revisit later) or 'Mark abandoned' (nothing came of it) — the lead equivalent of inactivating a job. Any reason you type carries over.

releases.title: Fix: snoozing a Needs-Action item to a custom date now applies on the first pick

items.label: In the “Needs action” snooze menu, picking a custom date now snoozes immediately. (The menu’s click-away layer was closing the menu when the native date picker dismissed — unmounting the field before the pick registered, so you had to act twice. Replaced it with a proper outside-click handler that the date picker doesn’t trip.)

releases.title: Communication Power (10): edit the focused-reply prompts

items.label: **The focused-reply scenario prompts are now editable.** Settings → Interaction Kinds has a new **Focused-reply scenarios** section: tweak the directive that finetunes each reply type (Schedule, Negotiate the offer, Politely decline, …). Your edit is appended to the draft's prompt as the dominant intent; clear a box to restore the packaged default.

releases.title: Communication Power (9): focused-reply scenarios

items.label: **Pick the TYPE of reply and the draft comes out finetuned for it.** The Draft-follow-up dialog now has a **Reply type** picker — Auto-detect, or a specific scenario (Schedule a time · Answer their questions · Nudge · Post-interview follow-up · Thank-you · Negotiate the offer · Ask for a referral · Politely decline). Each scenario injects a purpose-built directive into the draft's system prompt (not just the focus text), so e.g. "Negotiate the offer" leads with enthusiasm and makes a specific, grounded ask. Auto picks by rules (the recruiter's-first-message reply still fires automatically). You can still add free-text specifics on top.

releases.title: Communication Power (8): one canonical conversation-grouping engine

items.label: **Internal cleanup:** the logic that groups a record's messages into conversations was hand-rolled in ~7 places (the Communication page, the job/lead comms card, and four AI draft/summary routes), with subtle drift between them. It's now one shared `chain-builder` engine, so a message always lands in the SAME conversation everywhere — including a latent fix where the job-detail comms card and the AI routes now match the Communication page exactly. No visible change to your conversations (verified: 132 chains before and after).

releases.title: The “No comms” view: real job rows with logos, selectable to search email / import right there

items.label: The “No comms” filter now lists each 0-communication job/lead as a full row — company logo, title, full-height scroll — instead of the old cramped, logo-less strip. They’re searchable like any other row.

Selecting a 0-comm job now opens its Communication panel with the SAME action header as any other job — Search email, Import CSV, New message — so you can pull in that first acknowledgement / rejection email (or log the first message) without leaving the Communication page.

releases.title: “Needs action” is now a triage inbox — snooze or mark items handled

items.label: The dashboard’s “Needs action” list is now triageable: snooze any item (1 day / 3 days / 1 week / pick a date) or mark it handled. Snoozed items come back when the timer’s up; handled items stay hidden until their situation actually changes (e.g. a deadline moves or a follow-up re-escalates), and a collapsible “snoozed / handled” section lets you restore anything. Per-item state is saved per profile.

releases.title: Communication Power (7): rename custom interaction kinds

items.label: **Custom interaction-kind labels are now editable too.** Built-in kind labels became editable last release; now the bold name of each of your custom kinds is an inline field as well. The underlying id stays fixed, so existing messages keep their tag — only the displayed name changes.

releases.title: Find your 0-communication jobs to log a first message + search your email from the job page

items.label: The Communication page has a prominent 'No comms (N)' filter pill that narrows the list to ONLY jobs/leads with no messages yet — so after applying, connecting the first email (acknowledgement, rejection, recruiter reply) to the right opportunity is one click. (Replaces the easy-to-miss 'Show empty' checkbox.)

The job opportunity page now has a 'Search email' button on its Communication card (plus a per-chain email-import icon) — search Mail.app / Gmail for a received message and import it, exactly like the Communication page. Lets you log the very first communication on a job that has none yet.

releases.title: Communication Power (6): focused-reply presets

items.label: **One-click focused reply types when drafting with AI.** The Draft-follow-up dialog now has quick-pick chips — Schedule a time, Answer their questions, Nudge for a reply, Post-interview follow-up, Thank-you, Negotiate the offer, Ask for a referral, Politely decline — each dropping a purpose-built instruction into the (still editable) Focus field, which the draft honors as the dominant intent. Joins the recruiter-cold-outreach and re-engagement focused prompts so more reply situations get a tailored draft.

releases.title: Communication Power (5): re-classify messages across conversations

items.label: **Pick individual messages across different conversations and bulk re-classify them.** On the Communication page, hit **Select messages…** in a thread to show per-message checkboxes; tick any messages, switch to other threads and tick more (your selection carries across conversations), then **Re-classify** the whole set through the same review-and-apply dialog. Complements the by-kind (Settings) and whole-conversation re-classify already shipped.

releases.title: Communication Power (4): rename kinds, richer templates, offer-letter jump fix

items.label: **Rename any interaction kind's label** — not just its description. In Settings → Interaction Kinds, the bold name of each built-in kind is now an editable field (e.g. "Cold outreach" → "First touch"); the underlying id never changes, so existing messages stay linked. Clear the field to revert to the packaged default. The new name flows everywhere — dropdowns, pills, and the AI classifier's options.

**More outreach-template placeholders.** Templates now fill {{company}}, {{role}} and {{my_name}} in addition to {{contact}} — so a saved template can read "Hi {{contact}}, excited about the {{role}} role at {{company}} — {{my_name}}" and resolve all four when you apply it. The Settings template editor lists the available placeholders.

**Fixed: an "Offer letter" message link now jumps to the right doc.** Clicking a message's linked offer-letter pill (e.g. the ESOP) lands on the Attachments card, switches to the Offer Letters tab, and selects + previews that exact version — previously it switched the tab but didn't scroll, so the jump looked like it did nothing.

releases.title: Jobs get a “next action due” deadline too — captured from a parse, shown on the calendar + Needs Action

items.label: When you “Add with AI” a posting or recruiter thread that implies a follow-up by a certain day, that deadline is now captured on the Job (not just on Leads/engagements, which already had it). It appears on the job timeline, on the Calendar, and in the dashboard’s “Needs action” list — at ANY status, so it isn’t hidden for recruiter-sourced jobs the way the application deadline is (which only shows before you’ve applied).

releases.title: Communication Power (3b/3): re-classify a conversation

items.label: **Re-classify a whole conversation from the Communication page.** Open a thread and hit **Re-classify conversation** — the AI re-runs the interaction-kind classifier over that conversation's messages and shows the same review list (current → proposed kind), where you check the ones to apply. Complements the by-kind re-classify in Settings, so you can clean up either one thread or an entire kind.

releases.title: Communication Power (3a/3): bulk re-classify by kind

items.label: **Bulk re-classify messages by kind.** In Settings → Interaction Kinds, pick a kind and **Re-classify** — the AI re-runs over every message currently tagged with it, then shows a review list (current → proposed kind + reasoning). You check the ones to apply; nothing changes until you do. Handy after renaming/disabling a kind or sharpening its description.

releases.title: Fit scores can now be truly “Unscored” (nullable) instead of a misleading 0

items.label: A role the AI conservatively left unscored now stores “no score” (null) instead of 0 — so it can’t masquerade as a real worst-case “Fit 0/10”, and analytics/sorting stop counting an unjudged role as a definitive zero. The parse-review and watch-role editors let you clear a fit to leave it Unscored (blank = Unscored).
Fixed: editing an unrelated field of an unscored role used to silently re-write its fit as 0; it now preserves the Unscored state.
Migrated existing seed-default fit-0 watch roles to Unscored (only the ones with no rationale/requirements — a deliberate low score is preserved).

releases.title: Communication Power (2/3): precise message-link jumps

items.label: A message's **jump-to links now land on the exact file or timeline event**, not just the section. A document link scrolls to that file (and auto-switches the Attachments tab it lives in); a timeline link scrolls straight to that event (expanding the timeline if the event was older). The links already carried the file/event id — they just collapsed to the section before.
Jump-scrolling is also more reliable on these long detail pages: it retries while the page mounts and re-corrects as content settles, so a jump to something near the bottom actually lands.

releases.title: Sharper Leads vs Recruiter Outreach: consistent labels, clearer help, and safe reclassify (no more 404)

items.label: The Leads and Recruiter Outreach pages now share one consistent set of kind labels + sharper help text explaining the boundary: Recruiter Outreach = a recruiter reached out to YOU (inbound); a Lead is a relationship you cultivate (a head-hunter you know, a warm referral). The “Add with AI” review also shows readable kind names instead of raw values.

Reclassifying a lead’s kind is now safe. The inline “Kind” dropdown only offers same-page kinds, and crossing the boundary uses explicit “Graduate to Lead” / “Move to Recruiter Outreach” actions (with a redirect to the right page + an audit timeline entry). This fixes a bug where flipping kind could strand a record on the wrong page and 404 it on the next load — now enforced server-side, not just in the UI.
New “Move to Recruiter Outreach” action — the reverse of “Graduate to Lead” — for when a lead is really an inbound recruiter ping that belongs on the Recruiter Outreach page.

releases.title: Communication Power (1/3): outreach templates per interaction kind

items.label: **Save a subject + body template per interaction kind** (Settings → Interaction Kinds → Outreach templates). When you pick that kind while composing a message, a **Use template** button pre-fills the subject + body — and a brand-new, empty message auto-fills from it. Use **{{contact}}** in the template and it's replaced with the recipient's name on apply.

releases.title: Parse-review: edit a pitched role's status/fit/requirements inline + “Unscored” instead of a misleading Fit 0/10

items.label: On the “Add with AI” review screen for a recruiter engagement, each pitched role now lets you edit its Status, Fit (0–10), why-it’s-a-fit, and Key requirements inline — so you can correct the AI’s guesses before creating the engagement, instead of fixing them on the detail page afterward.

A role the AI conservatively left unscored now shows a neutral “Unscored” chip instead of a grey “Fit 0/10” that looked like a real worst-case score — across watch-role cards, the engagement & leads tables, role pickers, and Priorities. (A new shared FitChip is the single source of truth.)

releases.title: Interview Intelligence: one-click debrief + linked transcripts

items.label: **True one-click debrief.** After a live interview/meeting call, the “Call captured” nudge now has a **✨ Draft debrief** button that drafts the structured debrief from your call (notes + stored transcript) AND **saves it** — then jumps you to it to review. Before, it only jumped to the section and you had to open a modal, generate, and save. (Append-only, so it never overwrites anything you typed; falls back to a copyable prompt if no API key.)

The two transcript surfaces are now **cross-linked**: the in-call “Live transcript” peek links to the dedicated **Transcript** section (to clean it up + extract notes), and the Transcript section notes that extracted notes flow back into your **Live notes**. They stay separate on purpose — quick live peek vs. cleaned source — just easier to move between.

releases.title: Smart 'close out as rejection' button on rejection messages

items.label: A message whose interaction type is 'Rejection' now shows a 'Close out (rejected)' button (job comms only) that closes the opportunity in one step — Inactive (Rejected) plus the right application / interview / offer statuses — with an editable before→after preview.

It branches on context: a pre-interview rejection sets Application Progress → 'Application Rejected'; if interviewing had already begun (they went with someone else) it sets Offer Status → 'Went with Another Candidate' and a terminal Interview Status — Completed if you'd finished and were awaiting results, else Ended Prematurely (editable in the preview).

releases.title: Re-engagement now works for leads & recruiter relationships too — not just job applications

items.label: When a lead or recruiter relationship goes quiet, the AI compose flows on its page now offer the same 'Re-engage · N/2' draft — in an existing chain or a new one — addressed to the contact you're writing to.

The lead re-engagement AI is grounded in what actually matters for a relationship (not an application): the relationship + why you'd reach back out (reEngagementTrigger), the role(s) in play (watch roles), your relationship notes, the full message history, and meetings/calls — including open commitments from call debriefs as the natural hook.

The re-engagement attempt pill, attempt counting, per-contact targeting, and unified AI Logs all carry over to leads. (Marking a ghosted lead dormant/abandoned still uses the lead's own status — that lifecycle is unchanged.)

releases.title: Jobs table: reverted the Fixed view · Logs Overview: de-duplicated + richer

items.label: Removed the Jobs table **Fit / Fixed** column toggle — the fixed-width view didn’t look better, so the table is back to the original content-sized view, full stop.

Reworked the Logs **Overview** to cut repeated numbers: the top metrics strip is now the single place for the headline counts, and the cards below show only what’s unique — so the old duplicate “events / calls / operations” cards are gone.

And added more: an **Events 14-day sparkline** next to the AI one, your **most-active role** (by event count), a **week-over-week AI spend trend** arrow, a System **operation-mix** breakdown with recent issues, and clearer cost vs. failed-call labelling.

releases.title: Re-engagement drafts address the chosen recipient by name — even when the thread was with someone else

items.label: Hardened the re-engagement prompts so the draft always opens to the recipient you're writing to (the chain's contact or your chosen new-chain recipient), rather than defaulting to whoever the prior email thread happened to be with.

releases.title: Question Bank polish — accurate 'new since built' past 150 questions, safer concurrent edits, cleaner empty state

items.label: The 'N new since built — Rebuild to refresh' nudge now stays accurate even once you've recorded more than 150 interview questions (it was silently stuck at zero past that point).
Editing, pinning, and adding bank questions now save atomically, so two edits made at the same time (e.g. from two tabs) can't overwrite each other.
If you ever clear all your interview debriefs, rebuilding the bank now drops the mined themes while keeping your own anticipated questions — and the Rebuild button stays reachable.

releases.title: Re-engagement drafts now address the right person — the contact you're actually writing to

items.label: When you draft a re-engagement from inside an existing chain, it now writes to THAT chain's contact (not just the role's primary). In a new chain it writes to the recipient you picked — and if you haven't picked one yet, it drafts to the resolved contact and auto-selects them so the message and the recipient stay in sync.

The draft-reengagement endpoint accepts an optional contactId (with an email fallback for older id-less contacts); the job-detail and Priorities one-click actions are unchanged and still target the primary reachable contact.

releases.title: Logs Overview: a much richer home dashboard

items.label: The Logs **Overview** tab is no longer sparse. A new **6-tile metrics strip** up top (events, AI calls, AI spend, tokens, operations, errors — each with a this-week figure and clickable into its tab), and the three stream cards now show more: Activity adds today’s count + an actor split (you / AI / system), AI calls adds success rate · cache saved · your top feature, and System adds an operation-type breakdown (writes / pulls / calls).

A new **AI spend & usage** panel: cost **by provider** and your **top features** as bars, a **14-day calls sparkline** (with the peak day called out), and input/output tokens, cache savings, and error count. All derived from data already on the page — no extra load. Browser-verified.

releases.title: Jobs table: optional Fixed-columns view (finishes the virtualization item)

items.label: A new **Columns: Fit / Fixed** toggle on the Jobs table (top-right). **Fit** is the current view — columns size to their content (unchanged, still the default). **Fixed** (beta) gives every column a uniform width and uses CSS containment so the browser skips off-screen rows — smoother scrolling once your list gets large. Your choice is remembered per device.

Both views are kept side-by-side on purpose: Fixed is opt-in so it can be refined over time without touching the proven Fit view. This finishes the `jobstable-virtualization` roadmap item (the AI-call log got the same treatment in v4.213.0). Browser-verified: no column jitter on scroll, no clipped values, and expand / select / sort / filters all work.

releases.title: Batch re-score & offers — final correctness pass

items.label: Fit Re-score now reserves room for watch roles when scoring, so a large active-job pipeline can't crowd them all out of the run.
Applying a batch re-score re-checks each watch role first, so a role you promoted to a job (or dismissed) during the batch wait never receives a stale score.

Watch-role old→new deltas in a batch review now use the role's live score (matching how jobs already worked), and the Offers matrix flags itself stale when an offer's comp or status changes — not only when an offer is added or removed.

releases.title: Re-engagement everywhere it belongs — a pill on the message, a draft option in compose, and richer grounding

items.label: Re-engagement attempts now wear a distinct sky-blue '↩ Re-engagement' pill (· 2nd for the final nudge) in the Communication view and the job's Follow-Ups card, so you can spot a revival message at a glance.

When a stale role is re-engagement-eligible, both AI compose flows — 'Draft AI follow-up' inside an existing chain and '✨ New chain with AI' — now show a 'Re-engage · N/2' button that drafts the history-aware re-engagement message and tags it with the right kind on save.

The re-engagement AI now reads more than the message thread: the opportunity's own notes + your open concerns, and per-round talking points from interview debriefs — what was discussed, their concerns, the tone, and especially OPEN COMMITMENTS the company owed (e.g. 'they'd share next steps'), which it uses as the most natural, respectful hook.

releases.title: Batch AI, finished: fit batches score watch roles too, and the Offers matrix now persists

items.label: A Fit Re-score run as a batch now scores your active watch roles as well as your jobs — matching the instant button — and applies a watch-role's new score to the right place. (It was silently jobs-only before, quietly dropping your watch roles.)

The Offers decision matrix now persists: the recommendation + ranking survive reload and a batch comparison lands on the page, with a 'compared {time}' stamp and a nudge to re-compare when your offers have changed since. Previously it vanished the moment you navigated away.

The Batches tab is now honest across the board — only Fit Re-score (which you approve score-by-score) shows 'ready to review'; the weekly digest, question bank, and offer decision auto-save and simply link to 'Open'.

releases.title: Fit Re-score batch review — hardening so multi-batch and batch-mode cases are safe

items.label: Resolving a batch re-score now supersedes only that batch and OLDER ones — a newer batch you haven't seen is never silently buried.
Starting a fresh re-score while a batch review is open now clears the old review table immediately, so its Apply button can't write scores from the batch you just replaced.
The old→new deltas (and which rows are pre-checked) now use each role's LIVE fit score, not the snapshot from when the batch was submitted — so the comparison is always current.

Smaller correctness touches: the review surfaces the next pending batch after you resolve one; a batch whose results no longer match any role self-resolves instead of dangling; the Batches tab only says 'ready to review' once a batch has actually completed; and an apply where every write fails is kept for retry instead of being marked done.

releases.title: Insights now tracks re-engagement — what you're nudging, your reply rate, and how dead roles were let go

items.label: New 'Re-engagement' section on Insights with four metrics: In re-engagement (active roles you've nudged, mid-process), Awaiting reply (inside the wait window), Reply rate (of re-engaged roles, how many replied vs were given up on), and Let go (a split of inactivations between Unreachable — never had a contact — and No Response — reached out, got ghosted).

releases.title: Re-engagement, drafted for you — AI writes the history-aware nudge, and the job page tracks the whole revival

items.label: The 'Re-engage' action (on Priorities and now on each job) opens an AI-drafted message that READS the full conversation history + interview rounds + the contact, so the nudge references real touchpoints — not a blank box. You edit it, then 'Log attempt N' records it as a re-engagement comm; Copy + Open-in-email help you actually send it.

Two distinct AI voices, both editable in Settings → AI Prompts: 'Re-engagement Follow-up (1st)' (a warm nudge) and 'Re-engagement Follow-up (2nd / final)' (a graceful last check-in after the first got no reply). Every draft is captured in AI Logs (Draft Re-engagement 1st/2nd) with cost.

New 'Re-engagement' card on the job detail page with a progress tracker: Attempt 1 ✓ (date) → wait window → Attempt 2 (due/sent) → Inactivate. It shows exactly where a stale role is in its revival and what's next.

The 2nd attempt is logged under a distinct 'Re-engagement (2nd)' interaction kind (editable in Settings → Interaction Kinds) so the two nudges are visually distinct in Communication. Your earlier follow-up to the Quantiphi HR contact is now counted as the first re-engagement attempt.

releases.title: Fit Re-score batches are now reviewable — approve or keep each score, nothing applied behind your back

items.label: When you run a Fit Re-score as a batch, the completed results now open right into the review table on Insights → Fit Re-score — old→new deltas per role, with the changed ones pre-selected. Apply only the scores you agree with, or Dismiss without changing anything. (Previously a batch re-score parked its scores out of sight and applied nothing.)

The Batches tab now shows 'ready to review' (not the misleading 'applied') for a fit batch until you've resolved it, and its link goes straight to 'Review & apply'. Running a fresh re-score supersedes any older pending batch so you only ever review the latest.

releases.title: Logs Phase J.3: smoother AI-call log at scale (row virtualization)

items.label: The AI-call log table now uses **CSS containment** so the browser skips laying out and painting rows scrolled out of view — keeping scrolling smooth even with a thousand-plus rows loaded. Visible rows render exactly as before, and the scrollbar stays accurate. (The dashboard Jobs table gets the same treatment in a follow-up.)

releases.title: Logs Phase J.2: lighter, faster AI-call logs (detail-on-demand)

items.label: The AI-call log loads **much lighter**: each row used to carry ~9KB of prompt/response text the table never shows (only the detail drawer does) — roughly **900KB per 100 rows** shipped for nothing. Rows now arrive **slim**, and the full prompt/instruction/response/JSON is fetched **only when you open a row** (with a brief “Loading…”). The table, sorting, filtering, costs, and totals are unchanged.

releases.title: Logs Phase J.1: live-call transcription cost now tracked

items.label: Your **live-call (real-time) interview transcription now shows up in the AI logs + cost dashboard**. It runs browser↔OpenAI over WebRTC, so the server never saw it before — now the recorder reports the session (duration × streams × per-minute rate) when you stop, and it lands as a **“Live Call Transcription”** entry linked to the role. Previously this spend was completely invisible.
The per-minute transcription rates now live in one place (the pricing table), so the recorder’s live “~$” estimate and the logged cost always agree.

releases.title: Question Bank hardening — batch builds now save, and duplicate anticipated questions stay independent

items.label: Building the Question Bank with 'Run as batch' now saves its result like the instant build does — previously the cheaper batch run completed but its themes were silently discarded, leaving the page empty.
Two anticipated questions with the same wording no longer share an identity, so editing, pinning, or deleting one can't affect the other.

releases.title: Question Bank is now a living prep sheet — edit answers, pin, fill gaps, add your own questions

items.label: Edit any answer inline and pin the questions that matter to the top of their theme. Your edits are kept even when you Rebuild — the AI refreshes the themes and best answers, but your curated answers carry forward.
Add your own anticipated questions to prep for upcoming interviews — they sit in their own section and survive a Rebuild.

When you edit an answer, you can optionally tick 'also update my {company} interview answer' to write it back to that debrief — off by default, and it only writes when there's a single unambiguous match, so your interview records are never changed by accident.

releases.title: Logs Phase I: end-to-end AI → activity → operations tracing

items.label: Open any AI call in the Logs drawer and see **what it triggered** end-to-end: the **activity events** it produced AND the **backend operations** (writes/pulls/calls) it ran — all linked automatically by the call id. One AI call now shows its full downstream footprint, not just a single updated record.

The link is **bidirectional**: each System-log operation that ran inside an AI request now carries a **“Triggered by → AI call”** backlink, so you can trace a write back to the exact AI call behind it.

releases.title: Smart stale-role triage — inactivate when there's no one to reach, or re-engage twice then let go

items.label: The Priorities → Stale applications list now gives each stale role the RIGHT action based on whether you can reach anyone: if the role has no contact with an email/phone/LinkedIn, a one-click 'Inactivate · no contact' (reason: Unreachable) — there's no way to follow up, so don't let it linger.

If a stale role DOES have a reachable contact, you get a 'Re-engage (attempt N/2)' button that logs a re-engagement message to the job. After your configured number of attempts (default 2) with no reply within the wait window (default 7 days), it turns into a one-click 'Inactivate · no response' (reason: No Response). While you're waiting it shows 'awaiting reply · N days left'. A reply (any inbound message) cancels the countdown.

New Settings → Thresholds controls: 'Re-engagement wait (days)' and 'Re-engagement attempts'. New inactive reason 'Unreachable' (distinct from 'No Response') so reports can tell apart 'never had a contact' from 'reached out and got ghosted'.

releases.title: Question Bank no longer goes blank — it persists, hydrates, and links back to roles

items.label: Insights → Question Bank used to lose your built bank the moment you navigated away or reloaded (it lived only in the browser). It now saves to your profile and the page loads it back on every visit, with the build time shown in your timezone.
Themes are now collapsible (with a per-theme gap count), and each question links back to the role(s) it was actually asked in — click the company chip to jump straight to that job.
When new interview questions have landed since the bank was built, the header flags how many and nudges a Rebuild so the bank never silently goes stale.

releases.title: Logs Phase H: the Logs home dashboard (Overview)

items.label: The Logs page now opens on a new **Overview** dashboard (bare `/logs`) — a snapshot across all three streams: **Activity** (events + this-week + top categories), **AI calls** (calls + lifetime spend + recent), and **System** (operations + a prominent error/warning count with recent failures). Each card jumps into its tab.

The Overview also shows a **recent-activity** preview and **cross-links to the main Dashboard and Insights**, so the Logs surface ties into the rest of the app. Activity is now the explicit **/logs?tab=activity** URL.

releases.title: Logs Phase G.2: ops-log completeness + a mute toggle

items.label: The System log now also captures: **email imports on leads** (not just jobs) as pull ops, **per-attachment fetch failures** as warnings (the import still succeeds), and **Gmail token refreshes** as call ops — flagged as a warning with a “reconnect Gmail” hint when the refresh token has been revoked.

A **Logging on/off toggle** on the System tab — pause recording operations if it ever feels noisy (existing ops stay; the setting persists). Best-effort and gated cheaply, so it never affects save performance.

releases.title: Logs Phase G: the System / Operations tab

items.label: New **System** tab on the Logs page — the technical audit trail behind your Activity: every persisted **write** (which function ran + what fields changed + duration), integration **pulls** (e.g. importing Gmail emails into a job), and **errors/warnings** — distinct from Activity (what happened) vs System (the backend operation that did it).

Each operation is a row you can **expand** to see the function, fields changed, entity, duration, metadata, and full error detail. Filter by op type (writes/pulls/calls/deletes/errors), severity, an **Errors-only** toggle, and date; full-text search across function/fields/errors.
A **mini-dashboard** at the top: total operations, error & warning counts, average write time, plus by-function and by-type breakdowns.

Under the hood: a new `op` log type + a fire-and-forget `recordOp()` wired into the core write seams (patchJob/patchLead/updateSettings/saveAttachment) and the email-import/search paths — best-effort, so logging can never slow down or break a save.

releases.title: Logs Phase F: Activity overview dashboard, brushable timeline & power filters

items.label: The Activity tab opens with a richer **Overview** mini-dashboard (replacing the simple “This week” digest): stat cards (events · this week · by you · by AI), a per-category and most-active-entity breakdown, and a **brushable timeline histogram**.

**Brushable timeline** — events-per-day stacked by category colour: click a day to filter to it, or **drag across days to select a date range**. The selected window shows as a removable chip and the stream updates instantly.

**“See all of X”** — click any category, or a most-active job/lead, in the Overview to filter the stream to it (shown as a clearable chip). Adds a specific-entity filter on top of the existing type/actor/category/date filters.
**Collapsible groups** — in the By type / By entity / By day views, each group can now be collapsed/expanded.

releases.title: Logs Phase E: rename, dedicated tab URLs, richer rows & loss-warning fix

items.label: The Logs page (sidebar + header) is now just **Logs**, not “AI Logs” — it covers all your activity, not only AI calls.
The **Activity tab now has a dedicated, shareable URL** (`/logs?tab=activity`), matching the AI-calls tab.
**Richer, denser Activity rows** — each event fills the width with its owning job/lead/role inline + a You/AI actor chip + the AI-call link + time, so more shows per screen with far less empty space.
**Collapsible filters** — hide the filter chips/dropdowns to focus on the stream; the event count and view modes stay visible.

**Resolved the AI-logs “possible loss” warning.** The 22 missing calls were dropped in a June restore and are unrecoverable (confirmed by making `repair:logs` **profile-aware** — it was silently reading the wrong, pre-Profiles path). The warning is now **acknowledgeable**: click × to dismiss it durably; it returns only if the count genuinely drops further.

releases.title: Activity Log Phase D: weekly digest, export & windowing

items.label: The Activity tab opens with a **“This week”** digest — a standup-style summary of the last 7 days’ activity, broken down by category with your most-active jobs/leads, collapsible at the top.
**Export** the activity stream (your current filtered view) to **CSV or JSON**, matching the AI-calls export.
The activity stream is now **windowed** — it ships the newest 1,500 events to keep the Logs page fast as history grows, and notes “newest N of M loaded” when there’s more.

releases.title: Activity Log Phase C: contacts & settings changes now in the stream

items.label: **Tag changes** (add/remove) on a job now appear in the Activity log — closing a gap where even bulk tag edits left no trace — and editing your **company aliases** records a distinct **Company** activity event.

The Activity log now captures changes that don’t live on a job/lead timeline. **Adding, editing, or removing a contact** — on a job or a lead — now appears in the Activity stream, badged **Contact** and linked back to the record.

**Settings changes** are recorded too (badged **Settings**) — and the entry names exactly which settings changed (diffed against their prior values, so a full-object save still only logs what really changed). The Activity tab becomes a real audit trail, not just job/lead events.

New **Contacts** and **Settings** filters in the Activity tab. Under the hood these durable events share the existing logs store (the AI-calls tab + windowing are unaffected — they filter to AI calls) via a generic append path + a centralized recordActivity() recorder.

releases.title: Fix: the AI calls tab on the Logs page wouldn’t open

items.label: Clicking the **AI calls** tab on the Logs page did nothing — it snapped back to Activity, making the AI call logs unreachable. The tab switcher was clearing the URL’s tab parameter for the non-default tab, which the page then re-read as “Activity”. Now the AI calls tab carries an explicit ?tab=ai-calls and opens correctly (the Activity-row → AI-call deep links still work).

releases.title: Fix: recruiter & lead outreach times were wrong on the timeline (timezone bug)

items.label: An outreach message could show the wrong time on a lead/job timeline — e.g. a recruiter note that arrived 9:20 PM yesterday displayed as the next afternoon. Two linked causes: the timeline event followed a message’s responseReceivedAt (which could drift from its true sentAt), and the date/time pickers converted using the runtime timezone, so a non-Eastern context stamped a 9:20 PM wall-clock as 21:20Z.

All datetime-local ↔ ISO conversions now go through one timezone-EXPLICIT America/Toronto helper (src/lib/utils/datetime-input.ts), so a message/event time is correct no matter where the code runs (browser, SSR, headless) — proven identical under multiple runtime timezones and DST-aware. Applied across the outreach review, message editor, parser, and the timeline editors + status backdate.
Inbound messages now keep responseReceivedAt locked to sentAt so the two can’t diverge and throw the seeded ‘recruiter reached out’ event off.
Repaired the existing affected records (Wealthsimple, Deloitte, Compunnel) so their timelines and the Activity tracker now show the true message times.

releases.title: Activity Log Phase B: two-way AI ↔ activity linking

items.label: OCR’d offer letters, offer-version comparisons, and first-time conversation summaries now appear in the Activity log as **AI update** events — each linking back to the exact AI call behind it.

AI-driven changes are now traceable both ways. When AI applies a change — a status/lifecycle update, an offer-letter gap-fill, or a watched-role enrichment — the resulting timeline event is stamped with the AI call behind it, so the Activity log shows an **AI call** link on the row and the AI Logs drawer shows a **What this updated** link back to the activity.
The Activity tab gained an **AI** actor filter (alongside You and System), so you can see exactly what the AI changed across your jobs, leads, and watch roles.

Under the hood: timeline events now carry an optional aiLogId (type + schema), threaded through patchJob / patchWatchRole, so any current or future AI route that persists a change can link it with a one-liner.

releases.title: Logs → Activity: a global, cross-entity activity stream

items.label: The Logs page is now a two-tab surface. A new **Activity** tab shows a global, cross-entity stream of everything that has happened across your jobs, leads, and watch roles — status changes, rounds, offers, and sent/received messages — alongside the existing **AI calls** tab.
Filter the activity stream by entity type (jobs / leads / watch roles), who did it (you vs system), category, and date range — plus full-text search across the event, role, and company.
Four view modes — Newest, By type, By entity, and By day — and every row deep-links back to the job, lead, or watch role it belongs to.
Watch-role activity is split out from its parent lead, so each pitched role’s events read on their own. Existing AI-call deep links still open the AI calls tab.

releases.title: Roadmap filters: area open-counts + a cleaner layout

items.label: The Roadmap Area filter now shows how many open items each area has (like the type chips), sorts by that count (default) or A–Z, and greys out areas with nothing open.

Reformatted the Roadmap filter bar into tidy rows — search + Show completed on the first line, then Type, Area, and Effort/Value each on their own line — so nothing wraps awkwardly onto its own line anymore.

releases.title: AI Coaching: practice with an AI mock interview, per round

items.label: New “Mock interview” on any interview round's focus page: the AI plays a realistic interviewer for that round type, asking one question at a time — grounded in the round's prep (your expected questions + answers), the JD tie-ins, and your background — and probing your answers. You reply by typing or by voice (the mic from dictation), and when you're ready you hit “End & get feedback” for a coaching debrief of your strengths and gaps. Multi-turn and conversational; copy-prompt fallback when no API key is set.

releases.title: Roadmap type counts + a corrected “Active” jobs stat

items.label: Roadmap: each type filter (New feature / Enhancement / Bug fix / Verify) now shows how many items of that type are still open, the chips sort by that count (default) or A–Z, and types with nothing open are greyed out so the active ones stand out.

Fixed the “Active” card on Job Opportunities: it was actually counting all non-archived jobs (so it read 95) and labeling that “Active”. It now shows the jobs you're genuinely still pursuing (activeState = Active), with a clear “N tracked · M inactive” sub.

releases.title: AI Coaching: “Why you're losing” — a pattern read across your inactive opportunities

items.label: New on Insights → Quality: “Why you're losing”. One click reads across every opportunity that went inactive — why it died, how far it got, the interview-outcome labels, fit, and a comms digest — and surfaces the RECURRING reasons (e.g. fading after round 2, comp above band, a role type that never converts), each with the evidence and one concrete change to make, plus a headline “biggest lever”. Grounded in your Goals + AI rules; copy-prompt fallback when no API key is set.

releases.title: Collapsible filters, tag counts, and a stats strip that gets out of your way

items.label: The Job Opportunities filter panel now has two collapse levels: collapse the whole thing down to just the search bar (“Hide filters”, with a badge showing how many filters are active), and collapse the Tags row on its own. By default filters are visible but the long tags list is collapsed — and your choices are remembered.
Each tag now shows how many jobs carry it, and you can sort the tags by count (default) or A–Z.
The stats strip (Active / Stale / Offers / …) above the filters now slides away as you scroll the table down, so you get more room for the list — and slides back when you scroll to the top.

releases.title: Opt-in auto-archive for long-inactive jobs

items.label: New Settings → Thresholds option: “Auto-archive inactive jobs after (days)”. Set it to a number of days and any job that's been Inactive with no activity for that long gets archived automatically on your next visit. It's off by default (0), never touches Active jobs or ones with an open offer, and is fully reversible — you get an Undo toast, and archived jobs stay searchable.

releases.title: Time-aware “upcoming”, a smart wind-down suggestion, and clickable dashboard stats

items.label: Fixed: a meeting earlier today no longer lingers as “upcoming” / “in 0 days” all afternoon. Everywhere that shows what's coming up (the dashboard agenda, the Activity column, Needs action) now understands the time of day — a timed event drops off once it has passed (with a 1-hour grace so an in-progress meeting still shows), and today's still-upcoming events read “today” instead of “in 0d”.

Smart wind-down: when you've sent a couple of follow-ups with no reply for about three weeks, “Needs action” stops nudging another follow-up and instead suggests considering the opportunity inactive. Follow-up nudges are also spaced out now — it won't nag you the day after you followed up.
The stat cards on Job Opportunities (Active, Stale, Offers) are now clickable — each jumps to that filtered view.

releases.title: “Needs action” on your dashboard — one cross-domain list of what to do next

items.label: A new “Needs action” card on the dashboard pulls together everything that wants your attention in one place: offers to respond to, interviews in the next two weeks, application deadlines (upcoming or already missed), stale threads to follow up on, and lead next-actions — sorted overdue → soon, each a one-click link to act.
Stale-job follow-up nudges now surface here too — each links straight into the latest thread with a follow-up draft started.
Foundation for what's coming: it's built on one reusable “what needs action” engine (computeNeedsAction) that future proactive surfaces — a daily digest, reminders — will all share.

releases.title: Leads “Update with AI” now updates the lead itself too — headline, status, next action, notes — alongside its watched roles, in one pass

items.label: The Leads “Update with AI” flow is now lead-aware: from the messages you select (+ attached JDs + scraped posting links + your steer), the AI proposes focused updates to the LEAD itself — headline, anchor person/company/role type, status (active / dormant / abandoned — never auto-converts), re-engagement trigger, next action + date, and notes — AND, in the same pass, to each of its active watched roles. You get a “Lead” section plus a section per role, accept any subset, and it saves them together.

Because it can now update the lead on its own, “Update with AI” is offered for any lead with logged messages (not just ones with a watched role). Leads with no conversation and no role aren’t offered (nothing to read). Promoted / dismissed / filled roles are skipped in the role pass.

New /api/ai/enrich-lead route + enrichLead provider method (Anthropic / OpenAI / copy-prompt) reusing the existing role-enrichment for the per-role updates, so the conservative “null = no change”, blocked-link paste fallback, and before→after per-section diff all carry over unchanged.

releases.title: AI résumé & cover-letter tailoring for watch roles + interview outcomes in “Update status with AI”

items.label: Watch roles now get the same AI tailoring jobs have: an “AI tailoring” card on the watch-role detail with “Tailor résumé with AI” and “Draft cover letter with AI”. It uses your Master Résumé + the role’s requirements/fit, saves the result on the role, and shows it inline — re-tailor any time.
Under the hood the tailor-résumé and cover-letter routes are now owner-generic (a job or a watch role) via one shared adapter, so both surfaces stay in lockstep.

“Update status with AI” (on a job) now also reads interview outcomes: say “the technical went great” or “they thought I was too senior” and it proposes adding/removing the matching Interview Results labels — shown as a +/− diff you review before it saves (it merges into your existing set rather than overwriting).

releases.title: Set a phone's Cell / Work type when editing any existing contact

items.label: The Cell / Work / no-type phone selector is now on the edit-contact dialog everywhere you manage contacts (the Contacts page and each job/lead's contact card), not just the Add-with-AI flow — so you can re-type an existing number. The dialog loads the contact's current type, so editing other fields preserves it. A 'Work = stays with the company; Cell/none follows the person' hint makes the behavior clear.

releases.title: Leads get “Update with AI” — re-enrich a watched role from selected messages (parity with Recruiter Outreach)

items.label: New “Update with AI” button on the Leads list (next to New lead): pick a lead, then check which messages on its conversation — the original outreach, your follow-ups, and their replies — the AI should read, plus the role’s attached JD and any links shared in those messages. It proposes focused updates to the lead’s watched role(s): end-client company, compensation, key responsibilities/requirements, fit & interest, status, and more. You review a before→after diff per section and apply only the parts you want. Same flow Recruiter Outreach already had, now on regular leads.
