The per-role “Update with AI” (✨) button now also appears on watched-role cards on a regular lead’s detail page (previously recruiter-engagement only) — for a one-off update, paste a new message / forwarded JD and re-enrich just that role. The dialog wording follows the context (“watched role” on leads, “pitched role” on engagements).
Only offered for leads that actually have a non-closed watched role, and the per-role button is hidden on promoted/dismissed roles — so the action only shows where it can do something.

releases.title: “Update status with AI” now works on watch roles, not just jobs

items.label: A watch role's Priority & Status card now has the same ✨ "Update status with AI" button jobs have: describe what changed in plain English ("recruiter discussed it with the hiring manager", "they submitted me", "pass on this one") and the AI proposes the matching watch-role status / priority / status-reason changes.

Review-first, same as jobs: you see a before→after diff of exactly what will change before anything saves, and every proposed value is validated against the real watch-role status options so the AI can't invent one. (Backdating is job-only, so it's hidden here.)
Under the hood the status-update dialog is now owner-generic (job or watch role), reusing one reviewed flow instead of a second copy.

releases.title: Editable Add-Contact AI prompt + cell/work phone types that know who they belong to

items.label: The 'Add contact with AI' prompt is now editable in Settings → AI Prompts (Listing group), gets its own per-prompt model picker, and shows as 'Parse Contact' in the AI Logs / cost dashboard. The extractor reads your override and falls back to the built-in default.

Phone numbers can now be typed Cell / Work / (no type). A WORK number is treated as employer-bound — it only syncs between a person's records at the SAME company and won't follow them if they change jobs. A Cell — or no type at all — stays attached to the person and syncs everywhere, like the rest of their identity. The Add-contact-with-AI flow infers the type when the text makes it obvious (Mobile/Cell vs Office/Direct) and lets you set it in the preview.

releases.title: Fit re-score now covers your watch roles, not just jobs

items.label: The AI "Re-score fit" now judges your active watch roles alongside active jobs — a lead's pitched/watched roles are scored against your current goals in the same ranked shortlist (watch roles that are archived, promoted, dismissed, or filled elsewhere are skipped).

Each row is tagged so you can tell jobs from watch roles at a glance, and a watch-role row links straight to that role under its lead. Applying an accepted score writes back to the right place — the watch role's fit, not a job's.

releases.title: Overall-notes Synthesize uses the transcript; notes labeled by name (Alex / Brent)

items.label: "Synthesize" (Overall notes & takeaways) now grounds itself in the loaded interview transcript when one is stored — treating the full conversation as the most complete source, on top of your live capture + recap. It also works off the transcript alone, so you can synthesize even before taking any notes.

Real-time notes and the Overall-notes "Live capture" roll-up now label speakers by name — your first name (e.g. "Alex:") instead of "Me:", and on a 1:1 call the other person's name (e.g. "Brent:") instead of "Them:". Purely a display label; the underlying me/them/note tagging is unchanged, and multi-party calls still show "Them".

releases.title: Add contact with AI — paste a message, pick the roles, and AI fills the contact for you

items.label: New '✨ Add with AI' button on the Contacts and People pages. Paste anything about a person (a message they sent, an email signature, a LinkedIn blurb, or rough notes), pick one or more records to assign them to (jobs, leads, recruiter engagements), and AI extracts the contact fields — name, title, email, phone, LinkedIn, relationship, contact type, represents-company, how-you-connected, notes — with inferred fields flagged amber for you to confirm. You edit or approve the preview before anything is saved.

Assigning to multiple records links them as ONE canonical person automatically (shared identity, future edits sync), reusing the People merge engine. And before creating, it checks whether the person already exists (same email/name) and offers to attach to them instead — so the AI add flow never re-introduces duplicates.

Powered by the shared per-prompt model + auto-logging infra (feature 'parse-contact'), with the no-API-key copy-prompt fallback. The job contacts endpoint now also carries howConnected / representsCompany / canonicalPersonId so nothing the AI extracts is dropped.

releases.title: Cleaner extracted transcript notes — no redundant "Alex said / Brent said" prefix

items.label: Transcript "Extract notes" now writes each note as the point itself rather than prefixing it with who spoke ("Alex said…", "Brent said…") — the speaker tag already carries that. Notes read cleaner and scan faster; references to other people are still kept in the text.

releases.title: Removed the redundant primaryContact field — a job's primary is now purely contacts[].isPrimary

items.label: Completed the primaryContact deprecation: the legacy `Job.primaryContact` field is gone from the type, schema, and every writer (the create form, AI parse, recruiter-outreach parse, lead→job promote, job merge, demo seed). A job's primary contact now lives solely in contacts[] with isPrimary, resolved everywhere through the single getPrimaryContact() helper. The Job create form now writes its contact straight into contacts[] as the primary instead of the old side field. No data migration needed — every existing primaryContact was already present in contacts[].

releases.title: Smarter transcript → notes: AI curates real-time notes (and names the other person)

items.label: "Extract notes" on a cleaned transcript now ANALYZES the conversation with AI and distills it into a curated set of real-time notes — the key points you raised, the key points they raised, and a few general observations — instead of dumping every diarized line as its own note. Filler ('Yeah', 'Okay'), backchannel, and smalltalk are dropped; fragmented turns are merged. A long call now yields ~10–25 meaningful notes, not 50+.
On a 1:1 call, the other person is now labeled by name instead of "Them" — both in the cleaned transcript diarization and in the extracted real-time notes.

Re-extracting replaces the previous transcript-extracted batch instead of piling on duplicates, while leaving any notes you took live or by hand untouched. Extracted notes are stamped at their real call time (from the transcript's timestamps) and flagged backfilled.

releases.title: Calendar polish: time-zone labels, one-click reschedule, and Mail.app invite/attachment parity

items.label: Time-zone clarity: interview/meeting times now show the zone (EDT/EST) on the round & meeting pages and the calendar day panel. An imported invite sent in another zone (e.g. 2 PM Pacific) adds a prep note so the local-time display isn't misread.
One-click Reschedule: a Reschedule button on each interview round + lead meeting page — pick a new time/duration; it logs the change on the timeline and the calendar + .ics update to match.
Mail.app parity: importing from Apple Mail now captures file attachments and detects .ics interview invites (via the calendar attachment), matching what the Gmail importer already did.
Lead meetings created from an emailed invite now log a “meeting scheduled” event on the engagement timeline (parity with manually-added meetings).

releases.title: People directory: duplicate suggestions + primary-contact resolution cleanup

items.label: The People directory now surfaces a 'likely duplicates' panel: it auto-detects DISTINCT people who are almost certainly the same human using only strong signals (identical email, identical LinkedIn, or a shared contact record), excluding anyone already linked. Each suggestion has 'Review & merge' (opens the merge review pre-filled) and 'Not a match' (durably dismissed so it never re-appears). People are never auto-merged — every merge is confirmed by hand.

Primary-contact resolution is now centralized in one getPrimaryContact() helper (isPrimary → first contact → legacy field) and every reader — cover-letter AI, follow-up AI, XLSX export, job→lead demotion, the Job form, and the lead→job promote — was switched onto it. No reader touches the legacy job.primaryContact field anymore; it resolves via contacts[].isPrimary everywhere. (The redundant field itself is kept one more release as a safety net, then removed.)

releases.title: Fix: AI-parsed message times were stored 5–8 hours off (timezone)

items.label: When “Add with AI” captured a recruiter message, the message’s timestamp was saved in UTC while the time shown was your local (Eastern) time — so a 2:35 PM message landed as 9:35 AM. Times are now read as your local time, so the captured “When” matches the message. Affects every Add-with-AI destination (Job, Lead, Recruiter Engagement) and is daylight-saving-aware.

releases.title: Merge & link people — collapse duplicate contacts into one canonical person from the People directory

items.label: Each person in the People directory now has a 'Merge with…' action: search for a duplicate (likely matches — same email/name — float to the top), then a review step reconciles their STABLE identity (name / phone / LinkedIn) with a one-tap toggle on any genuine conflict, while title / email / contact-type / represents-company stay on each record (they belong to the employer, not the person). Confirm and every record they appear in is unified under one canonicalPersonId.

'Link N records' one-click action on any unlinked person who already appears in 2+ records — gives their scattered records a shared canonical identity so future name/phone/LinkedIn edits sync everywhere, without folding in a separate person.
POST /api/people/merge gained a dry-run preview (drives the review UI) and a canonicalize path (absorbed-optional) for the self-link case.

releases.title: Calendar: double-booking alerts, configurable reminders, and file attachments on any message

items.label: Double-booking detection: overlapping interviews/meetings now get a Conflict badge on the selected-day panel, a red ring on the week time-grid, and a marker on the dashboard Upcoming agenda. Compared by real instant, so it's timezone-correct.

Configurable reminders: set your calendar reminder lead-times on the /calendar page - e.g. 1 hour before interviews & meetings, 2 days before deadlines (or off). Fed into the synced/exported .ics so Calendar.app alerts you on your schedule.

Attach files to any message: the message edit dialog now has an Attach file control (and remove), so attachments aren't limited to email-captured ones - stored with the message and downloadable from the conversation.

releases.title: People directory — every contact deduped into one person across jobs & leads (foundation for cross-record merge)

items.label: New People page (left nav): every distinct human across your jobs AND leads, deduped by canonicalPersonId (else name). Search by name/email/company; filter by contact type, linked/unlinked, and 'appears in 2+ records'; sort by name, # of records, or most recently contacted. Click a person to see every role and lead they touch, their per-record relationship/relevance, and a per-record message count.

Career-spanning person identity: a canonicalPersonId now follows a human across EMPLOYERS. Person fields are split into STABLE identity (name, phone, LinkedIn — synced across all of their records) vs AFFILIATION (title, email, contact type, represents-company — synced only between records at the SAME company, never overwriting a different employer's value). So someone who moves from one company to another keeps one identity without their old title clobbering the new one.

Cross-record person MERGE engine + API (POST /api/people/merge, with a dry-run preview): folds two people into one canonical person, reconciling stable identity and stamping a shared id across every record. Pure, unit-tested merge planner mirrors the job-merge engine. (The in-directory merge UI + duplicate suggestions land in the next installments.)
GET /api/people now returns the richer directory (companies, per-record relationship overlay, comms counts, last-contacted) — also upgrading the existing 'attach existing person' picker.

releases.title: Jobs List Power Tools — tag filtering & chips, multi-select bulk actions, and export

items.label: Tag filtering: the jobs filter bar has a new Tags row with the same include / exclude tri-state as the status chips (click once to require a tag, again to exclude it). Retired tags hide behind a "+ N archived" toggle but stay matchable, honoring the active / archived tag lifecycle. Your tag filters are URL-encoded, so Saved Views capture them too.
Tag chips on rows: each job row shows its first few tags as compact chips (with a +N overflow), and the expanded row lists the full set.

Multi-select: a checkbox column plus a header "select all" (which honors the active filter) on the jobs table. A bulk-action toolbar appears the moment you select a row, with a live count and one-click clear.

Bulk actions: set priority, mark active, mark inactive (with a reason), add or remove a tag, and archive — applied to every selected job at once. Each job still runs the normal status cascades and records a timeline event.
Bulk-archive Undo: archiving a batch shows an Undo toast that restores them in one click (archiving is reversible — it sets an archived date, it doesn't delete).
Export the selection: download exactly the jobs you've selected as CSV (flattened columns incl. tags) or JSON.

releases.title: Email invites become interviews on your calendar — plus message attachments, reminders, and a dashboard “Upcoming” agenda

items.label: Email → calendar: importing an email that carries an interview invite (.ics) now offers to turn it into an interview round (jobs) or meeting (leads) — pre-filled with the time, duration, attendees, video link, and notes. Detected on Gmail (full MIME) reliably; Mail.app best-effort.

No duplicate invites: a re-sent invite updates the same round/meeting and a cancellation cancels it, matched by the iCalendar UID (handles Google UTC + Outlook “Eastern Standard Time” zones, DST-correct).
Attachments on messages: imported emails now capture their file attachments — stored with the message and shown as downloadable chips in the conversation view.

Recruiter engagements parsed with a follow-up deadline now drop a dated “next action due” marker on the engagement timeline (the calendar already surfaced the date), so it shows where the conversation lives — not just in the header field.

Calendar reminders: your subscribed/exported calendar now alerts 30 minutes before interviews & meetings and 1 day before offer + application deadlines and start dates (VALARM), so it actually notifies you.
“Add to Calendar” on each interview round + meeting page — a one-click single-event .ics (with the reminder) for when you don’t subscribe to the whole feed.
New dashboard “Upcoming” card: a next-7-days agenda of interviews, meetings, and offer/application deadlines, each deep-linking to the record.

releases.title: Quick-Wins Sweep — AI-logs export/clear, contextual empty states, and dictation & viewer fixes

items.label: AI Call Logs: a new Export bar downloads the calls you're currently looking at (the active filter) as CSV or JSON — the CSV flattens the usage, cost, and entity fields into columns.

AI Call Logs: a guarded "Clear log" control empties the active log. It backs the current file up first and never touches your archived history or lifetime cost totals — it resets the live view, it doesn't destroy history (the confirm spells this out).

Contextual empty states: Leads, Communication, and Contacts now explain what the page is for and offer a first action on a fresh start, instead of rendering bare chrome. Leads and Communication also distinguish "nothing here yet" from "nothing matches your filters".

Recruiter parse review: the pitched-roles editor's ★ now follows the real primary role (not just whichever sits in the first row), and you can click any role's star to make it the primary — so the collapsed engagement row always features the role you starred.
Dictation: when the OpenAI voice engine has no API key, the mic now tells you up front (add a key, or switch to Web Speech) instead of recording your whole clip and only failing afterward.
Dictation: the live caption / error bubble can now sit below the mic, so it no longer clips off the top edge of a dialog.
Linked docs: a plain web-page link now embeds with an "Open in new tab" fallback (for sites that block embedding) instead of dumping the page's raw HTML source as text.

HANDOFF.md refreshed: dropped the stale version/job-count claims and added a "last reviewed" date plus a scope note pointing at the always-current sources (releases, roadmap, constants, profile data).

releases.title: Update status with AI — plain-English lifecycle changes on the Priority & Status card

items.label: New ✨ button on a job's Priority & Status card: describe what changed in plain English ("haven't heard back in months — mark inactive due to no response", "no longer interested", "they replied and scheduled a call — back to active, high priority") and the AI proposes the matching status changes.

Full-lifecycle scope: it can set active/inactive + reason and priority, and also flip application / interview / offer statuses (which live on other cards) — e.g. "they went with someone else" sets the offer status too. Every proposed value is validated against your live status options (custom statuses included), so it can't invent one.
Review-first: you see a before→after diff of exactly what will change before anything saves. Works in both directions (wind down or re-engage / advance).
Backdating: if you mention when it happened ("in 3 months", "since March"), the AI dates the change and you can adjust it — the timeline records it as having occurred then.
The prompt is tunable in Settings → AI Prompts → Card Editing (AI) → "Update Status (AI)", with its own per-prompt model + context controls.

releases.title: “Add with AI” now reads the job links inside a pasted recruiter message

items.label: When you paste a recruiter’s message into “Add with AI” (no posting URL), it now auto-detects job-posting links in the body, fetches their job descriptions, and folds them into what the AI reads — so the parsed role is grounded in the real JD, not just the email.
If one of those links can’t be fetched (LinkedIn/Workday-style block), you get a paste box for it right on the input screen — paste the text, or just Parse to skip it.

The review screen shows a “Read N of M links (X fetched, Y pasted) · skipped K” line so you can see what the AI actually pulled in. (Only runs for pasted text — a fetched JD isn’t re-scraped for its in-body links.)

releases.title: Greenhouse postings now bring the company name through to the AI

items.label: When you fetch a Greenhouse job posting (Add with AI, “Fetch JD from URL”, or recruiter-outreach enrich), the extracted text now includes a “Company:” line — derived from the board — so the AI reliably picks up the employer instead of guessing from the URL. Lever, Ashby, and Workday postings already carried this; Greenhouse now matches.

releases.title: Enrich now insists on the job posting (or lets you skip), and tells you which links it used

items.label: When “Update with AI” can’t fetch a posting URL or a link from your messages, you now have to paste each blocked link’s text before it’ll run — or click an explicit “Run without them” skip link. No more accidentally running the AI without the job description it was supposed to read.

The enrich result now shows a small “Used N of M links (X fetched, Y pasted) · skipped K” line whenever any link was involved — even on a clean run — so you can see at a glance what the AI actually read.

releases.title: Add-with-AI URL fetch: smarter extraction + review the listing before the AI runs

items.label: On the “Add with AI” page, the URL tab now has a “Fetch from URL” button that pulls the posting and drops the text into an editable box for you to review or correct BEFORE the AI runs — no more sending a blind URL server-side and hoping.

Much stronger extraction under the hood: it now reads structured JobPosting data (JSON-LD) and pulls straight from the LinkedIn, Greenhouse, and Lever job APIs, with a readable-content fallback — so the title, company, location, comp, and full description come through far more often than the old plain-text grab. The same engine also powers the job-detail “Fetch JD from URL” and recruiter-outreach enrich flows.

If a site blocks the fetch (403 / login wall / JavaScript-only pages like LinkedIn, Workday, Indeed) or only a thin read comes back, the page switches to a paste box with a banner asking you to paste the listing — or add the role title, company, location, comp, and key requirements — with the link kept, before the AI runs.

releases.title: Blocked job posting? Paste it in — the app asks before the AI runs

items.label: When a posting URL can’t be fetched automatically (403, login wall, or a JavaScript-only page like LinkedIn / Workday), the “🔗 Fetch from URL” dialog now gives you a paste box right there — paste the posting text and it still saves as the job description, instead of just showing an error.

The recruiter-outreach “Update with AI” / enrich flow now pauses before the AI runs if it couldn’t fetch the role’s posting URL or a link shared in your selected messages: it lists each blocked link with a paste box so you can supply the content for a better result. Fill what you can, leave a box blank to skip that link, then continue.
Links that DID fetch successfully are reused as-is across the pause — no duplicate fetching, and a posting that loaded a moment earlier can never silently drop out of the AI’s context.

releases.title: Fit Analysis generation: app's third-person voice + grounded in the role's comms

items.label: Generating Fit Analysis from a JD now writes in the app's structured, third-person “fit memo” voice — refers to you by name, leads with the verdict, names real projects/comp/location facts — instead of the possessive first-person “I/my…” it used before. This matches how parse and cowork sessions already fill the section.

Fit Analysis generation now also reads the role's communications + contacts (recruiter/hiring-team messages, who referred it, what was confirmed, comp signals discussed), so it can ground the assessment in real pipeline intel — not the job description alone. Requirements & Responsibilities stays JD-only by design.
Applies to both job Fit Analysis and watch-role Fit Analysis (including pitched roles under recruiter-engagement leads, which pull the lead's recruiter conversation).
The Wand2 “polish” on a Fit Analysis card no longer pushes the wording back to first person.

releases.title: Fetch a job description from its posting URL + AI auto-reads jobUrl & message links

items.label: New “🔗 Fetch from URL” button on the Job Description attachment card (for both jobs and pitched roles). It scrapes the posting (prefilled from the record’s posting URL), shows you the extracted text, and loads it into the markdown editor so you save it as the record’s job-description.md — after which every AI flow (Generate-from-JD, enrich/Update, tailoring, cover letter) uses it.

The recruiter-outreach “Update with AI” / enrich flow now automatically (best-effort) reads the role’s posting URL and any links shared in the selected messages, folding that text into the AI’s context alongside the conversation + attached JD.

Scraping is server-side and shared across the app (the parse-with-AI URL tab uses it too): a spoofed browser user-agent + a host-aware referer (helps with some boards’ blocks), with http(s)-only + private-address guards. Boards that block automated fetches (LinkedIn, Workday) are skipped gracefully — paste remains the fallback.

releases.title: Cheaper AI: batch mode (~50% off) for the heavy analytical features

items.label: New batch mode: the weekly digest, fit re-score, interview question bank, and offer decision matrix can each be run as an OpenAI batch (~50% cheaper) when you don't need the answer immediately. Tick “Run as batch” on the feature, or set a global default in Settings → AI Provider. Results land in minutes–24h.

New Insights → Batches tab lists your submitted batches and their status, applies completed ones (also auto-applied when you open the app), and shows each result. A “Check now” button polls on demand.
Batched calls are logged at the 0.5× rate, so the AI cost dashboard reflects the savings. Prompts are shared with the live path (no drift), and results are re-validated before they’re applied.

releases.title: AI now reads PDF job descriptions everywhere (not just markdown)

items.label: When a saved job description is a PDF (not a markdown sidecar), its text is now extracted and used everywhere a JD is read: the “Generate from JD” card dialog now prefills from PDF JDs (previously blank), and the recruiter-outreach “Update with AI” / enrich flow folds the PDF JD into its context. Centralized in one helper (readJdText), so jobs and pitched roles both benefit. Scanned / image-only PDFs still fall back to paste.

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach: Update with AI — select messages from a chain to re-enrich a pitched role

items.label: New “✨ Update with AI” button on the Recruiter Outreach page: pick an engagement, then check exactly which messages on its chain (the initial outreach + your follow-ups + their replies) the AI should read, preview the proposed changes per section, and apply. Re-runnable as more replies come in.

The AI now also reads the JD you attached to the pitched role (markdown or PDF text) when updating it — so it can fill in responsibilities, requirements, comp, and re-score fit/interest from the real posting, not just the messages.

The Communication-chain “Update pitched role from this conversation” button got the same message picker — curate which messages count instead of feeding the whole thread (all pre-selected by default).

releases.title: Sync terms from recap — pull verbally-agreed comp into the offer fields without waiting for a new letter

items.label: New "✨ Sync terms" button on the Offer card: it reads your decision notes + the revision asks you've marked "Agreed" + your Q&A (and any recap you paste) and proposes the current AGREED comp terms — base, bonus, sign-on, equity, currency, start date, deadline.

Closes the gap where the fields kept showing the original written offer while the real numbers lived in your notes: now you can bring base/equity/start up to the verbally-agreed terms before the revised letter arrives — every change is shown old → new for you to review and uncheck before it's applied.
Per-prompt configurable like the other AI features (model + prompt, OpenAI or Anthropic) under Settings → AI Prompts → "Offer: Sync Terms from Recap".

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach: Add with AI — paste a recruiter message and it builds the engagement

items.label: New “✨ Add with AI” button on the Recruiter Outreach page (toolbar + empty state). It opens the same Add-with-AI parse flow as Jobs, but pre-scoped to Recruiter Engagement — paste a recruiter’s message or whole thread (or describe the situation) and the AI builds the engagement + pitched roles + the sender contact + the captured conversation, landing it back on Recruiter Outreach. The mode is locked to Recruiter Engagement (with a “Change” escape hatch), and you can still re-route to a Job/Lead on the review screen if a paste turns out to be something else.
The Add-with-AI page now accepts ?mode= and ?lock= deep-link params to preset (and optionally lock) the destination, so other surfaces can launch a pre-scoped parse.

releases.title: Accept a signed offer — upload the version you signed, auto-update statuses + sync final terms

items.label: New "✓ Accept offer" action on the Offer card: pick the version you signed, set the acceptance date, and optionally attach the signed copy (PDF/Word/photo). It files the signed copy under that offer version and stamps a ✓ Signed badge in Attachments.
Accepting cascades the statuses for you — Offer Status → Offer Accepted, Offer Progress → Offer signed (new value), Decision → Accepted — and logs an "Offer accepted" event on the timeline.

Optional "sync final terms" step reads the accepted version's letter and proposes base/equity/start updates for you to review before anything is overwritten — closing the gap where the grid kept showing the original terms.
An "✓ Accepted — {version} on {date}" banner shows on the offer, with a Rescind action that clears the marker (status changes stay; adjust manually if un-accepting).

releases.title: Cheaper AI: prompt caching (Anthropic cache breakpoints + visible savings)

items.label: AI calls now mark the static system prompt as an Anthropic prompt-cache breakpoint, so repeated Claude calls bill the cached portion at ~10% of input (OpenAI already caches automatically). Cheaper AI when using Claude; a no-op for OpenAI.

The AI cost dashboard now shows a “Cached” stat — how many input tokens were served from the prompt cache and the dollars it saved — so the caching benefit is visible. It's already active on your OpenAI calls (recomputed across all logged history).

releases.title: Much deeper "Draft prep with AI" — every section, grounded in your real context

items.label: "Draft prep" now fills the WHOLE prep board, not just the three question lists. It also writes a Call objective, Leverage points, Watch-outs, Sensitive disclosures, Contingencies, and Prior context — the same sections you can fill by hand — populating the situational ones only when the round actually warrants them.

Prep is now grounded by default: a plain "Draft prep" automatically builds on the previous round/meeting's recorded outcome + debrief when one exists (no longer only behind the "Draft from last round" button), and on THIS job's real compensation & offer state — the posted band, the live offer terms (base/bonus/equity/sign-on/benefits), the asks on the table, and your company-specific offer prefs — so comp talk anchors on real numbers instead of generic résumé defaults.

Comp, Offer-details, and Job-offer rounds now get explicit negotiation scaffolding: concrete leverage anchors, if-then contingencies (asked-your-number-first, lowball), and watch-outs — grounded in your offer-preference floor and the live offer.
Lead meetings get the same depth: meeting kinds (e.g. a comp-discussion or pre-screen meeting) now resolve to the matching round-type prep guidance instead of falling back to generic.

Re-drafting is safe: AI sections merge append-only and never overwrite anything you've written (your call-objective/prior-context/notes always win), with light de-duplication so repeated drafts don't pile up near-identical items. Also fixed a latent issue where the Smart-Add "also draft prep now" step saved prep items without stable ids.

releases.title: Fix: in-field dictation mic floated to the top-left corner

items.label: Fixed the in-field dictation mic (Company Brief, offer recap, debrief transcript, audit context, round notes, résumé keywords) drifting to the top-left corner instead of sitting in the field. Its absolute position was resolving against the button's own wrapper rather than the text field; it now anchors to the field — bottom-right for textareas, right-centered for the single-line input.

releases.title: Offer & negotiation pack: decision matrix, comp benchmarking, negotiation coach

items.label: New Insights → Offers: an Offer Decision Matrix that compares every job with an offer in hand (Offered Position / Negotiating Offer / Awaiting Decision) on comp, role, work model, and fit to your goals — with a reasoned recommendation + per-offer pros/cons.
Comp benchmarking: web-searches current market pay for a role's level/location/work-model and tells you whether the offer is above / at / below market, with cited sources.
Negotiation coach: turns an offer into a prioritized ask list with target numbers + a ready-to-send counter-offer draft, using the market benchmark and any competing offers as leverage.

releases.title: Admin dashboard: pipeline composition (tracked-but-not-applied profiles)

items.label: New 'Pipeline composition' chart on the admin dashboard — a stacked bar per profile showing every tracked role by lifecycle stage (Lead → Found → Applied → Interviewing → Offer → Accepted). Profiles that track roles but haven't applied yet now surface meaningfully (their roles show as 'Found') instead of an all-zero applied funnel.

releases.title: Admin dashboard: charts + pipeline metrics

items.label: The admin cross-profile dashboard now has charts (recharts, matching /insights): a per-profile comparison bar (jobs / active / interviewed / offers), an aggregate pipeline funnel (Applied → Responded → Interviewed → Offer across all profiles), and a weekly applications & responses trend.
More data: pipeline rates (response / interview / offer, % of applied) on the rollup and on each profile card, plus interviewed counts — all using the same definitions as the Insights page.

releases.title: Global settings: tabbed (no more one long scroll)

items.label: The landing Global settings page is now split into tabs — AI, Statuses & types, Interaction kinds, Thresholds, Prompts, Companies — instead of one long scrollable page.

releases.title: Landing global settings + admin dashboard + Touch ID hotkey

items.label: New 'Global settings' on the profile landing page (no need to enter a profile): edit every cross-profile setting — AI provider/keys + models, statuses & round/meeting types, interaction kinds, thresholds & automation, the prompt-access matrix + per-prompt models, and company aliases. Admin-gated when an admin passphrase is set; open otherwise. (Per-profile settings like career context, résumé, and mail still live inside each profile.)

New Admin dashboard (shown in admin view): cross-profile metric tiles per profile — jobs, active, upcoming interviews, offers, leads, last activity, setup % — plus an all-profiles rollup. Profiles you've marked 'admin can't bypass' are hidden (no metrics), respecting the lock.
Touch ID hotkey on the landing: press ⌘/Ctrl+Enter to fire admin Touch ID without the mouse (and pressing Enter with an empty passphrase in the admin dialog does the same).

releases.title: Smarter date inference — "Add with AI" now reads a meeting's date from the message it was asked in

items.label: When a message proposes a time but no explicit date (e.g. a recruiter at 12:40pm asking for "a quick call after 3:30pm"), the AI round/meeting drafter now infers the date from when that message was sent — same day if the asked time is later, the next day if earlier — instead of leaving the date blank. It only does this in "Fill-in" mode and always flags the date for you to confirm; "Conservative" still requires an explicit date.
Each selected message is now shown to the AI with its full sent timestamp (weekday + date + time, ET), so it resolves "Thursday 3pm", "tomorrow", and time-only asks more reliably.

releases.title: Interview question bank — every question you've been asked, themed

items.label: New Insights → Question Bank: mines every question you were actually asked across past interview debriefs, clusters them into themes (behavioral, system design, domain, comp, …), shows how often each was asked + which companies asked, and surfaces your best recorded answer per question.
Flags the gaps — questions you've been asked but never recorded a strong answer for — so you know exactly what to prepare next.

releases.title: Polish: lead link picker wording + cleaner meeting chip labels

items.label: The lead message link picker now reads "+ link to a meeting…" (was the job-area wording), and meeting chips/labels no longer say "Meeting · Meeting" — they show the kind + date cleanly (e.g. "Meeting · Intro call · 2026-06-30").

releases.title: Fix: AI Add-round/meeting dialog cut-off from the Communication page; + manually link a lead message to a meeting

items.label: Fixed the "Add with AI" round/meeting dialog being cut off on the right when opened from the Communication page — a long message preview in the picker was forcing the dialog wider than itself. Previews now clamp to one line, and the dialog stays within the screen.

You can now manually link a lead's message to one of its meetings — open the message editor (pencil) on a lead thread and pick the meeting under "Link to a meeting." (Job messages already had this for rounds/offer/etc.)

releases.title: Pipeline-wide fit re-score → ranked shortlist

items.label: New Insights → Fit Re-score: re-judges every active job's fit against your CURRENT goals/career context (fit is otherwise set once at parse and never revisited), and returns a ranked shortlist with an old→new delta + a one-line rationale per role.

Review-first: nothing is written until you tick the rows you agree with and Apply — which updates each job's fit score. Runs through your configured AI model with a copy-prompt fallback, and is logged to the AI cost dashboard.

releases.title: Fix: Company Brief web sources now persist

items.label: Fixed a bug where the web-search Company Brief's cited source links were silently dropped on save (the sources field was missing from the persistence schema), so a freshly generated brief showed sources momentarily but lost them after reload. Sources now persist and display — for both jobs and watch-role briefs.

releases.title: Smart Add Meeting — the ✨ AI round-drafter now works for lead meetings too (+ multi-attendee meetings)

items.label: Lead meetings now have the same "Add with AI" flow as interview rounds: describe the meeting and/or pick lead messages, and the AI drafts it (date/time in ET, attendees, kind, duration, method + link) for you to review and save — with the same Fill-in / Conservative modes and an optional "also draft prep now".

And from the Communication page: an "add meeting from this message" action on any lead message opens the same dialog pre-seeded with that message — and links the message to the new meeting (the message shows a chip that jumps to it; the meeting lists the message).
Meetings can now record a full attendee list (not just the single "with" contact), matching interview rounds — and it carries over losslessly when a lead meeting is promoted into a job round.
Attendees on both rounds and meetings now link to your saved contacts when names match (carrying contact ids), so meeting/round people connect to your contact records.

releases.title: Touch ID — unlock a profile (or admin view) with your fingerprint

items.label: Add Touch ID to a locked profile (Settings → Profiles → Manage lock → Add Touch ID), then unlock it with your fingerprint on the switch screen — no password typing. Touch ID is always an ADDITIONAL factor: every profile keeps its password as a fallback, so a browser/OS reset or a different browser can never lock you out.
Admin view can also be entered with Touch ID — register one in the Admin passphrase card; the passphrase stays as the fallback + recovery path.

Built on WebAuthn/passkeys (platform authenticator) over localhost. Credentials are device + browser specific (a Touch ID added in Safari won't appear in Chrome). Verified by an adversarial security review: enrolling a Touch ID requires the target's own password (not an admin bypass), challenges are single-use + short-lived, and the lock files are written atomically.

releases.title: Company Brief for recruiter-pitched roles (watch roles)

items.label: Watch roles (the end clients a recruiter pitches you) now have the full Company Brief — the same structured snapshot / signals / culture / why-it-fits / questions / watch-outs, including the opt-in web search with cited sources. It sits on the role detail between Fit and Requirements.
Briefs are keyed by company, so a watch role and any job at the same end-client share one brief — generate once, reuse everywhere.

releases.title: Interview-round participants now link to your saved contacts

items.label: When you add or edit an interview round, each participant whose name matches one of the job's contacts is now linked to that contact (carrying its id) — so round attendees connect to your contact records and cross-record contact features instead of being loose text. Names that don't match stay as free text; no new contacts are created.
Fixed: editing a round previously stripped the contact link from its participants (they round-trip through a text field) — the link is now re-resolved on every save.

releases.title: Profile locks + admin view — password-protect a profile

items.label: Lock any profile with a password (Settings → Profiles → Profile locks). A locked profile shows an unlock prompt on the switch screen; the lock is enforced server-side — every page AND API request for a locked profile is gated until you unlock.

Admin view: set one admin passphrase, then on the switch screen 'Enter admin view' to open every profile whose lock allows admin bypass — without each password. Per-lock 'admin can bypass' toggle decides which profiles admin can enter. Also the recovery path if you forget a profile's password.

Unlock sessions are an httpOnly, signed cookie (14-day) per device; 'Lock now' re-locks everything. Honest scope: this gates the app's screens + API, not at-rest file encryption — the JSON data stays readable on disk to anyone with filesystem access.

releases.title: Seed a profile from a résumé — upload a PDF or image

items.label: Onboarding → upload a résumé (PDF or image) to fill a profile's career context, context blocks, and identity in one pass — it extracts the text (or runs vision OCR on a scan/screenshot) and maps it into the fields for review before saving.
Same résumé upload built into the New-profile wizard: the extracted text drops into "About this person" so the AI drafts the new profile straight from a CV.
Text-layer PDFs are read with zero AI cost; only scanned/image résumés use the (logged) vision OCR. No API key → it asks you to paste the résumé text instead.

releases.title: Company Brief can search the web (opt-in, with cited sources)

items.label: Company Brief has a new “Search the web” toggle. When ticked, it runs a live web-research pass (using your existing OpenAI/Anthropic key — no new setup) to gather current facts: what the company does, size/stage, funding/ownership, recent news, work model (RTO), and Glassdoor-type sentiment — then grounds the brief on what it found and lists the source links. Off by default.
The web research is steered by your editable Company Research rules, so it prioritizes what you care about. Sources are shown under the brief and included when you copy it.
Both the research call and the brief are logged to the AI cost dashboard. If the selected model can’t search, it falls back cleanly to the JD + anything you pasted.

releases.title: Dictation mic polish: corner mic for large fields, a11y, Safari/Firefox fallback

items.label: In large text fields (company brief, offer recap, debrief transcript, audit context, round notes, describe-a-round), the dictation mic now sits in the bottom-right corner and lights up red while recording — out of the way of the text.
Fixed the one field (Add Round with AI) whose mic still showed the old nested box, and added right-padding so typed text never runs under the mic.
Accessibility: the mic now has a real accessible name (screen readers announced a generic button before), a clearer keyboard focus ring, and a hover background so the in-field mic reads as clickable.
The mic no longer vanishes on Safari/Firefox when the dictation engine is set to Web Speech — it falls back to the OpenAI engine instead of disappearing.
Dictation error messages now auto-clear after a few seconds instead of sticking in the floating bubble.

releases.title: Profile landing page shows setup completeness + a Manage link; new data-isolation guardrail

items.label: The profile landing page (Switch profile…) now shows each profile's setup completeness ('X% set up') alongside last-used, plus a 'Manage profiles →' link to the full Settings → Profiles page.

New Settings → Data → 'Profile data isolation' check: a deterministic, no-AI guardrail that scans every profile's AI context (career / context blocks / identity) for another profile's name or sign-off, and confirms shared settings hold no per-person data — with a pass/fail report pinpointing any leak. Codifies the earlier privacy hardening so it can't silently regress.

releases.title: Add an interview round straight from a message — ✨ on the Communication page

items.label: Every message on a job's Communication thread now has an "add interview round" action next to Edit: it opens the same Smart Add Round dialog with that message already selected as context, so you can turn "they want to chat Thursday at 2" into a drafted round without leaving the conversation. (Job threads only.)
The round you create is linked back to the source message — the message shows a chip that jumps to the round, and the round lists the message under its linked communications.

releases.title: Résumé tailoring Phase 2 — regenerate one section + pin must-keep bullets

items.label: On a tailored résumé you can now Regenerate just one section — the summary, a single role's bullets, or the skills — keeping everything else. Each regenerate replaces that section in place with an Undo, so you can iterate section-by-section instead of re-tailoring the whole résumé.
Pin must-keep bullets: click the pin on any experience bullet and it is preserved verbatim whenever you regenerate that role. Pinned bullets show a filled pin and survive regeneration.
The controls are inline on the rendered résumé (both the Classic and Serif layouts) — Regenerate next to each section heading, a pin toggle on every bullet.

releases.title: ✨ Add a round with AI — describe it + pick messages, and it drafts the round (date, who, type, link) for you to review

items.label: New "Add with AI" button beside "+ Add Round": write a sentence about the round and/or tick the messages that mention it, and the AI fills in the scheduled date/time (resolved in Eastern Time), who you're meeting (matched to your contacts), the round type, duration, and the meeting method + video link — then pre-fills the normal Add Round form for you to review and Save. Nothing is saved until you confirm.

Two modes, switchable per-run and as a default in Settings: "Fill-in" best-guesses as much as it can and flags the uncertain fields; "Conservative" only fills what's clearly stated. Low-confidence fields get an amber highlight in the review form with a 'double-check these' note.
Optional "also draft the prep now": creates the round AND drafts its round-type-aware prep in one step, so it's ready to open.
After it's created, jump straight into the new round or go back to the job scrolled to it.

releases.title: Live interview copilot: reliability hardening (adversarial-review fixes)

items.label: Fixed a class of teardown races: stopping a call or leaving the page mid-connection no longer leaks a timer, an orphaned (billed) OpenAI Realtime session, or a duplicate session from a double-click — each capture attempt now carries a generation token and bails cleanly if it is superseded.

If the realtime connection fails, the recorder no longer shows a fake “recording” state (mic + tab capture live, cost ticking, nothing transcribing) — it now only enters recording once a stream actually connects, otherwise it surfaces the error and stops.
Editing or deleting a note while transcription is streaming in no longer drops a just-arrived live line (the edit/remove paths now read the live notes array, matching the append path).

Pressing Stop no longer flashes a spurious connection error: in-flight token/handshake requests are now aborted on stop and late rejections stay silent; a real connect failure now keeps the per-stream error indicator visible.
Live-call auto-surface no longer spends a paid AI call on idle stretches (skips when no new notes), and a late suggestion from a finished call can no longer bleed into the next call.
Free-mic (Web Speech) recognition no longer busy-loops re-acquiring the mic on a persistent fault; single-mic mode no longer opens a second audio meter on the same stream.

releases.title: Sharper résumé tailoring — stronger grounding/JD-coverage prompt, now editable

items.label: Rewrote the résumé-tailoring AI prompt for quality: it now treats the JD requirements as a coverage checklist, enforces bullet quality (strong verb + concrete result + honest ATS keywords, one idea each), PRESERVES quantified metrics (%, $, scale, timelines) exactly, orders experience relevance-led (most JD-relevant role first) with strongest bullets first, curates + relabels skill groups to the JD, and writes sharper role-targeted summaries. Improves every new tailored résumé.

The résumé-tailoring prompt is now editable in Settings → AI Prompts → "Tailor Résumé (2-column)" — so you can hand-tune the grounding/steering yourself. (Previously the editable prompt there was the old flat one and did not affect the 2-column output.) The per-prompt model picker in that same spot already lets you bump the tailoring model/tier.

releases.title: Live interview copilot: one-tap “Draft debrief” jump after a call

items.label: The post-call nudge now has a “Draft debrief →” button that jumps you straight to the Debrief section, whose “Draft from transcript” already reads this call automatically (live notes + the stored transcript) — so a debrief is one tap away from finishing a call.
Renamed the live-notes panel’s collapsed transcript to “Live transcript” to distinguish it from the dedicated post-call Transcript section.

releases.title: Résumé layouts: tailor into a serif 1-/2-page style, picked per profile

items.label: Tailored & imported résumés can now render in a new "Serif Sidebar" layout (blush header, serif display name with a target-company tagline, script "Profile", and a Contact / Education / Skills / Professional-Development sidebar) in a 1-page or 2-page variant — alongside the original Classic Two-Column. Same résumé data, three visual styles.

Each profile sets its default résumé layout in Settings → Context → Master Résumé ("Résumé Layout"). New tailors/imports use it; pick a 1-page layout and the AI also writes tighter so it actually fits one page.
A live "Layout" dropdown on each job's Résumé page restyles any single version instantly (it's the same data, just re-rendered) and remembers the choice per version.
"Copy Canva fields" adapts to the layout — the serif style emits its own fields (tagline, split contact, flat skills, professional development) for the matching Canva brand template.

releases.title: Smarter interview prep — tailored by round type, grounded in your comp prefs + recent messages with the interviewer

items.label: "Draft prep" now tailors to the ROUND: an early recruiter / pre-screen comes back high-level (logistics, why you're looking, a comp range, a few headline examples) instead of a deep technical grilling; technical / panel rounds go deep; comp / offer rounds lean on your Offer Preferences. It uses the round's type AND number (a recruiter at round 1 = pre-screen; several rounds in = a follow-up).

Prep is now grounded in recent messages with the people interviewing you — if a recruiter emailed about what the call will cover, the prep reflects it. (Matched from the round's participants; newest few, with timestamps.)
Prep can now surface a real compensation range: the draft-prep AI reads your Offer Preferences (floor numbers, base↔equity balance) so an early screen isn't guessing your number.

New Settings → Custom Statuses → "Interview Prep Rules": editable guidance per round type (each ships with a sensible built-in default shown as the placeholder). Leave a box blank to use the default; customize the ones you want to steer.

releases.title: Live interview copilot 2c: collapsed transcript, single-mic fallback, native-app docs, post-call debrief nudge

items.label: A collapsed, read-only Transcript view in the live-notes panel — expand it to scan or search the full diarized conversation for something specific that was said (built from the captured notes).
Single-mic fallback for calls that aren’t in a browser tab (native Zoom/Teams): record your mic only and tap a You/Them toggle to label the current speaker as you go.
An expandable hint explains how to capture native-app call audio properly (join in-browser, or a free BlackHole loopback device).
After you stop recording, a nudge confirms the call was captured and points you to draft a structured debrief from those notes (the debrief AI already reads them).

releases.title: Live interview copilot 2b polish: no repeat ideas, smarter question detection, auto counter

items.label: Auto-surfaced ideas no longer repeat — each call dedupes, so every cycle only adds genuinely new suggestions (and ones you tap to keep won’t come back). A manual “Surface ideas” press still gives a fresh slate.
Smarter question detection: auto-surface now also fires on real interviewer prompts like “tell me about…”, “walk me through…”, “why did you…”, not only lines ending in “?”.
A small counter shows how many times it auto-surfaced this call (next to the Auto control).

releases.title: Live interview copilot 2b: smart auto-surface ideas (opt-in, configurable cadence)

items.label: While recording a live call, you can now turn on Auto-surface: the copilot re-runs Surface Ideas on the rolling diarized notes every N seconds AND the moment the interviewer ends a line with a question mark — so fresh, role-tailored ideas appear as the conversation moves, hands-free.

It is OFF by default each call (opt-in with one tap on the live panel) and the cadence is adjustable inline mid-call. It is debounced (skips when a call is already in flight, when there are no notes yet, and within a minimum gap) so it never spams the AI.
New setting (Settings → AI Provider → “Live-call auto-surface every N sec”, default 25, 0 = off) sets your persisted cadence default.

releases.title: Live interview copilot: cost estimate + a “free mic” hybrid that halves the OpenAI cost

items.label: The recorder now shows a running cost estimate next to the elapsed timer (e.g. “● 02:15 · ~$0.02”) so you can see roughly what a call is costing as it runs.

New “Free mic” option: transcribe YOUR side with the free browser engine and spend OpenAI only on the interviewer — roughly half the cost. Your side shows a “free” tag while recording. (Your mic audio goes to Google in this mode; off by default.)

releases.title: AI résumé tailoring now builds a polished 2-column résumé (and "From upload" is fixed)

items.label: "New tailored version" now generates a structured 2-column résumé in the SAME layout as your templates — built from the matching template (Senior IC / Leadership / Balanced) when one is set, otherwise from your Master Résumé. Real employers, dates, education, and certifications are preserved exactly; the summary, experience bullets, and skills are tailored to the role. It renders + edits + exports (Canva-ready) just like an imported résumé, replacing the old flat summary/skills/bullets editor (existing flat versions still open).

Fixed "From upload" throwing "no such file or directory … resume.pdf". It now reads the résumé actually assigned to the job — including résumés inherited from another record — instead of looking only for a file named resume.pdf in the job's own folder.

When no résumé is attached, the button becomes "Upload a PDF…" and opens a native Finder picker (defaulting to your Job Search folder). The PDF you pick is attached to the job and structured automatically.
The job-detail "Tailored Resume" card now reflects the new 2-column versions (roles + skill-group counts) instead of going blank after a generate.

releases.title: Transcript notes land at their real times, and the transcript cleaner's prompts are now editable in Settings

items.label: When a transcript has [mm:ss] timestamps, the cleaner now keeps them and 'Extract notes' stamps each note at its REAL time (call start + offset) instead of all at 'now' — so the extracted notes read in order on the timeline. No timestamps → notes are stamped sequentially as before.

The transcript cleaner + its lossless audit are now editable in Settings → AI Prompts ('Interview: Clean Transcript' / '… (audit)'), alongside the other interview prompts, with per-prompt model selection.

releases.title: Live interview copilot (beta): hardened with a connection test, audio meters, and key-gating

items.label: Test mic — a 10-second dry run that confirms the OpenAI Realtime connection works (and your words come back) before you rely on it in a real call.
Live audio level meters next to “You” and “Them” while recording, so you can SEE that both sides are actually being captured — the quickest way to catch a forgotten “Share tab audio”.
The recorder now hides itself with a clear hint when no OpenAI API key is set (instead of erroring on click).
Diarized notes get a colored left border by speaker (you = blue, them = violet) so the transcript is scannable at a glance during a fast call.

releases.title: Résumé tailoring focuses are now configurable per profile (with an AI-picks-the-angle option)

items.label: The Résumé page's 'Focus' dropdown is no longer a hardcoded IC/Leadership/General set — each profile now defines its own focuses in Settings → Context → Master Resume. A focus is a label + a description that gets injected into the tailoring AI as emphasis steering, with an optional pin to a specific Master Résumé variant (shown only when you have more than one).

Two Auto modes: 'Auto (by seniority)' picks a focus from the job's level (you map which seniority levels trigger which focus), and 'Let AI pick the angle' lets the model choose the strongest emphasis from the role + JD itself.

Seeded Alex's existing Leadership / Senior IC / General focuses (behavior preserved — old tailored versions still resolve) and Chelsea's profile with HR / Recruitment and Office Administration focuses.
Fixed a profile leak: the tailoring prompt no longer hardcodes 'ALEX'S NOTES' in the user prompt, so it reads correctly on any profile.

releases.title: Interview transcripts: drop a raw transcript, AI cleans + diarizes + fixes names + strikes smalltalk, then extract real-time notes — on interview rounds and lead meetings

items.label: New 'Transcript' section on every interview round and lead meeting. Paste a raw transcript → 'Clean up with AI' reformats it into a readable, diarized Me / Them / named-interviewer transcript, fixes proper-noun spelling from the role's company + contacts (e.g. 'Calabria' → 'Calabrio'), splits lines that mash two speakers together, and strikes through (doesn't delete) smalltalk for you to review.

Handles the question-flip: when the interviewer says 'do you have any questions for me?', the questions you ask afterward are correctly attributed to YOU, not them — the long-standing mis-assignment on reversed transcripts.

'Extract notes' turns the reviewed transcript into Real-time notes (one per substantive turn, flagged backfilled) — smalltalk is dropped automatically, and your edits/strikes are honored. The button shows the count and guards against double-adding.

One transcript, reused: Draft Debrief now drafts from your saved transcript (leave the paste box blank) instead of needing a re-paste; and the quick Backfill → AI-assign path now also handles the question-flip, splits mashed lines, and skips smalltalk.

Transcripts are stored as files (not inline), so they don't bloat your data; the cleaned version is editable + re-cleanable, with an audit pass that guards against the AI dropping substantive content. Carries losslessly when a lead meeting is promoted to a job round.

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach: AI re-scores a pitched role from follow-up info, plus full role editing

items.label: New “Update from new info” AI action on a pitched role (on the engagement’s Pitched Roles card, on the role detail page, and as “Update pitched role from this conversation” right on the Communication chain). Paste a recruiter’s follow-up reply (or let it read the whole chain) + add your own thoughts/steer, and it proposes FOCUSED, conservative updates — re-scoring fit & interest, refreshing the why-fit / concerns, and filling in comp, location, JD, requirements, and the end client when the recruiter finally names it. You review a before→after diff and accept it per section. Re-runnable as more info arrives. It never renames the role and never promotes it.
On the Communication chain version, when an engagement has multiple pitched roles you pick which one the new info applies to.
New editable “Enrich Pitched Role” prompt under Settings → AI Prompts → Chain (its own per-prompt model; reads your Career + Goals + AI scoring rules so fit/interest move on your rubric).

You can now edit a pitched role’s end-client company, staffing vendor, and logo URL from the role detail page’s “Edit details” (previously only the title was editable there) — parity with editing a job opportunity.

releases.title: Live interview copilot (beta): record a call and auto-add diarized notes in real time

items.label: Phase 2a of the interview copilot: a “Record call” button now sits atop the live-notes panel on interview rounds (and lead meetings). It captures TWO audio streams — your mic as “you” and the call’s browser-tab audio as “them” (pick the call tab + tick “Share tab audio”) — runs an OpenAI Realtime transcription on each, and drops finalized lines straight into your notes labelled by speaker. Diarization is by audio source, so it’s deterministic (no guessing who spoke).

BETA — real-time WebRTC transcription needs a live test (a real mic, a real call in a browser tab, and your OpenAI API key). If you don’t share tab audio it records just your side. Native-app calls (no browser tab) will need a loopback device; that and the smart auto-surface-ideas (configurable cadence) land in Phase 2b.

releases.title: Audit: pinned insight tiles + filters, and resolved items stay resolved across runs

items.label: Mini insight tiles at the top of the Audit page: ✨ Resolved by AI · ✓ Resolved by you (with an 'X accepted an AI suggestion · Y manual, AI couldn't help' breakdown) · 💡 Open suggestions · ✍️ Still need you. Counts update live as you resolve, and each tile is clickable to filter to it.
The insight tiles and both filter rows now stay pinned at the top while the job cards scroll underneath, so the filters are always one click away.

Bug fix: resolved items no longer appear to un-resolve. Running the AI resolver on one filter (e.g. medium) then another (e.g. low) — or just switching the filter — used to unmount the off-screen cards and lose their resolved state, making already-resolved fields look like to-dos again. The list now hides filtered rows via CSS instead of unmounting them, and a re-run merges results so it never disturbs what's already resolved. (Your data was always safe — this was a display regression.)
'Hide resolved' now visibly shrinks the list — resolved rows drop out of the Any view and the count reflects only what's left to do.

releases.title: Voice dictation reaches the last freeform inputs (debrief transcript, outreach messages, composer subject)

items.label: The dictation mic now also covers the “Draft debrief from transcript” box (speak or dictate a call recap), the editable message bodies in the recruiter-outreach review, and the composer Subject line — completing the speak-to-fill rollout across freeform AI inputs. (The 10 tiny inline debrief micro-fields are intentionally left mic-free to avoid clutter.)

releases.title: Voice dictation: speak to fill any AI text box (real-time, with a choice of engine)

items.label: A microphone button now sits next to the freeform “talk to the AI” inputs across the app — Parse-with-AI, Audit context, Offer negotiation recap, Offer gap-fill, Company-brief research, the interview live-notes composers, post-interview recap/overall/outcome notes, the message composer body, the AI card generate/rewrite dialogs, and resume emphasis keywords (16 inputs in all). Click it and speak; your words fill the box, then send to the AI as usual.

Real-time by default: with the browser (Web Speech) engine the text appears as you talk, like phone dictation, and it auto-restarts past pauses. Free, no API call. Pick your engine in Settings → AI Provider → Voice dictation: Web Speech (real-time, free, Chrome/Edge, audio goes to Google), OpenAI transcription (audio stays with OpenAI, any browser, records-then-transcribes), or Auto (Web Speech when available, else OpenAI).

Note: Anthropic has no speech-to-text, so it isn’t an engine option — Web Speech covers you regardless of which AI provider you use. A live interview copilot (listen to the call, diarize, auto-note, auto-surface ideas) is the planned next phase.

releases.title: Audit: filter by AI state — isolate what still needs you vs what the AI resolved or suggested

items.label: New 'AI state' filter row on the Audit page: Any / ✨ AI-resolved / ✓ You-resolved / 💡 Suggested / ✍️ Needs me — so after an AI run you can jump straight to the fields that still need manual input.
Counts on each AI-state pill are faceted by the active severity filter, and a 'Hide resolved' toggle keeps the All view to just open items.
Acts as a live worklist: resolving a field moves it out of 'Needs me' into 'You-resolved' (or '✨ AI-resolved' when the AI applied it) and the counts update — the to-do list shrinks as you go.
Filtering hides rows via CSS rather than unmounting them, so resolved rows keep their session state (and Undo) when you switch filters.

releases.title: Profile management (rename / archive / delete) + a per-profile setup completeness meter

items.label: New Settings → Profiles page to manage every profile: edit photo + accent + rename, archive/restore (hide without losing data), and delete. Deleting moves the profile's whole data folder to data/profiles-archive/ — recoverable from disk, never destroyed. You can't archive or delete the active profile (switch away first) or the last one.

Each profile now shows a completeness meter — 'X% set up' with a checklist of exactly what's still missing (career context, the six context blocks, identity anchors, Master Résumé), each deep-linking to where to fill it.

The meter appears in three places: per-profile on the Settings → Profiles page, on the Onboarding tab next to the audit, and as a small dismissible nudge on the dashboard when the active profile is under-filled.

releases.title: Audit: "Auto-resolve all" — run the AI resolver across every job in the current filter, in one click

items.label: A new 'Auto-resolve all' button runs the autonomous AI resolver across every job in the CURRENT filter (All / High / Medium / Low) — filter first to scope cost, then resolve the whole visible set at once.
Cost-safe: clicking shows 'Run AI on N jobs (~N model calls)?' with Run / Cancel before anything fires, a live 'Resolving x/N…' progress counter, and a Stop button to halt mid-run.
High-confidence fields auto-apply (✨) and medium ones surface 💡 suggestions across all cards at once; one aggregate summary ('N auto-resolved · M to review') instead of a toast per job.
'Undo all' reverts every AI change from the run in one click (each field is still individually undoable too).
Writes stay safe under the concurrent fan-out — all jobs.json writes are serialized server-side, so resolving many jobs at once can't corrupt the file. Completes the bulk-audit-fix backlog item.

releases.title: IP carve-out manager — define your personal tools once, copy each into the offer's IP schedule

items.label: New "IP carve-out / Pre-Engagement Inventions" section: write about all your personal tools / own IP in plain prose and "Itemize with AI" splits it into discrete items (name · category · description · carve-out rationale) for you to review before saving.

The inventory is profile-level — define it once and it's reused across every offer. Each item has a one-click Copy (plus Copy all) formatted for pasting straight into the offer letter's IP carve-out schedule in DocuSign.
Add items manually, edit inline, or delete; surfaced as a collapsible section in Offer Details and editable under Settings → Context → Offer Preferences.
Per-prompt configurable like the other AI features (model + prompt, OpenAI or Anthropic) under Settings → AI Prompts → "Offer: Itemize IP Carve-out".

releases.title: Audit: "Auto-resolve with AI" — the AI reads each job and fills the audit by confidence

items.label: New per-job "Auto-resolve with AI" button on the Audit page: it reads the job's existing data (statuses, dates, compensation, rounds, contacts, a comms digest + timeline) and infers each flagged field with a calibrated confidence — no typing needed.

High-confidence answers apply automatically (✨ "AI-confirmed", always undoable); medium ones show a 💡 suggestion you accept in one click; a medium answer that just matches the current value is auto-confirmed; low stays manual.

Data-quality flags (empty/duplicate message body, stale timestamp, premature offer status) get a looks-fine / needs-fix verdict with a rationale and are never auto-written; adding contacts or scheduling rounds is only ever suggested (prefills the form), never auto-created.
Optional "+ context" box folds in the old free-text flow — add anything the data doesn't capture and the AI weighs it above its own inference (replaces the separate "AI fix all" dialog).
Settings → Thresholds gains an "Audit auto-resolve (AI)" card: a two-thumb confidence slider (suggest / auto lines) + a master auto-apply toggle, mirroring Smart message linking.

New editable "Audit Resolve (autonomous)" prompt in Settings → AI Prompts, and every run is captured in AI Logs. AI-confirmed fields now persist their confidence + rationale on the job (aiResolutions).

releases.title: Profile landing page (/select) + profile pictures and accent colors

items.label: New full-screen profile landing page — open it from the profile switcher's 'Switch profile…' to see everyone at a glance and jump in. Shown on demand (not forced on every launch). The active profile is marked, and each card shows when it was last used.

Profiles now have pictures: upload a photo (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF) per profile, with a deterministic colored-initials fallback. Photos are served by profile id, so the landing page shows everyone's at once.
Pick a per-profile accent color (or leave it Auto). Edit a profile's photo + color right from the landing page (hover a card → the pencil).
The profile switcher and landing page now share one avatar component, so initials, colors, and photos stay consistent everywhere.

releases.title: Offer version comparison — AI delta between two offer versions (what changed, what stayed, what's new), with a re-runnable history

items.label: New collapsible 'Version comparison' section in Offer Details: pick an older → newer offer version (cycle) and run an AI delta that reads BOTH versions' document text plus your recorded offer + negotiation Q&A. It reports what changed in the terms (before → after), language/clause changes, what stayed the same, and what's NEW in the newer version (e.g. an ESOP the earlier version didn't include — shown as an addition, not a change).

Comparisons are saved as a re-runnable history, each labeled by version pair + date (e.g. v1 → v2, then v2 → v3) — click any past comparison to view it, re-run, or delete. Model + prompt are tunable per-prompt in Settings → AI Prompts → Offer (Compare Versions).

releases.title: Faster audits: pick a value inline — selecting it IS the fix (no expand, no Apply)

items.label: Inferred enum fields (Priority, Initiated-by, Active state) now show their options as inline chips right under the label, with the current value pre-selected — one click away, no chevron to expand and no dropdown.
Selecting a chip IS the apply: it writes + auto-confirms the field optimistically and the row instantly condenses to a ✓ check with the resolved value — no Apply button.

Every resolution has Undo (a toast action and an Undo button on the condensed row) that reverses both the value change and the confirm. Resolved rows stay visible as checkmarks so you can see your progress.
No more full-page refresh on each fix — clicks no longer reload the whole audit list, so working through many items is dramatically faster.

Active-state shows Active / Inactive with the inactive reason as a second chip row; complex fields (date applied, compensation, schedule round, add contact) keep a form behind a compact "Fill in" toggle and gain the same condense + Undo. Each card header shows live "N resolved" progress.

releases.title: All onboarding AI prompts are now editable and consolidated into the Onboarding tab; the audit splits into per-section prompts

items.label: The prompts that actually fill a profile are now editable: 'Seed / Fill Profile' (turns a brief or uploaded guide into the career/context/identity fields) and the 'Reformat Field' base prompt (the drift-guarded ✨ tidier). Previously these were hardcoded and not surfaced anywhere.

The Onboarding Audit is now split into per-section prompts — Career Context, Context Blocks, Identity, and Overridden Prompts — each with its own editable prompt (defaulting to a shared baseline plus a section-specific focus). Tune the bar for context blocks without touching the others.

All onboarding prompts now live and are edited inside the Onboarding tab (Setup / Audit / Prompts sub-tabs) instead of the main Prompts list — the dedicated section is self-contained, with its own per-prompt model pickers.
The audit got cheaper and more accurate: empty fields are judged instantly with no AI call, and only sections that actually have content hit the model — each with its own prompt.

releases.title: New “AI Models” settings tab: compare cost + use-case per model, and assign tiers in one click

items.label: Added a Settings → AI Models tab. Every OpenAI and Anthropic model gets a card showing input / output / cached-input cost per 1M tokens, a what-it’s-good-for blurb, and chips for the in-app prompts it best suits. Page-level Cache and Batch toggles preview how those prices change (cached ≈10% input; batch −50%). Each card shows which tier it currently holds and lets you set it as Default / Heavy / Medium / Light in one click — feeding the per-prompt model decision.

Expanded the model dropdown: added GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 Pro, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and GPT-4o mini (alongside GPT-5.5 Pro), each with pricing wired into the cost logs. The future audio models (GPT-Realtime 2, GPT-Realtime Whisper) appear in the catalog as “future · audio” placeholders for the planned in-app speech-to-text feature.
Bug fix: gpt-5.4-nano was being costed as gpt-5.4 in the AI logs (no nano pricing entry existed) — it now has its own (much cheaper) rate, so Light-tier costs are accurate.
Set the default tier mapping for OpenAI: Default & Medium = GPT-5.4 mini, Heavy = GPT-5.4, Light = GPT-5.4 nano.

releases.title: Filled-in blank values now render bold (and are click-to-edit); fill works on the OCR-formatted text without truncating it

items.label: Filling a template's blanks now inserts each value in **bold**, so your entered values stand out in the document. This also activates the (previously latent) click-to-edit: the bold filled values in the Text view are now hover/click-editable inline, and editing one syncs the matching Offer Details field.

Fill in / Update blanks now reliably works ON the current text — including a document you just formatted with OCR/reformat — and preserves that formatting: it only swaps the blanks (bolded) and keeps every heading, list, and table intact. So the intended flow works: OCR to format nicely → fill the remaining blanks in place.

Fix: filling a long contract used to truncate it (the blank-fill ran on the light model with a small output budget, so the tail/formatting could be lost). Blank-fill + blank-detection now use the heavy tier with a full-length output + input budget, matching the reformat — large contracts fill end-to-end.

releases.title: Creating a profile now lands you on its Onboarding tab to finish setup, and the create wizard captures mail identity

items.label: After you create a new profile, the app now drops you straight onto that profile's Onboarding tab (Settings → AI Prompts → Onboarding) — the hub where you download/upload the Collection Guide, fill identity, and run the readiness audit — instead of an empty dashboard.
The create wizard now captures the person's mail identity (sender email + phone) so sent-vs-received detection on their communications works from day one.

releases.title: Onboarding tab gets a downloadable Collection Guide, one-upload answer import, and the missing Identity editor

items.label: Download a tailored Collection Guide (Markdown or JSON) from the Onboarding tab — fill it in yourself, or paste the whole thing into ChatGPT (which knows the person) and have it fill every answer block. Examples are drawn from the current profile so the depth is clear.

Upload the filled guide back in one click — a tolerant importer parses it (structured JSON → the guide's answer blocks → AI fallback for free-form text), shows you exactly what it will write, and merges it into the profile's career context, context blocks, and identity. Existing fields are only overwritten by what you import.

New Identity editor in the Onboarding tab — the 10 structured identity anchors (name, sign-off, location, target roles, seniority, comp floor, contract rate, work auth, remote/hybrid, notice) were previously editable only during profile creation; now you can fill or fix them anytime. The Onboarding Audit flags any left empty.

releases.title: A real, separate Heavy model tier + GPT-5.5 Pro option, and a clearer AI Provider page

items.label: The AI Provider page now has a dedicated Heavy model, separate from your Default (main) model. Previously “Heavy” was just your main model under another name — which is why pinning a feature to Heavy used whatever your main model was (gpt-5.4-mini). Now Default / Heavy / Medium / Light are four independent slots, each clearly labelled, and each falls back to Default when left empty.

Crucially, only a feature you EXPLICITLY pin to the Heavy tier uses the Heavy model — un-pinned features keep using Default — so you can set a premium Heavy model (e.g. GPT-5.5 Pro) without inflating the cost of everything else.
Added GPT-5.5 Pro (gpt-5.5-pro-2026-04-23) as a model preset, with pricing ($30/1M input, $180/1M output) wired into the AI cost logs so its calls are costed correctly.

releases.title: OCR an offer's blanks or whole document on demand; reformat no longer touches your filled-in blanks; reformat + audit are per-prompt configurable

items.label: Fix: a failed contract reformat used to wipe your manually filled-in blanks (it re-read the bare PDF and wrote that back). The reformat now works from your CURRENT text — fills included — and on an audit failure it leaves your text completely untouched (nothing overwritten). 'View raw' / 'Revert to raw' remain explicit, separate actions.
