New OCR fill for template blanks: in the blank-fill panel, 'Read from PDF (OCR)' has an AI vision model read the actual filled-in values straight off the PDF image (the values that sit in a form overlay the text layer can't see) and pre-fills the form for you to review, then Fill. For when you'd rather not type them in.

On-demand whole-document OCR: an eye (vision) action on each offer doc re-OCRs the whole PDF and replaces the text — available anytime now (previously only auto-offered for scanned/no-text PDFs). Warns first if it would replace filled blanks.

Both OCR features + the reformat audit are first-class per-prompt AI features: pick the model/provider (OpenAI or Anthropic) and edit the system prompt in Settings → AI Prompts (Offer group). Offer reformat now defaults to the heavy tier so long contracts aren't truncated.

releases.title: Onboarding tab in AI Prompts — an editable Onboarding-Audit AI that confirms a profile's context is formatted, complete & leak-free, with one-click reformat

items.label: Settings → AI Prompts now has a secondary Onboarding tab. Run the Onboarding Audit to check the active profile's per-person context (career, context blocks, identity) plus any prompts you've overridden — each field gets a verdict for FORMATTING (clean vs run-on), COMPLETENESS (filled / thin / empty), and cross-profile LEAKAGE (another person's name or sign-off bleeding in).
The audit is driven by a new editable "Onboarding Audit" prompt in the AI Prompts library, so you can tune exactly how strict it is — assess-only, it never rewrites your content.

Formatting issues get a one-click Reformat (diff preview, accept/reject) powered by the drift-guarded reformat engine — it tidies Markdown structure without changing a single word, number, or name. Thin/empty fields get a Fix deep-link to the right settings page.
Onboarding Audit runs are logged like every other AI call (provider-aware, with a copy-prompt fallback when no API key is set).

releases.title: Profiles foundation (P0): registry schema v2 + a shared onboarding field registry + a logged, drift-guarded “Reformat field” AI primitive

items.label: Profile records now carry optional avatar, accent-color, archived, and last-used fields (schemaVersion 2). The upgrade is additive and lazy — existing profiles are read unchanged and only rewritten on the next switch/edit, so there is no migration step. This is the groundwork for upcoming profile pictures, a profiles management page, and an on-demand profile picker.
Switching a profile now stamps when it was last used, so future surfaces can order profiles by recency.

New shared onboarding field registry (one source of truth for the identity / career-context / context-block field set) feeding the create wizard today and the upcoming downloadable Collection Guide + answer-upload onboarding.

New “Reformat field” AI capability: cleans a profile/context field into tidy Markdown WITHOUT changing any words — provider-aware, logged like every other AI call, with a no-API-key copy-prompt fallback and a word-drift guard that rejects (and keeps the original) if the model drops/invents any number or reword. The per-field ✨ button that uses it ships next, in the onboarding overhaul.
Housekeeping: relocated a leftover smoke-test profile silo out of the live profiles directory.

releases.title: Contract reformat: use the heavy model + a full-length output budget so long contracts aren't truncated

items.label: Live testing of the new lossless reformat on the Superpanel employment agreement showed it kept the raw text because the reformat output was being truncated at the tail (the signature + witness/execution pages) — the audit correctly caught it. Root cause: the light-tier model's small output cap. Offer-document reformat now uses the heavy tier with an explicit 32k-token output budget and a 200k-char input window, so full-length contracts (incl. the ESOP) reproduce end-to-end and the audit can pass.

releases.title: Contract reformat is now lossless (audited) + raw-text safety net; attachment paths repaired app-wide; offer letters default to the letter

items.label: Offer/contract reformat (the ✨ button) no longer drops or summarizes anything. The prompt is now contract-grade — it reproduces every word/number/clause verbatim and only fixes PDF formatting — and a second AI audit compares the raw extraction vs the reformatted version. If the audit finds ANY lost or altered text, it auto-retries once, and if it still isn't perfect it keeps the verbatim raw text instead (you never see a lossy contract).

The pristine raw PDF extraction is now preserved as a separate sidecar (never overwritten by reformat). A 'View raw' toggle compares formatted vs verbatim, and 'Revert to raw' undoes a reformat. The raw is the audit's ground truth.
Opening the Offer Letters tab now defaults to the primary offer letter of the latest cycle (not a supporting ESOP/addendum that happened to be the most recent upload).

Fixed attachment paths app-wide after the Profiles migration: 155 stale stored paths (résumés, job descriptions, logos, round attachments, lead/watch-role docs) were repaired to the active profile's location, and every client URL-builder (resume/JD/logo panes, interview rounds, round/meeting focus pages, lead docs) now resolves both legacy and profile-scoped paths via a shared builder. Previously these could 404 or fail server-side reads.

releases.title: Profiles privacy hardening — non-default profiles no longer leak the default owner’s name or facts into AI prompts; new profiles get clean, formatted context + a Master Résumé

items.label: AI prompt identity substitution now also catches bare ALL-CAPS first names (e.g. section headers like “CONTEXT ABOUT ALEX”), closing a leak where a non-default profile’s prompts could still surface the default owner’s name in uppercase headings.

Settings → AI Prompts now shows the DEFAULT prompt text personalized to the ACTIVE profile (name-substituted) instead of always rendering the default owner’s name — so what you see in the prompt editor matches what actually gets sent for that profile.

Genericized the built-in prompt scaffolding (context-block starters, cover-letter voice defaults, recruiter-fit + summarize examples, interview/career fallbacks) so a fresh profile starts from neutral, person-agnostic defaults rather than the default owner’s specifics (former-title, comp band, city).

Per-person context for non-default profiles is now stored as clean, readable Markdown (headers, bullets, bold labels) to match the default profile — reformatted without changing a single word of the underlying content.
Out-of-band maintenance scripts now write the LIVE active profile’s data via the path getters instead of the frozen pre-Profiles root, so script-driven edits actually show up in the app.

Seeded a new profile (Chelsea) end-to-end: identity, three career-context lengths, six context blocks, mail identity, and a Master Résumé assembled from her source résumés — exercising the full new-profile onboarding path.

releases.title: Offer cycles — package multiple PDFs per offer (letter + ESOP), AI reads them together; "Other" attachments preview + convert to text

items.label: Offer Letters now group into offer CYCLES (packaged offer versions). Each cycle can hold multiple documents — the offer letter + the ESOP / stock-option plan + any addenda — so one revised offer's paperwork lives together. Add docs to a version with the per-cycle "+ Add doc", start a fresh version with "Upload new offer version", and edit a version's label + note inline.

Each document in a cycle has a role (Offer letter / ESOP / Addendum / Supporting doc). The primary offer letter keeps the template fill-in-the-blanks flow; supporting docs (ESOP, addenda) preview + extract text but skip the blanks UI.

Analyze / Extract now reads EVERY document in the offer cycle together (letter + ESOP), so equity terms — vesting, cliff, change-of-control, post-termination exercise window — from the ESOP actually inform the analysis instead of being flagged "missing". The prior cycle's letter is still used for base/equity ratio-drift comparison.

"Other" attachments got the full Offer-Letter treatment: inline PDF/image preview, a Text view of the extracted Markdown (convert-on-demand for older files), download, and a Delete button (it had none before).

Migration: existing offer letters were wrapped into per-version cycles, and the Superpanel ESOP was moved out of "Other" into its offer cycle (v2) with its text extracted. New uploads carry cycle + role automatically; the read layer back-fills cycles for any legacy data.
Hardened the attachment serve-URL builder (shared, profile-aware) so offer + "Other" previews resolve under the active profile — part of cleaning up the post-Profiles-migration path handling.

releases.title: Pipeline brush zoom — drag any window over a full-range mini-composition

items.label: A new 'Zoom' brush strip below the timeline shows a full-range mini stacked-composition; drag across it to select any custom [start, end] window — finer than the 30d/90d/6mo/1yr/YTD/All presets.

Drag the window edges to resize, drag the middle to pan, double-click (or Reset) to clear; focus an edge handle and use arrow keys to nudge it. Setting a window supersedes the preset and the whole timeline (axis, gridlines, composition) re-projects to fit the viewport width.
A date-range readout shows exactly which window you're viewing; clicking a preset clears the brush.

releases.title: Fix: offer-letter upload / delete / preview broken after Profiles migration

items.label: Offer-letter uploads silently failed to preview/read/delete after the Profiles migration: the attachment read/delete/write guards still hardcoded the legacy data/attachments root and rejected every profile-scoped path (data/profiles/<id>/attachments/…) → 'can't find the file'. The guards now accept the active profile's attachment dir (and the legacy root for back-compat).
The offer-letter preview URL now resolves correctly for both legacy and profile-scoped paths (it extracts the sub-path after 'attachments/<jobId>/' instead of assuming a fixed prefix).

Repaired the Superpanel offer letters: removed a duplicate v3 (same PDF uploaded twice while the bug was live) and re-pointed the older offer's stored paths at their migrated files so preview + AI text extraction work again.

releases.title: Profiles — per-profile AI tailoring (Profiles feature complete)

items.label: AI features now tailor to the ACTIVE profile end-to-end: recruiter replies, fit/interest scoring, cover letters, and outreach use that profile's own name, sign-off, target roles, location, comp anchors, and work authorization — no more hardcoded assumptions. Your (Alex's) prompts are byte-identical; a second profile gets its own.
The profile switcher's create flow can also set a profile's mail identity (sender email / phone) so communication direction detection works per profile.

releases.title: Profiles — create a new profile with AI-seeded context

items.label: Create a new profile from the switcher: enter a name + paste an “about this person” brief, and the AI drafts their full context — three career-context versions, goals, AI authoring rules, voice & framing, offer preferences, cover-letter voice, and company-research rules — for you to review and edit before saving.

Each new profile also captures structured identity anchors (name, sign-off, location, target roles, seniority, comp floor, contract rate, work authorization, remote/hybrid preference, notice period) — the foundation for fully person-tailored AI replies.
No API key configured? The wizard hands you the prompt to run in your own model, then parses the JSON you paste back — so the AI-seed path works even on the copy-prompt provider.

releases.title: Profiles — separate, switchable workspaces

items.label: New: Profiles let you keep fully separate, isolated workspaces (e.g. tracking a second person's job search). A profile switcher now sits right under 'Job Tracker' in the sidebar — a colored badge with the current profile's name and a dropdown to switch or create.

Each profile has its OWN jobs, leads, contacts, communications, AI logs, attachments, résumé/cover-letter templates, mail identity, and career/context — so Dashboard, Pipeline, Insights, Calendar, Audit, etc. all scope to the active profile.
Shared across ALL profiles (set once): AI providers & models, custom statuses, thresholds, interaction kinds, and the prompt-access matrix.
Create a new (empty) profile from the switcher; switching reloads into that profile's data. Cover-letter voice and company-research rules carry a shared default each profile can override.

Under the hood: all existing data was migrated into the default 'Alex Bisgould' profile (data/profiles/alex-bisgould/) with backups, and settings were split into a shared file + per-profile file — the app reads the merged view transparently, no behavior change.

releases.title: Pipeline polish — rich tooltips, stale-lane follow-ups, smart links & a mobile message sheet

items.label: Hovering a stage band or an event marker now shows a styled tooltip (stage + duration, or the bucketed event list with a 'click to open' hint) instead of the slow native one — one shared floating tooltip keeps hundreds of markers cheap, with keyboard-focus parity.
Stale & dead lanes get a hover 'Follow up' action: job lanes open the comms composer pre-targeted to that job; lead / watch-role / recruiter lanes open the record to follow up.

More smart links: KPI tiles focus the timeline on their slice (Interviewing / Offers / Leads & watch / Active / Closed / clear); the dead-time hatch jumps to the lane's last message chain; the closure cap opens the role's outcome (offer card for wins, the closure event otherwise); offer-stage markers deep-link to the offer card.
The lane scope is now a 3-way control — Active / All / Closed — replacing the active-only toggle, so closed roles are one click away.
Responsive pass: on phones the message detail opens as a bottom sheet (not a hidden side panel), and the filter chips collapse behind a 'Filters' button so the sticky header stays compact.

releases.title: Pipeline → Calendar smart-links

items.label: Click any event marker on the Pipeline timeline to jump to that day on the Calendar; the message side-card now has a 'View on calendar' link alongside 'Jump to chain'.
The Calendar accepts a ?date=YYYY-MM-DD deep-link and opens focused on that day.

releases.title: Pipeline, rebuilt — a unified opportunity timeline with dead-time, filters, message cards & an opportunity funnel

items.label: The /pipeline page is now a timeline-first hub: every opportunity — jobs, leads, watch roles AND recruiter outreach — as a swimlane on a real month/quarter time axis.

Each lane is a stage-colored band (Found → Applied → Interviewing → Offer → Accepted) with category-colored event markers; closed roles end at closure and show a blank/grey tail so you can see how long a role has been dead.

Dead-time: an active lane that's gone quiet hatches as stale (14d+) then dead (30d+) of no meaningful activity — bookkeeping doesn't count, and a booked future round/meeting suppresses it. Thresholds are configurable in Settings → Thresholds.
Filter bar: search, sort, and Type / Stage / Priority / Origin / Activity chips + per-event-category toggles; a compact sticky header keeps the title + filters in view; KPI strip up top.
Pipeline composition over time — a stacked area of how many opportunities sat in each stage week by week (how the pipeline changed).
Click a communication marker to open the message in a side card, with a jump-to-chain link to the Communication page.
Opportunity funnel card: where opportunities come from (jobs, leads & recruiter outreach) + how far applications get, with step conversions.
Company logos now show next to every opportunity, and the timeline always fills the full width (a touch narrower when a message card is open). Zoom presets: 30d / 90d / 6mo / 1yr / YTD / All.
Fixed a data quirk where orphan 'outreach-sent' events with no saved message (e.g. CDAI) showed a phantom 'communication today' and masked dead-time.

releases.title: Communication: tidier role-filter views — drop the pills the filter already implies

items.label: In the Watch roles / Pitched Roles filters, role rows no longer repeat a “Watch role” / “Pitched role” chip (the filter already says it), and a role with no role-specific messages no longer shows a “0” count — so the list reads cleaner. The role’s status badge and end-client logo stay.
When you’ve scoped the conversation to a specific role, the per-chain “role: <title>” origin pill is hidden — the column header already names the role, so it was just noise on every row.

In any single-type filter (Leads, Recruiter Outreach, Watch roles, Pitched Roles) the “Lead” / “Recruiter Outreach” badge in the conversation (right) pane header is now hidden too — extending the row-badge hiding from the earlier release to the reading pane.

releases.title: Add with AI: re-route a parse to Job / Engagement / Lead on the review screen, and fix the dropped recruiter deadline

items.label: Post-parse destination switcher: a 'Save as' control on the review screen re-routes an AI parse between Job opportunity, Recruiter Engagement, and Lead without re-running the AI. The recruiter contact and the captured conversation carry across the switch; the destination-specific draft is rebuilt from the parse.

Bug fix: the AI-parsed 'next action by' deadline was being silently dropped — the mapper computed and date-guarded it, but the review form never carried it into the create call, so every parser-created engagement landed with no deadline. It now persists (and is shown as an editable date on the review), so it reaches the Recruiter Outreach deadline column and the calendar.

releases.title: Communication: Watch roles & Pitched Roles now list the roles directly, plus an auto recruiter-reply draft

items.label: The Communication “Watch roles” and “Pitched Roles” filters now list the ROLES themselves as rows (role title + end-client logo, status, and a green “Watch role” / violet “Pitched role” chip) instead of the parent lead/engagement with a chevron to expand. Click a role to scope the conversation to it. Pitched roles whose messages aren’t tagged to a specific role fall through to the engagement’s full thread, so a role row never opens an empty pane.

New editable AI prompt “Recruiter Initial Reply” (Settings → AI Prompts → Chain, with its own per-prompt model). When you press the “Draft AI follow-up” button on a recruiter-outreach conversation you haven’t replied to yet, it now drafts your FIRST reply using your fit checklist — it asks only for what the recruiter hasn’t already given (role level + reporting line, the end client if unnamed, employment type, location & hybrid cadence, contract length, and comp band), asks their comp first and anchors yours only to qualify, and offers to route up to senior AI/ML leadership roles when the pitch sits below your lane. Same button; normal follow-ups are unchanged.

releases.title: “Add with AI” now captures each pitched role’s status, fit, bullets and the next-action deadline

items.label: When you paste a recruiter’s message into “Add with AI”, the parser now fills far more of each pitched role on the engagement — not just title/company/comp. For every role it infers a status (Watching / Discussed / Routed / Dismissed / Filled), a fit score + why-it-fits + concerns judged against your background and goals, and any role bullets the message actually states. It also marks the single strongest-fit role as primary instead of just the first one listed.

It’s deliberately conservative: status stays “Watching” and fit stays blank unless the message gives real evidence, so a cold first pitch doesn’t get over-claimed. You can still adjust everything on review and on the engagement page.
The engagement’s next action now also captures a due date when the message implies one (e.g. “reply by Tuesday” → a real date), with a guard so a malformed date never blocks the parse.

releases.title: Resume structurer AI calls now show up in the AI logs

items.label: The “structure resume” AI calls (PDF → 2-column layout, run from a job’s resume, from a template, or from Settings → Templates) were not being recorded in the AI call logs / cost dashboard because their routes weren’t wrapped in the logging context. They’re now logged under the “structure-resume” feature with proper cost/usage attribution.

releases.title: AI Prompts: the Per-prompt model picker now actually controls 8 more AI actions

items.label: Eight AI actions previously ignored the model you pinned in Settings → AI Prompts → Per-prompt models (the dropdown showed but did nothing) — they always used your main model. They now honor your choice: Open-thread triage, Summarize comms with a person, Audit fix, Merge note, Cover letter, Resume structurer, Company brief, and the Weekly-focus digest. No change unless you actually pin a model/tier for one of them (the default still resolves to your main model).

releases.title: Communication: Lead vs Recruiter Outreach badges get distinct colors, an icon-only mode, and a new Pitched Roles filter

items.label: In the Communication list’s mixed (All) views, the Lead and Recruiter Outreach badges now use distinct colors — Lead is green, Recruiter Outreach is violet — so the two types read apart at a glance instead of sharing one color.

A new Text / Icon toggle (top-right of the filter strip) switches those badges between the full “Lead” / “Recruiter Outreach” label and a compact color-coded icon. In icon mode a dormant engagement shows as a faded-yellow icon (no “dormant” text), mirroring the dimmed dormant look used elsewhere. Your choice is remembered across reloads.

The filter chips are reordered to All · Jobs · Leads · Watch roles · Recruiter Outreach · Pitched Roles, with a new “Pitched Roles” chip. “Watch roles” now scopes to roles tracked on ordinary Leads, while “Pitched Roles” scopes to roles a recruiter pitched on an engagement.

When the list is filtered to a single type (Leads, Watch roles, Recruiter Outreach, or Pitched Roles), the now-redundant type badge is hidden — only a small status chip shows for non-active rows — extending the behavior that previously applied just to Recruiter Outreach.

releases.title: AI Prompts: the merge-duplicate-role context note is now an editable prompt

items.label: The AI “merge note” — the short context blurb written when you merge a duplicate role into a survivor — is now a first-class editable prompt under Settings → AI Prompts → Classification & Audit (“Merge Note”). Previously its wording was hardcoded and the only AI feature with no editable prompt; you can now tune it like every other prompt, and it shows in the group-scoped Per-prompt models list.

releases.title: AI Prompts: per-prompt models scope to the group you are viewing + Card Blurbs live under Card Editing

items.label: Settings → AI Prompts: the Per-prompt models list now defaults to showing only the prompts in the group you are currently viewing (e.g. on the Helpers tab you see just the Helpers prompts, on Interview just the interview ones). A one-click “Show all” toggle still reveals every prompt when you need it.

The AI Card Blurbs (per-card personality) editor now appears under the “Card Editing (AI)” group instead of always sitting at the bottom of the page — it is the per-card content those card-editing prompts inject, so it now lives alongside them.

releases.title: Communication: tidier Recruiter Outreach list with dormant ones de-emphasized

items.label: When the Communication list is filtered to Recruiter Outreach, rows no longer repeat the redundant 'Recruiter Outreach' badge on every line — the filter already says it. The rows read cleaner (recruiter/company + role), and only a small status chip shows when an engagement isn't active.
Dormant (and abandoned) recruiter engagements now sort below the active ones and render dimmed with a compact 'dormant' chip, so live conversations lead the list.

releases.title: Miratech logo now shows (pinned to its real favicon)

items.label: The Miratech engagement now shows Miratech's real logo (pinned to its site favicon) instead of a generic globe — Google's favicon service had no icon for its domain. Any company can be pinned this way when the auto-resolved logo is wrong.

Reverted a globe auto-detect attempt that could flicker the avatar between the placeholder and the real favicon; explicit pinning is the reliable path for the rare domains Google's favicon service misses.

releases.title: Company logos fall back to the site's own favicon

items.label: When Google's favicon service errors for a domain, company logos now fall back to that site's own /favicon.ico (replacing the long-dead Clearbit fallback) before showing initials. Applies everywhere a company logo appears.

releases.title: Open-thread triage is its own AI prompt + call

items.label: The open-thread priority/legitimacy scoring (high / med / low / noise) is now a DEDICATED AI feature — 'Triage Open Threads' — run as its own call after the person summary, with its own editable prompt in Settings → AI Prompts (Helpers) and its own per-prompt model/context config. (It was previously folded into the summary prompt.)

Both the contact summarizer ('Summarize Person') and the new 'Triage Open Threads' prompt are visible and independently tunable in Settings → AI Prompts; the Weekly Focus Digest (dashboard prioritization) is there too.

releases.title: Company logos fall back to the site's own favicon (fixes missing logos)

items.label: Fixed company logos that rendered as initials when Google's favicon service had no icon for a domain (e.g. Miratech). The dead Clearbit fallback was replaced with the company site's own /favicon.ico, so logos like Miratech's now load. Applies everywhere a company logo shows (jobs, leads, recruiter outreach, contacts).

Confirmed the Compunnel engagement's end client as Manulife (per the recruiter's follow-up) and recorded the contract terms: 6+ months with extension, T4 or C2C, Toronto 3 days onsite, GenAI background a must-have (Azure nice-to-have).

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach: agency vs client representation, role status icons, sticky header

items.label: An engagement now represents the RECRUITER'S agency (who they actually work for), while each pitched role represents its own end client. So Himanshu's engagement is Axiom Global Technologies with a Capgemini role; Sunil's is W3Global with BMO and Citi roles. The list/table/detail show the agency logo + name for the engagement and each end-client's logo on its role.

Not every engagement has a pitched role — when a recruiter reaches out without naming a concrete role, it's a general outreach with zero roles (shown as 'General outreach') until a real role is mentioned.

Each pitched role's status now has its own icon + color — Watching, Discussed, Routed, Promoted (green), Dismissed and Filled-by-another (muted, de-emphasized) — so active roles stand out from closed ones at a glance.
On the Recruiter Outreach page the search bar, filters, and table column headers stay locked at the top while the rows scroll.

Audited all existing engagements so each is anchored to the recruiter's actual firm (Axiom, Compunnel, Miratech, Technical Source, W3Global, Cognizant), each role points at its true end client (incl. the Technical Source role's client = Zoom), and a no-concrete-role Artech outreach was reset to a general outreach.

releases.title: Contact-summary polish: wider dialog, top actions, stateful button

items.label: The per-person comms summary dialog is wider, and its Refresh + Copy actions now sit in a sticky header at the top — reachable without scrolling past the whole summary.

On the Contacts list, the 'Summarize all comms' button now reflects state: a cyan glow + 'View comms summary' when a saved summary exists, an amber 'Summary out of date — re-summarize' when it's gone stale, and the plain label when none has been generated.

releases.title: Merge a duplicate role into another — no data lost

items.label: New Merge action on the job detail header (next to Delete). Open it from the duplicate, pick the role it's really a copy of, and it gets folded in and deleted — instead of just throwing the duplicate away.

Nothing is lost: the survivor keeps all its own data, and the duplicate's messages, contacts (deduped by person), interview rounds, attachments, tags, and related-role links are all moved in. Chain ids and contact links are remapped so threads stay intact.

A review screen shows only the MEANINGFUL differences (identical fields are hidden). Statuses auto-resolve to the further-along value (e.g. 'Applied' beats 'Not Applied'); every conflict is overridable per-field before you commit.

An AI 'context note' distills what was genuinely different about the duplicate into a short note appended to the survivor's Notes — and stays quiet when the roles are effectively identical. Editable before you merge.
Safety: an automatic jobs.json backup is taken before the merge, and the duplicate's lead back-references are scrubbed so nothing is left pointing at a vanished role.

releases.title: Out-of-date contact-summary banner on the Contacts page

items.label: The Contacts page now shows a banner when any saved per-person comms summary is out of date (a newer message arrived since it was generated), with a one-click Regenerate per person. This makes a stale generation visible even when it has no open threads — which wouldn't otherwise surface on Priorities.

releases.title: Distinct icon for the chains-column 'Scan links' button

items.label: The chains-column 'Scan this role's messages' button now shows a Radar icon instead of a second ✨ Sparkles — it was sharing the exact glyph of the 'Draft a new chain with AI' button right next to it.

releases.title: Saved (stale-aware) contact summaries + open threads on Priorities

items.label: The per-person comms summary is now KEPT: reopening a contact's summary shows the saved one instantly (no re-run), with a 'stale' badge + Refresh once a newer message has arrived (tracked by message count / latest-comm watermark).

New 'Open threads with contacts' section on the Priorities page: it aggregates the open threads from your saved contact summaries so awaiting-action items surface alongside stale jobs and upcoming interviews. Check off a thread to mark it handled (it drops off); a summary that's gone out of date is flagged with a one-click Regenerate right there.

releases.title: Email import keeps only the new message (trims the quoted reply thread) + AI-classifies the interaction type

items.label: Importing an email (Gmail or Mail.app search → into a chain) now keeps only the NEW top message — the quoted reply history (“On … wrote:” blocks, Outlook “-----Original Message-----” / From:/Sent:/To: headers, trailing “>” quotes) is trimmed at the source, so the search preview AND the imported message are clean instead of carrying the whole prior thread.

Imported emails are now AI-classified to their interaction type (scheduling / follow-up / stale-pipeline / …) on the trimmed body, instead of always landing as “Other”; falls back to “Other” only when AI is unavailable.
Quote-trimming is conservative — a pure forward or an all-quoted body is left intact rather than emptied — and idempotent.

releases.title: Insights comp comparator — configurable target band

items.label: Set a target annual compensation band in Settings → Thresholds, and the Insights → Overview comparator shades it across every posted range: roles whose range reaches your target floor read green (meets/exceeds), those below read amber. The actual-offer dot follows the same coloring.

Leave the target off and the comparator keeps its prior median-midpoint reference line. The band only applies when its currency matches the comparator's dominant currency, so it never distorts a mismatched scale.

releases.title: Insights Phase 6 (final) — AI calls & logs: what the AI spend buys you

items.label: New Insights → AI tab, completing the 6-tab Insights expansion. Cost per outcome (total AI spend, plus job-attached spend per job tracked / interviewed-for / offer), and cost by entity type (jobs vs leads vs settings vs untagged).

Cache-hit efficiency (share of input tokens served from the prompt cache + a rough $-saved estimate), latency by model tier (median + p90), model mix over time, and weekly AI spend across your full history.

Complements the AI Logs page (which keeps the raw call table + by-provider/feature/day breakdowns) rather than repeating it. Reuses the canonical USD/duration formatters and the response/latency stats so numbers read identically across surfaces.

releases.title: Delete a role — permanently, with a clear impact preview

items.label: New Delete button on the job detail header (next to Edit). Opens a dialog that previews exactly what will be removed — messages, interview rounds, and attachments — before you commit.

Contact-aware delete. Contacts who appear only on this role are listed as 'forgotten'; contacts who also appear on other roles are shown as 'kept' (they stay connected to those roles). Nothing you'd want elsewhere is lost.
Two paths, clearly separated: 'Archive instead' (reversible — hides the role from every list and metric) and 'Delete permanently' (gated behind typing the company name to confirm).

Safety: a durable jobs.json backup is taken right before any permanent delete, and the delete now scrubs every lingering back-reference — peer related-job links plus any lead's promotion / prior-opportunity / converted-job links — so nothing is left pointing at a vanished role.

releases.title: Summarize all communications with a person (cross-record AI)

items.label: On the Contacts page (contact-first / per-person view), a 'Summarize all comms with <person>' button gathers every message exchanged with that person across ALL their jobs/leads (oldest→newest) and produces a rollup + key points + open threads, in a dialog. Identity is strict — same canonicalPersonId, else same normalized name (not email/phone broadening) — so it won't merge two different people.
New editable 'Summarize Person' prompt (Settings → AI Prompts) + a 'Contacts' group in the per-prompt context matrix (reads Career + Goals) + a logs/cost catalog entry. Ephemeral (not stored).
Fix: a cross-session compile break in delete-impact.ts (referenced lead.title — leads use headline) was correcting to keep the production build green.

releases.title: Insights Phase 5 — Leads & Recruiter Outreach: your relationship pipeline

items.label: New Insights → Leads & Outreach tab. A relationship-first view: leads by kind (recruiter outreach / head-hunter / warm referral / reconnect / exploratory) and lifecycle status, plus how you surface roles within them (contact-mentioned vs public board vs backchannel) and watch-role status (Watching → Promoted).

A Recruiter Outreach panel — where your recruiter engagements ended up (upgraded to a job / active / dormant / gone cold) — and an engagement-depth table showing how much you invest per relationship (average messages, meetings, and contacts per lead, by kind). On the current data: most roles come through contacts, and warm referrals draw the deepest engagement.

A lead → job conversion stat (promotions, rate, time-to-promotion), clearly framed as a small early sample. The deep merged opportunity-origin sourcing stays on the Pipeline tab — this tab is the lead-internal view.

releases.title: Editable structured resumes, template-structure controls, offer equity-drift check

items.label: Imported (structured) resumes are now EDITABLE inline: an Edit button on the 2-column view opens per-section editors — profile, experience roles + bullets, skill groups, education, certifications, awards, interests, with add/remove rows — and Save writes back into that version (marked 'edited').

Settings → Templates: each resume template now shows whether its 2-column text is cached ('✓ cached' + date), with a 'Structure now' / 'Re-structure' button (one-time AI; reused free for every later import/backfill) and 'Clear'.

Offer analysis now checks base/equity ratio drift: when a revised offer letter exists, the AI compares it against the PRIOR letter and explicitly flags a base bump funded by a shrunk equity grant (per your offer-preferences rule). Previously the engine supported this but the route never fed it the prior letter.

releases.title: Word-wrap sweep on the interview/meeting focus pages — long Debrief action items, questions, concerns, leverage, watch-outs & meeting location now wrap instead of running off-screen

items.label: Fixed the shared item-title field (EditableItem): long titles now wrap + auto-grow instead of scrolling off the right edge. This cascades to Debrief Action items, Questions asked, Concerns and Disclosures, and Prep Questions-to-expect, JD tie-ins and Leverage — anywhere a bold item title can run long.

Converted the remaining single-line inputs that held prose to wrapping auto-textareas: Debrief 'questions I asked', concern 'origin', and the action-item 'Due' field (was clipping in a fixed-width box); Prep watch-outs and disclosure why/when.
Meeting editor: the in-person Location field now wraps a long address/room note (its read-only display already wrapped).

releases.title: Job detail: jump straight to the Offer section from the side nav

items.label: The floating section table-of-contents on a job page now has an 'Offer' item (between Interview Rounds and Communication) that jumps straight to the Offer Status | Offer Progress pair — the top of the offer area, with the Offer details just below.

releases.title: Insights Phase 4 — Activity & velocity: the rhythm of your search

items.label: New Insights → Activity tab. A GitHub-style calendar heatmap of every timeline event per day (jobs + leads, last 20 weeks) shows when your search was busy vs. quiet.

Weekly cadence stacked by milestone — Discovery / Application / Interview / Decision / Outreach / etc. — so you can see whether a given week was about applying, interviewing, or networking (the milestone is derived from the event kind when it isn't tagged).

A response-time histogram (the distribution shape behind the Pipeline's box plot), a comms channel mix split outbound / inbound / system across jobs + leads, and a staleness distribution that flagged how many active roles have gone very quiet.

Consistency: 'first response' time is now one shared definition (lib/computed/comms-dates.ts) used by the Overview, Pipeline, and Activity tabs, so the median matches everywhere; it counts any applied role that drew a reply, not only ones still sitting at 'Applied'.

releases.title: Each pitched role shows its end-client's logo

items.label: Each pitched role now shows its OWN end-client company's logo (a BMO role shows BMO's logo, a Citi role shows Citi's) instead of the engagement's agency logo or a blank initials box. The logo is auto-derived from the company name, with a graceful fall back to initials when it can't be resolved.

Added an optional 'End-client website' field to each pitched/watched role (Add, Edit, and the AI parse review) for the cases where the auto-derived logo misses — type the company's site and that exact logo is used.
Same per-company logo resolution now applies anywhere a role appears — the Recruiter Outreach list & detail, the role detail page, and the Leads watch-role table.

releases.title: Add with AI: describe an engagement in your own words + edit the whole captured conversation

items.label: Add with AI is now a smart 3-way intake: paste a job posting, a recruiter's message or whole thread, OR just describe what's going on in your own words — and the AI routes it to a Job opportunity, a Recruiter Engagement, or a Lead. A clean 'What are you adding?' dropdown (Auto / Job / Recruiter Engagement / Lead) lets you force the destination.

When you describe a situation in prose (e.g. 'a recruiter reached out, we had a call, they're presenting me Tuesday'), the AI reconstructs the back-and-forth as separate messages and flags the recounted ones (vs verbatim pastes) so a call recount is logged as a summary, not a fake transcript.

The review screen now has a full multi-message conversation editor: every captured message is editable — direction (You / Them / System), channel, protocol, kind, subject, time, body, and a 'this is my recount' flag — and you can add or remove messages before saving. The whole thread is attached as comms (each message threaded under the recruiter).

Recruiter engagements that look interview-bound get an 'A real interview may be forming' hint on the review screen, so you know an 'upgrade to Job' prompt will be waiting on the engagement after you save. The AI also fills the engagement's next action from the thread.

releases.title: Weekly Focus digest on the Dashboard (Phase 5)

items.label: New 'This Week's Focus' card at the top of the Dashboard: an on-demand AI digest that reads your LIVE pipeline — stale follow-ups, upcoming interviews & deadlines, pending offers, high-priority roles, and quiet leads — and returns a RANKED 'do this this week' list. Each item names the role and gives a one-line why plus the concrete next step.

The digest is persisted (survives navigation; shows when it was generated + a Refresh button) and is built from the SAME computed signals as the Dashboard cards, so its urgency reads agree with them. It reads your Goals context, and a quiet pipeline returns a calm 'nothing urgent' message with no AI call. Action lives on the Dashboard; trends stay on /insights.
New editable 'Weekly Focus Digest' prompt (Settings → AI Prompts), a 'Dashboard' group in the per-prompt context matrix (reads Goals), and a logs/cost catalog entry.

releases.title: Parse a recruiter's multiple pitched roles at once + retire the legacy single-role model

items.label: Add-with-AI now extracts MULTIPLE pitched roles from a single recruiter message. When a staffing recruiter floats several roles in one note (e.g. BMO via HCL Tech AND Citi via Altimetrik), each becomes its own pitched role on the engagement — with the end-client company and the staffing vendor split apart automatically, instead of being crammed into one.

The parse review screen has a new editable role list: add a role the AI missed, delete a duplicate it hallucinated, and fix each role's title, end-client company, 'via' vendor, seniority, comp, and interest before the engagement is created. Collapsed rows keep it tidy.

Creating an engagement seeds one 'role discussed' timeline event per pitched role (capped, with a '+N more' when a recruiter blasts many), so the engagement's history starts where the conversation really did.

Retired the legacy single-'pitchedRole' model end to end: engagements now hold their roles only as watch roles. Removed the old single-role detail card, the single 'upgrade to job' / 'log discussed role' endpoints, and dropped the deprecated field from every record via a one-shot migration (backed up).
The manual 'New engagement' form gained a 'via (staffing vendor)' field, and 'Graduate to Lead' now carries over all of an engagement's pitched roles (not just one).

releases.title: Insights Phase 3 — Interview & Quality: are the roles you rate highly the ones that go the distance?

items.label: New Insights → Interview & Quality tab. A fit×interest scatter plots every role you scored, colored by how far it got (applied → responded → interviewed → offer), with same-score roles nudged apart so they don't stack.

Calibration check — 'is my judgment predictive?': response/interview/offer rates bucketed by the fit and interest you gave each role. On the current data your instincts hold up: top-fit roles interview far more often than the rest.

Interview-signal distribution: which outcome labels actually show up (Strong Mutual Interest, Mixed Signals, Salary Too Low…), colored by sentiment, pulling from interview rounds, per-job results, AND lead meetings.

'How deep things go': held interview rounds before a role resolved — for the ones that reached an offer vs. ended in rejection (e.g. offers take more rounds; most rejections come before any interview).

Consistency: the new calibration tables and the Pipeline segment tables now nest their stages (no 'more offers than interviews' rows), round counts exclude offer-phase rounds so 'rounds' means the same thing on every tab, and the shared Section / helper logic is de-duplicated across the Insights pages.

releases.title: Update the offer from a negotiation recap — paste a transcript, AI fills your answers

items.label: New '✨ Update from recap' on the Offer card: paste a meeting transcript (speaker labels optional — it infers who's who), a recount in your own words, or the company's email/text reply, and the AI reads it against your recorded asks.

It proposes, for you to review and apply: answers + statuses for each Question (Answered / Asked / Dismissed), statuses + a response note for each Revision (Agreed / Declined / Considering / …), an updated Thoughts summary, and Next-step action items. Every change is a checkbox — nothing is applied until you confirm.
New 'Next steps' section on the offer for action items (who owes what), populated by the extractor and editable by hand (check off / remove / add).

Verbally-agreed comp changes (e.g. a higher base or more options) are captured as an Agreed revision + a 'send the revised letter' action item — never silently rewritten into your recorded base/equity numbers, which keep mirroring the current written offer.

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach list: expand & upgrade each pitched role

items.label: The Recruiter Outreach table and cards now show ALL of an engagement's pitched roles, not just one. Each engagement row has a chevron that expands to a sub-table of every role the recruiter floated — with its end-client company, 'via' staffing vendor, status, fit, interest, and comp.

Upgrade any single pitched role to its own Job right from the list — each expanded sub-row has its own 'Upgrade to Job' button (same per-role flow as the detail page). A role already upgraded shows a 'View job' link instead.
Collapsed rows feature the primary (or best-fit) role with a '+N' badge so you can see at a glance how many roles an engagement carries; '0 roles' reads as a relationship with nothing pitched yet.

The row's ⋯ menu is now lead-level only (Open / Graduate to Lead / Mark dead) — the old single 'Upgrade to Job' moved onto the per-role sub-rows, since an engagement can hold several roles that each become a separate Job.
Manually-created engagements now seed their pitched role into the multi-role model automatically, and search matches across every pitched role's title, company, and vendor.

releases.title: Insights Phase 2 — Pipeline deep-dive + one shared response rate everywhere

items.label: New Insights → Pipeline tab: a conversion funnel with step-by-step drop-off (Applied → Responded → Interviewed → Offer → Accepted), how long each step takes (median + middle-50% box plot for time-to-response / interview / offer), round-type effectiveness (which interview rounds actually advance, small samples set aside), how opportunities ended (furthest stage reached + reason), and the same rates cut by how the role started, seniority, and priority.

ONE response-rate definition everywhere. The Dashboard, /insights, and the /jobs stats used to disagree (≈11% vs ≈30%) because each counted 'responded' differently. They now share a single HYBRID test — applied AND (an inbound message from the company OR the application progressed past 'awaiting') — so all surfaces report the same number (33% on the current data).

Two-track funnel: the conversion funnel is now strictly '% of applied' (each stage a subset of the one before, so no step can exceed 100%), and recruiter-sourced roles that skipped applying and entered at the interview stage are reported separately. The Overview funnel + rates were realigned to match the Pipeline tab — which surfaced that 0% of your applications converted to an offer while all offers came via recruiters.

Honesty guards: every rate shows its denominator, segment/round rates below 4 samples are muted or footnoted rather than shown as a misleading trend, offer-phase rounds are excluded from interview 'advance rate', and charts carry screen-reader summaries.

Insights now sees your WHOLE pipeline, not just jobs. A new 'Where opportunities come from' breakdown on the Pipeline tab merges jobs + leads + recruiter outreach into one origin view (I applied · recruiter-initiated · recruiter outreach · my networking · head-hunter, each with its own icon), a lead → job conversion line, and a top-line on the Overview (N jobs · M leads · K recruiter outreach). A lead that became a job is counted once. The application funnel/timing stay applied-jobs-scoped and are now labeled as such.

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach holds multiple pitched roles

items.label: A recruiter outreach engagement now holds MULTIPLE pitched roles — just like a lead holds multiple watch roles. When a staffing-agency recruiter pitches you several roles (e.g. BMO via HCL Tech and Citi via Altimetrik), each gets its own expandable row with its own company, fit, status, and conversation — instead of being squeezed into one.

Each pitched role carries its own end-client company and an optional 'via' staffing vendor — distinct from the engagement's anchor (the recruiter's agency). The role row shows 'BMO · via HCL Tech'; Add / Edit a pitched role now has both fields.

Upgrade a single pitched role → its own Job, seeded as Skipped / Recruiter Reached Out / recruiter-initiated, with a 'recruiter reached out' pre-job timeline event and the staffing vendor recorded in the job notes. Promote each role independently as conversations get real.
Zero pitched roles is now a first-class state: a recruiter who never floats a concrete role just shows an empty Pitched Roles card — no more forcing a placeholder role onto every engagement.
'Graduate to head-hunter lead' is now a clean kind-flip — the engagement already holds its roles as watch roles, so they carry over as-is (with a legacy fallback for un-migrated records).

Migrated 7 existing engagements' single pitched role into the new multi-role model, automatically splitting inline 'EndClient (via Vendor)' company strings into separate company + vendor fields (Capgemini · via Axiom, Manulife · via Compunnel, Undisclosed · via Miratech, Undisclosed · via Technical Source).

releases.title: Company Brief on the job detail (Phase 4)

items.label: New Company Brief card on the job detail: an AI-generated structured brief — snapshot · recent signals · culture & how they work · why it fits you · sharp questions to ask · watch-outs. Grounded in the job's JD + an optional paste-in research box. NO web access, so it flags uncertain specifics ('verify') instead of inventing them.

Briefs are SHARED per company (stored by normalized company name) — generate once and every job at that company shows the same brief; a note shows how many jobs share it. Generate / Refresh (with a fresh paste box) / inline Edit / Clear.

New 'Company Research Rules' context block (Settings → Context) to steer what every brief assesses, and a new editable 'Company Brief' prompt (Settings → AI Prompts) — both wired into the per-prompt model + context matrix and the logs/cost dashboard.

releases.title: Insights, leveled up (Phase 1) — tabbed workspace + interactive charts + Dashboard synergy

items.label: Insights is now a tabbed workspace — Overview · Pipeline · Interview & Quality · Activity · Leads & Outreach · AI — with a sticky header that mirrors Settings. This is Phase 1 of a larger expansion; the four analysis tabs beyond Overview preview the charts landing in the next phases.

Charts now use the recharts library. The Overview pipeline funnel and the weekly applications-vs-responses trend are interactive recharts charts drawn from a theme-aware palette (new --chart-* CSS tokens) that shifts tone in dark mode like the rest of the app.

Dashboard ↔ Insights cross-links: the Activity, Pipeline-funnel, and Rounds + response-rate cards each deep-link to the matching Insights tab, and the Insights header links back to the Dashboard — reinforcing the split (Dashboard = the high-level right-now snapshot, Insights = the deeper trends/distributions behind it).

Polish: the compensation comparator and chart legends draw from the shared chart tokens (so they theme correctly in dark mode), the funnel guards a zero-applied empty state, and the charts carry accessible labels for screen readers.

releases.title: Template caching + version migration & PDF backfill (Resume/CL v2 — Parts C & D)

items.label: Template resumes are now structured ONCE and cached in Settings (resumeTemplates[key].structured). Importing a template on the Resume page — or backfilling a template-based application — is instant and free after that (no per-job AI call).

New re-runnable backfill (scripts/backfill-resume-cl.mjs): turns your already-uploaded resume.pdf / cover-letter.pdf attachments into 'Sent' versions. Cover letters are free (text extract); resumes are AI-structured but gated to jobs that reached an interview. Dry-run by default — pass --apply (and --limit N / --all) to run; backs up jobs.json first; idempotent (skips a kind already backfilled).

New migration (scripts/migrate-doc-versions.ts): materializes any legacy single tailored-resume / cover-letter into the version history exactly as it already renders (idempotent, backup, legacy fields kept so old data keeps loading).
The structure-resume route returns the cached template structure when present (else structures once and caches it), and the stored 2-column resume schema was factored into a shared ResumeDocSchema.

releases.title: Resume workspace v2 — structured 2-column import + version history (Resume/CL v2 — Part B)

items.label: The Resume page is now VERSION-AWARE with two flavors in one history: a 'Tailored' version is the JD-mapped draft (summary · skills · requirement bullets · highlights, fully editable); an 'Imported' version is your FULL resume rendered in your 2-column layout. Switch versions, 'Mark as sent' the one you actually shared, delete the rest. The Sent version is mirrored to the job's detail card.

Import an existing resume → structured: 'From upload' (the job's resume.pdf) or a template button pulls the PDF text and the AI structures it into profile · experience roles · grouped skills · education · certifications · awards · interests, laid out 2-column (experience left, skills/education/etc. right) to emulate your real resume. Copy the text or a Canva field-map from it.

New 'Structure resume' AI capability (its system prompt is editable in Settings → AI Prompts) — faithful extraction only, never invents content. Uses .nullable() fields so OpenAI strict structured-output accepts the schema.
Fix: a freshly generated/edited cover-letter version now updates the job's Cover Letter card immediately (the sent version is mirrored back to the legacy field).

releases.title: Consistent Settings tab language — wrapping tabs, distinct tiers, cleaner Master Resume note

items.label: Settings tabs now read as a clear three-tier hierarchy: the top tabs are an accent underline, sub-areas (e.g. the AI Prompts categories and the Context sub-tabs) are filled pills, and the deepest level (prompt variants, Master Resume versions) is a light neutral underline — so you can always tell which level you're on.
Long secondary/tertiary tab rows now WRAP instead of overflowing the page — the Interview prompt sub-tabs no longer run off the right edge.
The Master Resume 'always the fallback' hint moved from beside the tabs (where it looked like a button) to a caption line directly below them, and updates per selected version.

releases.title: Cover-letter version history + 'Sent' pointer + PDF/template extraction (Resume/CL v2 — Part A)

items.label: The Cover Letter workspace now keeps a VERSION HISTORY: each Draft / New version / import adds a version, you switch between them, and you 'Mark as sent' the one you actually sent — that Sent version is the canonical letter shown (and the basis for the Canva export). Delete versions you don't want.

Import an EXISTING cover letter: 'Import upload' extracts the text from the job's uploaded cover-letter.pdf (no AI) into a new version, so a letter you already wrote/sent shows its real text. (Template import + resume's structured version history land in Part B.)

Shared version model under the hood (job.resumeVersions / job.coverLetterVersions) with a read-time back-compat shim — your existing tailored resume / cover letter automatically becomes the first 'Sent' version, no migration needed.

releases.title: Cover-letter AI tuned to Alex's real letter format

items.label: Reviewed a real sent cover letter and retuned the cover-letter prompt + the Cover Letter Voice starter to match: a formal-but-substantive opener (name the role, then a specific 'where I've been → where I'm going' hook), a quantified company-specific achievement, a 'what a resume can't convey — how I operate' paragraph, a company-research paragraph, and a confident close with 'Best regards,'. Em dashes are now allowed (they're in your real letters); greeting uses the contact's first name.

releases.title: Fixed dead 'back' buttons after an app update — focus, cover-letter & resume pages navigate cleanly instead of needing a manual refresh

items.label: Root cause was deployment skew: when the app was rebuilt while a tab stayed open, that tab held a stale build manifest, so a client-side navigation (e.g. the top-left back button on a meeting/round/cover-letter/resume page) silently failed to fetch its now-renamed JS chunk — a dead click until you manually refreshed. Enabled Next.js version-skew protection via a per-build deploymentId so an open tab now does a clean full navigation instead of a dead click.

build:prod now stamps a unique id per build (scripts/build-prod.mjs) and writes it to <dist>/DEPLOYMENT_ID; next.config reads it back at serve time so the running server and the assets it serves always agree (no false reloads, even on a bare next start).

releases.title: Jump-to-chain from any opportunity, Communication recruiter-outreach count, and a stale-build fix

items.label: Every chain in a Job / Lead / Recruiter Outreach / Watch-role's Communication card now has an ↗ button that jumps straight to that exact chain on the Communication page (deep-links via ?job=&chain=).
The Communication header now counts recruiter engagements separately — 'N jobs + N leads + N recruiter outreach' — matching the new filter chip.

Fixed: recruiter-outreach engagements were missing from the Communication page entirely. The page's job-wins message dedupe was built from ALL jobs including archived ones — so a demoted engagement (which copies its source job's messages, then archives the job) had every message deduped away and dropped from the list. Dedupe now only considers active jobs.

releases.title: Cover Letter workspace — a per-job page to draft, edit, and export a tailored cover letter (Phase 3)

items.label: New per-job Cover Letter workspace at /jobs/[id]/cover-letter: drafts a complete, tailored letter grounded in your Master Resume + the job's requirements + your fit notes, with a Short / Standard / Long length selector + optional emphasis keywords. A Cover Letter card on the job page links into it.

The letter is fully editable and saved onto the job (Regenerate replaces). Export as plain text (Copy letter) OR a Canva-autofill field map (greeting / body_1… / closing, derived from the letter) for a brand template.

New 'Cover Letter Voice' context block (Settings → Context) — your letter-specific structure/tone/clichés-to-avoid, separate from message Voice & Framing — read by the drafter. The cover-letter prompt is editable in Settings → AI Prompts (Resume & Cover Letter group).

releases.title: Prep board fix: long 'Questions to ask them' and the Leverage 'when to deploy' footnote now word-wrap instead of running off-screen

items.label: 'Questions to ask them' rows now wrap long questions onto multiple lines and grow vertically — they were single-line inputs that scrolled off-screen. The same fix lands on the Debrief board's 'Open items' rows, which shared the primitive.
The Leverage section's per-point 'When to deploy…' footnote now word-wraps instead of running past the edge of the card.

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach is now distinct on the Communication & Contacts pages

items.label: Communication page: a new 'Recruiter Outreach' filter chip (alongside Jobs / Leads / Watch roles), and recruiter-engagement threads now read as a 'Recruiter Outreach' badge instead of generic 'Lead'. The 'Leads' chip now excludes engagements, mirroring the /leads ↔ /recruiter-outreach split.
Contacts page: a recruiter-engagement role now shows a 'Recruiter Outreach' label (with the chat icon) instead of '🌱 Lead', so a recruiter who reached out reads as outreach, not a cultivated lead.
On both pages, the 'Open →' link for an engagement now routes to /recruiter-outreach/[id] (the stripped-down engagement view) rather than the full Lead page.

releases.title: Resume Tailoring workspace — a per-job page to generate, edit, and export a tailored resume (Phase 2)

items.label: New per-job Resume workspace at /jobs/[id]/resume: generate a tailored Summary + Skills line + requirement-mapped Experience bullets + Highlights, all grounded in your Master Resume (focus variant + emphasis keywords). The Tailored Resume card on the job page now links into it.

Every section is editable inline and saved onto the job (Regenerate replaces with a fresh AI pass). Export as labeled sections (Copy all) OR a Canva-autofill field map (summary / skill_1 / bullet_1 / highlight_1 → value) ready to paste into a brand template's data fields.
The tailor-resume AI now also returns a Skills keyword line + Highlights (previously just summary + bullets); existing tailored resumes keep working (new fields are optional).

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach: rich table view, list-level promote actions, and discussed-role timeline events

items.label: Recruiter Outreach now has a rich table view (card ↔ table toggle, persisted, defaults to table) — recruiter, company, role discussed, resume, comp, your interest, status, next action, activity, and message count in one scannable grid, so you can decide a promotion at a glance.

The table now mirrors Jobs/Leads: a dedicated Company column, a Resume column (template / custom / shared icons — track what you sent the recruiter), and a real Activity column (what happened + when). The leading column leads with the recruiter so an engagement no longer reads identically to its role.

Promote straight from the list: every row/card has a ⋯ actions menu — Open · Upgrade to Job · Graduate to Lead · Mark dead — with the same confirm + seeding as the detail page. No click-through needed.

Discussed roles are now timeline events. A recruiter often floats several roles over time — 'Log discussed role' records each as a pre-job, early-stage event (so you keep the history), while the single 'pitched role' stays the front-runner. Setting/changing the pitched role and creating an engagement with a role also log one automatically.

releases.title: Pre-send tone check in the composer — an advisory read of your draft before you send (Phase 1b.2)

items.label: The communication composer has a 'Tone check' button: an advisory read of your finished message — an overall tone label, 1-2 sentences on how it'll land, and 2-4 specific fixes (flags desperation/over-eagerness, oversharing, buried asks, length, typos, voice mismatch). It reads your Voice & Framing + Goals context and NEVER blocks send — it's advice, not a gate, and it doesn't rewrite.
The tone-check prompt is editable in Settings → AI Prompts (Helpers group), keeping every AI prompt tunable. Runs on the light model tier; falls back to a copy-prompt when no API key is configured.

releases.title: Duplicate-detection when adding a new opportunity — warns if a role looks like one you already track (Phase 1b.1)

items.label: Adding a job (manually or via AI parse) now warns if it looks like an opportunity you already track — a non-blocking banner with linked matches across jobs AND lead watch-roles. Match = normalized company (legal suffixes like Inc/LLC stripped) + fuzzy role-title; when a company has several similar roles, secondary fields (location, seniority, employment type, source) differentiate the genuine same-role match from 'other roles at this company'.

Active vs Inactive aware: a live match reads as 'already tracking this', while a prior Inactive one reads as 'you previously tracked this (e.g. Rejected)' so re-encounters are obvious rather than false alarms. Create is never blocked.

releases.title: Settings → AI Prompts is now complete — the last 5 hardcoded/missing prompts are editable (Phase 1a of the AI-enhancements wave)

items.label: Five prompts that were previously NOT editable are now in Settings → AI Prompts: Analyze CSV Import, Suggest Interaction Kind, Suggest Message Links, Audit Fix, and Tailor Resume. New groups 'Classification & Audit' and 'Resume & Cover Letter' hold them.

Override-safe dynamic prompts: 'Analyze CSV Import' and 'Suggest Interaction Kind' embed your LIVE interaction-kind list via a {interactionKinds} placeholder that's auto-filled at run time — so editing the prompt no longer risks freezing or dropping the allowed labels (keep the placeholder in your override).

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach phases 4–6: graduate to Lead, Parse routing, demotion, dashboard & nudge

items.label: Graduate to Lead: when a recruiter becomes an ongoing sourcing relationship, one click converts the engagement into a head-hunter Lead — and its pitched role becomes the new Lead's first watch role (immediately promotable). All contacts, messages, meetings, and timeline carry over.

Parse 'Add with AI' now coexists: a recruiter gauging interest defaults to a lightweight Recruiter Engagement (with the floated role captured as its pitched role), and only a clear ongoing sourcing relationship routes to a head-hunter Lead. You can switch the kind on review; engagements land on /recruiter-outreach.

Demote to engagement: a Job that was really an early recruiter ping can be moved back to Recruiter Outreach. Reverse-absorb re-points its contacts/messages/timeline onto a new engagement and archives the job (reversible). The button shows only on recruiter-initiated 'Skipped' jobs.

Dry-run migration (npm run migrate:recruiter-engagements): backs up, then PRINTS the candidates — existing head-hunter cold pings to relabel + never-interviewed 'Skipped + Recruiter Reached Out' jobs to demote — and writes nothing until you re-run with --apply.

Dashboard now has a Recruiter Outreach card (active / upgraded → Job / went nowhere / total), kept out of the Jobs and Leads metrics. Engagements are excluded from the Leads card to match the /leads ↔ /recruiter-outreach split.

Assisted upgrade nudge: an engagement shows an 'a real interview may be forming' banner when it has a scheduled meeting or interview-scheduling language in the thread — a one-click prompt to upgrade to a Job. Plus a one-click 'Mark dead' on engagement cards.

Bug fix: staleness now recognizes interviewStatus 'Recruiter Reached Out' / 'Interview Requested' / 'Interview Scheduled' as interviewing (they moved off applicationProgress in v3.4 but the stale check still looked for them there), so recruiter-initiated jobs get the correct stale threshold.

releases.title: Recruiter Outreach: a new early-engagement stage between Leads and Jobs

items.label: New /recruiter-outreach page for early recruiter engagements — when a recruiter pings you on LinkedIn to gauge interest. These are NOT job opportunities yet (so they stay out of your Jobs pipeline and metrics) and are lighter than Leads (no anchor relationship, no watch-role portfolio). Under the hood they're a new 'recruiter-engagement' Lead kind, so they inherit the full Communication thread, Contacts, timeline, status, and next-action machinery for free — and they appear automatically on the Communication and Contacts pages.

Each engagement carries one lightweight 'Pitched Role' (title, company, comp, seniority, arrangement, posting URL, your interest level) — the single role the recruiter floated, with none of the watch-role status/promote machinery. It seeds the Job on upgrade.

'Upgrade to Job' button: once a real interview emerges, one click spawns a Job seeded from the pitched role and lands it in the recruiter-initiated state — Application Status 'Skipped', progress 'N/A', interview 'Recruiter Reached Out', initiated by 'recruiter' — plus a backfilled 'recruiter reached out' timeline event. The engagement's contacts, messages, and meetings are copied onto the Job, and the engagement is marked 'converted' with a link back (it stays as history).

Recruiter-engagement leads are filtered out of the main Leads list so the two surfaces stay visually separate even though they share data/leads.json. New 'Recruiter Outreach' nav entry (desktop + mobile).
Added 'Recruiter Outreach' to the What's New feature areas so this pipeline's history groups together going forward.

releases.title: Lead-meeting 'Draft from last meeting' now earlier-only too (parity with rounds)

items.label: Lead meetings now match the round rule exactly: 'Draft from last meeting' only considers a meeting that happened STRICTLY BEFORE the current one — it no longer falls back to a later meeting in the rare out-of-order case (e.g. prepping the first meeting while a later one already has notes). The button gate and the draft-prep route share the same earlier-only check, so the button never shows when there's nothing valid to ground on.

releases.title: 'Draft from last round/meeting' works across jobs AND leads — stricter gating + cross-entity carry-over from a promoted lead's last meeting

items.label: Stricter gating, on jobs too: the 'Draft from last round/meeting' button now appears only when the previous session has recorded substance (a completed date / recap / outcome / debrief). Previously a job round offered it whenever ANY earlier round existed — even an empty, not-yet-recorded one — which produced thin, noisy drafts. Jobs and leads now share one substance check.

Cross-entity carry-over: when a job was promoted from a lead, a round with no prior round to ground on now offers 'Draft from last meeting' — drafting the round's prep from the originating lead's last substantive meeting. Pre-application context (recruiter screen, intro chat, pre-screen) flows across the lead→job promotion instead of starting the first round cold.

releases.title: Real-time notes backfill now leads with AI — flip 'Backfilled' on, paste a whole recap or transcript, and AI splits it into notes and tags each Me / Them / Note

items.label: Turning on 'Backfilled' now auto-switches Capture to AI-assign — the backfill default is paste-a-recap-and-let-AI-tag-it, not manual speaker picking. Turning it off restores the mode you were in (unless you manually switched meanwhile).
'Backfilled' moved to its own control line (was sandwiched among the capture modes, where it read like a 4th mode), with an inline hint that AI-assign is on while it's active.
When backfilling, the AI-assign box grows to fit a full transcript and the prompt now splits a long recap/transcript exhaustively — one paste in, many tagged notes out.
Fixed the Tagged composer's mislabeled 'Backfill mode' hint (now reads 'Backfilled' and points you to AI-assign for auto-tagging).

releases.title: Code health: cleared all 50 React 'set-state-in-effect' lint warnings (documented suppressions — no behavior change)

items.label: Silenced all 50 react-hooks/set-state-in-effect lint warnings with per-site eslint-disable comments that document WHY each is correct. Investigation found every one was a legitimate idiom — SSR/browser-API hydration on mount, dialog draft resets on open, prop-resyncs, and reset-before-fetch — not a bug. No behavior change; lint output is now clean so genuine issues surface instead of being buried. (A deeper refactor to key-remounts / useSyncExternalStore remains optional and is noted in the roadmap.)

releases.title: Two more AI gaps closed — Claude Code chat now drives the card 'translate' + 'polish' verbs, and lead meetings get 'Draft from last meeting'

items.label: Claude Code chat provider now supports the two card AI verbs in copy-prompt mode — Sparkles ('translate an instruction → card edit') and Wand2 ('polish style without changing facts'). Previously they returned 'coming in a follow-up' unless you had an Anthropic/OpenAI key; now they hand you a ready-to-paste prompt (with the fit-card context baked in for fit cards), matching Generate-from-JD. The Translate + Polish dialogs render the copy-prompt the same way Generate does.

Lead meeting prep gained 'Draft from last meeting' — the grounded-draft button interview rounds already had. It digests the previous meeting's recorded outcome, recap, notes, and debrief (concerns / open items / action items / new info / sentiment) and drafts the next meeting's prep from it (append-only, never overwrites). The button appears only when an earlier substantive meeting exists on the lead.

releases.title: Prompt variants — save multiple named versions of any AI prompt, switch the active one, and bundle context per variant

items.label: Settings → AI Prompts: every prompt now has a Variant bar — save multiple named versions (New / Duplicate / Rename / Delete), pick the active one, and edit it in place. The active variant's text is what the AI uses; 'Default (packaged)' restores the built-in. Any prompt you'd already customized shows up as a 'Custom' variant.

Context-aware prompts (parse-listing, emails, outreach, interview, etc.) can BUNDLE context per variant: turn on 'Bundle context' for a variant to give it its own Career / Goals & Interests / AI Authoring Rules selection + Career version. An active bundled variant overrides the Prompt Access matrix for that feature; un-bundled variants inherit the matrix.

releases.title: Real-time notes: 'Backfilled' is now a toggle that works with every input mode — including AI-assign, so you can paste a post-call recap and have AI detect Me / Them / Note while still flagging the entries backfilled

items.label: Replaced the standalone 'Backfill' input mode with an orthogonal 'Backfilled' toggle next to the mode buttons. Backfilled is a property of the entry, not a separate way to type — so it now composes with ALL three input modes: Tagged, By speaker, and AI-assign.

AI-assign + Backfilled = the missing combo: paste / describe what was said after the call and AI splits it into notes and tags each Me / Them / Note, with every resulting entry flagged backfilled (amber framing + the timeline '↻ backfilled' pill).

The toggle defaults OFF on every page load (it is not persisted) — backfilling is an intentional in-session action, so this prevents accidentally flagging genuine live notes the next time you open a different round. The retired 'backfill' mode preference migrates cleanly to Tagged.

releases.title: Start & seed conversations from scratch: log an inbound + your AI reply together, create/attach contacts inline and per-chain, fix the dropped email From, and start a chain for any job from the Communication page

items.label: Replying with AI now keeps the message you received: both the 'Reply to email' composer and 'New chain with AI' log the inbound (from the other party) AND your drafted reply, threaded into one chain — no more orphaned replies where only your side was saved.

Create a contact inline while composing — a channel-aware '＋ New contact' (email / LinkedIn URL / phone) right in the message editor's Linked-contact picker, even on a job that has no contacts yet. The new contact is linked to the message automatically.

Set the contact for a whole chain in one action: a new 'Set contact' control on every chain header (job/lead detail + Communication page) links or creates a contact across all of the chain's messages and pins a stable chainId — fixing '(unknown contact)' chains without editing each message.

Outbound emails composed in the app now default the From / mailbox to your primary address, so a manually-logged email keeps its Gmail/Outlook brand pill and From: row instead of silently saving account-less.

Start a conversation for a job/lead that has no messages yet: a '＋ New conversation' launcher on the Communication page (search any active job or lead) plus a 'Show empty' toggle that lists owners with no chains so you can begin their first one.

releases.title: Add with AI now ingests recruiter outreach — turn a recruiter's first message into a Job or Lead with the contact + message captured

items.label: The parse page (renamed 'Add with AI') now accepts a recruiter's outreach message, not just a job description. A 'What are you adding?' selector defaults to Auto-detect and can be forced to Job description, Recruiter outreach → Job, or Recruiter outreach → Lead.

Recruiter outreach identifies the SENDER and creates a new contact (relationship, head-hunter vs internal, the end client they represent, how-connected), and captures their message as a linked inbound communication (channel + LinkedIn InMail protocol + 'cold-outreach' kind, threaded to the contact).

Recruiter messages auto-set the right statuses — Skipped / Recruiter Reached Out / Initiated-by-recruiter — and seed a 'recruiter reached out' timeline event at the message's time, so you no longer set those by hand.
An editable review panel lets you fix the recruiter contact and their message (title, agency, represented client, links, the text, when it arrived) before saving.

Undisclosed clients are labeled per your AI Authoring Rules ('Undisclosed <industry> Client (via <Agency>)'), and relationship-only 'let's connect' messages route to a Lead (kind: head-hunter) instead of a Job.

The parse prompt + AI output schema were widened to carry routing (Job vs Lead), the contact, the message, and the status defaults — the conventions already in your AI Authoring Rules context block now actually flow into the new record.

releases.title: The Generate-from-JD and Format-JD AI prompts are now editable in Settings → AI Prompts

items.label: New 'Generate & Format (JD)' group in Settings → AI Prompts: the 'Generate from JD' prompt (behind the Fit Analysis + Requirements generate buttons) and the 'Format JD' prompt (behind the AI Format button on the Job Description attachment) are now editable + resettable like every other AI prompt — they were previously hardcoded defaults.

releases.title: AI Logs accuracy pass: unknown types fixed, distinct colors per prompt type, cost math audited to the cent — plus Master Resume tabs

items.label: Fixed: the message-link scorer (scan, email import, new-message checks) was logging as prompt type 'unknown' with no source route — it now logs as Suggest Message Links from a shared wrapper, while routes that set richer context keep winning. Two pre-fix rows remain labeled unknown as history.

Every prompt type now has a deliberately distinct badge color (previously 18 of 34 shared violet) — your high-volume types (interaction kind, subject, message links, section summaries, chain follow-ups) are pairwise distinct at a glance.
