Cost calculator audited end-to-end: token usage comes from the provider's own response (so system prompts + injected context are included by definition), and recomputing from raw token sums matched the stored totals to the fourth decimal for both models — including cached-input billing at the 90%-off rate (27,136 of your gpt-5.4-mini input tokens were cache hits). gpt-4o-mini totals match the public $0.15/$0.60 rates exactly. The one external assumption is the gpt-5.4-mini list price in pricing.ts ($0.75 in / $4.50 out) — reconcile once against your OpenAI usage dashboard if any doubt remains.
Master Resume (Settings → Context) is now three tertiary tabs — General / Leadership / Senior IC — instead of stacked editors; unsaved drafts survive switching tabs.

releases.title: Master Resume focus variants: Leadership vs Senior IC tailoring, emphasis keywords, and the lost-logs case closed

items.label: New: Master Resume focus variants — Settings → Context → Master Resume now holds the general master plus optional Leadership and Senior IC versions. Resume tailoring auto-picks by the job's seniority lean (Lead/Manager/Director/VP → Leadership; IC/Senior IC → Senior IC), with an Auto/Leadership/Senior IC/General override right on the Tailored Resume card. An empty variant falls back to the general master — with a toast telling you so.

New: emphasis keywords on the Tailored Resume card — type the keywords you're tailoring around (e.g. 'RAG evals, pre-sales') and the AI prioritizes bullets that honestly showcase them. The focus and keywords that produced each result are saved with it, so Regenerate remembers.

Closed: the pre-June-5 AI-log recovery (won't-fix, per Alex — local snapshots aged out). Ongoing logs remain durable by design: every entry is fsync'd to a permanent monthly archive AND the active file at write time, with self-healing reads and the /logs health bar watching the high-water mark.

releases.title: The verification sweep: 9 features verified end-to-end, a live-call regression fixed, and 6 backlog builds shipped

items.label: Verified end-to-end (with live AI calls on a disposable demo dataset): live-call mode, all five section-summary prompts + staleness/regen, Draft-debrief-from-transcript append-merge, backfill mode, the Debrief contact picker, linked-docs viewer, AI interaction-typing (incl. custom kinds + proposed labels), Generate-from-JD, prep/debrief persistence, and context-aware prompts. Sixteen roadmap items closed.

Fixed (found by the sweep): live-call mode had stopped hiding the Attach buttons — the v3.78 header redesign dropped their data-affordance tags. Re-tagged on both round and meeting pages; the AI Draft-prep buttons now correctly STAY visible mid-call per the live-mode spec.

Copy-prompt parity: Claude-Code-chat mode prompts for follow-ups, emails, chain follow-ups, and new outreach now carry the same assembled context (Goals, Voice & Framing, …) the keyed providers inject — and the AI-Prompts follow-up preview shows exactly what gets sent.
Regenerated drafts in the message editor now record their AI provenance (aiLogId), so the 'AI call' deep link renders on them like every other AI-written message.

Calendar 'Subscribe' fixed: the webcal:// link Calendar.app refused on localhost is now a copy-the-URL button with the File → New Calendar Subscription hint (pick iCloud as Location to sync to your phone).
Debrief contact picker now offers a Cross-record group — contacts from every other job and lead (deduped by canonical person), so names mentioned in one interview can link to people met elsewhere.
Opt-in: auto-regenerate stale interview section summaries on focus-page open (Settings → AI Provider; one light-tier call per stale section per visit; default off).
Per-section prompt overrides for the five interview section summaries (Settings → AI Prompts → Interview) — per-section wins over the single legacy slot, which stays as the fallback.
Legacy-outreach migration closed by verification: a shape-scan found zero legacy-form messages remain, so there is nothing to migrate; the read-adapter cleanup stays tracked separately.

releases.title: Smart message linking: edit/relink/remove any link, and confidence-tiered auto-link + 💡 suggestions

items.label: Every link on a message is now editable in place: a ⋯ menu on the chip lets you Relink to a different area or Remove it — no need to open the editor. Auto-applied links carry a subtle ✨ marker so you can tell them from ones you set by hand.

Smart auto-linking: the app now scores how confident it is that a message refers to a job area (interview round, offer, attachment, contact) by blending deterministic date/round rules with the AI. Above your 'auto' threshold it links automatically; in the middle band it shows a 💡 suggestion with the confidence % that you confirm (✓) or reject (✗) — and a reject is remembered so it won't nag again. Runs on email import, when you add/edit a message, and on demand.

New 'Scan links' button on a role's Communication card (and the chains column) re-scans all its messages and applies/suggests links — the way to backfill the hundreds you already have, or fix a role after adding a missing round.
Two confidence sliders in Settings → Mail ('Smart message linking') tune the auto and suggest thresholds, with a master on/off. Defaults: auto ≥ 85%, suggest ≥ 55%.

releases.title: Four asked-for features: saved filter views, follow-up nudges, next-round prep from the last debrief, and AI resume tailoring

items.label: New: Saved Views on the jobs FilterBar — name the current filter combination and re-apply it with one click. Views are chips inline in the bar (hover × to delete); stored in settings so they survive restarts. Applying is always explicit, never automatic.

New: follow-up nudges on /priorities — every stale application that has an open message thread gets a 'Draft follow-up →' button that jumps to the job and auto-opens that chain's follow-up dialog (AI drafting and all), ready to send.

New: 'Draft from last round' on interview prep — generates the NEXT round's prep grounded in the PREVIOUS round's recorded outcome, recap, and debrief (open concerns, action items, sentiment), so round 2 prep starts where round 1 actually ended. The plain '✨ Draft prep' button (role + JD + background) finally shipped alongside it. Both append-only: existing prep is never overwritten.

New: AI resume tailoring — paste your resume once into the new Master Resume context block (Settings → Context), then any job's 'Tailored Resume' card generates a summary line + resume bullets mapped requirement-by-requirement to that job's JD, grounded strictly in your real resume. Results persist on the job with per-bullet copy, copy-all, regenerate, and clear.
Master Resume is a full citizen of the context system: editable at Settings → Context → Master Resume, visible in the Prompt Access matrix, and injectable into any context-aware AI feature.

releases.title: First-run setup wizard, sample data, a real welcome, and full navigation on narrow screens

items.label: New: an in-app first-run wizard at /setup — pick how AI runs (Anthropic / OpenAI / Claude Code chat), save the API key (written to .env.local, never leaves the machine), optionally load sample data, and set your sender email. Opens automatically on a truly fresh install; finishing stamps settings.setupCompletedAt so it never auto-fires again (deleting settings.json on a real dataset can't re-trigger it).

New: a fictional sample dataset (6 jobs across the whole pipeline — one mid-interview with rounds, one at offer stage, one rejected — plus 2 leads) loadable from the wizard or the dashboard. Every record is tagged demo-data with a demo- id, and removal (one click) only ever touches records matching BOTH.

New: the dashboard greets an empty tracker with a welcome card (Add your first job · Parse a listing with AI · Load sample data) instead of a wall of zeros, and the Jobs page distinguishes 'nothing tracked yet' (with first-action links) from 'no jobs match your filters'.

New: narrow screens get a real navigation drawer — the hamburger opens every destination (generated from the same NAV list as the desktop sidebar) plus Quick Actions and What's New. Previously only 5 of ~17 destinations were reachable below tablet width.

De-personalized defaults for a portable app: fresh installs no longer default the sender email to Alex's gmail (existing settings keep their saved value), the app metadata description is generic, and first-run-setup.command is a deprecation shim — setup lives in the app now.

releases.title: Area links go both ways — and AI can tag links + System flags for you

items.label: Linked messages now show on BOTH sides: each interview round, contact, the offer, and the Attachments card list the messages linked to them, and clicking one jumps straight back to that message in Communication — auto-expanding the chain it lives in. (The link chips, System badge, and the link picker now appear on the job page's Communication card too, not just the /communication view.)

New ✨ AI suggest in the message editor: proposes which job areas the message references (e.g. a meeting invite → the round scheduled that day, a 'you'll meet Nicholas' → that contact) plus whether it's a System/automated email — each suggestion is a one-click accept, with reasoning shown. The email-import preview got the same power: 'AI links & flags' tags the selected emails before you import, and the import carries the tags.

Imported emails that are clearly machine-generated (Zoom/Teams/Meet invites, .ics attachments, ATS notices) are now auto-flagged System on import — no AI needed — while keeping the real sender in From/To.

Fixed: jumping between linked areas could double the URL hash (#a#b) via the Next 16 router and strand the scroll — same-page jump links are now native anchors, and the chain auto-expander reads the hash defensively.

releases.title: Production mode by default — faster pages, a fraction of the RAM — plus cached reads, durable writes, and a windowed AI-logs page

items.label: Job Tracker.app now launches a true PRODUCTION server: start.command rebuilds automatically when code changed (falling back to the previous good build if a build fails) and serves from an isolated .next-prod. Pages render 3-6× faster and the server idles at ~150MB RAM instead of the dev server's multi-GB footprint — the end of the multi-day RAM-bloat / swap-thrash problem. Development keeps hot reload via the new start-dev.command.

All data reads (jobs / leads / settings) now go through an mtime-keyed in-process cache: unchanged files are never re-parsed, while hand edits and Claude Code chat edits to data/jobs.json are still picked up instantly on the next page load.
Data durability: jobs.json and settings.json writes are fsync'd before the atomic rename (the AI-logs store already was), so a power cut can't leave a truncated data file behind the swap.

AI Logs is now windowed: the newest 100 calls load instantly with a "Load 100 older" button, while the cost dashboard still shows true lifetime totals (computed server-side over the full history via a per-shard parse cache). Deep links to calls older than the window still work.

New scripts/prune-backups.ts archived 72 old migration backups (47MB → one 8.6MB tar.gz in data/backups-archive/, newest 3 of each file type kept in place) — data/ shrank from 89MB to ~50MB. Re-run it any time to rotate future migration backups the same way.
Heavy pages (Dashboard, Jobs, Leads, Communication, Calendar, Contacts, AI Logs) show structured loading skeletons instead of a blank screen while the server renders.

Fixed: the first-ever production build crashed on a zod v4 internal circular-import error ("Cannot access 'h' before initialization"); zod is now resolved natively by Node for server code (serverExternalPackages).

releases.title: Link a message to a round / offer / attachment, and mark person-sent automated emails 'System'

items.label: New: link a communication to specific areas of a job — an interview round, the offer, an attachment, a contact, or a timeline milestone — right from the message editor. Each link shows a "jump to" chip on the message that scrolls you straight to that area on the job page (e.g. a Zoom-invite email → the matching round; an offer email → Offer details). Links are orphan-safe: if you delete the target later, the chip still shows what it pointed at instead of breaking.

New: a "System / automated" toggle on a message, independent of its Direction. For an automated email a real person actually sent (a meeting invite, a scheduling notice), it shows a "System" badge while keeping the real sender in From / To. (Direction "System" still covers genuine no-reply senders — so you now have both.)
You can also link as you compose — the picker is in the Add-message and new-chain composers too, not just when editing an existing message.

releases.title: Import emails as a new chain; 'System' direction no longer flips who sent it

items.label: You can now find & import emails as a NEW chain right from the chains column — the search-mail button sits next to "Import CSV as new chain." Search Mail.app or Gmail for any contact and pull the picked emails into a fresh chain, instead of only being able to append into a chain you'd already opened.

Fixed: marking an inbound email's Direction as "System" flipped the From/To — it rewrote "from Prasanna → you" into "from you → Prasanna." Now the headers only swap when you switch to or from "You (me)"; company↔system keeps who actually sent it. The dropdown also labels it "System (automated)."
Gmail import errors now show Google's actual message (e.g. the one-time "enable the Gmail API" hint) instead of raw JSON, and an expired token nudges you to reconnect in Settings → Mail.

releases.title: Click any filled-in offer-letter blank to edit it in place

items.label: In the letter's Text view, the values the AI filled into template blanks now show with a dotted underline — click one to edit it right there (Enter or click-away saves, Esc cancels). No need to open the whole text editor for a one-word fix.

Editing a filled value also syncs the matching Offer Detail when it maps to one (base salary, bonus, sign-on, equity, currency, start date, respond-by, benefits) — so the letter and your structured fields stay in agreement.

Under the hood: the gap-fill now records exactly what it inserted for each blank, so the right values are the ones made editable. (Letters filled before this update won't have clickable values until you re-run Update blanks.)

releases.title: Offer letters: cleaner icon actions + hand-edit the extracted text

items.label: The offer-letter actions (Edit, Open, Reformat, Remove) are now compact icon buttons with hover tooltips. The AI-powered ones read as AI: Reformat shows the ✨ sparkle (a spinner while it runs), and the Fill / Update blanks button gained a ✨ too.

New 'Edit text' mode in the letter's Text view — edit the extracted Markdown by hand to fix anything the AI mis-read (or a template gap-fill mis-identified as a blank), then Save. It overwrites only the letter's extracted text; your structured Offer Details are left untouched.

releases.title: Dropdowns no longer crash the Communication page; distinct email-import icon

items.label: Fixed a crash that could blank the Communication page (and any screen with a dropdown) on the new React: opening certain Select menus threw "Cannot use a ref … as a container to createPortal." The shared Select now renders the selected value as a plain leaf node, so it's never both a portal target and a children host — fixing every dropdown in the app at once.
The "Import emails" button on a chain now uses a distinct search-mail icon, so it no longer looks identical to the "Draft AI follow-up" compose button beside it.

Connecting Gmail now shows why an attempt failed (redirect-URI mismatch, no refresh token, etc.) right in Settings → Mail, instead of failing quietly and leaving the account "configured but not connected."

releases.title: Connect Gmail and pull email straight into a chain

items.label: New: connect your Gmail (read-only OAuth) and pull email for a contact straight into a chain — the same search → preview → import flow as Mail.app, but faster and without the long scan. The import dialog (✉ on any chain) now has a Mail.app / Gmail source toggle that reveals Gmail once it's connected, and defaults to Gmail when available. Subject, body, To / From / CC and the sent/received time come across automatically. Re-running never duplicates — and because it dedupes on the email's RFC Message-ID, the same email is a single message whether you pulled it from Gmail or Mail.app.

New 'Connect Gmail' card in Settings → Mail with the one-time Google setup documented right there: create a Google Cloud OAuth client, register the localhost redirect URI, paste your client ID + secret, then consent. Includes Reconnect / Disconnect. Your tokens are stored locally in a git-ignored file (data/integrations.local.json) — never in settings.json, never committed.

releases.title: Fill-in-the-blanks shows the raw offer letter side-by-side

items.label: When the AI finds the template blanks (________) in an offer letter for you to fill in, the raw PDF now shows right beside the form — on the right, staying in view as you scroll the fields — so you can see exactly which sections of the actual letter are empty. It stacks below the form on narrow screens, with a Hide / 📄 Show letter toggle. Available both in Attachments → Offer Letters and in the in-card 'Populate the offer first' Analyze flow.

releases.title: Pull emails from Mail.app straight into a chain — no more copy-paste

items.label: New: import emails from Mail.app into a chain. On any chain, the new ✉ button searches your local Mail.app (inbox + Sent) for that contact over a date window, previews the matches — subject, From, date, and which direction (Received vs You sent) — and imports the ones you tick as proper email messages, with To / From / CC and the sent/received time filled in. No more relying on copy-paste to get email into the tracker. Re-running never duplicates (deduped on the email's Message-ID). (Phase 1 — local Mail.app; Gmail-direct connect is the next phase.)
Long unbroken links in a message body now wrap inside the card instead of overflowing past its edge.

releases.title: Re-run the offer response email side-by-side, and safer field re-extraction

items.label: The offer Response-email drafter can now re-generate without losing your edits: once a draft is up, two buttons appear — '✨ Fresh re-draft' (violet — ignores your edits and drafts from scratch) and '✨ Refine w/ current' (sky — builds on what you've written) — and the result is shown side-by-side (Current vs New) so you can compare first.

Resolve the email comparison three ways: Keep current, Replace with new, or ✨ AI-merge — a dedicated AI call that blends both drafts into one, keeping the strongest opener/closing and covering every ask exactly once. (Session-only — nothing is saved until you copy or mark it sent.)

Extract-from-letter is now safe to re-run on an already-filled offer: it only auto-checks fields that are currently empty, and flags any field whose extracted value would OVERWRITE something you already recorded (amber 'overwrites' tag, left unchecked) so you opt in deliberately. Fields whose value already matches are dimmed as 'no change'.
Added 'Take all new' / 'Keep all current' shortcuts to the Extract picker, plus a one-line summary of how many fields would overwrite existing values.

releases.title: Re-run offer analysis: fresh vs. consider-current, side-by-side, with keep / replace / AI-merge

items.label: When an offer already has an AI analysis, the Offer card now shows two distinct Analyze buttons instead of one: '✨ Fresh analyze' (violet — re-analyzes from scratch, ignoring what's recorded) and '✨ Re-analyze w/ current' (sky — re-analyzes while considering the existing analysis so it doesn't re-raise points you've already captured). Jobs with no analysis yet keep the single '✨ Analyze' button.

Either button opens an inline side-by-side review — your Current questions + revisions on the left, the New AI run on the right, each item carrying its tier (must-address / negotiating / high-leverage / low-cost) and category badge, plus the new competitiveness read up top — so you compare before anything changes.

Three ways to resolve the review: Keep current (discard the new run, no change), Replace with new (overwrite), or ✨ AI-merge — a dedicated AI call that unions the two sets, collapses near-duplicate points, and preserves what's unique to each into one clean, tiered set.

releases.title: Interaction types: added Rejection + Offer received, Other pinned to the bottom, legacy kinds cleaned up

items.label: Two new interaction types: 'Rejection' (the company passed, cancelled, or decided not to move forward) and 'Offer received' (an offer or employment agreement was extended) — filling the gaps between Withdrawal and the offer accept/decline kinds.
'Other' now always sorts to the very bottom of the Interaction-type dropdown, below your custom types — so a newly-added label like 'Closing note' lands directly above Other instead of beneath it.

Cleaned up 5 messages carrying orphaned interaction kinds from earlier AI experimentation: offer-document / offer-summary / offer-notification → Offer received, offer-response → Offer negotiation, info-share → Role exploration. Backed-up, idempotent migration (scripts/migrate-legacy-interaction-kinds.ts); no legacy kinds remain.

releases.title: Tidier Offer card: company-prefs hidden until there's an offer, collapsed when empty

items.label: The Company-specific offer preferences block no longer takes up space on jobs that never reached an offer (e.g. withdrawn / no-offer opportunities) — it only appears once an offer is actually recorded, and even then it's collapsed by default until it has content. Cuts unnecessary vertical space on the Offer card.

releases.title: AI interaction-type: inline 'new label' panel, instant availability, readable labels

items.label: When the AI 'suggest type' returns a brand-new type (Other), the message editor now shows an inline 'Add label + apply / Keep as Other' panel below Interaction type — instead of a toast that could slip away — so accepting or dismissing it never closes the message you're editing.

A just-added AI interaction type now appears in the Interaction-type dropdown immediately, in the same session. Previously it was missing until a full page reload, and re-running AI 'suggest type' would reject it as 'outside your active list'.
AI-proposed type labels are now stored in readable sentence case ('Closing note' rather than the raw 'closing-note'), matching the built-in labels; the existing custom type was relabeled.
Message editor tidy-up: Sent at and Linked contact now share one row (Sent at half-width on the left with its note wrapping, the contact picker on the right) instead of stacking full-width.

releases.title: Offer card: shows only at the offer stage + inline negotiation context

items.label: The Offer (details) card now appears only once a job actually reaches the offer stage — an offer is recorded, an offer-status label is set, an offer letter is attached, or an offer-stage round has happened. It no longer shows a 'Record offer' prompt on jobs that are merely interviewing or finished interviews. (The Offer Status / Progress status pair stays always-visible as before.)

Added an inline, collapsible 'Negotiation context' on the Offer card showing the Recap + Outcome of your offer-stage calls (Comp Discussion, etc.) — the same context the offer AI reasons over, now visible right next to the offer.

releases.title: Multi-recipient To/CC/BCC now in the AI draft composers too

items.label: The contact-aware To / CC / BCC fields (chips that read 'Name <email>', a dropdown of the role's contacts excluding whoever's already addressed and your own mailboxes, comma-separated paste, and a skippable 'add this email as a contact' offer) now also appear in the two AI draft composers — 'Create new chain with AI' and 'Draft chain follow-up' — not just the manual message editor.

releases.title: Offer AI now reads your comp/negotiation call notes

items.label: Analyze Offer, the Response email, and Suggest company preferences now inject the Recap + Outcome of your offer-stage rounds (Comp Discussion, Offer Details Discussion, Job Offer, Offer Withdrawn) — so the AI is grounded in what was actually discussed or verbally agreed (e.g. “raised base to $210K, dropped equity in proportion, $300 stipend agreed verbally”) and won't re-raise settled items. Non-offer rounds (interviews, etc.) are excluded.

releases.title: Communication: start a new chain by hand + multi-recipient To/CC/BCC with contact lookup

items.label: New ＋ button beside the ✨ AI and ⬆ Import buttons on a role's chains: log a message you already wrote as its own brand-new chain. Reuses the message editor (channel, direction, recipient, time) and mints a unique chain id so it never merges into an existing thread with the same contact; the chain's purpose is seeded from direction (self- vs company-initiated).

To / CC / BCC are now multi-recipient fields: add people from a dropdown of the role's known contacts (excluding whoever's already addressed and your own mailboxes), or type / paste a comma-separated list. Each address shows as a chip reading 'First Last <email>' when it matches a known contact, matching how the From/To headers already render.
Enter a CC/BCC address that isn't a known contact and you get a skippable inline offer to add them to this role's contacts (optional name) — the chip then resolves to the name immediately.
Linking a contact on a new email now prefills the To field with their address when it's empty.

Chain message bubbles now resolve EVERY email party to 'Name <email>', not just the chain's own contact — a CC'd or BCC'd person who is a different role contact is matched against the full contact list (previously they showed as a bare address).

releases.title: Offer lifecycle automation (P2b): ✨ Analyze guides you to populate the offer first, then analyzes

items.label: When you run ✨ Analyze on an offer whose details aren't filled in yet (an auto-draft or a template letter), it now walks you through populating first — Extract from letter (real-text), Fill blanks (template overlay, no AI cost), or Run OCR (scanned) — then runs the analysis automatically. A populated offer goes straight to analysis as before.
The template gap-fill panel is now a shared component reused by both the Offer Letters tab and the guided Analyze flow.

releases.title: Context: Sparkles scores Fit cards with context, AI Authoring Rules gains listing conventions, Voice & Framing cleanup

items.label: The Sparkles card editor now injects your Career + Goals + AI Authoring Rules context when editing a Fit Analysis card, so 'score this role' / 'add a concern' no longer runs blind. Other card types (notes, core info) stay context-free. Configurable in Prompt Access (Listing & Generation group).

AI Authoring Rules gained a 'Listing data conventions' section (agency/undisclosed-client labeling, low-info-pitch ceilings, title-altitude + working-hours calibration, comp-math, LinkedIn InMail conventions, Job-vs-Lead routing, canonicalPersonId, double-coverage) plus an honest domain/credential-gaps note (MRM, banking SME, voice infra, AWS/Azure).

Populated settings.aiCardBlurbs for jobFitAnalysis / watchRoleFitAnalysis (which reference the scoring rubric) + jobCoreInfo / jobRequirements, so per-card AI edits inherit the scoring/filling discipline.

Voice & Framing: generalized the warm-intel relationship note into a reusable principle (leverage past-account / former-colleague connections, with GM and Verint as examples) instead of naming a specific target employer.

releases.title: Offer lifecycle automation (P2a): uploading a letter auto-recognizes the offer, advances status, and pre-fills the details

items.label: Uploading the first offer letter now auto-creates a draft offer (so the card stops prompting “Record offer”) and advances Offer Status → “Offered Position” only when it's behind — never regressing Negotiating or a terminal status — alongside the existing Offer Progress → “Written offer received”.

On upload the app auto-extracts the readable fields to pre-fill the draft (real-text letters fill base/bonus/dates; template letters stay blank for the guided flow). The draft shows a “Draft” chip + a hint, with base rendered as “—” until populated; saving the form confirms it. Auto-fill only ever touches an unconfirmed draft — it never overwrites a curated offer.
Running ✨ Analyze now advances Offer Progress → “Reviewing terms” (advance-only).

releases.title: Context blocks split: a new Voice & Framing block + a fit-scoring rubric in AI Authoring Rules

items.label: New 'Voice & Framing' context block (Settings -> Context -> Voice & Framing): writing voice, tone (no em dashes/emojis), front-door label, and lead-by-target-role framing. Split out of AI Authoring Rules so the email/outreach drafting prompts (draft-email/follow-up/chain-follow-up/new-outreach) now read writing voice WITHOUT the opportunity-scoring rules.

AI Authoring Rules now carries a real fit/interest scoring rubric (weighted dimensions), honest technology-relevance tiers (1-4), a role-archetype scoring lens, and whyGoodFit/potentialConcerns writing guidance. gen-fit ('Generate fit from JD') now reads it, so it scores against the rubric. Tagging rule updated from 1-3 to rich (7-12) tags.

Goals & Interests enriched: eligibility/work-authorization (Canadian citizen, Ontario, 2-week notice, travel), contract/freelance day-rates + structures, company-signals that raise/lower interest, pipeline operating norms, and a named references inventory. Career context: Dialogflow CX specificity, JavaScript webhook fulfillment, omnichannel.

releases.title: Generic Offer Preferences: equity guidance is now ratio-based, not a fixed dollar target

items.label: Refined the global (generic) equity preference: removed the fixed “~$30K USD” default (that was Superpanel-specific) in favor of the real principle — no required equity amount, keep base at/above floor, and protect the base↔equity ratio when equity is offered. The ideal value / share count scales with role, seniority, and company stage, and a base bump that's quietly funded by cutting the grant (a company-specific signal) is something to push back on to restore the ratio.

releases.title: Two-layer offer preferences: a generalized global block + per-company preferences the AI drafts

items.label: The global Offer Preferences block is now written as conditional concepts that adapt to each offer instead of baking in one company's specifics — e.g. 'if equity is offered, preserve ~$30K nominal; if not, weigh against base', 'if benefits are a stipend rather than a group plan, target a real dependent plan', 'if PTO is limited and carryover is prohibited, ask for ~5 days; unlimited PTO is fine as-is'. Your underlying targets are kept.

New per-opportunity Company-specific offer preferences on the Offer card: jot seed notes, hit ✨ Generate to have the AI draft prefs tailored to THIS offer (group plan vs stipend, equity present/absent, PTO/carryover…) from the letter + your notes + your global prefs, then edit + save. Stored on the job.

Analyze Offer and the Response email now inject BOTH layers — your generic global preferences and the company-specific ones — so asks adapt per company (no stipend push when there's a strong group plan, no carryover push under unlimited PTO).
Fixed: the offer-letter gap-fill prompt overrides (Identify / Fill Blanks) were missing from the settings schema and wouldn't have persisted if edited — now saved correctly.

releases.title: Smarter offer analysis: an Offer Preferences brain, a legal-aware tiered Analyze, and one combined response email

items.label: New Offer Preferences context block (Settings → Context → Offer Preferences) — your floor numbers, things to always check, IP / side-work protections, clauses to push back on, and negotiation/email tone. Seeded from your offer-review notes; both offer AI features now read it.

Analyze Offer is now legal-aware and tiered. It flags referenced-but-unattached documents, verbal terms not captured in writing, equity-math mismatches, and Ontario termination / non-solicitation / IP-carveout / jurisdiction-mismatch patterns — each tagged must-address-before-signing vs negotiating (questions) or high-leverage vs low-cost (revisions), and shown as grouped sections on the Offer card. Plumbed a prior-offer snapshot input for equity-ratio drift.

The offer email now folds BOTH your open questions AND your revision asks into a single, well-grouped response email (one round-trip to their counsel). Renamed “Questions email” → “Response email” (feature offer-question-email → offer-response-email).

releases.title: Offer letters: AI fills the template blanks (________) — no OCR cost

items.label: Many offer PDFs are a fillable template whose typed-in values (name, role, salary, start date, location) sit in an overlay the text layer can't read — so the extracted text is full of “________” blanks. A new “Fill in blanks” action (Offer Letters → Text) runs an AI to find every blank and infer what it is, then you fill them by typing values and/or describing them in plain English — a second AI slot-fills the letter text, leaving everything else untouched. No OCR cost.

Filling also auto-updates the matching Offer Details (base salary, start date, currency, response deadline) on the Offer card, and preserves the original blanked text as a backup so re-extracting can't lose your fills — toggle Filled ⇄ Original (blanks).
Both new prompts — Identify Blanks and Fill Blanks — are visible + editable in Settings → AI Prompts → Offer, and model-selectable under Per-prompt models.

releases.title: Backend rename: jobStatus → offerStatus (the field name now matches the Offer Status UI)

items.label: The core job field “jobStatus” is now “offerStatus” end-to-end — data, schema, API, /jobs filters + column, and the customStatuses key — so the backend name finally matches the “Offer Status” label in the UI. A one-time migration renamed all 101 jobs (with a timestamped backup), and a back-compat read still accepts older or hand-edited data using the old key.

releases.title: Offer letters: Document⇄Text toggle + extract-text, a Revised-offer chip, and a questions-email drafter

items.label: View any offer letter two ways — the rendered PDF (Document) or its extracted Markdown (Text) — via a toggle. Letters added before extraction existed get an instant “Extract text” button, and scanned PDFs an “Run OCR (AI vision)” button, right where the text would be.
New “✨ Questions email” on the Offer card drafts an email asking your open offer questions (editable + copyable), then can advance Offer Progress to “Questions sent”.
Adding a revised (v2+) offer letter now advances Offer Progress to a new “Revised offer received” stage (advance-only).

releases.title: Scanned offer letters: one-click AI vision OCR

items.label: Scanned / image-only offer-letter PDFs (no selectable text) now show a “Run OCR (AI vision)” button — it transcribes the PDF with your AI model into Markdown, so Extract details / Analyze / View text light up just like a normal text PDF.

OCR is manual and cost-aware (page-capped, uses your configured AI provider), with an editable “Offer: OCR Letter” system prompt in Settings → AI Prompts. This completes the Offer Letters overhaul: versioned letters → inline preview → import-from-folder → AI text/Markdown → fill-from-letter → vision OCR.

releases.title: Offer letters get smart: auto text-extraction, AI Markdown, fill-from-letter, and an Offer Progress cascade

items.label: Adding an offer letter now auto-extracts its text to a sidecar and (with an API key) reformats it into clean Markdown the AI can read — on both upload and import-from-folder.

New “✨ Extract from letter” on the Offer card reads the letter and proposes terms (base, bonus, sign-on, equity, currency, start date, deadline, benefits) for you to review and pick — it fills your existing offer, never overwrites silently.
“✨ Analyze” now grounds its competitiveness read and questions in the actual offer-letter text, not just the structured fields.

Offer Progress auto-advances when you add a letter — “Written offer received” for the first, and “Reviewing terms” when a revised letter arrives mid-negotiation (advance-only; it never downgrades a stage you set). A written letter also keeps the offer phase active so the cards stay editable.
Per-version “View text” / “Reformat” on the Offer Letters tab, and editable system prompts for the new “Offer: Format Letter” and “Offer: Extract Details” steps in Settings → AI Prompts.

releases.title: Offer Letters, versioned: inline PDF preview, version tabs, and import-from-folder

items.label: Offer letters are now versioned — each upload/import becomes v1, v2, v3… with an optional tag (Verbal / Revised / Final) and a note you can edit inline.
Click a version to preview the offer PDF inline right in the Offer Letters tab, with quick Edit / Open / Remove actions.

New “Import from folder” button copies an offer letter straight from your Job Search folder (or anywhere on disk) into the job — alongside the existing browser upload. The original file is left untouched.
Settings → Data: set a default folder the import picker opens in (blank = your Job Search folder); the picker also has one-click Job Search folder / Home shortcuts.

releases.title: Bring-your-own round types (jobs) and meeting kinds (leads)

items.label: Add your own interview/offer round types (jobs) and meeting kinds (leads) in Settings → Statuses → “Round & Meeting Types.” Custom values appear in the round and meeting dropdowns alongside the built-ins and persist on rounds/meetings just like a built-in.
Custom round types behave as ordinary interview rounds — only the built-in offer rounds (Comp Discussion, Offer Details Discussion, Job Offer) keep Offer Status editable mid-interview.
Custom values are plain text (no badge colors) and are de-duplicated against the built-ins (case-insensitive), so re-adding an existing name is a no-op.
Fixed Attachments → Other (extras) download links returning 404 — they now preserve the file's subfolder instead of using the bare filename.

releases.title: Offer detail layout: Offer Progress now sits beside Offer Status, and Interview Result is a full-width card below the rounds

items.label: Offer Progress now always appears next to Offer Status as a pair (it previously left an empty cell until an offer was in motion). Before an offer is in motion it shows a locked “N/A” with an explainer; it unlocks once you record an offer or set an offer-related status — and auto-resets if the job leaves the offer phase.

Interview Result is now a single full-width card with Positive on the left and Negative on the right, repositioned below Interview & Offer Rounds and above the Offer Status / Offer Progress row for a more logical top-to-bottom flow.

releases.title: Backlog sweep: /jobs hydration fix, clearer Offer Status dropdown + errors, offer-progress auto-reset, and a competitiveness read in AI Analyze

items.label: Fixed a React hydration mismatch on the /jobs table — the role/freshness icons no longer throw a console error on load (their hover tooltips moved to a stable wrapper, keeping accessibility intact).
Setting an Offer Status too early now returns a clear message (HTTP 400) instead of a confusing 404.
Offer Progress auto-resets to N/A when a job leaves the offer phase (offer cleared + status no longer offer-related), mirroring how Interview Progress behaves.
AI Analyze on an offer now leads with a short competitiveness read (below / at / above / unclear vs the market or target range), above the questions and revisions.

The Offer Status dropdown groups the no-offer terminal outcomes (No Offer Made, Went with Another Candidate, Withdrew from Process, Interview Process Ended) under a separator + “No-offer outcomes” header.

releases.title: Calendar subscription events now include who you’re meeting with and your prep notes — not just the title and video link

items.label: Your calendar subscription (and the exported .ics) now folds the key context from each interview and meeting into the event itself: who you’re meeting with (name + role) and a short prep summary, shown above the “Open in Job Tracker” link. Before, synced events only carried the title and the video-call link.
Data fix: the Compass Group (CDAI) Round 1 recruiter screen had been corrupted by the old timezone bug (it showed 7:00 PM, completed 3:30 PM); corrected to 11:00–11:30 AM on May 21.
Data fix: the Voices Round 1 phone screen had drifted to 9:00 PM through repeated edits; corrected to 1:00–1:30 PM on May 22, matching the prep note and the recruiter’s email.
Data fix: the Superpanel “R3 Comp Discussion” debrief note still described a ~60-minute call; updated the wording to ~30 minutes (12:00–12:30 PM ET) to match the corrected duration.

releases.title: Fixed interview/meeting times that disagreed between the calendar, the round page, and the edit form (a timezone bug)

items.label: Bug fix: the interview-round edit dialog showed the wrong time. Round times were stored in UTC, and the form string-sliced the raw value into the time field — so a noon interview showed as 4:00 PM, and saving shifted it +4 hours. The form now converts through the real instant (DST-correct), shows the correct local time, and round-trips cleanly. Same fix applied to the schedule-interview defaults, completed-at, follow-up-sent, and lead-meeting saves.

Round and meeting focus headers now show the full start–end time (e.g. “12:00 PM – 12:30 PM”), computed the same way as the calendar (scheduled time + duration) — so the calendar, the round page, and the edit form all agree on one time.
Data fix: the Superpanel “R3 Comp Discussion” round had conflicting durations (60 min + 1:00 PM end, but completed at 12:30); corrected to 30 minutes (12:00–12:30 PM).

One-shot migration normalized 75 round/meeting timestamps from UTC to the app's America/Toronto offset (instant-preserving), matching the debrief and real-time-notes convention so the old wrong-time display can't recur.

releases.title: Richer round/meeting types (Comp Discussion, Offer Details Discussion & more) that keep Offer Status editable

items.label: New round types when adding a round: Pre-Screen, Hiring Manager Reconnect, Comp Discussion, Offer Details Discussion, and Follow-up Meeting (alongside Recruiter Screen, Technical, Job Offer, etc.). The card is now “Interview & Offer Rounds.”

Smart unlock: adding a Comp Discussion / Offer Details Discussion / Job Offer round keeps Offer Status editable even mid-interview — so a comp or offer follow-up meeting won't re-lock it. The server gate and audit rule honor the same rule.
Lead meetings gained matching kinds (Comp discussion, Offer discussion) that carry over to the right round type when a lead is promoted/absorbed into a job.

Docs: refreshed the long-stale status-enum reference in AGENTS.md to current reality — user-extensible fields, the real values (including Offer Status + Offer Progress), and the round/offer-stage types. Completes the 5-phase offer-management revamp.

releases.title: New “Offer Progress” pill — track where an offer stands, filter by it on /jobs, and customize the steps

items.label: Added an “Offer Progress” field that tracks where you are within an active offer — seeded with Verbal offer only · Written offer received · Reviewing terms · Questions sent · Revisions requested · Awaiting revised offer · Comparing offers · Decision imminent (plus N/A). It's the offer-phase counterpart to Interview Progress.
Shows as its own card on the job detail page right after Offer Status (appears once an offer is in motion), and as a new “Offer Prog” column + tri-state filter on the /jobs Opportunities page.
Fully customizable in Settings → Statuses (add/remove your own values + badge colors), like every other status field. Changes are tracked on the job timeline.
Migrated all existing jobs to default Offer Progress = N/A (backup taken; migration is idempotent).

releases.title: Calendar: click a message to peek the whole conversation in a side card before jumping to Communication

items.label: Clicking a message — a Week Grid chip/line or a row in the day panel — now opens a chain peek card to the right of the day panel instead of jumping away. It shows the whole conversation as message bubbles (You vs the contact) with the message you clicked highlighted and scrolled into view.

From the peek card, 'Open in Communication →' jumps to that exact chain; ⌘/Ctrl-click a message in the grid still opens the Communication page directly (new tab). The calendar page widens to a three-column layout when the card is open.
Chains are reconstructed from the calendar's own message events (every message is an event), and message events now carry a subject + short body preview to render the bubbles — no extra data fetch.

The calendar is now an app-shell on desktop: the toolbar (week being shown), the grid, and the day panel stay fixed in view — only a long conversation scrolls, inside the chain card itself, instead of scrolling the whole page and pushing the grid out of sight. The day panel and month grid also scroll internally when tall.

releases.title: “Job Status” is now “Offer Status” — always visible, and it stops hard-locking once you reach the offer stage

items.label: Renamed “Job Status” → “Offer Status” everywhere — the detail card, the /jobs table column + filter, Settings → Statuses, the edit form, and the xlsx export. Label-only: your data and saved filters are unaffected (the field is still jobStatus under the hood).

The Offer Status card is now always shown on active jobs. In early stages it reads “N/A” and is locked with an explainer — so a role with an interview result (e.g. 66degrees) and one without yet (the reengaged Superpanel role) now both show the card instead of one silently hiding it.

Smarter lock: Offer Status unlocks once you've recorded an interview result or an offer exists — and stays unlocked. A post-offer follow-up meeting that flips interview status back to “In Progress” no longer re-locks it, so you can keep negotiating. It still blocks setting a verdict prematurely from scratch.
The server gate and the audit rule were relaxed the same way, so they no longer block a legitimate mid-process Offer Status or flag it as a data-quality issue.

releases.title: Calendar Week Grid: readable message chips when zoomed (time + who, decluttered with leader lines) + keyboard/pinch zoom

items.label: Zoomed-in Week Grid messages now show time + who they're with (not just a direction arrow). They use the full column width so the label fits, and click through to the conversation.

When several messages land too close together, they no longer stack into illegible arrows: each is pushed down to a readable slot with a thin leader line + dot back to its true time, and they sit side-by-side when the column is wide enough to fit more than one.

Zoom with the keyboard (⌘/Ctrl with + and −) or a trackpad pinch (ctrl + scroll), in addition to the on-screen buttons. The grid still auto-scrolls to business hours when you zoom so you never land in dead space.

releases.title: AI offer analysis: one click surfaces the questions to ask and revisions to request on a job offer

items.label: New ✨ Analyze button on the Offer card runs an AI pass over the recorded offer — weighing the role, the market/target range, and your career goals — and proposes (a) questions to ask / get clarity on and (b) concrete revisions to request, each with a one-line rationale.

Review-and-pick: suggestions appear in a panel with checkboxes (all pre-selected); keep the ones you want and they file straight into the Offer card's Questions list (tagged AI) and Revisions list. It won't duplicate items you've already added.

Configurable like every other AI feature: choose its model/tier in Settings → Prompts (Per-Prompt Models), edit its system prompt (Prompts → Offer), and tune which context it reads (Context → Prompt Access → Offer). Every call is logged to the AI Logs with full attribution. No API key? It falls back to a copyable prompt.

releases.title: Calendar Week Grid gets a vertical zoom so you can actually read messages, and the Week List is taller

items.label: Week Grid now has a vertical zoom (Fit → up to ~10× pixels-per-hour). Zoom in and a dense cluster of messages spreads apart so individual ones are clickable; the view auto-scrolls to business hours on zoom so you don't land in empty early-morning space.

When zoomed in, messages stop being thin lines and become labeled chips (time · direction · who it's about) laid out in a left lane, while interviews/meetings keep the right of the column — so you can read who a message is about without hovering. Zoomed out, they stay thin chronological lines for the overview.
Week List rows are taller, giving the per-role message breakdown (“Company · N messages”) more vertical room on busy days.

releases.title: Offer capture: record written offers with notes, revisions, and questions to ask — plus an Offer Letters attachment tab

items.label: The Offer card now captures far more than the numbers: a Thoughts box for your running reactions, a Revisions list of changes you may ask for (each cycling Considering → Requested → Agreed / Declined / Withdrawn), and a Questions-to-ask/clarify list (Open → Asked → Answered → Dismissed, with an optional answer field). All manual for now — AI will surface the questions for you in the next release.
New “Offer Letters” tab in Attachments for the written offer or signed contract itself (PDF, Word, or a photo), kept separate from “Other”, with working download links and one-click remove.

The Offer card now appears as soon as interviewing is underway (or once any interview result is recorded) with a compact “Record offer” prompt — so a written offer can be captured the moment it lands instead of staying hidden until a status is set.

Offer activity is tracked on the job timeline: recording an offer logs “offer received”, later edits (including notes / revisions / questions) log “offer updated”, and uploading an offer letter logs an attachment event.
Data model: OfferDetails gains thoughts / revisions / clarifications and Documents gains offerLetters — all optional and defaulted on read, so existing offers keep working with no migration.

releases.title: Calendar week views (List + hour-by-hour Grid), per-event month dots, and a fix that makes the calendar feed subscribable

items.label: The Week view now has a List ⇄ Grid toggle. List shows each day's events plus its messages collapsed by role/opportunity (“Company · N messages”), and the column grows tall enough to show them all. Grid is an hour-by-hour time grid that positions interviews/meetings by start time + duration, with all-day items (deadlines, applied, reminders) pinned in a row up top.

In Week Grid, messages render as thin chronological lines at the exact time they were sent (amber) or received (sky) — point-in-time marks sitting under the interview blocks — so a day's comms cadence reads at a glance without cluttering the timed events.

Month “Dots” view now draws one dot per event (two interviews on a day = two violet dots) instead of one dot per type, so density is visible at a glance. Messages stay a compact “N msgs · K roles” count since they're too numerous to dot.

Bug fix: the calendar feed (/api/calendar) sent “content-disposition: attachment”, which broke live subscriptions — Calendar.app would just loop on the subscribe URL. The feed now only forces a file download for the explicit “Export .ics” button (?download=1); the subscribe feed omits it. Verified live: subscribing works with the http:// URL (not webcal://), syncing interviews + deadlines through to iPhone via iCloud.

releases.title: Timeline tracking overhaul: silent actions now log, events are editable + backdatable, and missing history is reconstructed across active roles

items.label: Marking a resume as “Sent” — and which template you sent (e.g. Senior IC) — now records on the job timeline. Previously this saved silently with no activity entry, which is what kicked off this whole pass.

Granular auto-tracking for actions that were invisible before: interview-progress changes, round reschedule / cancel / result-change / removal, offer removed or edited, resume & cover-letter PDF (re)assignment, and resume/cover-letter choice changes. (Also fixed an old bug where only the LAST of several added rounds logged.)

Editable timeline events — hover any event for a pencil to fix its time, edit its text, or delete it. Built for “I’m logging this now but it actually happened earlier”: moving an event re-sorts the timeline AND shifts the Activity / staleness tracker, and the event gets a subtle “↻ backfilled” badge.

Backdate at the moment you change a status — the Application / Interview / Job status pills now ask “When did this happen?” (Happened now is one click; or pick an earlier time). Backdating moves both the timeline event and the status’s “last updated” stamp so everything agrees.
Subjectless phone / verbal / LinkedIn touches now show a channel label (e.g. “LinkedIn message”, “Phone call”) on the timeline instead of a blank “Outreach sent”.

Backfilled missing historical activity across recently-active roles — resume sends, round completions, and interview progress/results derived from existing data — each flagged “↻ backfilled” and fully editable. 66degrees, both Compass roles, Genesys, Superpanel, Electric Mind and more now read as complete stories.

Near-simultaneous status changes now group into one “N updates” node on the timeline — if you set interview status, application progress and interview progress within a couple of minutes, it reads as one update with each change listed beneath (still individually editable). Purely time-based, so fixing a time splits an event back out.

One-click delete — a trash icon on each timeline event (hover) removes a mis-logged entry without opening the editor. Handy when the wrong status got updated and you re-did it, leaving a duplicate on the same label.

releases.title: Calendar revamp: a two-pane workspace — month + week views, a docked per-day panel, a dot-density grid, richer event types, and messages collapsed by opportunity

items.label: New two-pane layout: a month or week grid on the left and a day panel docked on the right. Today is selected by default; click any day to see everything that happened or is scheduled on it. The old grid capped each day at 4 items — now nothing is hidden.

The day panel sorts By type (offers ▸ interviews & meetings ▸ applications ▸ deadlines ▸ messages) or Chronologically, and every item deep-links to the exact activity: an interview opens its round focus page, a meeting its meeting page, and a message jumps straight to that Communication chain.

Messages collapse by opportunity into one expandable banner per day — “N messages · M chains · ↑sent ↓received” with role tags — so a 30-message day stays readable instead of burying your interviews. Expand to see each message (time · direction · channel · contact) or open the whole thread in Communication.

Richer event types: added offer received, offer withdrawn, accepted-offer start date, application deadlines (pre-application, all-day), inbound messages received (not just sent), and soft “next action” / “next steps expected” reminders — alongside the existing interviews, meetings, applied, offer deadline, and sent messages.

Month grid gains a Pills ⇄ Dots density toggle. Dots show one colored dot per event type with a hover breakdown, while messages stay a compact “N msgs · K roles” count (a deliberate choice — a busy comms day doesn't fit a single dot). An interactive legend lets you filter event types in/out, and your view preferences (month/week, pills/dots, sort, filters) persist across reloads.

Application deadlines now appear on the calendar and in the .ics feed (completes the queued calendar-app-deadlines item). The subscribed/exported feed includes interviews, meetings, offers, and deadlines, but deliberately excludes message history and soft reminders so your real calendar stays clean.
Bug fix: offer-cycle rounds (“Job Offer” / “Offer Withdrawn”) were rendering as violet interview events — they now read as offer events at the top priority tier.

Bug fix: events are now bucketed by local day and ordered by true instant, so a late-evening message stored in UTC no longer lands on the next day and chains no longer sort out of order when timestamps mix timezone offsets.

releases.title: Interview focus header redesigned: a constant-height sticky bar (identity · status · section nav, never lost) with the call logistics scrolling away beneath it — no more collapse jump or oscillation

items.label: Replaced the resize-on-scroll header (one sticky element that swapped between a tall card and a short bar) with a scroll-away design. A constant-height sticky bar — back link · round/meeting title + status meta · Result · Edit · Live mode · the Jump-to section strip — stays pinned at all times. The header and section nav are never lost.

The call logistics (method · join link · attendees · attach · attachments/links) now live in a normal card right below the sticky bar that simply scrolls away under it as you scroll down — reclaiming its space with ZERO layout jump, because nothing's height ever changes. This eliminates the ~200px content lurch the old collapse caused.

Because the sticky bar never resizes, the scroll-anchoring oscillation/freeze class of bug is gone by construction — no scroll listener, no collapse state, no IntersectionObserver. Verified: bar height stays a constant 86px at scroll positions 0 / 150 / 600, with no scroll drift.

Tuned spacing so nothing tucks behind the bar: the sticky Real-time column now pins just below the bar (92px), and section jumps land 96px down (clear of the 86px bar). The bar is opaque so content scrolling under it is hidden cleanly.

releases.title: Bug fix: interview focus header no longer glitches/freezes when slow-scrolling, and the sticky bar is now opaque so it cleanly hides (not bleeds through) content scrolling under it

items.label: Fixed the sticky interview header rapidly collapsing and re-opening (and freezing the page) on a slow scroll. Root cause: collapsing the header shrank its layout box ~200px, the browser's scroll-anchoring then nudged the scroll position to compensate, which re-crossed the collapse threshold → re-expand → reflow → loop. Fix: disabled scroll-anchoring on the scroll container (`overflow-anchor: none`) so the shrink can't perturb scroll position, plus a hysteresis band (collapse and re-expand use different thresholds) so a value sitting on the line can't flip-flop frame to frame.

Made the sticky header background fully opaque (was translucent + blurred). The translucency let the Prep header (Expand all / Summarize, etc.) bleed through faintly as it scrolled under the bar, which read as the section strip 'covering' it. Solid background + a subtle shadow when collapsed makes the bar look intentional and hides tucked-under content cleanly.

releases.title: Interview section navigator moved into the sticky top header — a horizontal 'Jump to' strip that covers no content (replaces the floating side rail that overlapped the work area)

items.label: Reworked the interview focus-page section navigator from a floating fixed side rail (which overlapped the work area / sidebar) into an in-flow horizontal 'Jump to' strip that lives at the bottom of the sticky top header. Because it's normal-flow content inside the always-pinned header, it stays reachable while you scroll AND covers nothing.

The strip stays visible in both header states — full when at the top of the page, and in the dense collapsed bar once you scroll. Active section is still highlighted by scroll position, and clicking a chip smooth-scrolls to that section.

Four entries: Prep + Real-time · Overall notes · Debrief · Outcome (Prep and Real-time stay merged since they're always side-by-side). Each chip carries the same icon shown next to its section heading on the page.

releases.title: Bug fix: nested-button hydration error on the job detail page (chain purpose pencil was rendered inside the expand button)

items.label: Fixed a React hydration error ('<button> cannot be a descendant of <button>') on every job detail page with a communication chain. The inline chain-purpose editor (the pencil added in v3.76) renders its own <button>, but it was sitting inside the expand/collapse row — which is itself a <button> — so the two buttons were nested, which is invalid HTML.

Moved the chain-purpose pencil out of the expand button and into the right-side action cluster, alongside the AI summary / follow-up / import icons — the same convention the other interactive controls already follow (per the existing v3.5 'action icons sit outside the expand button' rule). The CommunicationStreams version was already correctly inside a <div>, so it needed no change.

releases.title: Interview focus ToC: hugs the sidebar's inner-right edge and expands leftward over it (no more covering the work area), section icons now show next to each page heading too

items.label: Repositioned the floating section navigator: instead of sitting at the screen's left edge (where it overlapped the app sidebar), it now hugs the inside-right edge of the sidebar. Uses `useSidebar()` to track the current sidebar state — when the sidebar is in full mode (224px) the ToC sits at 264px, in icons mode (64px) it sits at 104px, when hidden it sits at 40px from the viewport's left.

Expansion grows LEFTWARD over the sidebar area instead of rightward over the work area — the right edge of the panel stays anchored at the same pixel position as you toggle expand/collapse, so the labels never cover Prep / Real-time / Debrief content. Verified in a live Chrome session: collapsed rail right=264px, expanded right=264px (unchanged), expanded left=108.6px (grew leftward, overlaps the sidebar).

Merged Prep + Real-time into a single ToC entry. They're always side-by-side on xl: viewports (left 70% + right 30%) so two separate entries were a no-op duplicate — clicking either scrolled to the same row. Now just `Prep + Real-time` · `Overall notes` · `Debrief` · `Outcome` — 4 entries.

Added the matching icon next to each section's heading on the actual page so the ToC ↔ page mapping is unambiguous: BookOpen on Prep, Radio on Real-time, FileText on Overall notes, ClipboardList on Debrief, Trophy on Outcome. BoardHeader (shared by Prep + Debrief) takes a new optional `Icon` prop.

releases.title: Roadmap: toggle-off filters, colour-matched active chips, a section Table of Contents, and collapsible sections

items.label: Filter chips now toggle: clicking the active chip again clears it back to All. When a Type / Effort / Value chip is selected it lights up in that option's own colour (e.g. Medium effort goes yellow, matching its badge).

New right-rail Table of Contents lists every section (New feature / Enhancement / Bug fix / Needs verification / Completed) with counts — click to jump (it expands + scrolls to that section). Each section is collapsible via its heading, plus a Collapse-all / Expand-all toggle in the ToC.
The 'Show completed' button dropped its (N) count — that number now lives in the analytics cards at the top.

releases.title: Interview focus pages: floating section navigator (Prep / Real-time / Overall / Debrief / Outcome) — collapsible icon rail on the left edge

items.label: New floating side TOC on every interview focus page (round + lead-meeting), pinned to the LEFT edge so it doesn't fight the sticky Real-time notes card on the right. Five top-level section buttons: Prep / Real-time / Overall notes / Debrief / Outcome, each scroll-jumping to its anchor. Plus Top, Up-one-section, Down-one-section, and Bottom shortcut buttons (mirrors the JobDetailToc shape).

Collapsible: starts as an icon-only rail; click the chevron to expand and see each section's label next to its icon. Active section is highlighted based on scroll position (same approach JobDetailToc uses — the section closest to the top of the scroll viewport, with a bottom-of-page override so short tail sections like Outcome can be active).

Anchor IDs (`toc-prep` / `toc-realtime` / `toc-overall` / `toc-debrief` / `toc-outcome`) live on the wrapping section/Card on both RoundFocus and MeetingFocus, with `scroll-mt-20` so scrollIntoView jumps don't tuck the heading behind the sticky top bar.
Hidden below xl: viewports (matches the existing JobDetailToc / LeadDetailToc / WatchRoleDetailToc convention) since smaller screens don't have the side room for a floating rail.

releases.title: Roadmap gets What's-New-style filtering, analytics cards, and a big backlog backfill

items.label: Roadmap now has a sticky filter bar (stays put while the list scrolls) with full What's-New-style filtering: search + type chips + Area chips (Jobs, Communication, …) + Effort chips (S/M/L/XL) + Value chips (High/Med/Low) + a Reset. Plus six analytics cards across the top (Open, Completed, and open counts by type) mirroring What's New.
'Show completed' is now a styled pill (was a bare checkbox) that highlights when active and scrolls the completed section into view.

Backfilled the backlog: migrated the remaining HANDOFF wishlist into the roadmap (auto-archive, AI follow-up nudges, summarize-all-comms, AI resume tailoring, bulk audit-fix, multi-recipient comms, outreach templates, legacy-outreach cleanup, prune .bak, and more), and added curated 'Needs verification' cards for major recently-shipped features (live-call mode, AI generate-from-JD, AI Logs, editable settings/contacts, star + tag-archive, interview prep/debrief, context-aware prompts, AI call attribution, reply tracking).

releases.title: Relabel a conversation's purpose, and add reference links to lead meetings — both previously backend-only

items.label: Chain purpose is now editable: a pencil next to the purpose label (in the Communication thread header AND on each job/lead detail comms chain) opens a small dialog to change the label (company-initiated / self-initiated / external-initiated / application-follow-up / lead-follow-up / system-notification / other) plus optional notes. Purpose was auto-set from the first message and never editable; purposeNotes had no UI at all.

New PATCH /api/jobs/[id]/chains and /api/leads/[id]/chains endpoints upsert a single chain's meta by id, preserving its aiSummary / watchRoleIds. The editor only sends purposeNotes when you actually change it, so it never clobbers existing notes on surfaces that don't pre-fill them.

Lead meetings can now hold reference links (RoundLink[]) — a 'Links' editor (Label | URL per line) in the meeting workspace, mirroring interview rounds. The field existed on meetings but had no editor.

releases.title: Roadmap: 'Show completed' now scrolls the completed section into view

items.label: Toggling 'Show completed' on the Roadmap rendered the completed cards at the very bottom (after every open group), so on a tall backlog the toggle looked like it did nothing. It now smooth-scrolls the completed section into view (with scroll-margin so it clears the sticky header). The Details/spec expander and the toggle were both verified working in a clean build — if buttons ever feel unresponsive while a second editing session is running, that's stale hot-reload; a hard refresh (Cmd-R) reattaches the handlers.

releases.title: Bugfix: the sticky header on interview focus pages now actually collapses on scroll (was attaching its scroll listener to the wrong scroll container)

items.label: The collapsing sticky header on round + meeting focus pages wasn't collapsing on real-world scroll. Bug: the app shell scrolls inside `<main class='flex-1 overflow-y-auto'>` — not the window — so `window.scrollY` stayed at 0 and the collapse never triggered. The listener now walks up from the sticky bar to find the nearest scrollable ancestor (the `<main>` element) and listens there instead, falling back to window when no scrollable ancestor exists.
Verified end-to-end in a real Chrome session: at main scrollTop=50 (past the 32px threshold) the header collapses from ~249px tall to ~45px tall; scrolling back below 32px expands it again.

releases.title: Record a message's reply (date + gist) and edit a round's duration / next-steps date / follow-up-sent time — all previously backend-only

items.label: The message editor now has a 'Response received at' (date/time, with a 'Mark replied now' shortcut) and 'Response summary' field. These set responseReceivedAt / responseSummary, which had no editor anywhere (POST hardcodes them null) — so a reply's timing and gist could only be captured by hand-editing the JSON. Shown in edit mode (you record a response against an existing message).

The interview round editor (Edit Round dialog) now lets you set Duration on an existing round — previously it was only settable in the schedule dialog at creation, so a wrong duration couldn't be corrected.
The round editor also adds 'Next steps expected by' (date) and 'Follow-up sent at' (date/time) — the round fields nextStepsExpectedBy / followUpSentAt had no UI and weren't even displayed.
All persist through the existing comms + rounds PATCH endpoints (which already merge the full body), so no API or schema changes were needed.

releases.title: AI drafting prompts are now context-aware — emails, outreach & interview debrief read your Career / Goals / Authoring Rules, and the Prompt Access matrix lists every prompt grouped by category

items.label: The email & outreach drafting prompts (follow-up, rewrite / bullets / reply, chain follow-up, new outreach) and the interview debrief now inject your Career + Career Goals & Interests + AI Authoring Rules per the Prompt Access matrix — so drafts reflect who you are, what you're targeting, and your conventions. Unselected/empty blocks = unchanged output (no regression).

The Prompt Access matrix (Settings → Context → Prompt Access) now lists EVERY AI feature grouped by category (Listing & Generation / Email & Outreach / Interview / Other), with context pre-checked only where it helps. Prompts that don't use context are shown read-only for completeness.

releases.title: Roadmap upkeep is now part of every session, and completed Roadmap cards carry full specs

items.label: Completed Roadmap cards now have substantive 'Details / spec' sections (what shipped, key behavior, files touched, follow-ups) — not just a one-liner. The open backlog items already carried full implement-from specs; this brings the shipped cards up to parity.

AGENTS.md now mandates roadmap upkeep every session: read data/roadmap.json before scoping a new idea (to dedupe or continue partial/queued work), capture any deferred or outstanding work as a structured roadmap item with an implement-from spec, and on ship mark the item complete + add the matching What's New entry (the two stay in sync via the completed-card deep-link).

releases.title: Context settings sub-tabs are now real URLs — deep-link or bookmark Career, Goals & Interests, AI Authoring Rules, and Prompt Access

items.label: Each Context sub-tab is now its own route: /settings/context/career, /goals-interests, /ai-rules, and /prompt-access. The URL updates as you switch sub-tabs (so you can deep-link/bookmark/back-button), and /settings/context redirects to Career. Replaces the in-page tab switcher.

releases.title: New Roadmap page — a typed, filterable backlog with implementation specs, effort/value tags, and completed items that link to What's New

items.label: New /roadmap tab in the sidebar. Each backlog item is a card with a type (New feature / Enhancement / Bug fix / Needs verification), effort (S/M/L/XL), value (High/Med/Low), affected feature areas, and the release it was analyzed in. An expandable 'Details / spec' section holds in-depth instructions, rules, and the exact pages/code to touch — written so a future Claude session can implement straight from it.

Items are grouped by type and filterable by type, area, and free-text search. Completed items live in a toggleable 'Show completed' section, each stamped with the release that shipped it and a link that jumps to that entry on the What's New page (via the existing #v deep-link). A 'Mark complete' toggle stamps the current release and writes back to data/roadmap.json.

Seeded with the queued backlog (saved filter views, multi-select bulk actions, dashboard polish, comp target band, calendar application-deadline events, canonical-contact merge), verification + bug-fix items, and this session's shipped features as completed cards. Backed by an isolated lib/roadmap.ts model + roadmap-repo; new canonical 'Roadmap' release area.

releases.title: AI Generate from JD — fill Fit Analysis & Requirements from the job description, plus an AI 'Format JD' that cleans raw postings into markdown (jobs + watch roles)

items.label: New amber 'generate' icon on the Fit Analysis and Requirements & Responsibilities cards (jobs AND watch roles). It reads your saved Job Description (prefilled + editable, or paste your own) and fills the card's fields: Fit judges fitScore/interestLevel + why-fit/concerns against your Career + Goals; Requirements extracts responsibilities/requirements bullets. Review the before/after diff and Accept — nothing saves until you do.

New 'AI Format' button on the Job Description attachment tab (jobs AND watch roles): paste a raw posting (or 'about the role' text) and the AI cleans it into structured markdown, which you review and save as job-description.md — the same file the generators read from.

All three features are cost-tracked in AI Logs and matrix-aware (Context → Prompt Access): generate-fit reads Career + Goals, generate-requirements reads the JD only, format-jd applies your AI Authoring Rules. PDFs aren't text-extractable, so the generators fall back to pasted text.

releases.title: New Insights page — pipeline funnel, response & timing, weekly trends, and a compensation comparator

items.label: New /insights page (in the sidebar): a pipeline funnel (Applied → Responded → Interviewed → Offer with conversion off the applied total) plus top-line cards for response rate, interview rate, offer rate, median time-to-first-response, median time-to-offer, and average rounds per offer. Definitions match the dashboard's QuickStats so the two never disagree.

Trends-over-time chart: applications sent per week (bars) and responses received (line) across the recent window. Plus a compensation comparator showing each role's annual posted range with the actual offer (when known) on a shared scale, against the median midpoint — a configurable target band will land with the upcoming Settings work.
All charts are dependency-free inline SVG / CSS (no new packages). Metrics live in a pure computeInsights() helper over the jobs list (archived excluded; leads are pre-application and out of scope).

releases.title: Bugfix: the Settings → Context sub-tabs now switch when clicked

items.label: The Context area's sub-tabs (Career / Career Goals & Interests / AI Authoring Rules / Prompt Access) were stuck on Career — clicking the other tabs did nothing. The switcher relied on a data-attribute Tailwind class to hide inactive panels that wasn't being applied, so every panel stayed shown. Reimplemented to hide inactive panels with the native hidden attribute; all panels stay mounted so unsaved edits survive tab switches.

releases.title: AI now reads your Career Goals & Interests and AI Authoring Rules — parse-listing and interview prep are context-aware, and fit/interest scoring weighs your goals

items.label: Parsing a new opportunity now injects your Career Goals & Interests and AI Authoring Rules (Settings → Context) alongside your career background: it follows your metadata/tagging conventions and scores fitScore/interestLevel against your stated goals, flagging dealbreaker conflicts in Potential Concerns. Applies to both the API and copy-prompt paths, and is matrix-aware (Context → Prompt Access). Output is unchanged until you fill in those blocks — no regression.

Interview Draft Prep and Surface Ideas now also read your Goals & Interests per the Prompt Access matrix, and honor the matrix's Career toggle + version selection. Draft-from-transcript debrief is unchanged (keeps your full career context).
The parse-listing prompt Preview (Settings → AI Prompts) now shows the exact assembled context that will be sent, so the preview never drifts from runtime.

releases.title: Calendar export — download or subscribe (.ics / webcal) to push your interviews, lead meetings, and offer deadlines into Apple/Google Calendar

items.label: The /calendar page gains an 'Export .ics' button (one-time download) and a 'Subscribe' button (webcal://localhost:3939/api/calendar) that keeps Apple/Google/Outlook Calendar in sync while the tracker is running.

The feed (/api/calendar) includes your real appointments + deadlines: scheduled interview rounds, lead meetings, and offer-response deadlines. Timed events carry the actual round/meeting duration plus the video link / dial-in / location; offer deadlines render as all-day events. Past 'applied' dates and 'follow-up sent' log entries are excluded by default — append ?all=1 to include everything the calendar grid shows.
Refactored the calendar's event aggregation into a shared buildCalendarEvents() helper used by BOTH the calendar grid and the .ics feed, so the two can never drift apart.

releases.title: 'View the AI call' links — jump from an AI-drafted message or interview summary straight to the call that produced it

items.label: AI-generated interview section summaries now show a small 'AI call' link (beside the regenerate/clear controls) that opens the exact call in the AI Logs drawer — instruction vs injected prompt, tokens, cost, and the raw + processed response. Appears on summaries generated from now on (older ones predate the back-link).

AI-drafted messages (chain follow-ups + new outreach) show the same 'AI call' link in the edit dialog's AI-prompt panel, so you can see exactly what the model was told and what the draft cost. Shows for drafts created from now on.

releases.title: Career Context settings became a unified "Context" area — Career plus new Career Goals & Interests and AI Authoring Rules blocks, with a per-feature Prompt Access matrix

items.label: Settings → "Career Context" is now "Context", a tabbed area: Career (the existing Full / Balanced / Condensed editor), plus two new editable blocks — Career Goals & Interests (what you're looking for: target roles, interests, dealbreakers) and AI Authoring Rules (house rules + metadata conventions for how AI fills in new opportunities). The new blocks ship with editable starter templates.

New "Prompt Access" sub-tab: a per-feature matrix for choosing which context blocks each AI feature reads, and which Career version it uses. Curated to the context-relevant features for now (Parse Listing, Interview Draft Prep, Surface Ideas); more join as they gain context-awareness.
