Foundation only: these context blocks + access preferences are stored but not yet injected into prompts — prompt wiring (including a stronger parse-listing) lands in the next phase. The old /settings/career route now redirects to the Context area.

releases.title: Interview AI calls now attribute to their job/lead, and AI-drafted messages + summaries back-link to the exact call that produced them

items.label: Interview 'Section Summary' and 'AI-assign speaker' calls were being logged without an owner, so they never showed up in a job's or lead's AI activity section. They now record the job/lead (and the specific round/meeting) they belong to — so every interview AI call appears alongside the rest of that entity's AI activity.

AI-drafted chain follow-ups and new-outreach messages now save a back-link (aiLogId) to the exact AI call that wrote them: the draft routes return the call's log id and the comms save endpoints persist it. AI section summaries store the same link. Groundwork for a future 'view the AI call behind this' jump from a saved message.

releases.title: Settings: your email accounts and phone numbers are now editable in the UI — they used to be hand-edited in settings.json

items.label: New 'Your email accounts' and 'Your phone numbers' chip editors on Settings → Email / Communication. These set settings.userEmails / userPhones, which had NO UI anywhere despite driving the 'From' / mailbox dropdown in the message-edit + chain-follow-up dialogs and the phones reference panel — previously you could only change them by hand-editing settings.json.
Add an entry with Enter (or by clicking away), remove with ×; entries are trimmed and de-duplicated case-insensitively. Persisted via the existing Save button on the Mail settings card.

releases.title: Interview focus pages: sticky header collapses sooner into a single dense row, and Real-time notes now stays pinned with internal scrolling so the composer never leaves the screen

items.label: Sticky header on round + meeting focus pages now collapses as soon as you start scrolling (threshold dropped from 96px to 32px) instead of waiting until you'd scrolled past it.

Collapsed header layout is now a single dense row instead of two. Back link (truncated) · Round title · participants / time / method · Result dropdown · Edit · Live mode toggle — all in one bar. Frees ~32px of vertical for the work area below.

Real-time notes card on the focus page is now pinned to the viewport (sticks just below the collapsed header, height-capped to the viewport). The composer (mode toggle + textarea + Add button + AI Surface ideas) stays at the top of the card always; only the timeline of past notes scrolls inside the card. You can now scroll through 20 sections of Prep and never lose the composer or the most recent live notes.
RealtimeNotesPanel got a new `fillHeight` prop (default off) so the panel is unchanged anywhere it's not given a height cap — only the focus pages opt into the new behavior.

releases.title: Star / Save-for-later toggles and a full tag archive lifecycle on jobs — both were previously editable only by hand-editing jobs.json

items.label: New star ★ and bookmark toggles on every job — in the detail-page header (full + condensed sticky bar) and as quick-toggle icons on each row of the jobs table. These set Job.starred ('apply soon') and Job.savedForLater ('come back to this'), two independent flags that previously had NO UI anywhere and could only be changed by editing jobs.json.
Tags on the job detail page are now fully interactive (they used to render as read-only chips, editable only via the full Edit form). Add a tag inline, and archive any tag with one click.

Archived-tags lifecycle is now in the UI: archiving a tag moves it to archivedTags (kept, never deleted) and it appears in a collapsible 'Show archived (N)' section where it can be restored with one click. Adding a tag that's currently archived restores it instead of duplicating. archivedTags previously had no UI at all.
The list-row toggles stop event propagation so starring/saving from the jobs table never triggers a row navigation; all changes persist via PATCH /api/jobs/[id] and refresh in place.

releases.title: AI calls now show up on the job/lead they belong to — a new 'AI activity' section near the Timeline, with one-click deep links into each call's full detail, plus accurate model provenance

items.label: New 'AI activity' section on every job and lead detail page (near the Timeline): lists every AI call made about that entity — prompt type, sub-target (conversation / interview round / meeting), model, cost, and when — with a running call count and total spend at the top. Renders only when the entity has AI calls; expands from a 6-row preview to the full list.

Deep-linking both ways: each AI-activity row jumps straight to that call's detail drawer on the AI Logs page (instruction vs injected prompt, raw + processed response, tokens, cost). The /logs page now accepts ?focus=<id> to open a specific call directly, and there's a new 'AI Activity' entry in the job detail page's side table-of-contents.

Fixed the chain-summary provenance bug: AI chain summaries recorded aiModel as null. The logging wrapper now stashes the resolved model on the request context, so a saved summary stores the real provider AND model it was generated with.

Added an aiLogId back-link field to chain summaries, comms messages, and interview section summaries (types + Zod validation) so a saved record can point at the exact AI call that produced it. Chain summaries are wired now; drafted emails and interview summaries will carry it next.
The interview 'Draft Debrief' AI action now shows a proper label in the logs instead of its raw feature key.

releases.title: Leads: contacts and tags are now fully editable on the lead page — no more backend-only edits

items.label: Lead contacts are now editable directly on the lead detail page — add, edit, remove, set-primary, and 'Attach existing' all work at full parity with the job page. Previously the lead's Contacts card was read-only ('add via the API'), so fixing a name/email/phone on a lead meant hand-editing leads.json. The shared ContactsCard is now owner-generic (job | lead).
New /api/leads/[id]/contacts/attach endpoint mirrors the job one, so the people-directory 'Attach existing person' flow (with canonical-person auto-linking) works on leads too.
Lead tags are now editable from the Lead facts card (one per line), matching how watch-role and job tags work. Previously they rendered read-only with no editor.
Contacts stay lead-level: the watch-role page keeps its read-only contacts card with the 'Manage on the lead →' link, so there's still one canonical place to edit them.

releases.title: Manual 'Add message to chain' now defaults the direction to the opposite of the last message (for email / text / LinkedIn)

items.label: The manual '+ Add message to chain' dialog now defaults the Direction to the FLIP of the chain's last message for direct interactions (email / text / LinkedIn) — logging the next entry usually means logging the reply to whoever spoke last (it was hardcoded to 'You'). Email From/To orient to that direction automatically; the Direction toggle still re-swaps and every field stays editable.

Phone / video / in-person still default to 'You' (they're typically your own recounts), and the 'AI draft next message' flow is unchanged — it already assumes You for messages/emails and uses the 'Who initiated?' picker for calls.

releases.title: AI logs are now loss-proof — every call is mirrored to a permanent archive, the page self-heals if the live file is truncated, and a health bar warns you if anything ever shrinks

items.label: Root-cause fix for disappearing AI logs: the log was a single file (data/ai-call-logs.jsonl) with NO backup that the app would silently recreate empty if it ever went missing or got overwritten — so an external delete, an editor save, or the dev server starting from a different folder could wipe history invisibly (which is what lost some of your earlier calls). Every AI call is now ALSO written to a permanent, month-partitioned archive under data/ai-logs-archive/ that nothing auto-clears. The working file can be deleted or truncated without losing a single row.

Union read + self-heal: the AI Logs page now reads the deduped union of the live file AND the archive, so even if ai-call-logs.jsonl is emptied, every call still shows — and the live file is rebuilt from the archive on the next load. Verified end-to-end: emptying the live file then reloading restored all rows automatically with the dashboard totals intact.

New durability strip at the top of the AI Logs page: ‘N calls preserved · archived through <month> · K archive shard(s)’. A malformed line is surfaced as an amber ‘skipped’ chip instead of being silently dropped, and if the on-disk total ever falls below the most rows ever recorded, a red ‘Possible loss — run npm run repair:logs’ banner appears so you’re never in the dark about your cost history.

Hardening: log writes are now fsync’d (a crash can’t lose the tail); a high-water-mark manifest tracks the largest row count ever seen (powers shrink detection); and resetting the working file now takes a timestamped backup first and NEVER touches the archive — a ‘clear’ can’t destroy history.

New maintenance tool `npm run repair:logs` rebuilds the live file from the archive, dedupes by id, quarantines any malformed lines to ai-call-logs.corrupt.jsonl, and can import a recovered/exported log file with `-- --import <file.jsonl>`. Idempotent and backup-taking; `-- --dry` reports without writing.

releases.title: Live-call mode on interview focus pages (calm read-only workspace during the actual call) + section-aware AI summary prompts that frame each section differently

items.label: New 'Live mode' toggle in the sticky top header of every interview focus page (round + lead-meeting). Flip it on as the call starts and the page becomes a calm reference workspace — editing affordances (+ Add buttons, × Remove buttons, attach buttons, real-time note delete) all hide; the type bumps slightly (15px + 1.6 line-height) for at-a-glance readability; post-call sections (Overall notes · Debrief · Outcome) dim to 60% opacity + smaller type so they stay visible but don't compete.
Live mode pulses a red 📡 radio icon when on so it's obvious you're in 'live' state. Toggle persists per record in localStorage — reopening the same round/meeting restores the mode.

Live mode is additive — your per-item ✓ done checkboxes, AI Surface ideas / Synthesize / Draft buttons, the Result dropdown, and Edit details all STAY accessible (live capture, AI surfacing, and pipeline status changes are useful during the call; tagged with data-affordance-keep). Toggle exits the mode and brings back full editing.

The AI Section Summary now uses section-specific prompts instead of one generic one. Prep summaries frame future-tense ('Walking in with…'), Real-time summaries capture both sides past-tense, Overall summaries surface decision state, Outcome summaries lead with the result, and Debrief summaries highlight the most consequential open / blocking item. The single user override in Settings → AI Prompts still wins when present.
Resolves Phase 6 doc 3E — the original Round Page Enhancements brief had 'Live-call mode (Phase 2)' as a follow-up after sections + layout shipped. It's now in.

releases.title: New AI Logs page — every AI API call is captured with its prompt, model, token usage, and cost, plus a cost/usage dashboard and live filtering & search

items.label: New AI Logs page (sidebar → AI Logs) records every AI request the app makes — draft emails, chain summaries, job-listing parses, card edits, audit fixes, and all the interview-prep actions. Each row shows the prompt type, the target job / lead / watch-role (and sub-type, e.g. which round or meeting), provider, model + tier, input / output tokens, input / output / total cost, when, and status.

Per-call detail drawer: click any row for a right-side panel that splits the exact request into INSTRUCTION (the fixed system prompt) vs INJECTED (your custom data) so you can see precisely what was sent — plus the raw model response and the processed JSON the app actually consumed. Copy buttons on each block and a deep link back to the job / lead / round the call belongs to.

Cost / usage dashboard across the top: total spend, call count (success / error / manual), total tokens (in / out), average cost per call, a 14-day spend trend, and breakdowns by provider, by model, and by prompt type — each with an inline bar and its own running cost.

Filtering & full-text search that slices everything live: search across prompts / responses / targets, plus pills for status / provider / entity-type and selects for prompt type, model, and date range. The dashboard re-computes to match the active filter (it flips its headline to 'Spend (filtered)'), so 'how much have I spent on Classify Message lately' is two clicks.

Pricing is snapshotted into each row at call time from a built-in Anthropic / OpenAI price table, so historical costs stay accurate even if rates change later; unknown models show '—' instead of a misleading $0.00. Failed calls and copy-prompt (no-API-key) calls are logged too, marked error / manual.

Capture is non-invasive: a thin generateLoggedText wrapper plus request-scoped context record each call to an append-only data/ai-call-logs.jsonl without changing any AI behavior — the original call and its error handling pass through untouched, and one malformed log line is skipped rather than crashing the page.

releases.title: Interview focus pages now have a sticky top header — the back link + round/meeting context stay pinned, and the rich card collapses into a dense bar as you scroll

items.label: Sticky top section on every interview focus page (round and lead-meeting). The back-link row (← company · title or lead headline) never scrolls away, so you can always jump back to the job/lead with one click no matter how deep you are in the prep / debrief.

The rich round / meeting header card semi-collapses once you scroll. In its collapsed state it becomes a compact one-row bar showing the round/meeting name, who you're interviewing with (participants/contact), the scheduled time, and the meeting method (📞 Phone · 🎥 Video · 📍 In-person) — dense and at-a-glance.
Result dropdown + Edit details button stay accessible in the collapsed bar — you can change pipeline outcome or open logistics without scrolling back up the page.

Subtle backdrop-blurred background on the sticky bar so content scrolling under it is still hinted but the bar stays legible. A bottom border appears when collapsed to mark the edge between bar and scrolling content.

releases.title: New 'Network outreach' built-in for the Initiated By field — captures the case where you reached out via a network connection rather than a formal application

items.label: Added a 4th built-in to the Initiated By field: `network-outreach` ("Network outreach"). Captures the case where you initiated the conversation by reaching out to an existing network contact or re-engaging a past connection — and the role surfaced from that exchange, not from a posted application. Distinct from `self` (formal application via job board / website / cold pitch) and from `hiring-team` (they pinged you first). Renders with a teal badge to stand apart from the existing self/blue, recruiter/violet, hiring-team/fuchsia.

AI audit-fix prompt now knows when to pick `network-outreach`: extended the heuristics in src/lib/ai/audit-fix.ts so when you describe a job as 'reached out to a former colleague / warm intro / mutual connection / re-engaging a past contact,' the AI proposes the new value instead of `self` or `recruiter`.

Migration: scripts/migrate-to-v3_59_0.ts backfilled the two jobs you flagged — 66degrees AI Architect (was: recruiter → now: network-outreach) and the new Superpanel reengaged role (was: self → now: network-outreach). Idempotent + .pre-v3_59_0 backup taken.

releases.title: AI section summaries on interview cards (with stale indicator) and the parse-listing AI prompt now uses your real Career Context instead of a hardcoded background paragraph

items.label: New ✨ Summarize button on every section of an interview focus page (Prep · Real-time · Overall notes · Debrief · Outcome). Click to generate a 1–2 sentence AI summary; the result stores on the round / meeting and is shown in the compact interview card on the parent job / lead page in place of the old count-based preview.

Out-of-date detector: if you change a section's content after generating its summary, the summary now shows an amber ⚠ chip (both on the focus page and on the compact card), and a ↻ button regenerates with current content. No silent AI calls — staleness is a visual cue only.

Debrief joins the four existing summary slots (Prep / Real-time / Overall / Outcome), so all five sections of the focus page can have an AI summary. Additive data-model change — no migration needed; old records still validate.

The AI parse-listing prompt no longer hard-codes a 'Conv AI / NLU / Wysdom / Calabrio' background paragraph. It now pulls from Settings → Career Context (Condensed version, falling back to Full or the legacy single string). Edit your Career Context, hit parse — the AI's fit-scoring uses the new background.

Softened the parse-listing fit-score criterion from 'Conv AI / agentic AI alignment' to 'alignment between the role and Alex's stated background' so the prompt stays accurate as your career shape evolves over time.
Settings → AI Prompts now shows the parse-listing prompt with your real Career Context baked in, so you can see what's actually being sent to the model.

releases.title: Custom status dropdown bug fixed (per-job dropdowns now show your custom values), Settings header + tabs stay sticky on long pages, and Interaction Kinds editor is flatter with pre-filled editable descriptions

items.label: Bug fix: custom status values you add in Settings → Custom Statuses now appear in every per-job status dropdown (Application Status, Application Progress, Interview Status, Interview Progress, Job Status) AND in the Interview Results chip multi-select. Before this, customs persisted to settings.json and showed up in the dashboard filters but were invisible inside individual jobs. Built a useCustomStatuses() hook that merges the live custom map into each Select at render; CustomStatusesEditor busts the cache after PATCH so dropdowns mounted elsewhere refresh immediately.

Settings → sticky header + tabs. The 'Settings' h1 and the tab row now stay pinned at the top of every Settings sub-page while you scroll, so you can jump between AI Provider / Career Context / AI Prompts / Mail / Interaction Kinds / Custom Statuses / etc. without scrolling back up. Implemented by moving the header + tabs into the shared src/app/settings/layout.tsx (a single sticky block) and stripping the duplicated copies from all 10 sub-pages.

Settings → Interaction Kinds: flatter layout (dropped the cards-within-cards wrapping in favor of a single bordered list with divider rows + tighter row padding) and the description field for each built-in is now PRE-FILLED with the packaged default text instead of showing it as a grayed placeholder. The text is fully editable / copyable / selectable; clearing it (or restoring the original) reverts to the packaged default automatically so future packaged-description improvements still flow through.

releases.title: Interaction kinds become a live registry: more built-ins, rename `negotiation` → `offer-negotiation`, user-extensible via new Settings tab, and an AI Other+propose flow that one-click promotes a proposal into a real custom label

items.label: Renamed the broad `negotiation` interaction kind to `offer-negotiation` (post-offer back-and-forth specifically) and split out 6 new built-in kinds so the AI classifier has more precise slots to choose from: role-exploration, interview-prep, comp-discussion (pre-offer comp talk), offer-acceptance, offer-decline, withdrawal. Migration: scripts/migrate-to-v3_53_0.ts walks every job + lead chain and renames `negotiation` → `offer-negotiation` (idempotent, takes a .pre-vN.<ts>.bak backup, prints a count summary).

New Settings tab — Settings → Interaction Kinds. Lists every built-in (with enable/disable toggle + editable description override that tunes the AI's option list) and every custom you've added (full CRUD; labels auto-normalize to kebab-case ids). `other` is always on — it's the AI's escape valve. Built-ins are name-fixed but description-overridable so you can sharpen AI classification without forking a custom.

Every Interaction Type dropdown across the app now reads from the LIVE list (built-ins minus disabled + customs + description overrides) instead of a hardcoded enum: EditMessageDialog, NewChainOutreachDialog, ChainFollowUpDialog, CommunicationComposerDialog, OutreachCard inline composer, ImportCsvDialog preview. Legacy / disabled stored values render as grayed `(legacy)` entries so old messages keep their value while you re-pick from the active list.

AI classifiers (suggestInteractionKind + analyzeImport + chainFollowUp's suggestedKind) now receive the LIVE list at call time and classify into the same labels your dropdown shows. When nothing in the list genuinely fits, the AI returns 'other' plus a proposed kebab-case label + 1-sentence description for what it would call this kind.

Other+propose UI: when the AI returns 'other' with a proposal, you get a one-click [Add label + apply] alongside [Use Other anyway] — promoting writes a new custom kind to settings + busts the client-side cache so EVERY dropdown (and future AI calls) sees the new label immediately. Surfaces in three places: EditMessageDialog (sonner toast with two actions after AI Suggest), ChainFollowUpDialog (amber strip under the lock-in Interaction Type select), ImportCsvDialog (per-row pill in the CSV preview table).

Schema relaxation: CommsMessage.kind is now `z.string()` instead of a strict enum (and the TS type matches), so user-added customs round-trip through validation. Hard-coded `CommsKind` casts dropped at every dropdown setter site.

releases.title: New Interview focus pages — dedicated per-call workspace for prep, real-time notes, structured debrief, and outcome, with AI throughout

items.label: New Interview focus page per round and per lead-meeting — a full-bleed dedicated page (mirroring the watch-role detail) with Prep on the left ~70% and Real-time notes pinned right ~30% so you can see your prep AND capture live notes at once during the call; Overall notes, Debrief, and Outcome stack full-width below.

Structured Prep board — 10 sections (expected Qs · JD → my experience · questions to ask them · sensitive disclosures w/ reaction branches · contingency plans · watch-outs · leverage · prior context · linked docs · other notes). Collapsed sections turn into small icon chips in a dock; expanded sections live in a 2-col masonry. Per-item ‘done’ checkbox collapses the item to a single dim line as you cover things during the call. Each card has a Focus button that blows it up in a roomy modal for cramped editing.

Real-time note stream with four swappable input modes — Tagged composer (one box + Me/Them/Note chips), By speaker (separate fields per speaker), AI-assign (freeform → AI splits + tags), and Backfill (post-hoc entries flagged with a subtle ‘↻ backfilled’ badge so reconstructed-after-the-call notes are honest in the timeline). Pref persists per browser.

New Debrief board — 10 sections capturing what they asked + my answers, what I asked + their responses, new info learned (with a suggested category vocab), concerns surfaced (with origin / response / status / effectiveness, optionally linkable to a prep entry), disclosures made (with reaction / status, optionally linkable to the prep disclosure), action items (owner / due / status), open / unresolved items, names mentioned (linkable to job/lead contacts), sentiment labels + tone note, and actual call timing vs. scheduled. Same density / dock / masonry / focus-modal patterns as Prep.

Six new AI surfaces, all key-gated with a graceful ‘copy prompt’ fallback when no key is configured: Draft prep (from JD + Career Context), Surface ideas (during the call), Synthesize overall notes (from live notes + recap), Section summary (for card previews), AI-assign speaker (powers the AI-assign input mode), and Draft debrief from transcript (paste a call transcript / voice-memo; AI proposes structured entries across all 10 debrief sections; accepted items append to whatever you’ve already entered).

Linked-docs viewer — every prep doc URL or local file path is now clickable: PDFs and images render natively in a popup, Markdown / .txt / .log render with the app’s formatting, and any of them can be expanded inline directly below the row with a small eye-toggle.

Finder-style file picker for linking local files — a small folder-open button on each linked-doc row opens a server-side picker (breadcrumb + Up + filter + show-hidden) so you can navigate to any absolute path on the machine without typing it. On select, the URL fills in AND the label auto-fills from the filename if blank.

Lossless promotion preserved across the new fields — when a watch-role lead-meeting promotes into a job round, every prep section, every realtime note, the debrief, attachments, post-recap, and section summaries carry into the spawned round with zero data loss (same shared sub-types on both record kinds).

Six new editable system-prompt slots under Settings → AI Prompts → Interview (Draft Prep, Surface Ideas, Synthesize, Section Summary, Assign Speaker, Draft Debrief) plus configurable light-tier models (Anthropic + OpenAI) so cheaper actions like speaker-assign can route to a smaller model. Settings also reads from the three Career Context versions (Full / Balanced / Condensed) — heavy AI uses Full by default, condensed actions use Condensed.

Additive data model with no migration required — rounds and meetings get optional shared sub-types (InterviewPrep with 11 sub-arrays, InterviewDebrief with 10 sub-arrays, RealtimeNote.backfilled flag). Old data validates as-is; sparse records fill in defaults via the read layer and on-write zod schemas.

Real Superpanel R1 reconnect populated end-to-end — prep, the executed Calabrio disclosure (linked back to the prep entry), the full 4-paragraph recap, 41 reconstructed live-capture notes (each flagged ‘backfilled’), 7 questions they asked, 6 I asked, 11 buckets of new info, 2 concerns, 7 action items, 5 open items, 5 names, sentiment + actual timing, and the 5 outcome labels with reasoning — all from the post-interview brief.

releases.title: Fixed the resume/cover-letter “Pick from folder” picker spilling off-screen on Lead & Watch-role pages

items.label: The Attachments → “Pick from folder” picker on Lead and Watch-role pages rendered with its right half cut off (long filenames + the “(on Company)” tag + the Use button pushed past the edge). Real cause: the file-list rows weren’t truncating, so the widest filename forced the row — and the whole panel — wider than itself. Job pages were unaffected because that picker already truncates filenames.

Filenames now truncate with an ellipsis and the “(on Company)” tag is length-capped, so every row — and the Use button — stays inside the panel at any width. (Verified the widest row now fits with the Use button fully visible.)

Also hardened the shared Dialog centering — it now uses a viewport-pinned flex wrapper with a guaranteed gutter on all sides (and scrolls if a panel is taller than the screen) instead of transform-centering, so no dialog can clip against a screen edge. Click-outside and Esc to close are unchanged.

releases.title: Fixed AI "Parse Job Listing" failing on OpenAI (work-arrangement schema)

items.label: Parsing a job posting with AI now works when your AI provider is OpenAI. The work-arrangement field used a discriminated union that compiled to JSON-Schema 'oneOf', which OpenAI's structured-output mode rejects (Anthropic accepted it) — so every OpenAI parse failed with an 'oneOf is not permitted' error. The AI parse target now uses an equivalent plain union ('anyOf', which OpenAI accepts); the parsed shape and the canonical job schema are unchanged.

releases.title: Career Context now has three versions (Full / Balanced / Condensed) + a Copy button — richer, honestly-scoped content for AI features

items.label: Career Context now holds THREE editable versions — Full (complete portfolio), Balanced (everyday essentials with metrics), and Condensed (tight summary for short prompts / recruiter screens) — selectable via a Full/Balanced/Condensed switcher in the Settings → Career Context tab, each with its own Edit/Preview, size hint, and unsaved-changes marker. Saving writes all three at once.
New 'Copy all' button in the raw-text (Edit) view copies the entire current version to your clipboard.

Data model: settings now carry a structured careerContexts { full, balanced, condensed } object (legacy single careerContext kept as a fallback). The interview AI reads careerContexts.full by default — its connection is unchanged. Per-task version selection (letting AI buttons pick Balanced/Condensed to cut tokens) is intentionally left for a follow-up.

Rewrote the Full version from multi-session feedback: added a 'By the Numbers' scoreboard, honestly-tiered skills (deep / applied / developing), MLOps & AI-evaluation, Responsible-AI & governance, product & pre-sales/PoV, a 'why AI' origin story, the side-project note, Wysdom-vs-Calabrio era tags, a Job-Search Parameters block (comp, geography, availability, anti-positioning, references), and a Tailoring-Guidance section. Resolved the RAG and voice-bot-architecture over-claims toward honest scoping; softened 'Acting Director' / leave wording.

releases.title: Career Context is now its own Settings tab with a markdown Edit/Preview — and AI Provider has its own /settings/provider route

items.label: Moved the Career Context editor out of the AI Provider card into its own dedicated Settings → Career Context tab, so your background lives separately from provider/model/API-key config.

Career Context now has a Preview/Edit toggle: write it as plain markdown and the Preview renders the nicely formatted 'read' version using the app's house styling. It opens in Preview by default, and auto-returns to Preview after you Save.

Quality-of-life on the Career Context tab: a live character/approx-token size hint (so you can see how much text feeds the AI), an 'unsaved' marker, and a 'Discard changes' button to revert to the last saved value.

AI Provider settings now live at /settings/provider, and the Settings index redirects there. The AI features that use your career background (interview draft-prep, surfacing ideas) read the same field as before and are unchanged.
Seeded Career Context with a comprehensive markdown portfolio synthesized from your career documents.

releases.title: AI can now pick the interaction type from a message body — plus a one-click 'AI: subject + type' button in the message editor

items.label: New 'AI type' button next to Interaction type in the add/edit message dialog: reads the body and classifies it into one of the interaction types (cold-outreach / post-application / post-round / stale-pipeline / re-engagement / negotiation / thank-you / scheduling / referral-support / other), then sets the dropdown directly with a short reason in the toast (e.g. 'Set type to scheduling — confirms availability and coordinates a time'). It's a dropdown, so it's trivial to override.

New combined 'AI: subject + type' button next to the Body — one click fills both the subject (on channels that use one) and the interaction type. On channels without a subject (phone/video/in-person recounts) it just does the type and labels itself 'AI: type'.

Backed by a new /api/ai/suggest-interaction-type route + provider.suggestInteractionKind (Anthropic + OpenAI), reusing the same CommsKind taxonomy as the CSV-import classifier for consistent labeling. Soft-fails to a friendly toast in copy-prompt mode / when no API key is set, mirroring AI subject.

releases.title: Notes card on the Job detail page now stretches full-width like Attachments and Timeline

items.label: On /jobs/[id], the Notes card was sitting bare in the two-column grid and getting squeezed into a single-column slot — narrower than its counterpart on Leads and Watch Roles, with nothing rendering beside it. Wrapped it in the same lg:col-span-2 section pattern as Attachments / Contacts / Timeline so it now spans the full content width.

releases.title: Phase 3 lights up (Wand2 — AI rewrite for style without changing facts) + Settings → AI Prompts now exposes the universal templates and per-card blurbs for both Phase 2 and Phase 3

items.label: Wand2 button is now ACTIVE on all 10 freeform cards. Click → optional 'style preference' textarea (or leave blank for default polish) → AI proposes a wording/formatting rewrite WITHOUT changing facts → before/after diff per field → Accept or Reject. Same diff guardrail as Phase 2 (patch keys filtered against the card's FieldDescriptor[] client-side; hallucinated keys silently dropped).

The universal Phase 3 prompt embeds a HARD 'facts MUST NOT change' constraint plus explicit examples: tighten verbose phrasing, make bullet lists parallel, fix awkward grammar, keep first-person passages first-person. The diff preview reminds you to inspect for fact changes before accepting.

Settings → AI Prompts page (backfill from v3.50): the universal Phase 2 'AI Card Translate' prompt + the new Phase 3 'AI Card Style Rewrite' prompt are now both editable in the existing PromptEditor under a new 'Card Editing (AI)' group. Below the editor, a new tabbed AiCardBlurbsSection exposes ALL 22 per-card-type blurbs (11 translate × 11 style) grouped by Jobs / Leads / Watch Roles. Empty fields fall back to the packaged defaults.

AI provider plumbing: new rewriteCardStyle method on the AIProvider interface; implemented for Anthropic + OpenAI via generateObject against the same {patch, reasoning} schema as Phase 2. Claude Code chat = 501 stub (coming in a follow-up). API: POST /api/ai/card-rewrite-style.

Continuity doc: new docs/SESSION-HANDOFF.md captures v3.40 → v3.52 architecture decisions, file map, cardType registry, settings shape, and the open backlog — so future sessions can resume without re-discovering. Read it FIRST when picking up this work.

releases.title: International phone numbers in Contacts — any +country-code number is identified (🇬🇧 GB), validated, and canonical-formatted, not just North-American

items.label: Contact phone fields now accept international numbers, not just the North-American format. Type a +country-code number (e.g. +44 7429 424879) and the country is identified automatically — its flag + 2-letter ISO code (🇬🇧 GB) appears next to the field and in the contact list, with the line type (mobile / fixed-line) in the tooltip.

Each international number is checked against its detected country. A number that doesn't look valid is still saved (it never blocks you) but shows a subtle 'couldn't verify' note. North-American numbers keep the +1 (###) ###-#### auto-formatting and stay badge-free.
International numbers are tidied to canonical form on save (+447429424879 → +44 7429 424879), and click-to-call / tel: links now build a clean E.164 dial string for any country.

releases.title: Phase 2 lights up: Sparkles on every freeform card translates natural-language instructions into AI-proposed patches with a before/after diff preview

items.label: Sparkles button is now ACTIVE on all 10 freeform cards (Jobs CoreInfo/Fit/Requirements/Notes/Application + Leads Facts/Notes + WatchRole CoreInfo/Fit/Requirements/Notes). Clicking it opens a two-step dialog: (1) describe what you want to change in plain English; (2) review the AI's proposed before/after diff per field. Accept fires the same PATCH the manual pencil uses; Reject returns to step 1 to refine the instruction.

Prompt strategy: ONE universal 'AI Card Translate' prompt template (in Settings.prompts.aiCardTranslateUniversal — editable via Settings → AI Prompts) + per-card-type 'about this card' blurbs (in Settings.aiCardBlurbs.<cardType>). The universal template uses {cardName}/{cardBlurb}/{fields}/{currentValues}/{userInstruction} placeholders so card-specific personality lives in small overrides, not duplicated prompts.

AI provider plumbing: new translateCardEdit method on the AIProvider interface; implemented for Anthropic + OpenAI via generateObject with a permissive {patch, reasoning} schema. The dialog validates patch keys against the card's FieldDescriptor[] client-side — hallucinated keys get dropped silently. Claude Code chat mode returns 'coming in follow-up' for this call since structured-output round-trip via copy-prompt isn't straightforward.

New API route: POST /api/ai/card-translate. Looks up settings.aiCardBlurbs[cardType] (falling back to packaged defaults), dispatches to the active AI provider, returns {patch, reasoning}. Empty/contradictory instructions get a friendly 'AI returned empty patch — refine and try again' state in the dialog.
Phase 3 next (Wand2 — AI rewrite for style without changing facts). The third icon in the action rail stays as a disabled stub for now.

releases.title: Manual 'Add message to chain' stops reversing From/To, chain bubbles name the other party (email + text), and the contact picker shows just the name

items.label: Fixed: 'Add message to chain' was seeding the new message's email headers verbatim from the previous message — so an outbound reply to an inbound email got saved with From: the sender / To: you (backwards). The seed now derives the (you, them) pair from the last message and reply-swaps when it was inbound, so a new outbound message defaults to From: your mailbox / To: the contact. Back-to-back sends/receives stay correct because the headers follow the chosen Direction, not the last message's side.

The Direction toggle (You ↔ Them) in the add/edit message dialog now swaps the From/To email headers to match, so logging an inbound message keeps the headers right. accountEmail (always your mailbox) is left alone and every field stays editable for one-off corrections.

Chain bubbles now render the other party as 'Name <email>' — matching how your own address already expands to 'Alex Bisgould <email>' — on the To row when you email them and the From row when they email you. Resolved from the owner's contacts.

Text chains (iMessage / WhatsApp / SMS / RCS) now show a 'Name <phone>' counterparty row for parity with email headers, when a phone number is on file for the contact. Phone/video/in-person keep their existing 'You called … / … called you' recount header.

The 'Linked contact' picker in the message editor now shows just the contact's name. Long role strings (e.g. 'Senior Recruiter, 66degrees (was: Technical Recruiter in 2024)') were wrapping and spilling past the dropdown — the channel already conveys how you're reaching them.

releases.title: Application Deadline lives on the Application card with an auto-cascade — past deadline + no action ⇒ Missed Application Window + role closed

items.label: Application Deadline moved from the full-edit Identity section to the Application card, next to Role Open + Date Applied. Pre-application + a deadline set: the bottom-right cell swaps from 'Days Since' to 'Application Deadline' + a live countdown ('5 days left' / 'today' / 'passed 2 days ago'). After you've applied, 'Days Since' returns — the deadline is no longer actionable.

Inline pencil on the Application card opens a 3-field dialog (applicationDeadline + applicationStatus + roleOpen) — the trio you tweak together when a role gets reposted. Reopening flow: set a future deadline + flip status back to Not Applied + Role still open ✓; the cascade only fires when the deadline is in the past so a future deadline + manual reset won't re-trigger.

patchJob cascade: when the merged next state has a past applicationDeadline AND status is in a pre-application set (Not Applied / Drafting Application / Pending Referral), auto-set applicationStatus = Missed Application Window + roleOpen = false. Runs BEFORE the existing N/A cascades so they see the corrected status and force applicationProgress + interviewStatus to N/A. Timeline event fires naturally via the existing diff logic.

DeadlineAutoCascade client component on the job detail page fires the cascade ONCE on visit when hydrate detects 'cascade pending' (deadline past + status still pre-app). Sends a no-op PATCH that routes through patchJob's cascade and refreshes the page, so opening a stale job naturally settles its state. Banner explains what happened with a one-click path to set a new deadline if the role was reposted.
hydrate adds two computed fields: daysUntilDeadline (signed — negative if past) drives the countdown chip; applicationDeadlineMissedPending is the auto-fire trigger.

releases.title: Pencil-rename job titles + rebuilt /jobs/[id]/edit with stacked card sections, sticky Save/Cancel header, and the same rich composite editors as the per-card pencils

items.label: New Pencil next to the H1 job title opens a small rename-only dialog (mirrors the lead-detail rename pattern). Only `title` patches — company, industry, etc. each have their own pencils. The legacy 'Edit' button in the top-right is now a Pencil-iconified link to the full edit page; the sticky-scroll variant got the same treatment.

Rebuilt /jobs/[id]/edit page. The old long flat JobForm is replaced by a card-stacked layout that reuses the SAME field editors as the per-card pencil dialogs. Compensation is now a proper composite (low / high / live midpoint preview / currency / period / equity + bonus notes) instead of just a free-text label — the midpoint that drives the jobs-table sort is visible while you edit. Work Arrangement gets the Remote/On-site/Hybrid segmented control + days-on-site input.

Sticky 'Edit Job — {title}' header carries Back / Cancel / Save in the top-right (instead of buried at the bottom of a long scroll). The Save button is disabled until something actually changes; one PATCH covers all section edits via diff-on-save, so patchJob's cascades + timeline events still fire normally.

Sections: Identity (title / company / location / dates), Core Info (industry / seniority / employment / work arrangement / compensation / source / URLs), Fit Analysis (scores + free-text), Requirements & Responsibilities (string arrays), Status & Progress (priority / active state / app status / interview status / etc.), Notes, Tags. A read-only Contacts summary card links to the detail-page ContactsCard — contact editing stays there so the people-sync propagation has one source of truth.

Promoted FieldEditor + WorkArrangementEditor + CompensationEditor from EditCardDialog to named exports so the new edit shell renders the same controls inline. JobForm is left untouched and continues to power /new + /parse-listing for the create flow.

releases.title: Work Arrangement + Compensation now editable via the Core Info pencil — completes Phase 1 of card editing

items.label: Two new composite field kinds on EditCardDialog: work-arrangement and compensation. The 'Compensation + work arrangement deferred' note from v3.45 is gone — both now live inside the same Pencil-edit Core Info dialog on Jobs AND Watch Roles.

Work Arrangement editor: three-way segmented control (Remote / On-site / Hybrid). Picking Hybrid reveals a 'Days on-site per week' number input (clamped 0–7). The discriminated-union shape ({kind:'Remote'} | {kind:'On-site'} | {kind:'Hybrid', daysInOffice}) is preserved exactly so downstream code (formatWorkArrangement, hydrate, schema) keeps working without changes.

Compensation editor: free-text display label (rawText, shown on the card), structured Low/High numbers, currency dropdown (USD/CAD/EUR/GBP/AUD + back-compat for custom values already on a row), period dropdown (Annual/Hourly/Contract/Unknown), plus equity + bonus notes textareas. A live read-only 'Midpoint (sort key)' chip surfaces the (min+max)/2 — the exact value hydrate.ts.compMidpoint computes and JobsTable sorts on — so what you see in the editor matches the sort order on the Job Opportunities page.
Diff handler upgraded: composite object values use JSON-stringify deep-equality so unchanged Compensation / WorkArrangement objects don't generate noisy no-op PATCHes.
Next: Phase 2 (AI translate — Sparkles button) and Phase 3 (AI rewrite-for-style — Wand2 button) on the same cards. Both icons are already rendered as stubs in the action rail.

releases.title: Lead meetings link to watch roles — 'Likely for' on the lead, and a read-through meeting window on the watch role with a folded-in Promote

items.label: A lead meeting can now be linked to one or more watch roles (or none) right from its card — a 'Link to a role ▾' dropdown (no need to open the editor). Once linked, the meeting shows a clear 'Likely for: <role>' indicator, so a reconnect that's really a pre-screen for a specific role reads at a glance.

Watch roles now show a 'Lead meetings for this role' window: any lead meeting tagged to that role appears at full detail (when / method / with, notes, outcome tags) right on the role page — mirroring the existing 'Lead-level conversations' read-through pattern. The meeting still lives on the lead; Add/Edit/Delete route there via a 'Manage on the lead →' link.

The quick actions stay live inside the role window — inline status, Quick Reschedule, and outcome tags all edit the same underlying lead meeting, so you can prep for the role without bouncing to the lead.

The Calendar carries the association too: a linked lead meeting shows its watch role as a subtle suffix on the event chip (e.g. '66degrees: Pre-screen w/ Maria · AI Architect') with the full 'Likely for: <role>' in the hover tooltip.

The old '📅 N meetings about this role — Promote to job' nudge banner is folded into the new window (single surface, same Promote button + hint). The window only appears when a meeting is actually linked to the role.
Tidied the lead meeting card: the redundant status pill in the header is gone now that the inline status dropdown carries it.

releases.title: Pencil edit on freeform cards across Jobs, Leads, Watch Roles — Phase 1 of card editing (AI translate + rewrite coming next)

items.label: Every freeform detail-page card now has a top-right action cluster: an active Pencil button + two greyed-out AI stubs (Sparkles, Wand2) with tooltips explaining what they'll do in the next two phases. Clicking the pencil opens a dialog with the right fields for that card and PATCHes only the changed values on Save. Reserving the layout means future AI buttons won't shift card headers.

Cards wired in Phase 1: Jobs (Core Info, Fit Analysis, Requirements & Responsibilities, Notes); Leads (Lead facts, Notes — replaced the old inline 'Edit' toggle with the new dialog pattern); Watch Roles (Core Info, Fit Analysis, Requirements & Responsibilities, Notes). Compensation + work-arrangement deferred from the Phase 1 dialog (complex shapes; still edited via the full Edit page / FullEditDialog).

New shared building blocks: CardActionRail (the icon cluster), EditCardDialog (generic field-driven editor with text / textarea / number / url / date / enum / string-array / boolean field kinds + automatic diff-on-save), CardEditButton (client wrapper that drops into a server card with one prop block — no closure crossing the server→client boundary).

Phase 2 (next): clicking Sparkles will let you write a natural-language instruction (e.g., 'add a concern about commute' or 'rewrite the requirements as a bulleted list ranked by importance'); the AI translates that into a card-specific patch. Each card type ships its own prompt, exposed in Settings → AI Prompts. Phase 3: Wand2 polishes wording / formatting WITHOUT changing facts — for content you wrote yourself that just needs a stylistic pass.

releases.title: Lead Meetings get the Interview-Rounds treatment — rounds-style cards, inline status, Quick Reschedule, and one-tap outcome tags

items.label: Lead Meetings restyled to mirror the Interview Rounds cards on jobs — fuller bordered cards with the meeting type, method, and role tags up top, a clear when / duration / with line, then logistics (join link, dial-in, location) and prep/outcome notes below. The Upcoming and Past / logged groups stay split.

Inline status dropdown on every meeting — set Scheduled / Completed / Cancelled / No-show / Rescheduled straight from the card (replacing the single mark-complete check). Completing auto-stamps the logged time; re-opening a meeting back to Scheduled clears it. The control is tinted to match the status.

Quick Reschedule on upcoming meetings — a compact date/time picker that moves a meeting to a new slot, keeps it upcoming, and logs the move to the lead's timeline. No need to open the full editor just to shift a time.

Outcome quick-tags on past meetings — one-tap chips (Went well, Advancing, Strong interest, Needs follow-up, Lukewarm, Not a fit, Salary mismatch, On hold) capture how a meeting went without opening the editor. Backed by a new optional outcomeLabels field that defaults to empty, so existing meetings are untouched.

releases.title: Chain follow-up defaults to most-recent channel/protocol; manual + Add message at the bottom of every chain

items.label: Chain Follow-Up dialog now defaults the channel + protocol to the chain's MOST RECENT message instead of the first/dominant one. When a thread has moved from email → LinkedIn DM (or SMS → iMessage), the composer seeds where the thread is NOW. You can still change either before locking in, and the protocol selector still surfaces whenever the chosen channel has sub-types.

New + Add message to chain button at the bottom of every chain in both the Communication page right pane AND the OutreachCard expanded view on job/lead detail pages. Opens the same editor you see when editing a message — same channel + protocol + email-headers fields — but starts blank with channel/contact pre-filled from the chain's most-recent entry. Defaults to status=sent, timestamped now (the common case is logging a message that already happened); flip to draft via the status pill at the top.

EditMessageDialog parameterized with mode: 'edit' | 'add'. Add mode POSTs a fresh CommsMessage to /api/<owner>/[id]/comms with chainId set (threads into the existing chain). Delete + regenerate-from-prompt are hidden in add mode; Save button reads 'Add to chain'.

releases.title: Job detail & Contacts pages no longer crash on records missing a required array; removed two accidentally-promoted orphan jobs

items.label: Fixed a 500 that took down the entire job-detail page (OutreachCard's `scopedOwner.comms.length`) and could take down the Contacts page (`j.comms.filter(...)`) whenever a job was missing a required array such as `comms`. A single malformed row no longer crashes the whole route.

jobs-repo and leads-repo now normalize every required array (Job: comms, contacts, timeline, tags, rounds, interviewResults, keyResponsibilities, keyRequirements; Lead: comms, contacts, watchRoles, meetings, promotions, priorJobOpportunityIds, chains, tags, timeline) to [] at the single read chokepoint (readFileNoLock → normalizeJob / normalizeLead). Runtime now honors the non-optional array types for ALL consumers instead of relying on per-call-site `?? []` guards that one site can forget. Records written outside createJob()/patchJob() — hand-edits or promote/absorb — are healed on read.

Removed two orphan job records a promote/absorb session wrote directly into jobs.json without going through job creation (so they lacked `comms`): the 66degrees 'Gemini/AI Architect' role and 'genesys-senior-ai-architect-presales'. These were not real promoted opportunities — their watch roles remain Watching on their leads. Pre-removal snapshot preserved at data/jobs.json.pre-orphan-removal-*.bak.

releases.title: Watch-roles nest under leads in Communication & Contacts, Contacts gets Active/Stale badges, per-chain related linking

items.label: Lead rows in the Communication AND Contacts left panes now expand to show their non-archived watch roles nested underneath (chevron toggle). Clicking a nested watch-role row strict-scopes the right pane to ONLY chains (Communication) or contacts (Contacts) whose messages tag that watchRoleId — items unanchored to any role disappear; click the parent lead row to see them again. A small violet chip in the right-pane header names the active role and clears the scope on click. Works in both job-first AND company-first view modes.

Contacts page now has Active/Inactive/Both filter chips (mirrors Communication) plus an Active dot + amber 'stale' chip on each row. The dot only appears in 'Both' mode (otherwise the chip is redundant with the filter); the stale chip surfaces independently. Stale precomputed via the same isJobStale / isLeadStale helpers Communication uses. The old 'Hide companies with no active roles' checkbox now dims when an explicit Active/Inactive filter is selected (it's only meaningful in Both mode).

Per-chain selective 'Include related' linking: toggling Include Related ON for the first time on a job now opens a popover listing each related opportunity's chains with checkboxes (default: all checked, mirroring the old all-or-nothing behavior). Save persists the subset to job.linkedRelatedChainIds; subsequent toggles flip visibility while respecting the saved selection. A small gear button next to the toggle reopens the picker anytime to edit the choice. Undefined = include all (back-compat); empty array = explicitly include none.
Schema: added optional Job.linkedRelatedChainIds (string[]). No migration needed — existing jobs have undefined and continue to surface all related chains via the toggle, matching v3.34 behavior.

releases.title: One shared activity timeline for jobs, leads & watch roles — colored icons + Recent / All / By-type views

items.label: Jobs and watch roles now use the same nicer timeline as leads: a vertical rail with a colored per-kind icon dot (watch-role / interview / communication / status / meeting / …) and a day-gap (+Nd) between events. The watch-role timeline went from a flat list to the full treatment.

Long timelines get three view modes (shown once a timeline has more than 6 events): Recent (just the latest, expandable to All), All (full chronological history), and By type — collapsed into categories (Communication, Interviews, Application, Status & Outcome, Watch Roles, Meetings) showing the most recent in each, expandable to that category's full history.
Extracted one shared ActivityTimeline component + a server-safe row builder so all three owners stay consistent. The job timeline keeps its manual 'Add event' button.
Removed the dead, unused TimelineCard + buildTimeline helper (the job page already used JobTimelineStrip).

releases.title: Leads get a real activity Timeline card

items.label: Lead detail pages now have a proper Timeline card (like jobs and watch roles): a vertical, chronological activity feed with a colored icon per event. It merges the lead's logged lifecycle events — watch roles added / promoted / dismissed / status changes, lead status, next-action updates, meetings, conversation moves, related-job links — with a derived line per communication (sent / received). Added to the side ToC.

One-shot backfill (migrate-lead-timeline-backfill) populates older leads whose timelines predate per-event logging — synthesizing 'Lead created', 'Watch role added' (per role), and promotion events where missing. Idempotent, with a .bak backup.

Fixed an unrelated build break from the external removal of the 'Pending' round result: completed the documented back-compat tolerance (runtime checks cast to string; a historical migration stub now seeds 'Discussing'). Restores a clean typecheck.

releases.title: Related-chain link badge, Active/Stale dots on the Communication left pane, Watch-roles snapshot on the Dashboard

items.label: Related-opportunity chains imported via the 'Include related' toggle now render with a sky-colored 🔗 'from {Company}' pill, making it obvious those threads are anchored to the related job — clicking still navigates to the origin. Today, 'Include related' is all-or-nothing at the job level (everything on the related jobs surfaces here); per-chain selective linking is on the backlog for a follow-up.

Job rows in the Communication left pane now show a small Active/Inactive dot + a 'stale' chip (no activity 14+ days). Only renders when the Active filter chip is set to 'All' so the badges don't fight the filter when you've already scoped to one state.

Dashboard Leads grid gains a Watch roles tile — total count of watched candidate roles across active+dormant leads, plus 'across N leads' subline. Sits next to the lead status funnel so the watch-role pipeline finally has a visible top-line number.

Still queued (deferred from the v3.39 mega-request): Active/Stale badges on the Contacts left pane (needs a stale-precompute on the contacts page), and watch-roles nested under leads in BOTH view modes of Communication and Contacts with click-scoping. Both will land in a focused follow-up.

releases.title: Chains-column action buttons collapsed to icons so they fit in narrow panes

items.label: The three buttons in the chains-list column header on the Communication page — Include related (N) / Import CSV / ✨ New chain with AI — are now icon-only 7×7 buttons with title-attribute tooltips. Previously the text labels overflowed the column (especially in company-first's 4-pane layout, but also in job-first whenever the Include-related button appeared). The Include-related toggle gets a small numeric badge in its top-right corner so the count stays visible without taking horizontal space. Icons: Link2 (related), Upload (import CSV), Sparkles (new chain with AI). Mirrors the existing icon-action convention used in the right-pane chain header (UserCircle / MailPlus / Sparkles / etc.).

releases.title: Absorb model — pull conversations & meetings between leads, watch roles, and jobs (copy or cut)

items.label: Promoting a watch role now opens an 'absorb' picker: choose per conversation whether to Leave it on the lead, Copy it (lives on both the lead and the job), or Move it (cut from the lead — job-only). Pick which lead meetings to absorb as pre-screen interview rounds. Replaces the old bulk role/general/all dropdown.

Absorb more from a lead AFTER promotion: a job promoted from a lead gets an 'Absorb more from this lead…' button on its Lead-origin card — same copy/move/meeting picker, additive and idempotent (re-absorbing the same thread is a no-op).
Reverse comm-link: a conversation that scheduled a meeting now shows a 📅 jumping to that meeting (the inverse of the meeting→conversation link).
Global Communication gains a 'Watch roles' filter chip — show only the threads about a watched role (role-tagged on a lead, or watch-role-origin on a job).

Watch roles no longer carry their own Meetings card — meetings live on the lead. A role with a tagged meeting instead shows a nudge to promote it (and absorb the meeting as a pre-screen round), since a real meeting usually means it's become a job opportunity.

releases.title: Rename a lead inline, wider Communication + Contacts layout

items.label: Lead detail header now has a pencil icon next to the headline that opens a small Rename dialog. Single Headline input, Save / Cancel, Enter-to-save / Escape-to-cancel. PATCHes the lead via the existing /api/leads/:id route. Anchor person / company / role-type stay where they are — each has its own editor below.

Communication + Contacts pages widened from max-w-7xl (~1280px) to max-w-screen-2xl (~1536px). The extra horizontal space flows into the middle columns so status badges, chain action buttons, and contact rows have room to breathe.

releases.title: Related opportunities polish — collapsed empty state, same-lead sibling jobs, and a per-chain jump into the related-comms union

items.label: The 'Related opportunities' card on a job now collapses to a single small 'Link a related opportunity' link when nothing is linked — no more empty card taking up vertical space. It expands into the full card as soon as something is linked (or surfaced via a lead).

The card's 'Via lead' section now also surfaces SIBLING jobs promoted from the same lead (other watch roles that became their own job opportunities), not just the lead's prior re-engaged opportunities — each with one-click 'Link directly'. (Watch roles themselves stay non-linkable; they connect through the existing promotion bridge.)

In the Communication view, a selected chain's thread now shows a '→ See full history across N related opportunities' link when the job has linked opportunities; clicking it opens the related-chains union in the middle column.

releases.title: WhatsApp video icon, per-row CSV-subject regenerate, and dialog a11y sweep

items.label: New WhatsAppVideoIcon brand mark (green tile + white bubble + camera glyph with the classic 'tape side' lens-flare wedge). Completes the 3-way WhatsApp split — text (phone glyph) / call (microphone) / video (camera) — so chain headers can tell each apart at a glance. messageProtocolMeta wires it for the whatsapp-video protocol; text and call are untouched.

CSV import preview now has a per-row 'Regenerate subject' button (Sparkles icon next to each Subject input). Click it to reject the current AI suggestion and ask /api/ai/suggest-subject for a fresh one against THAT row's body alone — owner + contact + channel context piped through. The row gets a spinning loader while regenerating; other rows stay interactive. Combined with the existing AI-seeded default + free-text editing, every row now supports the full modify / reject-and-regenerate / confirm-via-import-button flow.

Silenced 10 dialogs' Radix 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined}' a11y warnings at the primitive level. DialogContent in src/components/ui/dialog.tsx now defaults aria-describedby to undefined (the documented Radix opt-out for dialogs whose visible title is self-describing); consumers that explicitly render <DialogDescription> still wire up correctly because Radix's context wins. One central fix instead of 13 per-dialog tweaks across ImportCsvDialog, EditMessageDialog, ChainFollowUpDialog, ChainMergeSplitMenu (×2), CommunicationComposerDialog, LogoUploadModal, AddTimelineEventButton, ResumeReassignDialog, OwnerAttachmentsCard, and InterviewRoundsCard (×3).

releases.title: Communication view can fold in related opportunities — read the full conversation arc across linked jobs

items.label: On the Communication page, when you select a Job that has linked 'related opportunities' (jobs tied together as the same underlying opportunity over time — re-engagements, requisition re-posts, variant applications), a new 'Include related (N)' toggle appears above the chains list. Turn it on and the middle column folds in the chains from every related job beneath a 'From related opportunities' divider — each row badged 'from <company>' — so the whole conversation arc (e.g. the Feb Superpanel cycle alongside the May re-engagement) reads in one place.

Clicking a related chain jumps straight to that opportunity (selects the owning job + its chain) so the thread on the right and all its actions target the correct job. Because related links are bidirectional, the toggle stays meaningful as you hop between linked opportunities.

releases.title: CSV import now AI-suggests per-message subjects in the preview, editable inline

items.label: The Import CSV preview now AI-suggests a short Subject for each kept message whose body is substantive enough to warrant one (rough rule: 20+ words OR 150+ characters AND a clear topic). Short replies like 'Sure' / 'Thanks!' / acks get no suggestion. Suggestions are surfaced inline as an editable input per row in the preview table — keep, tweak, or blank out before confirming.

The subject pass runs in the SAME analyzeImport AI call as the relevance filter + kind label — no extra round-trip, no extra latency cost. The system prompt now spells out a three-job contract (keep/skip, kind, subject) plus length thresholds + style rules (≤60 chars, no Re: prefix, no trailing period, reference real specifics from the body, never generic 'Update' / 'Following up').

Schema + provider plumbing: AnalyzeImportDecisionSchema + AnalyzeImportDecision now carry an optional nullable `subject`; both anthropic + openai providers normalize null/undefined to null on the way out; the import-csv/confirm route accepts a per-row `subject` and trims it before persisting. Older copy-prompt-mode imports and bodies the AI deemed too short still ship with `subject: ""` (no behavior change vs. v3.24).

releases.title: Meetings on leads & watch roles — reconnects/pre-screens with a time, on the calendar, carried into jobs

items.label: Leads (and watch roles) now have a Meetings card — capture a reconnect, pre-screen, intro, or info chat with its time, method (video/phone/in-person) + join link, who it's with, and prep/outcome notes. On a watch role the card is scoped to that role and auto-tags new meetings; on the lead you can tag a meeting to one or more roles. Upcoming vs past split, mark-complete, edit, delete.

Meetings show on the Calendar (teal) alongside interviews, applied dates, follow-ups and offer deadlines — each links back to the lead. Gives an upcoming meeting an actual home instead of stuffing it into an interview round prematurely.

Promoting a watch role carries its tagged meetings into the new job as pre-screen interview rounds (time, method, participants, prep/outcome notes preserved) — symmetric with the conversation carry-over. The calendar de-dupes so a carried meeting shows once (as the job round), not twice.
A meeting can be linked to the conversation that set it up (the comm chain), with a jump-link from the meeting to that thread.
New lead-meeting timeline events (scheduled / updated / removed) so the lead's activity log captures meeting changes.

releases.title: Communication provenance across leads, watch roles & jobs — context, carry-on-promotion, and origin pills

items.label: A watch role's Communication now shows the lead's general (relationship-level) conversations BELOW the role's own threads — read-only context with a 'Manage on the lead →' link, so you see the surrounding relationship without leaving the role.

Promoting a watch role to a job now lets you choose which conversations come along: just this role's, this role + the lead's general threads, or everything on the lead. They're copied (the originals stay on the lead).

Every message now records where it ORIGINATED. A job's Communication tags each chain 'from lead' / 'from watch role: <title>' / 'on this job'; a lead's Communication tags chains 'general' vs 'role: <title>'. The 'Lead origin' card on a promoted job names the watch role it came from (new promotedFromWatchRoleId).

The global Communication page shows a small origin pill on each chain row and DEDUPES promoted threads by message id — a conversation carried into a job is shown once (under the job, with its origin), not double-counted across the lead and the job.

One-shot backfill migration (migrate-comms-origin) stamped provenance on existing comms — 37 lead messages — using id cross-reference + a date fallback, and set promotedFromWatchRoleId on existing promoted jobs. Idempotent, with .bak backups.

releases.title: What's New, reimagined — feature buckets, filters, summary stats, and copy-an-idea-to-Claude

items.label: Releases are now grouped by **feature/idea**. The page defaults to a 'By feature' view (collapsible buckets, one per area) with a toggle to the classic 'Timeline'. Each bucket has a **Copy notes** button that copies that idea's combined release notes as Markdown — paste it into a fresh Claude Code session to keep building on the feature.

Every release now carries an `areas: string[]` tag (multi-valued — a release usually touches more than one feature). A deterministic keyword backfill (`npm run migrate:release-areas`, idempotent + hand-editable) tagged all existing releases; the canonical vocabulary lives in `src/lib/release-areas.ts`, and the AGENTS.md release workflow now includes `areas`.

Filtering + summary: top-of-page stat cards (total releases, New / Better / Fix counts, # feature-areas, releases this week), New/Better/Fix type chips, an area filter, and debounced search across titles + item text. Filter/search/view state is mirrored to the URL so a filtered view is shareable.

Per-release polish: collapsible releases with expand-all / collapse-all, `#vX.Y.Z` anchor links + a copy-this-release button, and inline `code` / markdown rendering of item text. Release types + Markdown helpers were extracted into `src/lib/releases.ts`.

releases.title: Related opportunities — link a job to the same opportunity over time, jump between them, and let AI read across them

items.label: New 'Related opportunities' card on every Job Opportunity page. Link a job to other jobs that represent the SAME underlying opportunity across time — a re-engagement, a refreshed requisition, an ATS re-post, or a variant application — via a searchable picker (by company or title). Links are bidirectional and peer (no parent/child); unlink any time. One-click navigation between the linked roles (e.g. the Feb Superpanel cycle ↔ the May re-engagement).

The card also surfaces opportunities reachable through a bridging lead: a job promoted from a re-engagement lead shows that lead's prior closed jobs under a 'Via lead' subsection, each with a one-click 'Link directly' to promote it to a real peer link. Linking two jobs that a lead bridges also mirrors the link into that lead's 'Previously interviewed for' list, keeping the lead and job views in sync.

AI cross-read (opt-in): the 'Draft chain follow-up' and 'Create new chain with AI' composers now show an 'Include related opportunity context' checkbox when the job has linked opportunities. When ticked, a BOUNDED summary of each related job (status, outcome, last interview round, and the last few messages — capped, never a full history dump) is fed into the prompt so the draft can draw on prior rapport and history without you re-explaining it.

Data model: new Job.relatedJobIds (bidirectional peer links) with atomic relate / unrelate API endpoints, plus a new Job.archivedTags field. The old 'related-to:<jobId>' tag workaround is migrated NON-destructively — the redundant tags are MOVED into archivedTags (kept, not deleted) and the link is promoted to relatedJobIds. Hard-deleting a job scrubs dangling links from its peers.

releases.title: CSV import bugfix — append-mode messages now inherit the chain's contact + canonical toLabel

items.label: Fix: when importing a CSV in APPEND mode (button on an existing chain row), the confirm route was leaving `toContactId` null on every imported message because it only resolved a contact from `body.contactId` / `body.newContact` — both of which the dialog deliberately omits in append mode (the chain already has a contact). The route now inherits `toContactId` from the most recent prior message on the target chain when neither was supplied, so the imported messages link to the same external party the chain was already tracking (Julien, Astha, etc.).

Fix: `toLabel` was set to `r.senderName` per-row, which resolves to 'Me' for outgoing messages (an outgoing message's sender is you, not the contact). `toLabel` is meant to be the OTHER party of the conversation, consistent across both directions. The route now resolves a single `externalLabel` once before the loop — preferring the resolved contact's actual name, falling back to the chain's existing toLabel, then to the first non-isFromMe row's senderName as a last resort — and applies it uniformly to every imported message. This is what makes chain grouping work in OutreachCard + CommunicationStreams.

releases.title: Lead & watch-role detail pages get the full job-opportunity layout (tabbed attachments, split resume cards, side ToC)

items.label: Watch-role detail pages now use the same wide, two-column layout as Job Opportunities (Priority & Status across the top, Core Info beside Fit Analysis, Requirements below) instead of the old narrow single column — and they finally have a floating section Table of Contents on the right, like leads and jobs.

Both leads and watch roles get the nice tabbed Attachments card from the job page: switch between Resume / Cover Letter / (Job Description, watch-roles only) / Logo / Other, with an inline PDF + markdown viewer, Canva URL, and pick-from-folder. Leads previously had no real attachment UI for a resume or cover letter at all.

Resume & Cover Letter are now split into two 'Resume Used' / 'Cover Letter Used' cards (matching jobs), each with a Choice dropdown, template preview, and a 'Sent' toggle. Watch roles still inherit the lead's choice by default and can override per role.
Fixed: the tailored resume / cover-letter description used to save on every keystroke. It now only saves when you click Save or press ⌘/Ctrl+S — no more mid-typing writes.
'Find matching PDF' (the fuzzy folder scan that finds a resume/cover-letter whose filename mentions the company) now works on leads and watch roles too, not just jobs.

Watch-role contacts are no longer a cramped one-liner — they render with the same rich rows as the lead/job pages (primary + relationship badges, role, email/phone/LinkedIn, notes), read-only, with a 'Manage on the lead →' link since contacts are shared at the lead level. The Logo tab on a watch role edits the shared lead logo.

releases.title: Interview cards always visible on active jobs (matches Communication's always-on pattern)

items.label: Interview Rounds, Interview Status, Interview Progress, and Interview Result cards now always render on ACTIVE job detail pages — they no longer hide until interviewing is in-flight. The Status / Progress / Result cards already show 'N/A' for their dropdowns when nothing has happened, so they just stay visible with that empty value (mirrors the dashboard table where every job has these columns).

Interview Rounds gets a contextual empty-state pane when rounds.length === 0, branching on applicationStatus + applicationProgress: 'Haven't applied yet' for Not Applied; 'Reviewing — not yet applied' for Reviewing; 'Application submitted — waiting to hear back' for Applied with no recruiter signal; 'A recruiter is engaged — expect interviews to begin soon (current progress: X)' for Applied with Application Received / Under Review / Recruiter Reached Out / Interview Requested; 'Application skipped — connected directly with a recruiter' for Skipped; 'Application rejected before any interviews' for Applied + Rejected; plus closed-door messages for Missed Application Window and Role No Longer Open. Add Round button stays visible.
ARCHIVED jobs keep the prior progressive-reveal gates — the four cards only render on an archived record if there's actually something to show. Keeps retired pages quiet.

releases.title: Sidebar controls: 3-phase dark mode, fullscreen, split screen, and a collapsible sidebar

items.label: New theme toggle in the sidebar footer cycles Light → Dark → System (sun / moon / monitor icons). Dark mode is now a real choice you control — not just whatever your Mac is set to — and it's remembered across reloads with no flash on load.

Fullscreen / expand button hides the browser chrome and dock so it's just the app. Exit from the bottom-left button (its arrows flip when active) or with ⌥Esc — plain Esc also exits, which the browser enforces and can't be turned off.

Split screen: click the split icon to duplicate the current page into a second pane side-by-side; ⌥-click for a stacked (top/bottom) split. Drag the divider to rebalance the panes (e.g. 70/30), and use the per-pane dropdown to repoint the second pane at any other page — so you can see Contacts and Communication at once. Click the split icon again to close it.

Collapsible sidebar: the header chevron collapses it to an icons-only rail (labels become hover tooltips) to reclaim space; a hide button in the footer tucks it away entirely, with a small floating button to bring it back. Useful on its own or alongside split screen.

Dark mode moved from a system-only media query to a class-based theme so the manual toggle works (existing dark styling is preserved). These controls are desktop-only; the mobile top bar is unchanged.

releases.title: Leads table: expandable watch-role sub-rows, company logos + networker chips, and jobs-style resume icons

items.label: Leads table rows with watch roles now have a chevron that expands an inline sub-table — its own header (Watch role, Location, Seniority, Status, Fit / Int / Overall, Resume, Salary, Flags) with each title linking straight into the watch-role page. Multiple leads can be expanded at once.

Leads + watch roles now show a company logo (like the card view): a single anchored company shows its logo + name; a networker referring to multiple companies shows a networking icon + a chip per company; no company shows the networking icon + '—'. The set of companies is derived from the lead's anchorCompany plus its watch roles' companies. The card view headers adopt the same logic.

Resume now renders as the same 2-icon indicator as Job Opportunities (tailored/template/none + shared/not) for both leads and watch-role rows — shared via a new ResumeStateIcons component. Watch-role sub-rows also show Fit / Interest / Overall (fit+interest) and salary when known.
The Leads table view is now wider (full page width) to fit the extra columns; the card grid stays constrained. Stale + duplicate-URL flags surface in the watch-role sub-rows too.

releases.title: Watch Roles wrap-up (Phases 8 + 9): stale-role flag, cross-lead duplicate-URL warning, and a Leads card/table view

items.label: Stale watch-role flag: an active role (Watching / Discussed / Routed) with no activity (status change, tagged comm, or edit) for longer than the new 'Stale watch role (days)' Setting (default 30) gets an amber '⚠ Nd stale' badge on its card and a '⚠ stale' badge on the role detail header. Activity is computed from dateAdded + role-stamped timeline events + role-tagged comms.

Cross-lead duplicate-URL warning: if a watch role's posting URL (normalized — protocol/www/query/trailing-slash stripped) is also watched on another lead OR already tracked as a job opportunity, the card + detail show an orange '⧉ Duplicate URL' badge, with a tooltip listing exactly where (which jobs / which leads).

Leads list gains a card ↔ table view toggle (persists in localStorage). The table shows a lead-appropriate column subset: lead/company, kind, status (+ stale), active watch-role count + primary role, resume status, next action (+ date), and last activity — with a Promote action.
Lead cards + table now show compact resume-status badges (shared? + template name vs 'Tailored'). New Settings field: staleThresholdWatchRoleDays (defaults to 30 for existing settings).

releases.title: Resume sharing on leads + watch roles (Phase 7 of 6): template/tailored choice, Canva URL, and a Job-Search-folder picker
