items.label: New Resume & Cover Letter card on the lead detail page: mark 'resume shared', choose template (Senior IC / Leadership / Balanced) vs tailored (+ note), set a Canva URL, and attach the PDF — even though you're not formally applying. Cover letter has the same controls.

The PDF can be picked from your Job Search folder (lists resume PDFs via /api/resumes/available; the chosen file is COPIED into the lead/role attachments dir so it's owned and stable) or uploaded directly. New endpoint POST /api/leads/[id]/resume-from-folder handles both lead and watch-role targets.

The watch-role detail page's Resume & Cover Letter section is now fully editable and INHERITS the lead's resume/cover-letter choice by default ('Inheriting lead's: …'), with a per-role 'Override for this role' / 'Use lead's instead' toggle. PDFs + Canva URLs are always per-owner.
Lead detail TOC gains a Resume section. The reusable LeadResumeCard targets the lead or a watch role via their existing PATCH + attachments endpoints (no changes to the working jobs resume flow).

releases.title: Watch Roles polish (Phase 6b): tag existing messages to roles + backfill role-attribution on seeded timeline events

items.label: EditMessageDialog now has a 'Tag to watch role(s)' control on lead messages — a row of role chips you can toggle to assign a general/shared message to one or more watch roles (or untag it back to general). Threaded through OutreachCard → ChainRow → OutreachRow. Complements the role page's auto-tagging of newly composed messages.

Migration scripts/migrate-fix-watchrole-timeline-attribution.ts backfills watchRoleId on watch-role timeline events created before the field existed (the 66degrees roles seeded in v3.23), so each role's detail-page Timeline shows its 'added' event instead of starting empty.

releases.title: Subject field is always available on text-channel messages (including sent + CSV-imported)

items.label: EditMessageDialog now shows the Subject field on EVERY text-channel message regardless of status — drafts, sent, and discarded. Previously the field only rendered for text drafts (and any message whose subject was already non-empty), which meant CSV-imported text messages and historical sent texts had no path to add a subject after the fact. The AI subject suggestion button from v3.27.1 works on these messages too, so you can have the AI propose a subject from the existing body.

Verbal channels (phone / video / in-person) still keep the Subject field hidden — their body is a narrative recount and a separate subject line would be redundant. Email and LinkedIn InMail are unchanged (subject always shows).

releases.title: Watch roles open into a full job-style detail page (Phase 6 of 6)

items.label: New watch-role detail page at /leads/<lead>/roles/<role> — a job-opportunity-style view with Priority & Status (inline status/priority/surfaced/primary + Promote), Core info, Fit analysis, Requirements & Responsibilities, Resume & Cover Letter, Attachments, Communication, Contacts, Notes, and a Timeline. No application/interview/offer cards — those only exist once the role is promoted. The watch-role cards on the lead now link into it.

Communication is role-scoped: the shared OutreachCard gained a restrictToWatchRoleId mode, so the role page shows only the messages tagged to that role and auto-tags anything composed there (manual, AI new-chain, and follow-up composers all forward the watchRoleIds). The card header notes '· this role'.

Watch-role Attachments: upload a JD / resume / cover letter (or other file) right on the role page; files store under the role's attachments dir and list with open/remove. Contacts are shown shared-from-the-lead with a 'manage on lead' link.

Editing reuses the Phase-3 full editor ('Edit details') plus inline status/priority/surfaced/primary controls; resume status is display-only here (full resume-share UI is the next phase). Watch-role timeline events are now stamped with their watchRoleId so the role page can show a scoped activity slice.

releases.title: AI Subject button in EditMessageDialog + clearer aiPrompt copy

items.label: New AI button next to the Subject input in EditMessageDialog. Empty subject → AI generates one from the current body and fills the field directly. Subject already populated → AI's candidate is shown in an inline 'AI suggestion' bubble below the input with Apply / Keep current buttons (hand-editing the field dismisses the candidate). Uses the existing /api/ai/suggest-subject endpoint with owner + channel + protocol + contact context so the line can reference the company, role, or recipient.
Soft-fails when the active provider can't synthesize subjects inline (e.g. Claude-Code copy-prompt mode) — surfaces a toast pointing to Settings instead of erroring.

EditMessageDialog's AI-prompt textarea now uses clearer labels + helper text — distinguishes 'used to generate this draft (edit to regenerate)' for drafts where the prompt was captured, 'no focus was captured for this draft' for older AI-generated drafts that predate v3.21 prompt persistence, and 'type to regenerate' otherwise. The prompt body's wiring (persist focus / guidance from NewChainOutreachDialog + ChainFollowUpDialog, load on re-open, Regenerate button) was already in place since v3.21 — only the copy was tightened.

releases.title: Watch Roles: role-scoped communication, watch-role attachments + lead/role resume files, and promotion that carries it all (Phase 5 of 6)

items.label: Lead communications can now be tagged to watch role(s): POST /api/leads/[id]/comms accepts watchRoleIds[] (general when empty, one or more roles otherwise); the existing PATCH already retags. This is the data path behind 'communication on the lead in general, or specifically about a watch role'.

New watch-role attachments endpoint (POST/DELETE /api/leads/[id]/watch-roles/[watchRoleId]/attachments) for resume / cover-letter / JD / extra files, stored under data/attachments/<leadId>/roles/<watchRoleId>/ so roles (and the lead's own resume) never collide. Updates that role's documents.

The lead attachments endpoint is broadened beyond logo to resume / cover-letter / job-description / extra (lead-level documents), so you can attach a shared resume PDF to a lead even without a formal application.

Promotion now carries it all: the new job is seeded with the watch role's documents, resumeUsed/coverLetterUsed/resumeShared (inheriting the lead's when the role's are unset), and priority — and it carries the communications that were occurring on THAT role (watchRoleIds includes it) plus their chains. The legacy 'copy all messages' option still copies the full thread.

Resume-file folder picker (fuzzy-match from the Job Search folder, like jobs have) is intentionally deferred to the Phase 7 resume UI; Phase 5 supports Canva URL + manual upload. The template-vs-tailored choice + Canva URL are set via the existing lead/watch-role PATCH endpoints.

releases.title: WhatsApp voice call icon — distinct from WhatsApp text

items.label: WhatsApp protocols (whatsapp-text on text channel, whatsapp-call on phone channel, whatsapp-video on video channel) were already wired since v3.9 and selectable in every protocol picker (New Outreach, Chain Follow-Up, Edit Message). Until now they all rendered the same speech-bubble-with-phone brand mark, which made a text chain and a voice call indistinguishable at a glance.

New WhatsAppCallIcon brand mark: same green tile + white bubble base, but with a microphone glyph instead of the phone handset. Used only for the whatsapp-call protocol. WhatsApp text + WhatsApp video keep the existing phone-glyph icon.

releases.title: Watch Roles → 'a Job minus the pipeline': data model for priority, resume sharing, documents, and role-scoped communication (Phase 4 of 6)

items.label: Watch roles gain Job-like fields: priority (High/Medium/Low), resumeShared, resumeUsed + coverLetterUsed (template vs tailored), and a documents object (resume / cover-letter / JD paths + Canva URLs + additional files) — so a promoted job seeds richly and resume-sharing is trackable per role. No application/interview/offer machinery (that only exists once promoted).

Leads gain lead-level resume sharing (resumeShared, resumeUsed, coverLetterUsed, documents) for the 'I shared my resume with this contact even though I'm not formally applying' case. Watch roles inherit the lead's by default and can override per role.

Communication can now be scoped to watch roles: CommsMessage and Chain carry an optional watchRoleIds[] (general when empty, one or more roles otherwise), and TimelineEvent carries an optional watchRoleId. This is the data layer for role-scoped comms + a role-scoped timeline slice (UI + promotion-carry land in later phases).

Migration scripts/migrate-to-v3_26.ts backfills the new fields on all leads and watch roles (idempotent, with backup) and seeds the 66degrees candidate roles' priorities (Gemini Architect = High anchor; Principal Cloud + Workspace = Low).

releases.title: Import CSV buttons added to the Communication Streams view (3-pane)

items.label: Fix: v3.25.0 only mounted the Import CSV affordance on the job/lead detail page's OutreachCard. The 3-pane Communication Streams view (/communication) was missing both entry points. Now: middle pane has an 'Import CSV' button next to '✨ New chain with AI' (new-chain mode), and the right-pane chain header has an Upload icon next to the MailPlus follow-up icon (append mode for that chain).

releases.title: Text-message CSV import — append to a chain or seed a new chain on a job / lead / watch-role

items.label: New 'Import CSV' button at two surfaces: (a) on each chain row → APPEND mode (imported rows attach to that chain), and (b) at the OutreachCard header → NEW-CHAIN mode (server mints a fresh chainId). Works on jobs, leads, and lead watch-role chains.

CSV parser handles iMessage exporter format (chain_name / date_utc / sender_name / is_from_me / message / attachments / service). Proper RFC-4180-style escaping for messages with commas + newlines + quotes.
Consecutive same-sender messages within 60 seconds are auto-coalesced into one message with bodies joined by '\n---\n' — matches the burst-typing convention used elsewhere in the app.
Attachments column is preserved as an inline '[Attachment: filename.pdf]' marker in the body. iMessage's internal pluginPayloadAttachment GUIDs are filtered out automatically.

AI relevance filter + kind labeler (analyzeImport) — runs as a single call to whatever provider Settings has configured (Anthropic / OpenAI / Claude Code chat copy-prompt). Decides per-row keep/skip based on an optional 'what this chain is about' hint + owner context, then assigns a CommsKind label (cold-outreach / re-engagement / scheduling / referral-support / thank-you / etc.). Adjustable in the preview before confirming.

Smart dedupe for APPEND mode — finds the latest existing message in the destination chain and skips CSV rows that match by sender + sentAt within ±2 minutes. Rows older than the chain tail with no match are kept but flagged as 'backfill' so the user can review.

Editable preview table — every parsed row shows keep checkbox + sender + timestamp + body + AI kind dropdown. Duplicate rows are pre-checked as 'skip' (rose tint); backfill rows are highlighted amber. 'Keep all' / 'Skip all' shortcuts at the top.

Contact linkage on new-chain imports — auto-matches the CSV's sender_name against the owner's existing contacts (case-insensitive, with a 'first-token' partial-match fallback). If no match, the dialog prompts to either pick an existing contact or create a new one with the phone pre-filled from the CSV.
Service column maps to messageProtocol: iMessage → 'imessage', SMS → 'sms', RCS → 'rcs', WhatsApp → 'whatsapp-text'. Unknown services fall back to 'sms' with a per-row warning icon in the preview.

Reply-to columns (reply_to / reply_to_preview) are intentionally skipped in v1 — the app's chain model doesn't yet have a per-message reply field. Adding one is a future schema upgrade; current import-time fidelity stays text-only.

releases.title: Watch Roles UI — see, add, edit, and promote candidate roles inside a lead (completes the Watch Roles feature)

items.label: Lead detail page now has a 'Watched Roles' section: each tracked role renders as a card with a fit badge, status pill, how-it-surfaced tag, why-fit/concerns, a primary-anchor star, and a JD link. The primary role is starred and visually elevated; promoted/dismissed roles drop to a dimmed 'closed' group.

Add a watched role via a quick-add dialog (title, JD URL, location, seniority, fit, surfacedBy, primary), and edit the full rich detail (work arrangement, employment type, compensation, key responsibilities/requirements, interest, status, tags, notes) via a full editor dialog. Per-card Promote, Dismiss, and Remove actions; clicking the star soft-sets the single primary anchor.

New 'Previously interviewed for' card surfaces a re-engagement lead's prior closed opportunities (from priorJobOpportunityIds) with the re-engagement trigger and links to each prior job — resolved server-side. The 66degrees lead shows its 2024 Conversational Architect process (Offer Declined · Strong Mutual Interest).

Lead Facts now shows and edits Next action + Next action by; the Status card lists all promotions[] (each linking to its spawned job) instead of a single converted link. Leads list cards surface the active watch-role count + primary role title + the next action, and the activity label now reflects timeline events (e.g. 'Watch role added').

The list Promote dialog is now watch-role-aware (pick which role to promote, defaulting to the primary) and fixes a latent bug where its seed fields never populated when the selected lead changed (useState-as-effect misuse). Lead detail TOC gains Watched Roles + Prior Opportunities sections.

releases.title: Verbal-recount bubbles in Communication Streams now read as recounts, not attributions

items.label: Phone / video / in-person recounted-summary message bubbles in the Communication Streams view no longer display '{contactName} · {kind}' as a header (which read as if the bubble was a message FROM the contact). They now use an initiator-aware natural-language header: 'You called Astha Sethi', 'Astha Sethi called you', 'You video-called Karl', 'You met with Howard', etc. The body is Alex's narrative summary of a 2-party conversation, so the bubble shouldn't pose as anyone's authored words.

Verbal-recount bubbles also get a neutral muted background with a dashed border (instead of the blue 'from me' / plain 'from them' tints) to reinforce that this is a recount, not a direct message. The 'Recounted summary' badge stays on the right of the header for clarity.

releases.title: Settings → AI Prompts surfaces all 9 system prompts; verbal-recount audit migration

items.label: Settings → AI Prompts now exposes all 9 system prompts (not just 3): Parse Listing, Follow-Up Email, Rewrite Email, Bullets → Email, Reply Email, Chain Follow-Up, Chain Summary, New Outreach (cold start), and Suggest Subject. Each is independently editable + resettable, persisted to data/settings.json, and falls back to the built-in default when null.

Grouped tab UI: prompts are organized into 5 categories — Listing / Email Drafts / Chain / Outreach / Helpers — with a category-level unsaved-changes dot and a slot-level dot inside multi-slot categories. The save button writes only what's actually changed.

Schema + provider wiring: PromptOverridesSchema now persists chainFollowUpSystem / newOutreachSystem / suggestSubjectSystem; both anthropic + openai providers honor user overrides on draftChainFollowUp / draftNewOutreach / suggestSubject (falling back to the channel-aware default when null).

v3.23.1 migration script — audits every verbal-channel (phone / video / in-person) recount-summary message on active jobs + leads, confirms each is in v3.22 narrative form, and idempotently backfills the `from` field (initiator: 'me' = Alex started, 'company' = the other party). All 4 current active verbal messages were already compliant.

releases.title: Watch Roles — track multiple candidate roles inside a lead, promote each into its own job (data model, migration + API)

items.label: New WatchRole entity nested inside a Lead — a specific posting or whispered req tracked within a relationship. Shape is 'Job-parity minus the application/interview pipeline': title, jobUrl, location, work arrangement, employment type, seniority, compensation, key responsibilities/requirements, fitScore (0–10), why-good-fit, concerns, interest, surfacedBy, status, an optional 'primary' anchor star, notes, tags. A lead can now hold 0..N candidate roles instead of one free-text anchorRoleType.

Multi-promotion: Lead.convertedToJobId is superseded by a promotions[] array, so one relationship can spawn several jobs over time. Promoting a watch role leaves the lead ACTIVE (the 'converted' status is now a manual 'relationship exhausted' state, no longer auto-set). The deprecated convertedToJobId is kept as a back-compat alias mirroring the first promotion.
Re-engagement linking: leads gain priorJobOpportunityIds[] (links to past closed jobs the lead continues) plus reEngagementTrigger, and a nextAction / nextActionBy pair for 'what happens next'.

Leads now keep a lightweight timeline[] (reusing the Job TimelineEvent shape). patchLead auto-logs status and next-action changes, and dedicated repo helpers log watch-role add / update / status-change / promote / dismiss events. No heavy patchJob cascade engine — lightweight by design.

Migration scripts/migrate-to-v3_23.ts backfills the new fields on all leads (0 were 'converted', so no synthetic promotions) and seeds the 66degrees re-engagement lead with its 3 public-board candidate roles (Gemini Architect = primary anchor, Principal Cloud Architect, Workspace Architect), the link to the 2024 Conversational Architect opportunity, a re-engagement trigger, and a next action.

Reworked POST /api/leads/[id]/promote to be watch-role-centric: pass watchRoleId and the new Job is seeded from that role's rich fields (location, comp, seniority, JD bullets, fitScore, jobUrl, surfacedBy→initiatedBy) instead of the old near-empty stub. Appends to promotions[], marks the watch role Promoted, leaves the lead active, and 409s if that watch role was already promoted. Falls back to anchor-based seeding when no watchRoleId is given.

New watch-role API routes: POST/GET /api/leads/[id]/watch-roles (create with sensible defaults + company inheritance, list) and PATCH/DELETE /api/leads/[id]/watch-roles/[watchRoleId] (edit with isPrimary soft single-select + status-change timeline logging, remove).

releases.title: Verbal-channel recount mode — phone / video / in-person follow-ups become post-hoc summaries

items.label: Draft Follow-Up on a chain whose channel is phone / video / in-person now flips into RECOUNT mode — the AI writes a post-hoc narrative summary of a conversation that already happened, not talking points for an upcoming call. Output names both parties, covers both perspectives, states what was agreed or left open. Plain prose, not bullets.

New 'Who initiated?' selector in ChainFollowUpDialog when the channel is verbal — two pills (I initiated / They initiated). Drives the AI's opening attribution ('Alex called Maria…' vs 'Maria called Alex…') and the resulting message's `from` field, so the bubble renders on the right side of the chain. Defaults to 'I initiated'; flip it when they reached out.

The Focus textarea reframes itself on verbal channels: label becomes 'Your notes from the conversation (AI will write a clear recount)' with a different placeholder showing how to drop in rough notes (bullets, fragments, half-sentences). The AI weaves those notes into a coherent recount.

Updated AI prompts (system + user) and provider input across Anthropic / OpenAI / Claude-Code-chat to support the new recount mode + initiatedBy field. POST /api/ai/chain-follow-up now accepts an `initiatedBy: "me" | "them"` body field; the existing chain-follow-up shape is unchanged for non-verbal channels.

releases.title: Editor: status pill row, layout reorder, sent-time prefill, smarter Recipient + Subject visibility

items.label: Status (draft / sent / discarded) is now a 3-pill segmented control at the top of the Edit dialog, with an icon per state — Pencil for Draft (amber), paper-plane for Sent (green), X-circle for Discarded (grey). The active pill is filled; clicking another pill switches state. Replaces the hidden-in-the-grid dropdown so the message's state is the first thing you see.

Sub-type / protocol now sits next to Channel in the routing grid (they're related — protocol is the sub-type OF the channel). Interaction type + Direction get their own row. Status moved out to the pill row above; Sent at gets its own row so the 'Mark as sent now' affordance has space.

Sent messages with no captured sent-at timestamp now pre-fill the Sent-at field with the message's creation time, so legacy / quick-marked sent messages show a real date instead of a blank yyyy-mm-dd placeholder. Adjustable before Save changes — the diff persists your edit.

Recipient label (free text) field now only appears when there's no linked contact (the linked Contact's name resolves the recipient automatically when one is set). When there's no contacts list AND no existing free-text label, the field is hidden entirely. Relabeled to 'Recipient (free text — no linked contact)' so its purpose is obvious.

Subject field now also shows for DRAFTS on the text channel — so you can add an iMessage Subject header even when the AI didn't generate one. Hidden for sent/discarded text messages with no subject to keep the historical view clean.

releases.title: Editor: AI prompt always visible on drafts, subject shows when set, Mark-as-sent shortcut

items.label: AI prompt panel in the Edit dialog now shows for ANY draft on an AI-able channel (email / text / linkedin), not only for drafts with aiMode='chain-follow-up' or 'new-outreach'. Pre-v3.21 drafts and drafts whose aiMode was stripped during edits now get the prompt + Regenerate affordance too. Empty textarea when no prompt was captured — type a fresh one and Regenerate.

Regenerate now routes by msg.chainId instead of aiMode (which gets stripped or set inconsistently). If the draft is in an existing chain → chain-follow-up route (reads chain history for context). Otherwise → new-outreach route. Works on drafts that were created manually or via older AI flows.

Subject field in the Edit dialog now appears whenever there's a non-empty subject, regardless of channel — so AI-generated subjects on long text/iMessage drafts (per the v3.21 text-channel prompt change) surface and stay editable. Same change applied to the AI composer dialogs (ChainFollowUp + NewChainOutreach).

New 'Mark as sent now' button in the Edit dialog next to the Sent-at label, shown only for drafts. One click sets status=sent and auto-fills sentAt with the current time. The Sent-at input below stays editable so you can tweak the timestamp before clicking Save changes to confirm.

releases.title: Fix Messages.app body landing in the To: field instead of the message body

items.label: Open-in-Messages: after typing the phone and pressing Return, the recipient pill resolves correctly — but Messages.app's Return doesn't move focus out of the To: field (it waits for additional recipients). The next ⌘V pasted the body INTO the To: field alongside the resolved contact, leaving the actual message-input field empty. Fix: send Tab after Return to move focus to the message body field, THEN ⌘V.

releases.title: Messages.app body fix, AI subject for long texts, prompt persistence + Regenerate on drafts

items.label: Open-in-Messages now actually fills the body AND the recipient. Old `sms:DIAL;body=…` URL was unreliable on modern macOS — the body was silently dropped, and sometimes the recipient too, leaving you with an empty new compose. New POST /api/integrations/messages-app/open route uses AppleScript + System Events to ⌘N → type the phone → Return → ⌘V the body from the clipboard. Same Accessibility permission you already granted for the Mail.app reply fix covers this.

AI text drafts can now produce a subject for longer messages. The text-channel prompt was unconditionally 'no subject'; updated so short texts still come back subjectless, but multi-paragraph / 60+-word texts get a short header (which iMessage's optional Subject feature renders bold above the body). The dialogs surface the subject field whenever it's non-empty, regardless of channel.

AI prompt notes are now persisted on every AI-generated message (new `aiPrompt` field on CommsMessage). When you open a draft in the Edit dialog, the original focus / guidance you typed at generate time appears in a dedicated panel — fully editable. A ✨ Regenerate button re-runs the matching AI route (chain-follow-up or new-outreach) with your tweaked prompt and replaces the draft's subject + body, ready to review and Save changes.

releases.title: Fix Mail.app reply wiping the body + thread

items.label: 'Open in Mail.app' on a follow-up reply no longer wipes the email chain and leaves an empty body. Root cause: the AppleScript was doing `set content to body & quotedThread` on a freshly-`reply`'d outgoing message, which races with Mail's async quoted-text population — Mail's `content` read back empty, so the write set just the body (or empty), and the rich-text view replaced Mail's quoted block with a plain string. Both the body and the chain visibly disappeared within ~half a second of the reply window opening.

New approach: AppleScript opens the reply window via `reply foundMsg with opening window` (proper In-Reply-To header → real threading on the recipient side), then uses System Events to ⌘V the AI body — which the dialog already put on the clipboard — at the cursor. Mail's auto-quoted thread stays intact; your draft lands above it. First run on macOS will prompt for Accessibility permission so System Events can drive Mail; if denied, the reply window still opens and a toast tells you to ⌘V manually.

Failure mode is also better: if the keystroke fails for any reason, the route returns `ok-nopaste` (the reply window is still open and the body is still on the clipboard) instead of leaving you with an empty wiped compose.

releases.title: Send drafts via app + trash icon + discarded messages hidden by default

items.label: Open a draft in the Edit dialog and click the new 'Open in app' button — same Send-via-app hand-off as the AI composers. Auto-saves your edits to the draft first, then opens Mail.app (AppleScript reply or compose) / Gmail/Outlook web / Messages / LinkedIn. For email replies, the dialog now knows the prior inbound email in the chain (sender + subject) so Mail.app's AppleScript can open the actual thread reply window with your draft prepended. Phone-prompt persists to the contact like the AI composer flow.

Trash icon in the Edit dialog footer hard-deletes the message (removes it from jobs.json / leads.json). Distinct from status='discarded' which keeps it as a record. Confirms first — irreversible. New DELETE verb on the jobs comms route (leads already had it); jobs was the only owner missing it.

Discarded messages are now HIDDEN by default in both chain views (job/lead detail OutreachCard + /communication right pane). When a chain has any, a small 'N discarded hidden — Show discarded' toggle appears. Cleans up chains that accumulated 'wrote-then-changed-my-mind' records without losing them; you can still surface them whenever needed.

releases.title: Mail.app body fix, /communication draft refresh, phone-prompt persists everywhere

items.label: Open-in-Mail.app no longer drops the body. Root cause: macOS Mail truncates `mailto:` bodies above ~700–2000 chars, silently. v3.20 fell back to mailto: when the AppleScript reply route returned NOT_FOUND (which is what happens when Mail.app doesn't have the source email indexed — i.e., when you read mail in Gmail web). The new POST /api/integrations/mail-app/compose route opens a Mail.app compose window via AppleScript with the FULL body via argv (no URL encoding limits). It's now the primary path for Mail.app — reply tries first; on not-found, falls back to AppleScript compose-new; only resorts to mailto: if AppleScript itself fails.

/communication page: Open-in-App now refreshes the page after auto-saving the draft, so the new draft message shows up in the chain immediately. v3.20 saved the draft server-side but missed the router.refresh() call, so it wasn't visible until manual reload.

Phone-prompt persistence on the /communication page: StreamChain now carries the linked contact's id (resolved in the chain builder from the first message's toContactId, with back-fill from later messages). Open-in-Messages's 'save phone to contact for next time' now PATCHes the contact from /communication too, matching the job-detail behavior.

Last-resort fallback (mailto:) now copies the body to the clipboard FIRST so you can paste if Mail.app's compose window comes up with a truncated body — covers the unlikely case where you've denied AppleScript permission.

releases.title: Send-via-app hand-off + separate Subject/Body copy

items.label: Copy buttons split: tiny Copy icon next to the Subject AND a separate one next to the Body in both AI composers (chain follow-up + new chain). Copying the body no longer drags the 'Subject: …' line with it. The old combined Copy button is gone.

New 'Open in <App>' hand-off button in both AI composers. Saves the draft to the chain first (so you don't lose it), then opens the right app: Messages.app for text, the contact's profile for LinkedIn, and Mail.app / Gmail web / Outlook web for email — labeled to match your mailClient preference. Body always goes to the clipboard as backup. Come back to the Tracker to mark sent.

Email reply-as-reply via AppleScript: when mailClient = Mail.app AND the chain has a prior email, the new POST /api/integrations/mail-app/reply route shells out to osascript to find the matching email by sender+subject and opens a proper reply window with your AI draft prepended above the auto-quoted thread. macOS will prompt for Automation permission the first time. Falls back to a new compose when no match is found.

Gmail / Outlook web pragmatic reply: opens the thread via a sender+subject search URL and stages the body on the clipboard. One click on Reply + ⌘V and you're sending. Best-feasible without OAuth — neither service supports a deep-link to a pre-filled in-thread reply.

Open-in-Messages with smart phone handling: uses the contact's saved phone when present. If missing, an inline prompt asks for the number — entering it saves it to the contact (so future sends skip the prompt) and immediately opens Messages.app to the right conversation with the body pre-staged via the sms: URL.
LinkedIn hand-off: opens the contact's profile (or LinkedIn messaging hub when no profile URL is saved) with the body on the clipboard. Click Message, paste with ⌘V.

releases.title: AI messages keep their sub-channel + suggest a subject from the body

items.label: AI-composed messages now persist the sub-channel / protocol (LinkedIn DM vs InMail, iMessage vs SMS, Zoom vs Teams, etc.), not just for cold-start LinkedIn but for every channel and the follow-up composer too. Previously the follow-up dialog never sent a protocol and the cold-start dialog only sent one for LinkedIn — so the chain's (channel · protocol) pill came up blank.

Both AI composers (chain follow-up + new chain) now have a 'Sub-channel / protocol' dropdown in the lock-in form. It auto-fills smartly — a follow-up inherits the chain's existing protocol; a cold-start uses your up-front pick or a sensible per-channel default (text→iMessage, phone→Voice call, video→Zoom, LinkedIn→DM) — and you can override it before saving.

AI subject suggestions: for subject-bearing channels (email + LinkedIn InMail), a '✨ Suggest subject' button reads your current body and proposes a line you can edit. It also auto-fills when you click 'Lock in as sent' — but only if you've edited the body since the subject was last set, so it never clobbers a subject you're happy with. New POST /api/ai/suggest-subject + suggestSubject on the Anthropic + OpenAI providers; gracefully no-ops in Claude-Code copy-prompt mode.

The per-message Edit dialog's protocol dropdown now shows friendly labels (LinkedIn InMail, Google Meet, FaceTime audio…) instead of raw values, sharing one channel→protocol source of truth with the composers.

releases.title: Manual chain purpose auto-derived, AI sent-at fixed, Cancelled interview round status

items.label: Chain purpose no longer shows 'unlabelled' for manually-created chains. The /communication page now falls back to display-time derivation when no explicit purpose is stored: first message from you → Self-initiated, from company → Company-initiated, from system → System-notification. Existing metadata wins — this only fills the gap.

Sent-at timestamp in AI message dialogs now reflects when you click 'Lock in as sent', not when you opened the dialog. Previously both the chain follow-up and cold-start outreach dialogs initialized the suggested sent time when the dialog was first opened — if you spent time editing, that timestamp could be many minutes stale.

New 'Cancelled' round result for company-initiated cancellations — distinct from 'Withdrew' (your own exit). When a round is Cancelled, an optional free-text cancellation reason field appears in the edit form: pick from presets ('Company went with another candidate', 'Hiring freeze', 'Role eliminated', etc.) or type your own. The reason is shown beneath the round row in orange when set.

releases.title: Cold-start chains are tagged 'Self-initiated' (not 'unlabelled purpose')

items.label: A chain you start via 'New chain with AI' now reads Self-initiated. Previously the composer created the chain with no purpose metadata, so it showed 'unlabelled purpose'. The comms POST now accepts an optional chainPurpose and upserts the chain's metadata entry (jobs + leads); the cold-start composer sends 'self-initiated' since you're the one starting the thread.

Backfill migration (scripts/migrate-to-v3_18_1.ts) labeled the cold-start chains you already created — any chain containing a 'new-outreach' message that lacked a purpose is set to self-initiated. Idempotent, backs up jobs.json + leads.json, only fills missing/null purpose (never clobbers an explicit label).

releases.title: Cold-start AI outreach reaches the Communication page + multi-recipient targeting; /contacts edits per-role context

items.label: The '✨ New chain with AI' button now also lives on the /communication page — in the Chains pane header once you've focused a role/lead — not just on the job/lead detail pages. Same composer, reachable from the hub you actually browse comms in.

Pick WHO you're reaching out to: the cold-start composer now shows a multi-select checklist of the role's existing contacts (name · title · email). Choose one OR several. Selected people are sent to the AI so it addresses them by name (group greeting for 2+), the email To: field auto-fills their addresses, and the locked-in message records them all as recipients. Verified: a 2-recipient group note came back naming both.

/contacts editor parity: the per-role overlay (relationship-to-this-opening + Key/Involved/Peripheral relevance) is now editable directly from the Contacts page — previously you could only set it from the job's Contacts card. The 'this opening only — not synced' framing is shown there too.

releases.title: Create new chain with AI — cold-start outreach button on every role

items.label: New '✨ New chain with AI' button in the Communication section of every job AND lead. Opens a composer where you pick the channel (+ LinkedIn DM vs InMail), the interaction type, and an optional recipient, then write your guidance — REQUIRED here, since a brand-new outreach has no prior thread to infer from. Generate calls the v3.17.0 engine (reads the role's notes, interview rounds, and all existing chains for grounding) and returns a channel-appropriate draft.

Edit the draft, then 'Lock in as sent' or 'Save as draft' — either way it starts its OWN new chain (fresh chainId, never merged into an existing thread) with the right channel / protocol / interaction-type, recipient, timestamp, and email From/To/CC/BCC headers when it's an email. Mirrors the v3.14 follow-up lock-in flow, including the draft 'not sent yet' state.

Verified end-to-end: generation returns a real draft, lock-in forms a distinct chain with correct metadata, and the existing follow-up generator now also distinguishes LinkedIn DM vs InMail styling (v3.17.0).

releases.title: AI writing styles know LinkedIn DM vs InMail — plus a cold-start outreach engine

items.label: AI message drafting is now (channel, protocol)-aware: LinkedIn splits into a DM style (no subject, 40-90 words, peer-to-peer, light sign-off) and an InMail style (has a subject, 80-130 words, cold-formal opener since you're not connected). Email / text / phone-talking-points unchanged. This applies to the EXISTING chain follow-up generator right now — it reads the chain's LinkedIn sub-type and matches it.

New cold-start outreach engine: POST /api/ai/new-outreach drafts the FIRST message of a brand-new chain (not a reply/follow-up). Guidance is REQUIRED and is the dominant intent; the role's notes, interview rounds, and every existing chain are passed as background so the message is grounded and doesn't repeat another thread. New newOutreach prompts + draftNewOutreach on all 3 AI providers (Anthropic / OpenAI / Claude-Code copy-prompt).

The 'Create new chain with AI' button + dialog (pick channel/protocol/interaction-type, write your guidance, generate, then lock-in/draft into a new chain) lands next as v3.17.1 — the generation engine it calls is shipped and verified here.

releases.title: Attach an existing person to a role (with auto-link)

items.label: New 'Attach existing' button on a job's Contacts card opens a searchable directory of everyone you already track (deduped across all jobs + leads). Pick someone and they're added to this role with their name/title/email/phone/LinkedIn/company-type copied — and crucially LINKED, so future edits to those person-level fields sync across all their roles. The per-opening context (relevance + role-relationship) starts fresh on the new role.

Auto-link on attach: if the person you pick wasn't linked yet (a lone record), attaching mints a canonicalPersonId and backfills it onto their existing record(s) too — so the whole set becomes connected going forward. New GET /api/people endpoint powers the picker; POST /api/jobs/[id]/contacts/attach does the linking.
Remove-from-role is now explicit: the confirm spells out that removing only detaches them from THIS opening and leaves their records on other openings untouched.

releases.title: Contacts: one person, many roles — person-level truth + per-opening context

items.label: A contact is now treated as one PERSON whose stable facts — name, title/role, email, phone, LinkedIn, contact-type, represents-company — auto-sync across every opening they're attached to (linked by canonicalPersonId, jobs + leads). Edit once, updates everywhere. Expanded from v3.15's identity-only sync after real data showed it was safe for these fields.

NEW per-role overlay on each contact: 'What they are to this opening' (free text) + a Relevance marker (Key / Involved / Peripheral). These are PER-OPENING and never sync — the same person can be the key hiring manager on one req and peripheral on another. Editable in the job's Contacts card under a dashed 'For this opening only' section; shown on each contact row with a colored relevance pill.

Grounded in your real data: notes, relationship, and how-we-connected were found to carry per-opening nuance (e.g. Tariq is the 'Referrer' for the Architect role but just a known contact for the PS role), so they were classified as per-role (not synced) rather than risk clobbering them.

Migration scripts/migrate-to-v3_16.ts: links same-person duplicates by canonicalPersonId, gap-fills blank email/phone/LinkedIn from siblings, and reconciled Bobby's two Genesys records — his shared title 'Genesys manager' became the synced role, while each opening's specifics ('leads the team' / 'created the req — likely hiring manager') moved into the new per-role field with Key/Involved relevance. Idempotent, backs up jobs.json + leads.json, never writes your own phone number.

releases.title: Shared contacts stay in sync — edit a person once, their identity updates on every role

items.label: When the same person is attached to multiple openings (linked by canonicalPersonId, e.g. the 5 Genesys folks on 2 roles), editing their email / phone / LinkedIn on one role now silently propagates to every other role — across both jobs AND leads. No more silently-stale duplicate records. The Edit-contact dialog confirms with a 'synced identity to N other roles' toast.

Deliberately scoped to person-IDENTITY fields only (email/phone/LinkedIn). Job-context fields are NOT auto-synced: role, notes, isPrimary stay independent per opening. This protects intentional per-role context — e.g. Bobby is described as 'leads the team' on one Genesys role and 'hiring manager who created the req' on another; those don't get clobbered.

Propagation runs server-side in the contacts PATCH route (new lib/storage/people-sync.ts), so it applies no matter which editor you use, and routes through patchJob/patchLead so each sibling write is still mutex-guarded and atomic. Only the fields you actually touched are synced — untouched identity fields (e.g. an existing LinkedIn URL) are never overwritten.

releases.title: Contacts — company count no longer double-counts people shared across roles

items.label: Company-first view: the per-company contact count is now DISTINCT people, not the sum of each role's contact list. Genesys showed '6 jobs · 10 contacts' when 2 of its openings shared the same 5 employees — it now correctly reads '6 jobs · 5 contacts'. All 5 people stay attached to BOTH roles (the attach-to-many-roles behavior is unchanged); only the rolled-up COUNT recognizes them as the same humans.

Dedup uses the same case-insensitive normalized-name key the contact-first view already uses (lowercase + collapse whitespace + trim), so the company sidebar count now reconciles with the number of distinct rows you see when you toggle to contact-first. The page-level grand total sums these deduped per-company counts, so it always adds up to the visible sidebar numbers.

releases.title: Save AI follow-ups as draft — adds to chain with a 'not sent' badge

items.label: The Chain Follow-Up dialog now has a 'Save as draft' button alongside 'Lock in as sent'. Saving as draft adds the message to the chain with status=draft and sentAt=null — it joins the thread immediately, shows up everywhere the chain renders, and stays fully editable. Because sentAt stays null, drafting does NOT count as activity (the chain's staleness clock isn't reset by an unsent draft).

Both save variants share the same inline form (interaction type + channel + email headers). The Sent-at picker only appears for the 'sent' variant; drafts skip it. Once a draft is in the chain you can mark it sent later from the job/lead chain row ('Mark sent' button), or edit it via the per-message Edit dialog.

Draft indicator on the /communication thread bubble: messages with status=draft now render an amber 'Draft · not sent' pill (FileEdit glyph) next to the author/kind line. The /jobs/[id] + /leads/[id] OutreachCard already surfaced drafts via the status pill + 'N drafts' chain-row badge.

releases.title: Sender dropdown — From-email combo + phones reference panel

items.label: Email From/accountEmail fields in the message Edit dialog and the Chain Follow-Up dialog are now dropdowns of YOUR own email accounts, with an 'Other (custom)…' sentinel that swaps to a free-text input. Auto-classification logic stays: as you pick a Gmail or Outlook address, the brand pill renders inline next to the field. The dropdown applies symmetrically: `accountEmail` (your mailbox) always uses the dropdown; `fromEmail` uses it only when direction = me (you sent the message) and falls back to free input when direction = company (their From: header).

Sources of the dropdown: settings.userEmails (configurable list) ∪ {settings.senderEmail} ∪ distinct accountEmail values from message history. New helper lib/utils/user-accounts.ts collectUserEmails() does the dedupe-merge; case-insensitive on trimmed addresses. Configure list editing in Settings → Mail is a follow-up patch; for now edit data/settings.json directly to add userEmails: ["..."] / userPhones: ["..."].

Phone-numbers reference panel for text/phone/video/in-person channels: when you have userPhones configured, the message Edit dialog + Chain Follow-Up lock-in form render a small read-only chip panel with your numbers. Click a chip to copy. (Real per-message senderHandle field for non-email channels is queued for a future patch — the schema doesn't track that yet.)

Settings schema: new optional fields userEmails: string[] and userPhones: string[]. Defaults to [] so pre-v3.14.3 settings.json validates without migration. Threaded through /jobs/[id], /leads/[id], /communication server pages → OutreachCard / LeadDetail / CommunicationStreams → dialogs.

releases.title: Per-message Edit — channel-aware editor on every chain message

items.label: New inline Edit (Pencil icon) button on every message — both on /jobs/[id] + /leads/[id] OutreachCard expanded chain rows AND on /communication right-pane thread bubbles. Opens a channel-aware EditMessageDialog that exposes ALL editable fields on a CommsMessage: subject, body, channel, interaction type, direction (me / company / system), status (draft / sent / discarded), sent-at, linked-contact, free-text recipient label, recounted-summary flag, sub-type protocol (iMessage / SMS / Zoom / InMail / etc.), and the email headers when channel=email (accountEmail / fromEmail / to / cc / bcc).

Diff-aware PATCH: the dialog only sends fields you actually changed, leaving everything else untouched on the server. When you switch channel OUT of email, the email-only fields auto-clear (fromEmail=null, toEmails=[], etc.) so stale Gmail/Outlook badges don't linger across a channel switch. Same auto-clear for messageProtocol when the new channel doesn't support the prior value.
Chain identity preservation: edits NEVER touch the message's chainId, so any merge/split assignments survive. If you want to rebucket a message, use the chain-level Merge/Split menu (v3.12).

From-field brand pill: the email From input auto-classifies the domain via emailAccountFromAddress() and renders the Gmail (red) / Outlook (sky) brand pill in real time as you type — matches the per-message badge that renders on the bubble.

API: /api/jobs/[id]/comms?msgId=... and /api/leads/[id]/comms?msgId=... PATCH already supported partial updates via spread merge; no route changes needed. Server now accepts and persists accountEmail / fromEmail / toEmails / ccEmails / bccEmails / messageProtocol on PATCH bodies (these fields were added to POST in v3.14.1; PATCH inherits via spread).

releases.title: Chain follow-up lock-in: email From / To / CC / BCC with auto-fill + brand pill

items.label: Lock-in form on the ChainFollowUpDialog now exposes email-header inputs (From / To / CC / BCC) when the lock-in channel is email. Auto-filled from the most recent email message in the chain: continuing your thread copies fields as-is; replying to an inbound message reply-swaps (their From becomes our new To; the mailbox of yours they wrote TO becomes our new From; their CCs minus your own address stay). User can edit anything before sending.

From input shows a Gmail (red) or Outlook (sky) brand pill once the domain resolves via emailAccountFromAddress(). Persisted as both accountEmail and fromEmail so the per-message brand badge in chain bubbles reads correctly afterward.

/api/jobs/[id]/comms and /api/leads/[id]/comms POST handlers extended to accept and persist accountEmail, fromEmail, toEmails[], ccEmails[], bccEmails[], and messageProtocol. Empty / non-string entries filtered out server-side. Existing POST callers unaffected when fields are omitted.
Address inputs accept comma- or semicolon-separated lists; parsing trims whitespace and drops empties before submission.

releases.title: AI chain follow-up — draft channel-aware replies with optional focus and one-click lock-in

items.label: New 'Draft AI follow-up' button (MailPlus icon) on every chain — both on the /communication chain header AND on the /jobs/[id] + /leads/[id] OutreachCard chain rows. Opens a new ChainFollowUpDialog that reads the full chain history, owner context (job/lead facts, interview rounds), and sibling-chain summaries to draft a follow-up message.

Optional 'Focus' input in the dialog — free-text describing what you want to follow up about (e.g. 'ask if they have a senior role open again'). When provided, the AI honors your focus as the primary intent; when blank, the AI auto-infers from chain history (warm re-open if quiet >30d, post-interview thank-you if a round just happened, reply to the last unanswered inbound, etc.).

Channel-aware tone: the dialog has a Channel select that drives the AI's writing style — email gets a subject + ~120-word body; LinkedIn gets 80-120 words conversational; text/iMessage gets 1-3 short sentences (~40 words, no greeting/sign-off); phone/video/in-person produce talking-point bullets instead of a written script.

Lock-in flow: after editing the draft, click 'Lock in as sent' → inline form opens with Interaction Type (auto-filled from the AI's suggested CommsKind), Channel (defaults to chain primary, overridable), and Sent-at datetime (defaults to now, editable for retroactive logs). Submitting POSTs to /api/<owner>/[id]/comms with chainId set to the source chain — the new message joins the existing chain immediately, updates the owner's activity, and appears in /communication.

Works for both jobs and leads. New endpoint POST /api/ai/chain-follow-up handles the dispatch; all 3 AI providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Claude Code chat) implement draftChainFollowUp. Output JSON: { subject, body, suggestedKind }. The audit trail captures aiGenerated=true, aiProvider, aiMode='chain-follow-up' on each saved message.

releases.title: Dashboard: new Leads section (status funnel + conversions + stale watch)

items.label: New Leads card on the / Dashboard below the existing job cards. Four sub-sections: (1) Status funnel (Active / Dormant / Converted to job / Abandoned) with proportional bars; (2) Activity counts (added in 7d / 30d, stale ≥14d count); (3) Lead → Job conversion — rate + top 3 recent conversions, each linking to the spawned job via convertedToJobId; (4) Stale watch list — top 5 active leads with no activity for 14+ days (uses the same isLeadStale rule as the Communication page filter).

Conversion rate denominator includes archived/abandoned leads on purpose. Abandoning counts as 'tried and didn't pan out', so excluding them would artificially inflate the rate when you close several leads at once.

releases.title: Lead detail: floating TOC + full chain-grouped Communication card

items.label: OutreachCard is now owner-agnostic. Lead detail pages get full parity with job detail: chain-grouped Communication, AI summary, Merge/Split, channel segment dividers, Recounted-summary, per-message Gmail/Outlook badge, contact jump, deep-link hash. ChainRow / OutreachRow / NewOutreachDialog all take ownerId + ownerKind; API calls route to /api/jobs/[id]/comms or /api/leads/[id]/comms accordingly.

New floating LeadDetailToc on the lead detail page — top / bottom / up / down jumps plus 5 section anchors (Facts, Contacts, Communication, Notes, Status). Same shape as JobDetailToc; icons reflect lead-specific section labels.

Lead detail body wrapped in section anchors (toc-facts, toc-contacts, toc-communication, toc-notes, toc-status) so cross-page links from /communication and /contacts deep-scroll correctly via DetailHashScroll.

Caveat: AI email-generate tabs (Generate / Rewrite / Bullets / Reply) inside the New Communication composer are gated to ownerKind=job. /api/ai/email currently reads job-only context (application status, interview rounds). Manual entry works for leads — which is what the use-case asked for. Lead-aware AI email generation is a future patch.

releases.title: Contacts page chain rows show all (channel, protocol) segments

items.label: Each chain row under a contact on /contacts now renders every (channel, protocol) pair in the chain — matching the chain-row treatment on /communication. Was only showing the first / primary channel, which hid cross-channel chains. ContactStreamChain now carries `segments[]` populated server-side; the renderer iterates each segment with its channel icon + protocol pill (when set).

releases.title: Per-message Gmail / Outlook badge inside email chain bubbles

items.label: Each email message in an expanded chain now renders its own Gmail / Outlook brand badge inline (next to the recounted-summary badge). Computed per-message from `accountEmail` via `emailAccountFromAddress()`. Previously only the chain-level DOMINANT account was visible (in the chain row / header), which masked mixed-account chains — e.g. Alex's Gmail outgoing + recipient writing to his Outlook. Wired into both the /jobs/[id] OutreachCard expanded thread and the /communication right-pane bubbles.

releases.title: Chain row: (channel, protocol) pair pills with flex-wrap

items.label: Cross-channel chain rows now pair each protocol with ITS channel instead of rolling everything into one dominant-protocol pill at the end. A phone + text/iMessage merged chain shows 📞 phone | 💬 text · [iMessage badge] — the iMessage badge sits next to the text channel, not detached. Single-channel chains look the same as before.

Chain row containers switched to flex-wrap so 3+ segments wrap onto a second line instead of clipping. Applied in three places: OutreachCard chain row collapsed pill (job detail), CommunicationStreams middle-pane chain list, and CommunicationStreams right-pane chain header.

New shared helper `chainChannelSegments(messages)` returns deduped (channel, protocol) pairs in first-seen order. Two messages with same channel + same protocol collapse to one segment; same channel + different protocols produce two segments (e.g. text/iMessage + text/SMS).

releases.title: Channel segment dividers inside cross-channel chains

items.label: When a chain spans multiple channels (e.g. phone call → iMessage follow-up), the expanded thread now shows a small horizontal divider with a channel icon + protocol pill at the point the channel switches. One divider per contiguous segment — a 5-message phone segment followed by a 3-message iMessage segment shows exactly 2 dividers, not 8. Single-channel chains get one divider at the top (or none on tight layouts where it's redundant). Wired into both the /jobs/[id] OutreachCard expanded chain AND the /communication right-pane thread via a shared <ChannelSegmentDivider/> component.

releases.title: Cross-channel chains: manual merge/split + multi-channel icons + 'Recounted summary' flag

items.label: Communication chains can now span MULTIPLE channels — a phone call followed up by text, or a LinkedIn thread that moved to email, can all live in one chain. Each chain row / header now renders ONE channel icon per unique channel in the chain, so a phone+text merged chain shows both icons (single-channel chains look exactly as before).

New chain-row dropdown menu (… button next to the AI summary icon) with two actions: (1) Merge into another chain… — pick a sibling chain on the same job/lead; every message in the source chain is re-keyed to the target's chainId. (2) Split off messages… — tick a subset of messages in the chain; ticked messages peel off with a fresh chainId. Both wired through new POST /api/jobs/[id]/comms/bulk-chain-id and /api/leads/[id]/comms/bulk-chain-id endpoints.

New `isSummary` flag on CommsMessage. Defaults to true on phone / video / in-person messages (since you typically recount the conversation rather than transcribe it). UI shows an amber 'Recounted summary' badge on both the OutreachCard expanded messages and the /communication thread bubbles. Override checkbox in the New Communication dialog when you pasted a real transcript.

AI chain-summary prompt updated to (a) note chains may span multiple channels and treat channel switches as conversation continuity, and (b) treat 'Recounted summary' messages as paraphrased recall rather than verbatim quotes. The user prompt now tags each message with a [RECOUNTED SUMMARY] marker when applicable.

Backfill migration (scripts/migrate-summary-flag.ts) flagged 2 existing phone/video/in-person messages across 92 jobs as isSummary=true. Idempotent — safe to re-run. Pre-v3.12 backups written to data/jobs.json.pre-v3.12.<timestamp>.bak and data/leads.json.pre-v3.12.<timestamp>.bak.

releases.title: Fix /jobs redirect loop + sticky Dashboard / Jobs headers + drop Dashboard Parse-with-AI

items.label: BUGFIX: navigating from `/` (Dashboard) to `/jobs` (Job Opportunities) immediately bounced back to `/`. The FilterBar's restore-from-sessionStorage + every URL-write path hard-coded `router.replace('/?...')` — fine when the table lived at `/`, broken once it moved to `/jobs`. Now reads the current pathname via `usePathname()` so the FilterBar stays put wherever it's mounted (and is portable to any future host route).
Sticky banner on `/` (Dashboard) so the title + Job Opportunities button stay pinned while you scroll through the metric cards. Matches the pattern used by Communication, Contacts, Settings, etc.

Same backdrop-blur + border-b decoration on `/jobs` for visual parity. The layout already prevented the header from scrolling (overflow-hidden parent + shrink-0 header), this just brings the visual treatment in line with the other pages.
Dropped the Parse-with-AI button from the Dashboard header. The Dashboard's single CTA is now the Job Opportunities link; Parse-with-AI lives on `/jobs` and in the sidebar Quick Actions.

releases.title: Metrics Dashboard + Job Opportunities + Role/Stale icons + Chain Summary prompt + bugfix

items.label: BUGFIX: chain summary 500 error. Three legacy rounds in jobs.json predate the v2.26 outcomeLabels field. `roundsContextBlock` called `r.outcomeLabels.length` without a guard, which surfaced as 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' and a 500 from POST /api/ai/summarize-chain. Added ?? [] guards on outcomeLabels and participants. Also matched chainIdFor to the communication page's safeStr(toLabel, safeStr(from)) fallback so chain IDs stay consistent when a message lacks both toLabel and a resolved contact.

ROUTING: app home `/` now renders a new metrics Dashboard. The job-opportunities table moved to `/jobs` (renamed accordingly in the sidebar). Detail sub-routes `/jobs/[id]`, `/jobs/new`, `/jobs/parse` keep working alongside `/jobs/page.tsx`.

NEW DASHBOARD: card-grid metrics at `/`. (1) Activity counts — applied in last 7d/30d, added in last 7d/30d, skipped-to-interview total, in-flight interview count, stale count. (2) Pipeline funnel — Discovery / Applied / Interviewing / Awaiting Decision / Offer, with click-to-filter links into `/jobs`. (3) Rounds + response rate — completed-rounds total, rounds by type, % of Applied jobs that received any company-side comm. (4) Compensation targeting — avg min/mid/max comp across active jobs. (5) Stale watch list — top 5 Very Stale jobs with deep-link to job detail.

STALENESS TIERS: new `stalenessTier` computed field (fresh / cooling / stale / very-stale) based on days since last activity. Thresholds: <7 Fresh, 7-14 Cooling, 14-30 Stale, 30+ Very Stale. Used by the dashboard stale-watch and the new ROLE column.

JOBSTABLE ROLE COLUMN: new column between Title and APP STAT with two icons. (1) Role open/closed — DoorOpen (emerald) when job.roleOpen=true, DoorClosed (muted) otherwise. (2) Staleness tier — Sprout (emerald, Fresh), Clock (amber, Cooling), AlertCircle (orange, Stale), Skull (rose, Very Stale). Each icon has a hover-title explaining the state + days since last activity.

AI CHAIN SUMMARY PROMPT IN SETTINGS: third tab on /settings/prompts ('Chain Summary') alongside Parse Listing and Follow-Up Email. Live preview pulls the first chain on a chosen job. Override persists to settings.json.prompts.summarizeChainSystem; both Anthropic and OpenAI providers honor it.

SETTINGS PAGE WIDER: new `src/app/settings/layout.tsx` wraps every sub-page (Settings home, Prompts, Statuses, Companies, Mail, Templates, Thresholds, Data) in an 80%-width container with auto side margins (≈10% padding either side). Per-page `max-w-3xl/4xl` constraints removed.

releases.title: AI chain summaries + cross-page nav between Communication, Contacts, and Jobs

items.label: New AI Sparkles button on every communication chain — both on the /jobs/[id] OutreachCard chain rows AND on the /communication right-pane ChainHeader. Click → opens a dialog that summarizes the chain. The prompt feeds the chain messages plus, as context, the role's interview rounds and short summaries of any sibling chains on the same job/lead. Returns a structured: summary (2-4 sentences), pointsOfInterest[], actionItems[].

Chain summaries are CACHED on the Chain itself (Chain.aiSummary). When you reopen the chain the dialog renders the cached summary instantly. If new messages arrived since the summary was generated, an amber 'Summary is stale — N new messages' banner appears with a Regenerate button. New POST /api/ai/summarize-chain route + new summarizeChain method on all three AI providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Claude Code chat copy-prompt). Persisted via patchJob / patchLead.

Contact jump icon (UserCircle) on every chain (both pages) — appears whenever the chain resolves to a real contact. Click → navigates to /contacts?focus=<name>&view=contact-first, which auto-switches Contacts to contact-first view, selects the matching contact, and scrolls the row into view.

Comm jump icon (→) per chain in the Contacts page. The Communications block under each contact now shows ONE ROW PER CHAIN (channel + count + last date), not every message. Each chain row has an arrow that navigates to /communication?job=<ownerId>&chain=<chainId>, which auto-selects the right job/lead and chain on arrival.

Open Job / Open Lead links from /communication now jump to the Communication section of the destination (`#toc-communication`). The same links from /contacts jump to the Contacts section (`#toc-contacts`). New <DetailHashScroll> client component on both /jobs/[id] and /leads/[id] handles the hash scroll (the page's <main overflow-y-auto> isn't the document scroll root, so native hash anchors didn't work). Added `#toc-contacts` and `#toc-communication` anchors on the Lead detail page to match the Job detail page.

Data model: extended Chain with optional aiSummary (summary, pointsOfInterest[], actionItems[], generatedAt, aiProvider, aiModel, messageCountAtGeneration, lastMessageAtGeneration). Back-compat: pre-v3.10 chain entries validate without migration since the field is optional/nullable.

releases.title: Sub-channel pills: iMessage blue, SMS green, LinkedIn diff, icon-only in chain rows

items.label: iMessage badge recolored to blue (matches the blue-bubble convention) and SMS gets its own green-tile icon (matches the green-SMS-bubble convention). RCS stays green-toned but uses the Lucide MessageSquare glyph.

LinkedIn Message vs InMail are now visually distinct: the primary channel icon (LinkedIn brand) shows once, and the sub-channel pill switches between a chat-bubble (Message) and an envelope (InMail). No more two-LinkedIn-icons stack.

Chain-row pills are now ICON-ONLY (no text label). The label still appears in the ChainHeader (right pane / drilled-in view) where space allows, and the `title` attribute provides the platform name on hover. Reclaims horizontal space in the chain list.

releases.title: Rename outreach → comms + brand icons on every sub-channel pill

items.label: Rename: `OutreachMessage` → `CommsMessage`, `OutreachChannel` → `CommsChannel`, `OutreachKind` → `CommsKind`, `OUTREACH_CHANNEL_VALUES` → `COMMS_CHANNEL_VALUES`, `OUTREACH_KIND_VALUES` → `COMMS_KIND_VALUES`, `OutreachMessageSchema` → `CommsMessageSchema`. Field rename: `Job.outreach[]` and `Lead.outreach[]` → `.comms[]`. Dropped the deprecated `Job.followUps?` alias and the `FollowUpSchema` re-export.

API: route paths moved from `/api/jobs/[id]/outreach` and `/api/leads/[id]/outreach` to `.../comms`. The legacy `/follow-ups` job route still exists (it serves a different purpose — the AI-drafted follow-up flow) but now also POSTs into `job.comms[]`.

Brand SVGs added for every sub-channel pill where the platform has a recognizable mark: iMessage (Apple-green chat bubble), WhatsApp (green tile + phone), Google Meet (multi-color camera + monitor), Zoom (blue tile + camera), Microsoft Teams (violet tile + 'T'), Cisco Webex (teal tile + 'W'), FaceTime (green tile + video camera). Protocols without strong brand marks (SMS, RCS, voice call, etc.) use Lucide icons in the family color tone. The pill is unchanged when `messageProtocol` is null — no 'unknown' placeholder.

Migration v3.9 ran across data: 117 messages on 17 jobs had their `outreach[]` array renamed to `comms[]`; both leads got their empty arrays normalized; no `followUps` to drop (already absent). Idempotent + backed up to data/jobs.pre-v3_9-<ts>.bak.json + data/leads.pre-v3_9-<ts>.bak.json.

releases.title: Comms protocol sub-types: iMessage / Zoom / InMail / etc. + new video channel

items.label: New `messageProtocol` field on OutreachMessage captures the platform within a channel: iMessage / SMS / RCS / WhatsApp text/call/video / LinkedIn message vs InMail / Voice call / FaceTime audio/video / Google Meet / Zoom / Teams / Webex / other. Drives a small color-coded pill next to the primary channel icon in chain rows + ChainHeader (CommunicationStreams) and in OutreachCard ChainRow (job detail page). Mirrors how Gmail/Outlook badges identify the email account.

New `video` channel added to OUTREACH_CHANNEL_VALUES. Phone is now voice-only; video gets its own Lucide Video icon. NOTE: these comms-channel values are independent of InterviewRound.meetingMethod — comms is for non-interview interactions (lead-up, between rounds, offer comms, networking).

Color tones group by family: Apple (iMessage / FaceTime) → blue, Google (Gmeet) → green, Microsoft (Teams) → violet, Cisco (Webex) → cyan, WhatsApp → emerald, LinkedIn (Message / InMail) → sky, generic → muted. The pill shows a short label (e.g. 'iMessage', 'Zoom', 'InMail') so the medium is readable at a glance.
Migration v3.8 backfilled all 7 of Superpanel's text-channel records with `messageProtocol='imessage'` (the Julien Emery thread). Idempotent + backed up.

OutreachMessage gained a clarifying comment that the `outreach[]` array carries ALL comms (incoming pitches, replies, system notifications, networking touches), not just outbound outreach. A full rename remains a separate refactor.

releases.title: Communication view modes: Job-first (default) + new Company-first 4-pane

items.label: Communication page gains a view-mode toggle: Job-first (default, the existing 3-pane layout — jobs/leads → chains → thread) and Company-first (new 4-pane: companies → roles at that company → chains for the selected role → thread). Mirrors the Contacts page's mode-toggle pattern.

Company-first view aggregates jobs and anchored leads under their company; unanchored leads (no anchorCompany) bucket into a synthetic '(Unanchored leads)' row at the bottom of the company list. Each company row shows role count + chain count + company logo (when available). Selecting a company auto-selects its most-recent-comm role; selecting a role auto-selects its most-recent chain.

Existing filters (Active/Inactive/Stale, Kind: Jobs/Leads/All, Hide system-only) apply BEFORE the company aggregation — so a company shows only the jobs that pass the filter strip, and disappears entirely when no jobs survive. Filters work identically across both view modes.

View mode persists in localStorage ('comms-view-mode') so reopening the app keeps your last-used view. SSR continues to render the default Job-first markup; the saved mode is restored client-side on hydrate.

releases.title: Brand Gmail/Outlook icons + From/To/CC/BCC headers + system-only filter + Quantiphi fix

items.label: Email account badges now render the actual brand marks — inline SVG Gmail (red envelope + M trapezoids) and Outlook (2025 fluent gradient tile + O / envelope tab). Replaces the v3.5 'G' / 'O' letter chips on the /communication chain list, chain header, and the per-job OutreachCard chain row.

Email messages now show their actual mail headers — From / To / CC / BCC — in a small monospace block above the body. Renders only for email channels and only the populated rows (a record with only a To: address still looks clean). Visible in both the /communication thread pane and the per-job OutreachCard.

New 'Hide system-only' filter on the Communication page. When checked: jobs/leads whose chains are ALL system-only are hidden, and individual system-only chains inside otherwise-active jobs are also hidden. When unchecked (default): everything shows but system-only chains get a small Bot icon + 'system' pill and an amber row-tint so you can skip them at a glance.

Data model: OutreachMessage gains optional `fromEmail`, `toEmails[]`, `ccEmails[]`, `bccEmails[]`. All optional + empty defaults so pre-v3.6 records validate without migration. Cowork can now populate these to drive the new headers block.

Migration v3.6 corrective backfills: (1) Quantiphi's 11 email messages re-pointed from abisgould@gmail.com → alexbisgould@hotmail.com (v3.5's gmail default was wrong for that thread). (2) Stamped the `from` enum on 62 messages that lacked it (mostly post-v2.21 records like Quantiphi's 11 + others). Idempotent + backed up.

releases.title: Email account badges + subject collapse + bodies open by default + comms audit checks

items.label: Email chains now show a small Gmail (G, red) or Outlook (O, sky) badge next to the channel icon — both on the /communication chain list + chain header AND on the per-job OutreachCard chain rows. Makes it obvious at a glance whether a chain is on abisgould@gmail.com or alexbisgould@hotmail.com. Non-email channels skip the badge.

Subject collapse: when every message in a chain normalizes to the same subject (after stripping leading Re:/Fwd:/FW:, recursively, case-insensitive), the chain header surfaces the subject once and the per-message subject row is omitted. Chains with mixed subjects keep the per-message subject as before, since those are typically genuine pivots.
Message bodies are now expanded by default in the per-job OutreachCard and per-lead FollowUpsCard. The per-message Show/Hide toggle still works if you want a compact scan.

Audit page gains two new per-message checks: (a) any non-draft outreach message with an empty body flags 'Outreach message has an empty body'; (b) any message body that embeds 2+ speaker turns (regression to the legacy multi-turn shape) flags 'Single outreach message contains multiple back-and-forth turns'. Both are readonly hints — fix in cowork, then Confirm to dismiss.

Data model: OutreachMessage gains an optional `accountEmail` field (the user's email address used for that message). Migration v3.5 backfilled accountEmail = settings.senderEmail for every email-channel message that didn't already have one (59 messages across 15 jobs); cowork can override per-message where Alex actually used the other account.

releases.title: Dashboard filters: Interview Progress chip row + Resume Sent toggle + Resume Type tri-state (Custom/Template/None)

items.label: Added Interview Progress filter chip row between Interview Status and Job Status on the dashboard. Filter wiring shipped with v3.4.0, but the UI control was missing — clicking chips cycles through unselected → include → exclude exactly like the other status chip rows. The four mid-flight pulse values (N/A / Awaiting Next Steps / Coordinating Next Round / Delayed) are filterable independently.

New 'Resume sent' toggle in the dashboard toggle row, distinct from the existing 'Has resume file' toggle. 'Has resume file' = an uploaded PDF or Canva URL exists; 'Resume sent' = job.resumeShared = true (the resume was actually sent to the company). The two answer different questions: 'do I have material for this role?' vs 'did I send anything to them?'

New 'Resume Type' tri-state chip row (Custom / Template / None). Each job classifies as exactly one type based on resumeCreated + resumeUsed.kind: Custom if you tailored one OR used a custom; Template if you used a template; None otherwise. Combine with 'Resume sent' to ask things like 'show me Applied jobs where I sent only a template' or 'show me Skipped jobs where I drafted a custom but haven't sent it yet'.
Renamed the existing 'Has resume' toggle to 'Has resume file' for clarity vs the new 'Resume sent' toggle. Same underlying behavior; just unambiguous now.

releases.title: Skipped → appProgress=N/A cascade + new resumeShared field + dashboard Resume icon column

items.label: Cascade: applicationStatus='Skipped' now forces applicationProgress='N/A'. The Skipped path means a recruiter/insider reached out — there's no formal application pipeline to track progress on. interviewStatus stays free so Skipped jobs can interview directly via the Recruiter Reached Out → Interview Scheduled → In Progress path. Migration cleaned up 5 pre-existing Skipped jobs that had stale appProgress values (Compass CDAI Eng Mgr, Mosaic AI, Voiceflow, Superpanel, 66degrees).

New resumeShared boolean on Job, distinct from the existing resumeCreated. Created = you tailored a custom one. Shared = you actually sent it. The 2×2 grid: not-sent + nothing = early Skipped chat; not-sent + custom = drafted but waiting; sent + template = applied with stock resume; sent + custom = applied with tailored resume. patchJob auto-stamps resumeShared=true on first transition to applicationStatus='Applied' (applying necessarily means sending). User can toggle independently for the Skipped path where you might send a resume only after the recruiter asks for one.

Resume Used card on the job detail page now has TWO checkboxes in its header: 'Created' (tailored a custom resume) and 'Sent' (resume was sent to the company). Each persists independently via PATCH /api/jobs/:id.

Dashboard table: new Resume column inserted between App Stat and App Prog. Cell shows 2 icons encoding 2D resume state — TYPE on the left (Sparkles for custom, FileText for template, Minus for none) + SENT on the right (filled Send for shared, muted Send for not-yet-sent). Tooltip explains the combination. The 47 Applied jobs render Sparkles/FileText + filled Send; the 5 Skipped jobs render Minus + muted Send (unless 'Sent' was checked); etc.

Migration script (scripts/migrate-to-v3_4_2.ts) backfilled resumeShared on all 92 active jobs: true for the 54 Applied jobs, false for the 36 in other states. Also reset 5 Skipped jobs' appProgress to N/A. Idempotent + backup.

releases.title: Enum tightening: Awaiting Decision moved from Interview Progress → Job Status, added Coordinating Next Round, smart-update fixed Quantiphi appProgress

items.label: Awaiting Decision removed from Interview Progress (it was a post-completion concept — interviews done, waiting on offer-or-not verdict — that didn't fit the mid-flight-pulse axis). Added to Job Status instead, slotted between N/A and Waiting on Offer. Distinct from 'Waiting on Offer' which implies they've already said yes; 'Awaiting Decision' is for the limbo when interviews wrap but there's no verbal commitment yet.

Added 'Coordinating Next Round' to Interview Progress — captures the in-between-rounds scheduling-back-and-forth phase that 'Awaiting Next Steps' doesn't quite cover (the next round is confirmed, you're just sorting times). Final Interview Progress values: N/A / Awaiting Next Steps / Coordinating Next Round / Delayed.

Smart-update migration (scripts/migrate-to-v3_4_1.ts) ran cleanly: fixed 1 inconsistent row (Quantiphi — Applied + interview In Progress, but appProgress was still 'Awaiting Response' from before the application advanced; snapped to 'Application Progressed'). Zero rows had the removed 'Awaiting Decision' interviewProgress value (no data to migrate there). Idempotent + backup.

AI prompts auto-pick up the enum changes via the existing statusEnumsSection injector — Claude Code chats know about the new Job Status 'Awaiting Decision' value and the new Interview Progress 'Coordinating Next Round' without any prompt-template edits.

releases.title: Status pipeline rebalance: new Interview Progress (mid-flight pulse) + Application Progressed conclusion + InterviewStatus pre-interview stages + APP STAT / APP PROG / INT STAT / INT PROG dashboard headers

items.label: New Interview Progress field (mid-flight pulse) — separate axis from Interview Status. Values: N/A / Awaiting Next Steps / Awaiting Decision / Delayed. Renders as its own card on the job detail page (sits next to Interview Status when interviewing is in-flight). Hidden by progressive-visibility when interviewStatus is N/A or terminal; patchJob's cascade also forces N/A in those cases so the field never carries stale state outside an in-flight stage.

Application Progress rebalanced. Pre-first-interview stages (Recruiter Reached Out / Interview Requested / Interview Scheduled) moved OUT to Interview Status. Mid-flight pulse value (Awaiting Next Steps) moved OUT to Interview Progress. New terminal value: 'Application Progressed' = applied AND moved on to the interview pipeline. AppProgress now reads cleanly as 'their response to your application' without conflating with the interview pipeline.

Interview Status now ONLY tracks chronological stage on the interview pipeline. Values reordered for natural progression: N/A → Recruiter Reached Out → Interview Requested → Interview Scheduled → In Progress → Final Round Scheduled → Completed / Ended Prematurely. Mid-flight pulse values (Awaiting Next Steps / Awaiting Decision / Delayed) moved to the new Interview Progress field so the two dimensions don't get mixed.

Migration script scripts/migrate-to-v3_4.ts touched 7 jobs cleanly: 6 had pre-interview stages stuck in applicationProgress (Compass CDAI, Electric Mind, Rogers, CDAI AI Eng Mgr, Voiceflow, Google AI TM) — moved to interviewStatus, applicationProgress set to 'Application Progressed'. 1 (Voices) had 'Awaiting Next Steps' duplicated across both fields — moved to interviewProgress, interviewStatus advanced to 'In Progress' since rounds had happened. All 91 active jobs initialized with interviewProgress='N/A' field. Idempotent + backup.

Dashboard column headers renamed: APP → APP STAT, INTERVIEW → INT STAT. APP PROG kept. New INT PROG column shows the mid-flight pulse (— when N/A). Consistent 8-char abbreviation style across the four status columns.

patchJob cascade updated. PROGRESS_NO_INTERVIEW dropped the moved values (Recruiter Reached Out, Interview Requested) — those are valid InterviewStatus values now.
